He comes before God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection as a noble master, until he joins the messengers. And a man whom God has given knowledge in the world, but he is stingy with it toward the servants of God, taking greed from them and selling it for a price—that one comes on the Day of Resurrection bridled with a bridle of Fire. A caller will call out before the heads of creation: "This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so. God gave him knowledge in the world, but he was stingy with it toward His servants, took greed from them, and sold it for a price." He will be punished until the reckoning of the people is finished.'"

More severe than this is what is reported that a man used to serve Moses, peace be upon him, and he kept saying: "Moses, the chosen one of God, told me; Moses, the intimate of God, told me; Moses, the speaker with God, told me," until he became wealthy and his property multiplied. Moses, peace be upon him, missed him and kept asking about him, but found no news of him. Until one day a man came to him with a pig in his hand and a black rope around its neck. Moses, peace be upon him, said to him: "Do you know so-and-so?" He said: "Yes." He said: "This is that pig." Moses said: "O Lord, I ask You to return him to his state so that I may ask him what brought this upon him." God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: "Had you called upon Me with the supplication with which Adam called upon Me, and those below him, I would not have answered you in this. But I will inform you why I did this to him: because he sought the world through religion."

More severe than this is what Muʿādh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, reported, as a stopped (mawqūf) and in one narration as raised (marfūʿ), from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that he said: «Among the temptations of the scholar is that speech is more beloved to him than listening.» For in speech there is embellishment and excess, and error is not safe for its speaker; while in silence there is safety and knowledge.

Among the scholars is one who hoards his knowledge and does not like it to be found with anyone else—that one is in the first level of the Fire. Among the scholars is one who, in his knowledge, is like a sultan: if anything of his knowledge is rejected, or anything of his right is belittled, he becomes angry—that one is in the second level of the Fire. Among the scholars is one who directs his knowledge and the rare reports of his hadith to the people of honor and wealth, and does not deem the needy worthy of it—that one is in the third level of the Fire. Among the scholars is one who sets himself up for legal rulings (fatwā) and gives rulings in error, and God, Exalted, hates the pretentious—that one is in the fourth level of the Fire. Among the scholars is one who speaks with the speech of the Jews and Christians to make his knowledge appear abundant—that one is in the fifth level of the Fire. Among the scholars is one who takes his knowledge as a means of manliness, nobility, and reputation among the people—that one is in the sixth level of the Fire. Among the scholars is one whom pride and self-conceit carry away: if he admonishes, he is harsh, and if he is admonished, he takes offense—that one is in the seventh level of the Fire.

So upon you, O brother, is silence, for in it you overcome Satan. And beware of laughing without wonder, or walking without purpose.

In another report: «The servant is granted praise that fills what is between the east and the west, yet it weighs not with God the wing of a gnat.»

It is reported that a man from Khurasan brought to al-Ḥasan, after he had left his gathering, a purse containing five thousand dirhams and ten garments of fine cloth, and said: "O Abū Saʿīd, this is spending money, and this is clothing." Al-Ḥasan said: "May God give you well-being. Keep your spending and your clothing with you. We have no need of that. Whoever sits in a gathering like mine and accepts from people like this will meet God, Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection with no portion of good."

From Jābir, may God be pleased with him, as stopped and raised: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: «Do not sit with every scholar, but only with a scholar who calls you from five to five: from doubt to certainty, from ostentation (riyāʾ) to sincerity, from desire for the world to asceticism, from pride to humility, and from enmity to sincere counsel.»

God, Exalted, said: {So he came out to his people in his adornment. Those who desire the life of this world said, "Oh, would that we had like what was given to Korah! Indeed, he is of great fortune." But those who had been given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of God is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds"} (28:79-80). Thus God distinguished the people of knowledge by their preference for the Hereafter over the world.

Among the marks is that his action does not contradict his speech. Rather, he does not command anything unless he is the first to act upon it. God, Exalted, said: {Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves?} (2:44). And He said, Exalted: {Greatly hateful to God is it that you say what you do not do} (61:3). And He said, Exalted, in the story of Shuʿayb: {And I do not intend to differ from you in what I forbid you} (11:88). And He said, Exalted: {And fear God, and God will teach you} (2:282). And He said, Exalted: {And fear God and know} and {And fear God and listen} (5:108). And He said, Exalted, to Jesus, peace be upon him: "O son of Mary, admonish yourself; if you are admonished, then admonish the people; otherwise, be ashamed before Me."

The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: «On the night of my night journey, I passed by people whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire. I said: "Who are you?" They said: "We used to command good and not do it, and forbid evil and do it."»

And he said, peace be upon him: «The destruction of my community is through a wicked scholar and an ignorant worshipper. The worst of the worst are the worst of the scholars, and the best of the best are the best of the scholars.»

Al-Awzāʿī, may God have mercy on him, said: "The churches complained of what they found of the stench of the corpses of the disbelievers, and God revealed to them: 'The bellies of the evil scholars are more foul than what you are in.'"

Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, said: "It has reached me that the wicked among the scholars will be dealt with on the Day of Resurrection before the idol worshippers."

Abū al-Dardāʾ, may God be pleased with him, said: "Woe to the one who does not know—once; and woe to the one who knows but does not act—seven times."

Al-Shaʿbī said: "On the Day of Resurrection, a people from the people of Paradise will look upon a people from the people of the Fire and say: 'What brought you into the Fire, when we were admitted to Paradise by virtue of your discipline and teaching?' They will say: 'We used to command good and not do it, and forbid evil and do it.'"

Ḥātim al-Aṣamm, may God have mercy on him, said: "There is none on the Day of Resurrection with more intense regret than a man who taught people knowledge, and they acted upon it while he did not act upon it—so they succeeded by his means, and he perished."

Mālik ibn Dīnār said: "When the scholar does not act upon his knowledge, his admonition slips from the hearts as rain slips from smooth rock."

And they recited:
"O admonisher of the people, you have become accused, for you blame them for things you yourself commit. You counsel them with effort in admonition, yet by my life, you are the one who commits the deadly sins. You blame the world and people desiring it, while you desire it more than they."

And another said:
"Do not forbid a trait and then commit its like—a shame upon you, when you do it, is great."

Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, may God have mercy on him, said: "I passed by a stone in Mecca upon which was written: 'Turn me over and take heed.' I turned it over, and upon it was written: 'You do not act upon what you know, so how do you seek knowledge of what you do not know?'"

Ibn al-Sammāk, may God have mercy on him, said: "How many are those who remind of God while forgetting God! How many are those who warn of God while being audacious against God! How many are those who bring near to God while being far from God! How many are those who call to God while fleeing from God! How many are those who recite the Book of God while being detached from its signs!"

Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, may God have mercy on him, said: "We have been eloquent in our speech and did not err in grammar, but we erred in our deeds and did not correct them."

Al-Awzāʿī said: "When grammatical correctness (iʿrāb) comes, humility (khushūʿ) departs."

Makhūl reported from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm that he said: "Ten of the Companions of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, told me: 'We were studying knowledge in the mosque of Qubāʾ when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, came out to us and said: "Learn whatever you wish to learn, for God will not reward you until you act."'"

Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "The example of one who learns knowledge and does not act upon it is like a woman who committed adultery in secret, became pregnant, and her pregnancy became apparent, and she was disgraced. Likewise, whoever does not act upon his knowledge, God, Exalted, will disgrace him on the Day of Resurrection before the heads of the witnesses."

Muʿādh, may God have mercy on him, said: "Beware of the slip of the scholar, for his status among creation is great, and they follow him in his slip."

ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "When the scholar slips, a scholar of creation slips with his slip." And ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Three things by which the age is demolished, one of them being the slip of the scholar."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "There will come upon the people a time in which the sweetness of hearts will become salty, and on that day neither the scholar nor the learner will benefit from knowledge. The hearts of their scholars will be like salty marshes upon which the rain of heaven descends, yet no sweetness is found in them. That is when the hearts of the scholars incline to love of the world and prefer it over the Hereafter. Then God, Exalted, will strip from them the springs of wisdom and extinguish the lamps of guidance from their hearts. Their scholar will tell you, when you meet him, that he fears God with his tongue, while wickedness is apparent in his deed. How fertile are the tongues on that day, and how barren the hearts! By God, there is no god but He—that is only because the teachers taught for other than God, Exalted, and the learners learned for other than God, Exalted."

In the Torah and the Gospel it is written: "Do not seek knowledge of what you have not learned until you act upon what you have learned."

Ḥudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, said: "You are in a time in which whoever abandons a tenth of what he knows is destroyed. And there will come a time in which whoever acts upon a tenth of what he knows is saved—because of the abundance of the idle."

Know that the example of the scholar is like the example of the judge. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «The judges are three: a judge who judged with the truth while knowing it—that one is in Paradise; a judge who judged with injustice while knowing or not knowing—he is in the Fire; and a judge who judged with other than what God commanded—he is in the Fire.»

Kaʿb, may God have mercy on him, said: "There will be at the end of time scholars who make the people abstain from the world while they do not abstain; they frighten the people but do not fear; they forbid frequenting rulers but go to them; they prefer the world over the Hereafter; they eat with their tongues; they draw near the rich and not the poor; they are jealous over knowledge as women are jealous over men; one of them becomes angry at his companion if he sits with another. Those are the tyrants, the enemies of the Merciful."

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: «Satan may make you procrastinate through knowledge.» It was said: "O Messenger of God, how is that?" He said: «He says: "Seek knowledge and do not act until you know." So he remains saying "seek knowledge" and procrastinating action until he dies without having acted.»

Sari al-Saqaṭī said: "A man withdrew for worship, and he was eager to seek the knowledge of the outward. I asked him, and he said: 'I saw in a dream a caller saying to me: "How long will you waste knowledge? May God waste you!" I said: "But I memorize it." He said: "The preservation of knowledge is acting upon it." So I abandoned seeking and turned to action.'"

Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, said: "Knowledge is not in the abundance of narration; knowledge is reverence (khashyah)."

Al-Ḥasan said: "Learn whatever you wish to learn, for by God, God will not reward you until you act. The foolish have as their concern narration, and the scholars have as their concern observance."

Mālik, may God have mercy on him, said: "Seeking knowledge is good, and spreading it is good, if the intention is sound in it. But look at what is incumbent upon you from morning to evening, and do not prefer anything over it."

Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, said: "The Quran was revealed to be acted upon, but you have taken its study as your action. And there will come a people who will straighten it like arrows; they are not the best of you."

The scholar who does not act is like the sick man who prescribes medicine, and like the hungry man who describes the delicacies of food without tasting them. In its meaning is His saying, Exalted: {And woe to you for what you describe} (21:18).

In the report: «What I fear for my community is the slip of a scholar and the argument of a hypocrite over the Quran.»

Among the marks is that his concern is with acquiring the knowledge that is beneficial for the Hereafter, which encourages obedience, avoiding the sciences whose benefit is little and in which argumentation and idle talk abound.

The example of one who turns away from the knowledge of deeds and occupies himself with disputation is like a sick man with many ailments who has found a skillful physician at a time when he fears his death is near, yet he occupies himself with asking about the properties of drugs and medicines and the rarities of medicine, abandoning his crucial need for which he will be held accountable. That is pure foolishness.

It is reported that a man came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and said: "Teach me of the rarities of knowledge." He said: «What have you done with the head of knowledge?» He said: "And what is the head of knowledge?" He said: «Have you known the Lord, Exalted?» He said: "Yes." He said: «What have you done regarding His right?» He said: "What God willed." He said: «Have you known death?» He said: "Yes." He said: «What have you prepared for it?» He said: "What God willed." He said: «Go and master what is there, then come and we will teach you of the rarities of knowledge.»

Rather, the learner should be of the kind reported from Ḥātim al-Aṣamm

chapters.title_en: The Seventh Chapter on the Intellect, Its Nobility, Its Reality, and Its Divisions
chapters.arabic_text: || الباب السابع في العقل وشرفه وحقيقته وأقسامه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to bind, restrain, or hold back" — as in the rope (ʿiqāl) that hobbles a camel; hence the intellect is that which restrains the soul from base desires and error.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿaql is the faculty of grasping necessary, universal truths (ḍarūriyyāt) and deriving theoretical knowledge (naẓariyyāt); it is the locus of moral responsibility (taklīf).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — the binding/restraining faculty; metaphorical (majāz) — the light of discernment (nūr al-tamyīz) that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Sentence with Topic-Comment (Mubtadaʾ-Khabar) — The chapter title employs a genitive construct chain (iḍāfah) with coordinated nouns, each governed by the preceding, establishing a hierarchical exposition of the intellect's aspects.
chapters.translation: I say: This is the seventh chapter, concerning the intellect (al-ʿaql) — its nobility (sharafuhu), its reality (ḥaqīqatuhu), and its divisions (aqsāmuhu).

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Honour of the Intellect (Bayān Sharaf al-ʿAql)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان شرف العقل

اعلم أن هذا مما لا يحتاج إلى تكلف في إظهاره لا سيما وقد ظهر شرف العلم
من قبل العقل والعقل منبع العلم ومطلعه وأساسه والعلم يجري منه مجرى الثمرة
من الشجرة والنور من الشمس والرؤية من العين فكيف لا يشرف ما هو وسيلة
السعادة في الدنيا والآخرة أو كيف يستراب فيه والبهيمة مع قصور تمييزها
تحتشم العقل حتى إن أعظم البهائم بدنا وأشدها ضراوة وأقواها سطوة إذا رأى
صورة الإنسان احتشمه وهابه لشعوره باستيلائه عليه لما خص به من إدراك الحيل
ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الشيخ في قومه كالنبي في أمته (1) وليس ذلك
لكثرة ماله ولا لكبر شخصه ولا لزيادة قوته بل لزيادة تجربته التي هي ثمرة
عقله
ولذلك ترى الأتراك والأكراد وأجلاف العرب وسائر الخلق مع قرب منزلتهم من
رتبة البهائم يوقرون المشايخ بالطبع
ولذلك حين قصد كثير من المعاندين قتل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما
وقعت أعينهم عليه واكتحلوا بغرته الكريمة هابوه وتراءى لهم ما كان يتلألأ
على ديباجة وجهه من نور النبوة وإن كان ذلك باطنا في نفسه بطون العقل  فشرف
العقل ما يدرك بالضرورة وإنما القصد أن نورد ما وردت به الأخبار والآيات في
ذكر شرفه وقد سماه الله نورا في قوله تعالى الله نور السموات والأرض مثل
نوره كمشكاة وسمى العلم المستفاد منه روحا ووحيا وحياة فقال تعالى {وكذلك
أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا} وقال سبحانه أومن كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له
نورا يمشي به في الناس وحيث ذكر النور والظلمة أراد به العلم والجهل كقوله
{يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أيها الناس
اعقلوا عن ربكم وتواصوا بالعقل تعرفوا ما أمرتم به وما نهيتم عنه واعلموا
أنه ينجدكم عند ربكم واعلموا أن العاقل من أطاع الله وإن كان دميم المنظر
حقير الخطر دنيء المنزلة رث الهيئة وأن الجاهل من عصى الله تعالى وإن كان
جميل المنظر عظيم الخطر شريف المنزلة حسن الهيئة فصيحا نطوقا فالقردة
والخنازير أعقل عند الله تعالى ممن عصاه ولا تغتر بتعظيم أهل الدنيا إياهم
فإنهم من الخاسرين (2)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما خلق الله العقل فقال له أقبل فأقبل ثم
قال له أدبر فأدبر ثم قال الله عز وجل وعزتي وجلالي ما خلقت خلقا أكرم على
منك بك آخذ وبك أعطي وبك أثيب وبك أعاقب (3)
فإن قلت فهذا العقل إن كان عرضا فكيف خلق قبل الأجسام وإن كان جوهرا فكيف
يكون جوهر قائم بنفسه ولا يتحيز فاعلم أن هذا من علم المكاشفة فلا يليق
ذكره بعلم المعاملة وغرضنا الآن ذكر علوم المعاملة
وعن أنس رضي الله عنه قال أثنى قوم على رجل عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
حتى بالغوا فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم كيف عقل الرجل فقالوا نخبرك عن اجتهاده
في العبادة وأصناف الخير وتسألنا عن عقله فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن
الأحمق يصيب بجهله أكثر من فجور PageV01P083
الفاجر وإنما يرتفع العباد غدا في الدرجات الزلفى من ربهم على قدر عقولهم
(1)
وعن عمر رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه  وسلم ما اكتسب رجل
مثل فضل عقل يهدي صاحبه إلى هدى ويرده عن ردى وما تم إيمان عبد ولا استقام
دينه حتى يكمل عقله (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرجل ليدرك بحسن خلقه
درجة الصائم القائم ولا يتم لرجل حسن خلقه حتى يتم عقله فعند ذلك تم إيمانه
وأطاع ربه وعصى عدوه إبليس (3) وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال قال
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لكل شيء دعامة ودعامة المؤمن عقله فبقدر عقله
تكون عبادته أما سمعتم قول الفجار في النار لو كنا نسمع أو نعقل ما كنا في
أصحاب السعير (4) وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه قال لتميم الداري ما السودد
فيكم قال العقل قال صدقت سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كما سألتك فقال
كما قلت ثم قال سألت جبريل عليه السلام ما السودد فقال العقل (5) وعن
البراء بن عازب رضي الله عنه قال كثرت المسائل يوما على رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم فقال يا أيها الناس إن لكل شيء مطية ومطية المرء العقل وأحسنكم
دلالة ومعرفة بالحجة أفضلكم عقلا (6) وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال لما
رجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من غزوة أحد سمع الناس يقولون فلان أشجع
من فلان وفلان أبلى ما لم يبل فلان ونحو هذا فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم أما هذا فلا علم لكم به قالوا وكيف ذلك يا رسول الله فقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم إنهم قاتلوا على قدر ما قسم الله لهم من العقل وكانت نصرتهم
ونيتهم على قدر عقولهم فأصيب منهم من أصيب على منازل شتى فإذا كان يوم
القيامة اقتسموا المنازل على قدر نياتهم وقدر عقولهم (7) وعن البراء بن
عازب أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال جد الملائكة واجتهدوا في طاعة الله سبحانه
وتعالى بالعقل وجد المؤمنون من بني آدم على قدر عقولهم فأعملهم بطاعة الله
عز وجل أوفرهم عقلا (8) وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت قلت  يا رسول الله بم
يتفاضل الناس في الدنيا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to bind, restrain, hold back" — the intellect as that which restrains the soul from base appetites; also "comprehension" and "understanding."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿaql is the faculty of rational discernment (tamyīz) that distinguishes truth from falsehood and good from evil; it is the instrument of taklīf (moral accountability) and the locus of divine address.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "binding" (al-rabṭ); metaphorically (majāz), it denotes the rational faculty that "binds" a person to obedience and restrains him from transgression.
- Root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Light, illumination, that by which things become manifest; radiance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur'an, nūr is the light of guidance (hidāyah) and knowledge (ʿilm), contrasted with ẓulmah (darkness) as ignorance (jahl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal light is physical; metaphorical light is the intellect and revelation, as in the Āyat al-Nūr.
- Root: ج-ه-ل (j-h-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ignorance, folly, acting without knowledge; also harshness or roughness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Jahl is the privation of knowledge, and in ethical terms, the state of the soul that acts contrary to reason.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal ignorance of facts; metaphorical ignorance as moral corruption and disobedience.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Emphasis and Restriction (Qāʿidat al-Taʾkīd wa al-Ḥaṣr) — The repeated use of "إنما" (innamā) and "على قدر" (ʿalā qadr) in the hadiths functions to restrict causation of reward and rank solely to the measure of intellect, requiring the translator to preserve this restrictive force.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that this matter does not require laborious effort to demonstrate, especially since the honour of knowledge has already become manifest through the intellect — for the intellect is the source of knowledge, its point of emergence, and its foundation. Knowledge flows from it in the manner of fruit from the tree, light from the sun, and vision from the eye. How then could that which is the means of felicity in this world and the Hereafter not be honoured? Or how could doubt be cast upon it, when even the beast, despite the deficiency of its discernment, stands in awe of the intellect? Indeed, the greatest of beasts in body, the most ferocious in predation, and the most powerful in assault — when it beholds the form of a human being, it stands in awe of him and fears him, due to its perception of his dominance over it, by virtue of what he has been uniquely given of the capacity to devise stratagems. For this reason, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «The elder among his people is like the prophet among his nation» (1). And that is not due to abundance of wealth, nor greatness of stature, nor increase of strength, but rather due to the increase of his experience, which is the fruit of his intellect.

For this reason, you see the Turks, the Kurds, the coarse Bedouin Arabs, and all of creation — despite the closeness of their station to the rank of beasts — honouring the elders by natural disposition.

And for this reason, when many of the obstinate opponents intended to kill the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), when their eyes fell upon him and were anointed with his noble forehead, they stood in awe of him, and there appeared to them what was radiating upon the silk of his face from the light of prophethood — even though that was hidden within his soul, hidden in the manner of the intellect. Thus, the honour of the intellect is perceived by necessity. Rather, our purpose here is to cite what has come down in the reports (akhbār) and verses (āyāt) concerning its mention of honour. Allah has named it "light" (nūr) in His saying: {«Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth; the likeness of His light is as a niche»} (Q. 24:35). And He named the knowledge derived from it "spirit" (rūḥ), "revelation" (waḥy), and "life" (ḥayāh), for He said, Exalted is He: {«And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command»} (Q. 42:52). And He said, Glorified is He: "Is he who was dead, and We gave him life, and made for him a light by which he walks among the people..." (Q. 6:122). And wherever He mentions light and darkness, He intends thereby knowledge and ignorance, as in His saying: {«He brings them out of darknesses into the light»} (Q. 2:257). And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "O people, comprehend (iʿqilū) from your Lord, and enjoin one another to intellect, that you may come to know what you have been commanded and what you have been forbidden. And know that it will aid you before your Lord. And know that the intelligent one (al-ʿāqil) is he who obeys Allah, even if he be ugly in appearance, contemptible in rank, base in station, and shabby in attire. And the ignorant one (al-jāhil) is he who disobeys Allah, Exalted is He, even if he be beautiful in appearance, great in rank, noble in station, and handsome in attire, eloquent and articulate. For verily, monkeys and swine are more intelligent in the sight of Allah, Exalted is He, than the one who disobeys Him. And do not be deceived by the veneration of the people of this world for them, for they are among the losers" (2).

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The first thing Allah created was the intellect. He said to it: 'Come forward,' so it came forward. Then He said to it: 'Go back,' so it went back. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: 'By My Might and My Majesty, I have created no creation more honourable to Me than you. Through you I take, through you I give, through you I reward, and through you I punish'" (3).

If you say: "This intellect — if it is an accident (ʿaraḍ), how was it created before bodies? And if it is a substance (jawhar), how can it be a self-subsistent substance without occupying space (taḥayyuz)?" — Know that this belongs to the science of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah), and it is not fitting to mention it in the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah). Our purpose now is only to mention the sciences of practical conduct.

And on the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: A people praised a man before the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) until they exaggerated. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "How is the man's intellect?" They said: "We inform you of his diligence in worship and the various kinds of goodness, and you ask us about his intellect?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Verily, the foolish one (al-aḥmaq) attains through his ignorance more than the wickedness of the wicked one. And verily, the servants will be raised tomorrow in the degrees of nearness to their Lord only according to the measure of their intellects" (1).

And on the authority of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "No man has acquired anything like the merit of an intellect that guides its possessor to guidance and turns him back from ruin. And the faith of no servant is perfected, nor his religion upright, until his intellect is completed" (2). And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Verily, a man attains through his good character the rank of the one who fasts and stands in prayer at night. And the good character of no man is perfected until his intellect is completed. At that point, his faith is perfected, he obeys his Lord, and he disobeys his enemy, Iblis" (3).

And on the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "For everything there is a support (dʿimāmah), and the support of the believer is his intellect. According to the measure of his intellect is his worship. Have you not heard the saying of the wicked in the Fire: {«Had we but listened or comprehended, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze»} (Q. 67:10)?" (4).

And on the authority of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said to Tamīm al-Dārī: "What is lordship (al-sūdād) among you?" He said: "The intellect." He said: "You have spoken truthfully. I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) just as I have asked you, and he said as you have said." Then he said: "I asked Gabriel (peace be upon him): 'What is lordship?' He said: 'The intellect'" (5).

And on the authority of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: Questions multiplied one day before the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), so he said: "O people, for everything there is a mount (maṭiyyah), and the mount of a man is his intellect. And the best of you in guidance and knowledge of the proof is the most excellent of you in intellect" (6).

And on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) returned from the expedition of Uḥud, he heard the people saying: "So-and-so is braver than so-and-so," and "So-and-so has done what so-and-so has not done," and the like. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "As for this, you have no knowledge of it." They said: "How is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Verily, they fought according to the measure of what Allah apportioned to them of intellect. Their victory and their intention were according to the measure of their intellects. Those of them who were struck down were struck down at various stations. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, they will divide the stations according to the measure of their intentions and the measure of their intellects" (7).

And on the authority of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib, that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The angels strove and exerted themselves in obedience to Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, through the intellect. And the believers among the children of Adam strove according to the measure of their intellects. The most obedient of them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the most abundant of them in intellect" (8).

And on the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), she said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, by what do people excel one another in this world?" He said: "By the intellect." I said: "And in the Hereafter?" He said: "By the intellect." I said: "Are they not only recompensed for their deeds?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "O ʿĀʾishah, have they done anything except according to the measure of what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, gave them of intellect? So according to the measure of what they were given of intellect were their deeds, and according to the measure of what they did shall they be recompensed" (9).

And on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "For everything there is an instrument and a tool, and the instrument of the believer is his intellect. For everything there is a mount, and the mount of a man is his intellect. For everything there is a support, and the support of religion is the intellect. For every people there is a goal, and the goal of the servants is the intellect. For every people there is a caller, and the caller of the worshippers is the intellect. For every merchant there is a commodity, and the commodity of the strivers (mujtahidūn) is the intellect. For every household there is a steward, and the steward of the houses of the truthful (ṣiddīqūn) is the intellect. For every ruin there is a rebuilding, and the rebuilding of the Hereafter is the intellect. For every man there is a progeny to which he is attributed and by which he is remembered, and the progeny of the truthful by which they are attributed and remembered is the intellect. For every journey there is a pavilion, and the pavilion of the believers is the intellect" (1).

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Verily, the most beloved of the believers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is he who exerts himself in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and is sincere to His servants, and completes his intellect, and is sincere to his own soul, and thereby sees clearly and acts upon it during the days of his life, and thus succeeds and prospers" (2).

And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The most complete of you in intellect is the most severe of you in fear of Allah, Exalted is He, and the best of you in consideration of what He has commanded you and forbidden you, even if he be the least of you in supererogatory acts" (3).

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Reality of Intellect and Its Divisions
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان حقيقة العقل وأقسامه

اعلم أن الناس اختلفوا في حد العقل وحقيقته وذهل الأكثرون عن كون هذا
الاسم مطلقا على معان مختلفة فصار ذلك سبب اختلافهم
والحق الكاشف للغطاء فيه أن العقل اسم يطلق بالاشتراك على أربعة معان كما
يطلق اسم العين مثلا على معان عدة وما يجري هذا المجرى فلا ينبغي أن يطلب
لجميع أقسامه حد واحد بل يفرد كل قسم بالكشف عنه فالأول الوصف الذي يفارق
الإنسان به سائر البهائم وهو الذي استعد به لقبول العلوم النظرية وتدبير
الصناعات الخفية الفكرية وهو الذي أراده الحارث بن أسد المحاسبي حيث قال في
حد العقل إنه غريزة يتهيأ بها إدراك العلوم النظرية وكأنه نور يقذف في
القلب به يستعد لإدراك الأشياء ولم  ينصف من أنكر هذا ورد العقل إلى مجرد
العلوم الضرورية فإن الغافل عن العلوم والنائم يسميان عاقلين باعتبار وجود
هذه الغريزة فيهما مع فقد العلوم وكما أن الحياة غريزة بها يتهيأ الجسم
للحركات الاختيارية والإدراكات الحسية فكذلك العقل غريزة بها تتهيأ بعض
الحيوانات للعلوم النظرية ولو جاز أن يسوى بين الإنسان والحمار في الغريزة
والإدراكات الحسية
فيقال لا فرق بينهما إلا أن الله تعالى بحكم إجراء العادة يخلق في
الإنسان علوما وليس يخلقها في الحمار والبهائم لجاز أن يسوي بين الحمار
والجماد في الحياة ويقال لا فرق ألا إن الله عز وجل يخلق في الحمار حركات
مخصوصة بحكم إجراء العادة
فإنه لو قدر الحمار جمادا ميتا لوجب القول بأن كل حركة تشاهد منه فالله
سبحانه وتعالى قادر على خلقها فيه على الترتيب المشاهد
وكما وجب أن يقال لم يكن مفارقته للجماد في الحركات إلا بغريزة اختصت به
عبر عنها بالحياة فكذا مفارقة الإنسان البهيمة في إدراك العلوم النظرية
بغريزة يعبر عنها بالعقل وهو كالمرآة التي تفارق غيرها من الأجسام في حكاية
الصور والألوان بصفة اختصت بها وهي الصقالة
وكذلك العين تفارق الجبهة في صفات وهيئات بها استعدت للرؤية فنسبة هذه
الغريزة إلى العلوم كنسبة العين إلى الرؤية ونسبة القرآن والشرع إلى هذه
الغريزة في سياقها إلى انكشاف العلوم لها كنسبة نور الشمس إلى البصر فهكذا
ينبغي أن تفهم هذه الغريزة
الثاني هي العلوم التي تخرج إلى الوجود في ذات الطفل المميز بجواز
الجائزات واستحالة المستحيلات كالعلم بأن الاثنين أكثر من الواحد وأن الشخص
الواحد لا يكون في مكانين في وقت واحد وهو الذي عناه بعض المتكلمين حيث قال
في حد العقل إنه بعض العلوم الضرورية كالعلم بجواز الجائزات واستحالة
المستحيلات وهو أيضا صحيح في نفسه لأن هذه العلوم موجودة وتسميتها عقلا
ظاهر وإنما الفاسد أن تنكر تلك الغريزة ويقال لا موجود إلا هذه العلوم
الثالث علوم تستفاد من التجارب بمجاري الأحوال فإن من حنكته التجارب
وهذبته المذاهب يقال إنه عاقل  في العادة ومن لا يتصف بهذه الصفة فيقال
PageV01P085
إنه غبي غمر جاهل فهذا نوع آخر من العلوم يسمى عقلا
الرابع أن تنتهي قوة تلك الغريزة إلى أن يعرف عواقب الأمور ويقمع الشهوة
الداعية إلى اللذة العاجلة ويقهرها فإذا حصلت هذه القوة سمى صاحبها عاقلا
من حيث إن إقدامه وإحجامه بحسب ما يقتضيه النظر في العواقب لا بحكم الشهوة
العاجلة وهذه أيضا من خواص الإنسان التي بها يتميز عن سائر الحيوان فالأول
هو الأس والسنخ والمنبع
والثاني هو الفرع الأقرب إليه
والثالث فرع الأول والثاني إذ بقوة الغريزة والعلوم الضرورية تستفاد علوم
التجارب
والرابع هو الثمرة الأخيرة وهو الغاية القصوى فالأولان بالطبع والأخيران
بالاكتساب
ولذلك قال علي كرم الله وجهه
رأيت العقل عقلين ... فمطبوع ومسموع
ولا ينفع مسموع ... إذا لم يك مطبوع
كما لا تنفع الشمس ... وضوء العين ممنوع
والأول هو المراد بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما خلق الله عز وجل خلقا أكرم
عليه من العقل (1) والأخير هو المراد بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا تقرب
الناس بأبواب البر والأعمال الصالحة فتقرب أنت بعقلك (2) وهو المراد بقول
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه ازدد عقلا تزدد من
ربك قربا فقال بأبي أنت وأمي وكيف لي بذلك فقال اجتنب محارم الله تعالى وأد
فرائض الله سبحانه تكن عاقلا واعمل بالصالحات من الأعمال تزدد في عاجل
الدنيا رفعة وكرامة وتنل في آجل العقبى بها من ربك عز وجل القرب والعز (3)
وعن سعيد بن المسيب أن عمر وأبي بن كعب وأبا هريرة رضي الله عنهم دخلوا على
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله من أعلم الناس فقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم العاقل قالوا فمن أعبد الناس قال العاقل قالوا فمن أفضل
الناس قال العاقل قالوا اليس العاقل من تمت مروءته وظهرت فصاحته وجادت كفه
وعظمت منزلته فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم {وإن كل ذلك لما متاع الحياة الدنيا
والآخرة عند ربك للمتقين} إن العاقل  هو المتقي وإن كان في الدنيا خسيسا
ذليلا (4) قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث آخر إنما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to bind, restrain, or hold back" — the intellect is that which restrains its possessor from error and base desires; also used for the rope (ʿiqāl) that hobbles a camel.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿaql is the faculty by which one apprehends necessary and theoretical knowledge; it is the instrument of discernment (tamyīz) and the locus of taklīf (moral accountability).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The term is used both literally (ḥaqīqah) for the innate faculty and metaphorically (majāz) for the acquired sciences that are its fruits, just as "knowledge" (ʿilm) is called "fear" (khashyah) metaphorically.
- Root: غ-ر-ز (gh-r-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To implant, insert, or fix something into another thing; a ghārīzah is an innate disposition or instinct placed within a creature.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The natural constitution (fiṭrah) by which the soul is prepared to receive knowledge; it is the divinely implanted capacity for cognition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the physical embedding of a thing; metaphorically extended to the innate faculty of intellect as something "planted" in the heart.
- Root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sight, perception, insight; baṣīrah is the inner vision of the heart.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The faculty of perception, divided into outward sight (baṣar) and inward insight (baṣīrah); the latter is the means of apprehending metaphysical realities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical sight; metaphorical for intellectual discernment, as in the Quranic verse {فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى الْأَبْصَارُ وَلَٰكِن تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ} where blindness is attributed to hearts.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Ishtirāk (Homonymy) — When a single term (ism) applies to multiple distinct meanings (maʿānin mukhtalifah), it is invalid to seek a single definition (ḥadd wāḥid) encompassing all senses; rather, each sense must be defined separately, as with the term ʿayn (eye, spring, spy, gold coin).
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that people have differed concerning the definition (ḥadd) of intellect and its reality, and most have been heedless of the fact that this name is applied to different meanings, and this became the cause of their disagreement.

The truth that unveils the covering in this matter is that "intellect" (al-ʿaql) is a name applied by homonymy (ishtirāk) to four meanings, just as the name "eye" (al-ʿayn), for example, is applied to several meanings. Whatever runs this course, it is not fitting to seek for all its divisions a single definition; rather, each division should be singled out for exposition.

**The First** is the attribute by which man is distinguished from all other beasts, and it is that by which he is prepared to receive theoretical sciences (al-ʿulūm al-naẓariyyah) and to manage the hidden intellectual crafts. This is what al-Ḥārith ibn Asad al-Muḥāsibī intended when he said in defining intellect that it is an innate disposition (gharīzah) by which one is prepared for the apprehension of theoretical sciences — as if it were a light cast into the heart by which one is prepared for the apprehension of things. He who denied this and reduced intellect to mere necessary sciences has not been fair. For the heedless one and the sleeper are called "intelligent" (ʿāqilān) by virtue of the existence of this innate disposition in them, notwithstanding their lack of sciences. Just as life is an innate disposition by which the body is prepared for voluntary movements and sensory perceptions, so too intellect is an innate disposition by which some animals are prepared for theoretical sciences. If it were permissible to equate man and donkey in innate disposition and sensory perceptions, such that one might say, "There is no difference between them except that God — by virtue of the course of His custom (majrā al-ʿādah) — creates in man sciences which He does not create in the donkey and the beasts," then it would likewise be permissible to equate the donkey and the inanimate object in life, saying, "There is no difference, except that God creates in the donkey particular movements by virtue of the course of custom." For if the donkey were supposed to be an inanimate dead thing, it would be necessary to say that every movement observed from it is something God is able to create in it in the observed order. And just as it is necessary to say that its distinction from the inanimate in movements is only by an innate disposition peculiar to it, expressed by the term "life," so likewise man's distinction from the beast in apprehending theoretical sciences is by an innate disposition expressed by the term "intellect." It is like a mirror that is distinguished from other bodies in reflecting forms and colors by a quality peculiar to it, namely polish (ṣiqālah). Likewise, the eye is distinguished from the forehead in qualities and configurations by which it is prepared for vision. The relation of this innate disposition to the sciences is like the relation of the eye to vision; and the relation of the Quran and the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) to this innate disposition, in conducting it to the unveiling of sciences, is like the relation of the sun's light to the eye's sight. Thus should this innate disposition be understood.

**The Second** is the sciences that come into existence in the essence of the discerning child (al-ṭifl al-mumayyiz) concerning the permissibility of possible things (jawāz al-jāʾizāt) and the impossibility of impossible things (istiḥālat al-mustaḥīlāt) — such as the knowledge that two is more than one, and that a single person cannot be in two places at one time. This is what some theologians (al-mutakallimūn) meant when they said in defining intellect that it is some of the necessary sciences, like the knowledge of the permissibility of possible things and the impossibility of impossible things. This too is sound in itself, for these sciences exist, and calling them "intellect" is evident. The corrupt thing is only to deny that innate disposition and to say, "There exists nothing but these sciences."

**The Third** is the sciences acquired from experiences (tajārib) through the courses of circumstances. For he whom experiences have seasoned and whom doctrines have refined is called "intelligent" (ʿāqil) by custom; and he who is not characterized by this quality is called stupid, inexperienced, and ignorant. This is another type of sciences called "intellect."

**The Fourth** is that the power of that innate disposition reaches the point where one knows the consequences of affairs (ʿawāqib al-umūr), suppresses the lust that calls to immediate pleasure, and overcomes it. When this power is attained, its possessor is called "intelligent" inasmuch as his advance and retreat are according to what consideration of consequences requires, not according to the rule of immediate lust. This too is among the special properties of man by which he is distinguished from all other animals.

The first is the root (aṣl), the stock (sinkh), and the source (manbaʿ). The second is the branch (farʿ) nearest to it. The third is a branch of the first and second, for by the power of the innate disposition and the necessary sciences, the sciences of experience are acquired. The fourth is the final fruit (al-thamarah al-akhīrah) and the ultimate goal (al-ghāyah al-quṣwā). The first two are by nature (bi-al-ṭabʿ), and the last two are by acquisition (bi-al-iktisāb).

For this reason, ʿAlī — may God honor his face — said:

*I saw intellect as two intellects: one innate (maṭbūʿ) and one heard (masmūʿ).*
*The heard is of no avail if the innate is not present,*
*Just as the sun is of no avail when the eye's light is obstructed.*

The first is what is meant by his saying — peace and blessings be upon him: "God created nothing more noble before Him than the intellect." The last is what is meant by his saying — peace and blessings be upon him: "When people draw near to God through the doors of righteousness and good deeds, draw near you through your intellect." It is also what is meant by the saying of the Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — to Abū al-Dardāʾ — may God be pleased with him: "Increase in intellect, and you will increase in proximity to your Lord." He said: "May my father and mother be your ransom! How can I do that?" He said: "Avoid the forbidden things of God, perform the obligatory duties of God, and you will be intelligent. Work righteous deeds, and you will increase in honor and dignity in the immediate world, and you will attain in the deferred hereafter, through them, proximity and might from your Lord."

It is related from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib that ʿUmar, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and Abū Hurayrah — may God be pleased with them — entered upon the Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — and said: "O Messenger of God, who is the most knowledgeable of people?" He said: "The intelligent one." They said: "Then who is the most worshipful of people?" He said: "The intelligent one." They said: "Then who is the most virtuous of people?" He said: "The intelligent one." They said: "Is not the intelligent one he whose manliness (murūʾah) is complete, whose eloquence is manifest, whose hand is generous, and whose station is great?" He said — peace and blessings be upon him: {«وَإِنَّ كُلَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَالْآخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ»} — "And all that is but the enjoyment of the life of this world; but the hereafter with your Lord is for the God-fearing." Indeed, the intelligent one is the God-fearing one, even if he be base and lowly in this world. He said — peace and blessings be upon him — in another hadith: "The intelligent one is only he who believes in God, affirms His messengers, and acts in obedience to Him."

It is likely that the origin of the name in the original language is for that innate disposition, and likewise in usage. It is only applied to the sciences because they are its fruit, just as a thing is known by its fruit. Thus it is said: "Knowledge is fear," and "The learned one is he who fears God" — for fear is the fruit of knowledge. So it would be metaphorical (majāz) for other than that innate disposition. But the purpose here is not to investigate language.

The point is that these four divisions exist, and the name is applied to all of them. There is no disagreement concerning the existence of all of them except regarding the first division. The correct view is that it exists — indeed, it is the root. These sciences are, as it were, embedded (muḍammanah) in that innate disposition by primordial nature (bi-al-fiṭrah), but they appear in existence when a cause occurs that brings them forth into existence — as if these sciences were not something entering upon it from outside, but as if they were latent within it and then appeared. Its example is water in the earth: it appears by digging the well, and it collects and is distinguished by sense — not that something new is conveyed to it. Likewise, the oil in the almond and the rose-water in the rose.

For this reason, God — exalted be He — said: {«وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ ۖ قَالُوا بَلَىٰ»} — "And when your Lord took from the loins of the children of Adam their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves: 'Am I not your Lord?' They said: 'Yes, indeed.'" What is meant is the affirmation of their souls, not the affirmation of their tongues. For they divided, in the affirmation of tongues — where tongues and persons exist — into one who affirms and one who denies. For this reason, God — exalted be He — said: {«وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَهُمْ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ»} — "And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say: God." Its meaning is that if you consider their states, their souls and inner beings testify to that. {«فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا»} — "The primordial nature of God upon which He originated people" — that is, every human being is originated upon faith in God — exalted be He — nay, upon the knowledge of things as they are. I mean that it is, as it were, embedded in them by the nearness of their preparedness for apprehension.

Then, since faith was implanted (markūz) in souls by primordial nature, people divided into two divisions: one who turned away and forgot — and they are the disbelievers — and one who turned his thought and remembered — as if he were one carrying a testimony who forgot it through heedlessness and then remembered it. For this reason, God — exalted be He — said: {«لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ»} — "Perhaps they will remember" — and {«وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ»} — "And that those of understanding may remember" — and {«وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثَاقَهُ الَّذِي وَاثَقَكُم بِهِ»} — "And remember the grace of God upon you and His covenant which He made with you" — and {«وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ»} — "And We have made the Quran easy for remembrance — is there then any who will remember?" Calling this pattern "remembrance" (tadhakkur) is not far-fetched. For it is as if remembrance is of two kinds: one is that one recalls a form that was present in existence in one's heart but became absent after its existence; the other is that one recalls a form that was embedded in it by primordial nature.

These are realities evident to one who looks with the light of inner insight (nūr al-baṣīrah), but heavy upon one who relies upon hearing and imitation (al-samāʿ wa-al-taqlīd) without unveiling and direct vision (al-kashf wa-al-ʿiyān). For this reason, you see him floundering in such verses and forcing upon the interpretation of "remembrance" as the affirmation of souls all kinds of forced interpretations. Fancies of contradictions in the reports and verses occur to him, and perhaps this overcomes him until he looks upon them with the eye of contempt and believes them to be incoherent.

His example is the example of a blind man who enters a house and stumbles in it against the vessels arranged in the house, and says: "Why are these vessels not removed from the path and returned to their places?" It is said to him: "They are in their places; the defect is only in your sight." So likewise, the defect of inner insight runs its course — nay, it is more harmful and greater. For the soul is like the rider and the body like the horse, and the blindness of the rider is more harmful than the blindness of the horse. Because of the resemblance of the inner insight to the outer sight, God — exalted be He — said: {«مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَىٰ»} — "The heart did not lie in what it saw" — and said: {«وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُرِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ»} — "And thus We showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth." And He called its opposite "blindness," saying: {«فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى الْأَبْصَارُ وَلَٰكِن تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ»} — "For indeed it is not the eyes that become blind, but the hearts within the breasts become blind" — and said: {«وَمَن كَانَ فِي هَٰذِهِ أَعْمَىٰ فَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ أَعْمَىٰ وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا»} — "And whoever is blind in this life will be blind in the hereafter, and further astray from the path." These matters that were unveiled to the prophets — some of them were by outward sight (al-baṣar) and some by inner insight (al-baṣīrah), and all were called "vision" (ruʾyah).

In sum, whoever's inner insight is not penetrating attaches to religion only its husks (qushūr) and its examples, without its core (lubāb) and its realities (ḥaqāʾiq).

These, then, are the divisions of what the name "intellect" is applied to.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Disparity of Souls in Intellect
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان تفاوت النفوس في العقل

قد اختلف الناس في تفاوت العقل ولا معنى للاشتغال بنقل كلام من قل تحصيله
بل الأولى والأهم المبادرة إلى التصريح بالحق
والحق الصريح فيه أن يقال إن التفاوت يتطرق إلى الأقسام الأربعة سوى
القسم الثاني وهو العلم الضروري بجواز الجائزات واستحالة المستحيلات
فإن من عرف أن الاثنين أكثر من الواحد عرف أيضا استحالة كون الجسم في
مكانين وكون الشيء الواحد قديما حادثا وكذا سائر النظائر وكل ما يدركه
إدراكا محققا من غير شك وأما الأقسام الثلاثة  فالتفاوت يتطرق إليها أما
القسم الرابع وهو استيلاء القوة على قمع الشهوات فلا يخفى تفاوت الناس فيه
بل لا يخفى تفاوت أحوال الشخص الواحد فيه وهذا التفاوت يكون تارة لتفاوت
الشهوة إذ قد يقدر العاقل ترك بعض الشهوات دون بعض ولكن غير مقصور عليه
فإن الشاب قد يعجز عن ترك الزنا وإذا كبر وتم عقله قدر عليه وشهوة الرياء
والرياسة تزداد قوة بالكبر لا ضعفا وقد يكون سببه التفاوت في العلم المعرف
لغائلة تلك الشهوة ولهذا يقدر الطبيب على الاحتماء عن بعض الأطعمة المضرة
وقدم من يساويه في العقل على ذلك PageV01P087
إذا لم يكن طبيبا وإن كان يعتقد على الجملة فيه مضرة لكن إذا كان علم
الطبيب أتم كان خوفه أشد فيكون الخوف جندا للعقل وعدة له في قمع الشهوات
وكسرها
وكذلك يكون العالم أقدر على ترك المعاصي من الجاهل لقوة علمه بضرر
المعاصي وأعني به العالم الحقيقي دون أرباب الطيالسة وأصحاب الهذيان
فإن كان التفاوت من جهة الشهوة لم يرجع إلى تفاوت العقل وإن كان من جهة
العلم فقد سمينا هذا الضرب من العلم عقلا أيضا فإنه يقوي غريزة العقل فيكون
التفاوت فيما رجعت التسمية إليه وقد يكون بمجرد التفاوت في غريزة العقل
فإنها إذا قويت كان قمعها للشهوة لا محالة أشد
وأما القسم الثالث وهو علوم التجارب فتفاوت الناس فيها لا ينكر فإنهم
يتفاوتون بكثرة الإصابة وسرعة الإدراك ويكون سببه إما تفاوتا في الغريزة
وإما تفاوتا في الممارسة فأما الأول وهو الأصل أعني الغريزة فالتفاوت فيه
لا سبيل إلى جحده فإنه مثل نور يشرق على النفس ويطلع صبحه ومبادىء إشراقه
عند سن التمييز ثم لا يزال ينمو ويزداد نموا خفي التدريج إلى أن يتكامل
بقرب الأربعين سنة ومثاله نور الصبح فإن أوائله تخفى خفاء يشق إدراكه ثم
يتدرج إلى الزيادة إلى أن يكمل بطلوع قرص الشمس
وتفاوت نور البصيرة كتفاوت نور البصر والفرق مدرك بين الأعمش وبين حاد
البصر بل سنة الله عز وجل جارية في جميع خلقه  بالتدريج في الإيجاد حتى إن
غريزة الشهوة لا تظهر في الصبي عند البلوغ دفعة وبغتة بل تظهر شيئا فشيئا
على التدريج وكذلك جميع القوى والصفات ومن أنكر تفاوت الناس في هذه الغريزة
فكأنه منخلع عن ربقة العقل ومن ظن أن عقل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مثل عقل
آحاد السوادية وأجلاف البوادي فهو أخس في نفسه من آحاد السوادية وكيف ينكر
تفاوت الغريزة ولولاه لما اختلف الناس في فهم العلوم ولما انقسموا إلى بليد
لا يفهم بالتفهيم إلا بعد تعب طويل من المعلم وإلى ذكي يفهم بأدنى رمز
وإشارة وإلى كامل تنبعث من نفسه حقائق الأمور بدون التعليم كما قال تعالى
يكاد زيتها يضيء ولو لم تمسسه نار نور على نور وذلك مثل الأنبياء عليهم
السلام إذ يتضح لهم في بواطنهم أمور غامضة من غير تعلم وسماع ويعبر عن ذلك
بالإلهام وعن مثله عبر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث قال إن روح القدس نفث
في روعي أحبب من أحببت فإنك مفارقه وعش ما شئت فإنك ميت واعمل ما شئت فإنك
مجزي به (1) وهذا النمط من تعريف الملائكة للأنبياء يخالف الوحي الصريح
الذي هو سماع الصوت بحاسة الأذن ومشاهدة الملك بحاسة البصر ولذلك أخبر عن
هذا بالنفث في الروع ودرجات الوحي كثيرة والخوض فيها لا يليق بعلم المعاملة
بل هو من علم المكاشفة
ولا تظنن أن معرفة درجات الوحي تستدعي منصب الوحي إذ لا يبعد أن يعرف
الطبيب المريض درجات الصحة ويعلم العالم الفاسق درجات العدالة وإن كان
خاليا عنها فالعلم شيء ووجود المعلوم شيء آخر فلا كل من عرف النبوة
والولاية كان نبيا ولا وليا ولا كل من عرف التقوى والورع ودقائقه كان تقيا
وانقسام الناس إلى من يتنبه من نفسه ويفهم وإلى من لا يفهم إلا بتنبيه
وتعليم وإلى من لا ينفعه التعليم أيضا ولا التنبيه كانقسام الأرض إلى ما
يجتمع فيه الماء فيقوى فيتفجر بنفسه عيونا وإلى ما يحتاج إلى الحفر ليخرج
إلى القنوات وإلى ما لا  ينفع فيه الحفر وهو اليابس وذلك لاختلاف جواهر
الأرض في صفاتها فكذلك اختلاف النفوس في غريزة العقل
ويدل على تفاوت العقل من جهة النقل ما روي أن عبد الله بن سلام رضي الله
عنه سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث طويل في آخره وصف عظم العرش وأن
الملائكة قالت يا ربنا هل خلقت شيئا أعظم من العرش PageV01P088
قال نعم العقل قالوا وما بلغ من قدره قال هيهات لا يحاط بعلمه هل لكم علم
بعدد الرمل قالوا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to bind, restrain, or hold back" — the intellect as that which restrains the soul from base impulses; also "comprehension" and "discernment."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿaql is the innate faculty (gharīzah) by which one grasps necessary truths (ḍarūriyyāt) and distinguishes the possible (jāʾiz) from the impossible (mustaḥīl); it is both a natural light and an acquired knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, ʿaql is the "tether" (ʿiqāl) that binds the camel; metaphorically, it is the power that binds the soul against passion (hawā). The term is transferred (manqūl) from the physical to the spiritual.
- Root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The self, soul, or spirit; also "breath" and "vitality." In plural (nufūs), it denotes individual human souls as distinct entities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul as the locus of both intellect and passion; its disparity (tafāwut) is a central theme in understanding human moral and cognitive variation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "breathing out"; metaphorically, the inner essence that differentiates one person from another in capacity.
- Root: غ-ر-ز (gh-r-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To implant, insert, or fix firmly; the "innate disposition" (gharīzah) as something embedded in the nature of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The primordial faculty given by God, distinct from acquired knowledge; its strength or weakness determines the degree of intellectual attainment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "to plant" (as in a shoot); metaphorically, the natural endowment that grows and develops over time.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taʿlīq (Suspension) and Conditional Clauses — In sentences like "If you say... then know that..." (fa-in qulta... fa-ʿlam), the protasis is suspended (muʿallaq) from the apodosis, requiring careful parsing of the logical sequence. Also, the use of "ammā... fa-" (as for... then) to structure contrastive topics, as in the division of the four categories of intellect.
chapters.translation:
I say: People have differed concerning the disparity of intellect, and there is no point in occupying oneself with transmitting the words of those whose attainment is meager. Rather, the foremost and most important thing is to hasten to declare the truth plainly.

The plain truth in this matter is to say: disparity extends to the four categories, except the second category — namely, the necessary knowledge of the permissibility of possible things and the impossibility of impossible things. For whoever knows that two is more than one also knows the impossibility of a body being in two places, and of one and the same thing being both eternal and originated, and likewise all similar cases — everything that one apprehends with verified apprehension without any doubt. As for the other three categories, disparity does extend to them.

As for the fourth category — namely, the dominance of the power in suppressing the appetites — the disparity of people in it is not hidden; indeed, the disparity of the states of a single person in this regard is not hidden either. This disparity is sometimes due to the disparity of the appetite itself, for a rational man may be able to abandon some appetites but not others. But it is not confined to that, for a young man may be unable to abandon fornication, yet when he grows older and his intellect is perfected, he becomes able to do so. And the appetite for ostentation (riyāʾ) and leadership grows stronger with age, not weaker. And it may be caused by disparity in the knowledge that identifies the harmful consequence of that appetite. For this reason, a physician is able to abstain from certain harmful foods, while someone equal to him in intellect is not able to do so if he is not a physician — even though he believes in general that it is harmful. But when the physician's knowledge is more complete, his fear is more intense, and thus fear becomes a soldier for the intellect and a provision for it in suppressing and breaking the appetites.

Likewise, the learned man is more able to abandon sins than the ignorant man, due to the strength of his knowledge of the harm of sins. By "learned" I mean the true scholar, not the wearers of cloaks (arbāb al-ṭayālisah) and the practitioners of idle talk (aṣḥāb al-hadhyān). For if the disparity arises from the side of appetite, it does not revert to a disparity in intellect; but if it arises from the side of knowledge, we have also called this kind of knowledge "intellect," for it strengthens the instinct of intellect. Thus the disparity reverts to that to which the name is applied. And it may be due merely to disparity in the instinct of intellect itself, for when it is strong, its suppression of appetite is necessarily more intense.

As for the third category — namely, the sciences of experience (ʿulūm al-tajārib) — the disparity of people in it is undeniable, for they differ in the frequency of correct hits and the speed of apprehension. Its cause is either a disparity in the instinct or a disparity in practice. As for the first — namely, the root, the instinct — disparity in it cannot be denied, for it is like a light that shines upon the soul, whose dawn and the beginnings of whose shining appear at the age of discernment (sinn al-tamyīz). Then it continues to grow and increase with a growth of hidden gradualness until it is completed near the age of forty. Its likeness is the light of dawn, for its first beginnings are so hidden that their perception is difficult; then it gradually increases until it is completed with the rising of the disk of the sun.

And the disparity of the light of insight (nūr al-baṣīrah) is like the disparity of the light of sight — the difference between the dim-sighted (aʿmash) and the sharp-sighted is perceptible. Nay, the sunnah of God, Mighty and Majestic, runs through all His creation in gradual origination (al-tadrīj fī al-ījād), such that even the instinct of appetite does not appear in the boy at puberty all at once and suddenly, but appears little by little, gradually. And likewise all powers and attributes. Whoever denies the disparity of people in this instinct is as if he has slipped free from the tether of intellect. And whoever supposes that the intellect of the Prophet, peace be upon him, is like the intellect of the common rabble (sawādiyyah) and the boorish Bedouins — he is himself viler than the common rabble. How can one deny the disparity of the instinct? Were it not for it, people would not differ in understanding the sciences, nor would they be divided into the dull who do not understand even with explanation except after great toil from the teacher, and the intelligent who understand with the slightest hint and gesture, and the perfect one from whose very soul the realities of things arise without instruction — as God, Exalted is He, said: {«يَكَادُ زَيْتُهَا يُضِيءُ وَلَوْ لَمْ تَمْسَسْهُ نَارٌ ۚ نُورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ»} (Its oil would almost glow forth even if no fire touched it — light upon light) [Q. 24:35]. And that is the case of the prophets, peace be upon them, for obscure matters become clear to them in their inner selves without learning and without hearing, and this is expressed as inspiration (ilhām). And of its like the Prophet, peace be upon him, expressed when he said: "Verily the Holy Spirit (rūḥ al-qudus) breathed into my heart (nafatha fī rawʿī): Love whom you love, for you shall part from him; live as you wish, for you shall die; and work what you wish, for you shall be recompensed for it." (1) And this mode of the angels' informing the prophets is different from explicit revelation (al-waḥy al-ṣarīḥ), which is the hearing of a voice by the sense of hearing and the seeing of the angel by the sense of sight. For this reason, he reported it as "breathing into the heart" (nafth fī al-rawʿ). And the degrees of revelation are many, and delving into them is not fitting for the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah); rather, it belongs to the science of unveiling (ʿilm al-mukāshafah).

And do not suppose that knowing the degrees of revelation requires the station of revelation, for it is not unlikely that a physician knows the degrees of health while being ill, and a sinful scholar knows the degrees of justice while being devoid of it. For knowledge is one thing, and the existence of the known object is another thing. Thus, not everyone who knows prophethood and sainthood is a prophet or a saint, and not everyone who knows piety (taqwā), scrupulousness (waraʿ), and their subtleties is pious.

And the division of people into: one who is alerted from himself and understands; and one who does not understand except by alerting and teaching; and one whom neither teaching nor alerting benefits — is like the division of land into: that which collects water and strengthens until it bursts forth by itself into springs; and that which needs digging so that it may come out into channels; and that which digging does not benefit — the dry land. This is due to the difference of the substances of the earth in their qualities. Likewise is the difference of souls in the instinct of intellect.

And that which indicates the disparity of intellect from the side of transmitted report (naql) is what has been related that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, may God be pleased with him, asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, in a long hadith at the end of which is the description of the greatness of the Throne (al-ʿArsh), and that the angels said: "O our Lord, have You created anything greater than the Throne?" He said: "Yes — the intellect." They said: "And what has reached of its measure?" He said: "Alas! Its knowledge cannot be encompassed. Do you have knowledge of the number of grains of sand?" They said: "No." God, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Verily I have created the intellect in diverse kinds, like the number of grains of sand. Among people, some are given one grain, some two grains, some three and four, some a large measure (farq), some a camel-load (wasq), and some more than that." (1)

If you say: "What is the matter with certain groups of the Sufis who blame the intellect (al-ʿaql) and the rational (al-maʿqūl)?" — then know that the cause of this is that people have transferred the name of the intellect and the rational to disputation and debate by means of contradictions and impositions (al-munāqaḍāt wa-al-ilzāmāt), which is the craft of dialectical theology (ṣināʿat al-kalām). They were not able to establish to them that "you have erred in the naming," since it could not be erased from their hearts after the tongues had circulated it and it had become firmly rooted in their hearts. So they blamed the intellect and the rational — that which is so named among them.

As for the light of insight (nūr al-baṣīrah) by which God, Exalted is He, is known and by which the truthfulness of His messengers is known — how could its blame be conceived, when God, Exalted is He, has praised it? And if it is blamed, then what after it is to be praised? For if the praised thing is the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ), then by what is the soundness of the Sacred Law known? If it is known by the blamed intellect that is not to be trusted, then the Sacred Law would also be blamed. And no attention is paid to the one who says: "It is apprehended by the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn) and the light of faith (nūr al-īmān), not by the intellect" — for we mean by "intellect" exactly what he means by "the eye of certainty" and "the light of faith," namely, the inner attribute by which the human being is distinguished from the beasts, and by which he apprehends the realities of things.

And most of these confusions (takhbīṭāt) have arisen only from the ignorance of certain people who sought the realities from mere words, and so they stumbled in them due to the stumbling of people's terminologies in words. This much is sufficient for the exposition of the intellect. And God knows best.

The Book of Knowledge is completed, by the praise of God, Exalted is He, and His grace. And may God bless our master Muḥammad and every chosen servant from the people of earth and heaven.

It is followed, if God, Exalted is He, wills, by the Book of the Principles of Creed (Kitāb Qawāʿid al-ʿAqāʾid).

And all praise is due to God alone, first and last.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

chapters.title_en: The Book of the Principles of Creed, Containing Four Chapters
chapters.arabic_text: | كتاب قواعد العقائد وفيه أربعة فصول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق ع د (Q-ʿ-D)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To sit, settle, establish firmly; a foundation or base upon which something rests.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes the foundational axioms of belief (ʿaqāʾid) that are firmly seated in the heart, not merely intellectual postulates.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical sitting; metaphorical (majāz) extension here signifies the stable, unshakable grounding of doctrinal principles.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʾIḍāfah (Genitive Construction) — The phrase «كتاب قواعد العقائد» employs a chain of annexation (kitāb + qawāʿid + al-ʿaqāʾid), where each genitive specifies and delimits the preceding noun, creating a hierarchical definition of the work’s scope.
chapters.translation: I say: This is the Book of the Principles of Creed (qawāʿid al-ʿaqāʾid), and within it are four chapters.

chapters.title_en: Section 24 — On the Exposition of the Creed of the People of the Sunnah Regarding the Two Words of Testimony, Which Are Among the Foundations of Islam
chapters.arabic_text:
|| الفصل الأول في ترجمة عقيدة أهل السنة في كلمتي الشهادة التي هي أحد مباني الإسلام

فنقول وبالله التوفيق الحمد لله المبدىء المعيد الفعال لما يريد ذي العرش
المجيد والبطش الشديد الهادي صفوة العبيد إلى المنهج الرشيد والمسلك السديد
المنعم عليهم بعد شهادة التوحيد بحراسة عقائدهم عن ظلمات التشكيك والترديد
السالك بهم إلى اتباع رسوله المصطفى واقتفاء آثار صحبه الأكرمين المكرمين
بالتأييد والتسديد المتجلي لهم في ذاته وأفعاله بمحاسن أوصافه التي لا
يدركها إلا من ألقى السمع وهو شهيد المعرف إياهم أنه في ذاته واحد لا شريك
له فرد لا مثيل له صمد لا ضد له منفرد لا ند له وأنه واحد قديم لا أول له
أزلي لا بداية له مستمر الوجود لا آخر له أبدي لا نهاية له قيوم لا انقطاع
له دائم لا انصرام له لم يزل ولا يزال موصوفا بنعوت الجلال PageV01P089
لا يقضى عليه بالانقضاء والانفصال بتصرم الآباد وانقراض الآجال بن هو
الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وهو بكل شيء عليم
التنزيه وأنه ليس بجسم مصور ولا جوهر محدود مقدر وأنه لا يماثل والأجسام
ولا في التقدير ولا في قبول الانقسام وأنه ليس بجوهر ولا تحله الجواهر ولا
بعرض ولا تحله الأعراض بل لا يماثل موجودا ولا يماثله موجود ليس كمثله شيء
ولا هو مثل شيء
وأنه لا يحده المقدار ولا تحويه الأقطار ولا تحيط به الجهات ولا تكتنفه
الأرضون ولا السموات
وأنه مستو على العرش على الوجه الذي قاله وبالمعنى الذي أراده استواء
منزها عن المماسة والاستقرار والتمكن والحلول والانتقال لا يحمله العرش بل
العرش وحملته محمولون بلطف قدرته ومقهورون في قبضته
وهو فوق العرش والسماء وفوق كل شيء إلى تخوم الثرى فوقية لا تزيده قربا
إلى العرش والسماء كما لا تزيده بعدا عن الأرض والثرى بل هو رفيع الدرجات
عن العرش والسماء كما أنه رفيع الدرجات عن الأرض والثرى
وهو مع ذلك قريب من كل موجود وهو أقرب إلى العبد من حبل الوريد وهو على
كل شيء شهيد إذ لا يماثل قربه قرب الأجسام كما لا تماثل ذاته ذات الأجسام
وأنه لا يحل في شيء ولا يحل فيه شيء تعالى عن أن يحويه مكان كما تقدس عن أن
يحده زمان بل كان قبل أن خلق الزمان والمكان وهو الآن على ما عليه كان
وأنه بائن عن خلقه بصفاته ليس في ذاته سواه ولا في سواه ذاته وأنه مقدس
عن التغير والانتقال لا تحله الحوادث ولا تعتريه العوارض بل لا يزال في
نعوت جلاله منزها عن الزوال وفي صفات كماله مستغنيا عن زيادة الاستكمال
وأنه في ذاته معلوم الوجود بالعقول مرئي الذات بالأبصار نعمة منه ولطفا
بالأبرار في دار القرار وإتماما منه للنعيم بالنظر إلى وجهه الكريم
الحياة والقدرة وأنه تعالى حي قادر جبار قاهر لا يعتريه قصور ولا عجز ولا
تأخذه سنة ولا نوم ولا يعارضه فناء ولا موت وأنه ذو الملك والملكوت والعزة
والجبروت له السلطان والقهر والخلق والأمر والسموات مطويات بيمينه والخلائق
مقهورون في قبضته
وأنه المنفرد بالخلق والاختراع المتوحد بالإيجاد والإبداع خلق الخلق
وأعمالهم وقدر أرزاقهم وآجالهم لا يشذ عن قبضته مقدور ولا يعزب عن قدرته
تصاريف الأمور لا تحصى مقدوراته ولا تتباهى معلوماته
العلم وأنه عالم بجميع المعلومات محيط بما يجري من تخوم الأرضين إلى أعلى
السموات وأنه عالم لا يعزب عن علمه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء بل
يعلم دبيب النملة السوداء على الصخرة الصماء في الليلة الظلماء ويدرك حركة
الذر في جو الهواء ويعلم السر وأخفى ويطلع على هواجس الضمائر وحركات
الخواطر وخفيات السرائر بعلم قديم أزلي لم يزل موصوفا به في أزل الآزال لا
بعلم متجدد حاصل في ذاته بالحلول والانتقال
الإرادة وأنه تعالى مريد للكائنات مدبر للحادثات فلا يجري في الملك
والملكوت قليل أو كثير صغير أو كبير خير  أو شر نفع أو ضر إيمان أو كفر
عرفان أو نكر فوز أو خسران زيادة أو نقصان طاعة أو عصيان إلا بقضائه وقدره
وحكمته ومشيئته
فما شاء كان وما لم يشأ لم يكن لا يخرج عن مشيئته لفتة ناظر ولا فلتة
خاطر بل هو المبدىء المعيد الفعال لما يريد لا راد لأمره ولا معقب لقضائه
ولا مهرب لعبد عن معصيته إلا بتوفيقه ورحمته
ولا قوة له على طاعته إلا بمشيئته وإرادته فلو اجتمع الإنس والجن
والملائكة والشياطين على أن يحركوا في العالم ذرة أو يسكنوها دون إرادته
ومشيئته لعجزوا عن ذلك
وأن إرادته قائمة بذاته في جملة صفاته لم يزل كذلك موصوفا بها
PageV01P090
مريدا في أزله لوجود الأشياء في أوقاتها التي قدرها فوجدت في أوقاتها كما
أراده في أزله من غير تقدم ولا تأخر بل وقعت على وفق علمه وإرادته من غير
تبدل ولا تغير
دبر الأمور لا بترتيب أفكار ولا تربص زمان فلذلك لم يشغله شأن عن شأن
السمع والبصر وأنه تعالى سميع بصير يسمع ويرى ولا يعرب عن سمعه مسموع وإن
خفي
ولا يغيب عن رؤيته مرئي وإن دق
ولا يحجب سمعه بعد ولا يدفع رؤيته ظلام
يرى من غير حدقة وأجفان ويسمع من غ
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Bearing witness, testifying; presence and attestation — the act of affirming what is known with certainty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The testimony of faith (shahāda) as the verbal and cognitive acknowledgment of divine unity and prophethood, the gateway to belief.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — witnessing with the tongue and heart; metaphorical (majāz) — the creed itself as a witnessed covenant.
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Tying, binding firmly; a knot — hence belief as a firm, unloosened conviction.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAqīda as the heart's binding to truth, distinct from mere opinion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical tying; metaphorical — intellectual and spiritual commitment.
- Root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Oneness, uniqueness; being alone without peer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tawḥīd as the affirmation of God's exclusive essence, attributes, and acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — numerical singularity; metaphorical — absolute incomparability in all respects.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Predicate Attribution (al-Isnād) — In sentences like "He is one, no partner to Him," the predicate (khabar) follows the subject (mubtadaʾ) to assert a permanent, essential attribute, not a transient state.
chapters.translation:
I say, and with God is success: Praise be to God, the Originator, the Restorer, the Doer of whatsoever He wills, Possessor of the Glorious Throne and Mighty Severity, the Guide of His chosen servants to the right path and the straight way, the Benefactor upon them, after the testimony of His Oneness, by guarding their creeds from the darknesses of doubt and hesitation, the One who leads them to follow His chosen Messenger and to trace the footsteps of His most noble Companions, honored and aided with divine support and guidance, the One who manifests Himself to them in His Essence and His Acts through the beauties of His attributes, which none perceives save one who lends his ear while witnessing. He makes them know that He, in His Essence, is One with no partner, Single with no equal, Eternal Refuge (Ṣamad) with no opposite, Unique with no rival; and that He is One, Eternal with no beginning, Everlasting with no start, of continuous existence with no end, Perpetual with no termination, Self-Sustaining (Qayyūm) with no interruption, Everlasting with no cessation. He has not ceased and shall not cease to be described with the attributes of majesty; He is not judged by passing away or separation through the succession of ages or the expiration of terms. Rather, He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and He is Knower of all things.

[The doctrine of transcendence (tanzīh):] And that He is not a body with form, nor a substance with limits and measure; that He does not resemble bodies, neither in measurement nor in susceptibility to division; that He is not a substance, nor do substances inhere in Him; nor an accident, nor do accidents inhere in Him. Rather, He does not resemble any existent, nor does any existent resemble Him. "There is nothing like unto Him" {«لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ»}, and He is not like anything.

And that no measure bounds Him, no regions contain Him, no directions encompass Him, neither the earths nor the heavens surround Him.

And that He is established upon the Throne (istiwāʾ) in the manner He stated and with the meaning He intended — an establishment purified from touching, settling, resting, indwelling, and moving. The Throne does not carry Him; rather, the Throne and its bearers are carried by the subtlety of His power and are subdued within His grasp.

And He is above the Throne and the heaven, and above all things unto the depths of the earth — a "above-ness" that does not bring Him nearer to the Throne and the heaven, just as it does not distance Him from the earth and the soil. Rather, He is exalted in degrees above the Throne and the heaven, even as He is exalted in degrees above the earth and the soil.

Yet with all that, He is near to every existent, and He is nearer to the servant than his jugular vein, and He is Witness over all things — for His nearness does not resemble the nearness of bodies, just as His Essence does not resemble the essence of bodies.

And that He does not indwell in anything, nor does anything indwell in Him. Exalted is He above being contained by place, even as He is sanctified from being bounded by time. Rather, He was before the creation of time and place, and He is now as He ever was.

And that He is separate from His creation by His attributes: there is none other than Him in His Essence, nor is His Essence in anything other than Him. And He is sanctified from change and transition; events do not inhere in Him, nor do accidents befall Him.
