||| كيفية التيمم

من تعذر عليه استعمال الماء لفقده بعد الطلب أو بمانع له عن الوصول إليه
من سبع أو حابس أو كان الماء الحاضر يحتاج إليه لعطشه أو لعطش رفيقه أو كان
ملكا لغيره ولم يبعه إلا بأكثر من ثمن المثل أو  كان به جراحة أو مرض وخاف
من استعماله فساد العضو أو شدة الضنا فينبغي أن يصبر حتى يدخل عليه وقت
الفريضة ثم يقصد صعيدا طيبا عليه تراب طاهر خالص لين بحيث يثور منه غبار
ويضرب عليه كفيه ضاما بين أصابعه ويمسح بهما جميع وجهه مرة واحدة وينوي عند
ذلك استباحة الصلاة ولا يكلف إيصال الغبار إلى ما تحت الشعور خفت أو كثفت
ويجتهد أن يستوعب بشرة وجهه بالغبار ويحصل ذلك بالضربة الواحدة فإن عرض
الوجه لا يزيد على عرض الكفين ويكفي في الاستيعاب غالب الظن ثم ينزع خاتمة
ويضرب ضربة ثانية يفرج فيها بين أصابعه ثم يلصق ظهور يده اليمنى ببطون
أصابع يده اليسرى بحيث لا يجاوز أطراف الأنامل من إحدى الجهتين عرض المسبحة
من الأخرى ثم يمر يده اليسرى من حيث وضعها على ظاهر ساعده الأيمن إلى
المرفق ثم يقلب بطن كفه اليسرى على باطن ساعده الأيمن ويمرها إلى الكوع
ويمر بطن إبهامه اليسرى على ظاهر إبهامه اليمنى ثم يفعل باليسرى كذلك
ثم يمسح كفيه ويخلل بين أصابعه وغرض هذا التكليف تحصيل الاستيعاب إلى
المرفقين بضربة واحدة فإن عسر عليه ذلك فلا بأس بأن يستوعب بضربتين وزيادة
وإذا صلى به الفرض فله أن يتنفل كيف شاء فإن جمع بين فريضتين فينبغي أن
يعيد التيمم للثانية
وهكذا يفرد كل فريضة بتيمم والله أعلم
PageV01P136
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ي-م (t-y-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To intend, to aim at a goal; al-tayammum is the act of heading toward pure earth with a specific ritual purpose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qur’an {«فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا»} (5:6), it denotes a deliberate substitution for water when water is unavailable—an act of legal concession (rukhṣah) grounded in divine facilitation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical heading toward a thing; metaphorical (majāz) = the ritual wiping of face and hands with earth, as the intent is the essence, not mere dust.
- Root: ص-ع-د (ṣ-ʿ-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Elevated, pure surface of the earth; a tract of ground that is clean and fit for use.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṣaʿīd is the outward layer of the earth—whether soil, sand, or rock—provided it is pure (ṭāhir); it is not restricted to dust alone.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): In the verse, ṣaʿīd is used literally for the ground’s surface, but the legal requirement is purity, not a specific substance.
- Root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pass the hand over a surface; to wipe gently.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Masḥ in ritual law signifies the transfer of purity (ṭahārah) by wiping, as opposed to washing (ghasl); it is a symbolic act of submission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical wiping; metaphorical = the legal act of purification by earth, where the gesture suffices over substance.
- Root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Inability, incapacity; the state of being unable to perform an act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAjz is the legal cause (ʿillah) for tayammum; it is a valid excuse (ʿudhr) that transforms obligation into concession.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = physical incapacity; metaphorical = any lawful impediment (e.g., fear of harm), extending the root meaning to legal necessity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with In (إِنْ) — The sentence «من تعذر عليه استعمال الماء...» uses a relative clause (ṣilah) with an implied conditional nuance; the protasis (condition) is the unavailability of water, and the apodosis (result) is the obligation to wait for the prayer time and perform tayammum. The rule governs the sequence of legal obligations in a periodic sentence, where the condition precedes the commanded act.
chapters.translation: I say: Know that when a person is unable to use water—whether due to its absence after having sought it, or due to an obstacle preventing access to it, such as a wild beast or an imprisoning force—or when the water present is needed for his own thirst or for the thirst of his companion, or when the water belongs to another and its owner will not sell it except at more than the fair price (thaman al-mithl), or when he has a wound or an illness and fears that using water would corrupt the limb or cause severe distress—then he should wait until the time of the obligatory prayer (farīḍah) enters. Thereafter, he should intend (yaqṣid) a pure elevated ground (ṣaʿīd ṭayyib) upon which there is clean, pure, loose soil, such that dust rises from it. He should strike it with both palms, spreading his fingers apart, and wipe with them his entire face once, intending at that moment the permissibility of the prayer (istibāḥat al-ṣalāh). He is not obligated to convey the dust to what lies beneath the hair—whether sparse or thick—but he should strive to cover the surface of his face with the dust. This is achieved with a single strike, for the area of the face does not exceed the area of the two palms, and a predominant assumption (ghālib al-ẓann) suffices for complete coverage. Then he removes his ring and strikes a second time, spreading his fingers apart. He then places the back of his right hand against the inner side of the fingers of his left hand, such that the tips of the fingers do not exceed, from one side, the width of the index finger (musabbihah) from the other. He then passes his left hand from where it was placed over the outer side of his right forearm up to the elbow. Then he turns the inner palm of his left hand onto the inner side of his right forearm and passes it down to the wrist (kūʿ). He passes the inner side of his left thumb over the outer side of his right thumb. He then does the same with the left arm. Thereafter, he wipes his palms and interlaces his fingers. The purpose of this obligation is to achieve complete coverage up to the elbows with a single strike. If that proves difficult, there is no harm in covering with two strikes or more. When he has prayed the obligatory prayer with this tayammum, he may perform voluntary prayers (nawāfil) as he wishes. If he combines two obligatory prayers, he should renew the tayammum for the second. Thus, each obligatory prayer is singled out with its own tayammum. And God knows best.

chapters.title_en: The Third Division of Cleanliness: Purification from Apparent Excretions
chapters.arabic_text: || القسم الثالث من النظافة التنظيف عن الفضلات الظاهرة وهي نوعان أوساخ وأجزاء
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-ف (n-ẓ-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of cleanliness, purity, and freedom from filth; also used for clarity of speech and freedom from blemish.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, denotes both physical purity (ṭahārah) and spiritual purification from moral defilement; here applied to bodily excretions as a prerequisite for ritual worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical dirt; metaphorical (majāz) for moral or spiritual impurity—here used literally for bodily waste.
- Root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus, or what remains after need; also virtue and superiority.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological context, refers to residual matter expelled from the body (e.g., urine, feces) as opposed to essential parts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for surplus; metaphorical for merit—here literal for bodily excess.
- Root: و-س-خ (w-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dirt, grime, or filth adhering to a surface; also moral defilement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical impurity requiring removal for ritual validity; contrasted with ḥadath (ritual impurity requiring ablution).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical grime; metaphorical for sin—here literal.
- Root: ج-ز-ء (j-z-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A part, portion, or component of a whole; also a unit of division.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In this context, refers to detached bodily parts (e.g., skin flakes, nails) that are not intrinsically impure but require removal for cleanliness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a part; no metaphorical extension here—used in its primary sense.
- Sībawayh Rule: **Al-ʿAṭf bi-ʿalā al-Tafṣīl** (Coordination for Specification) — The phrase "وهي نوعان" (and they are two types) introduces a bipartite division, with "أوساخ وأجزاء" (dirt and parts) coordinated by wa (and) to enumerate the two categories, each governed by the same syntactic status (nominative predicate of an implied kāna or as badal).
chapters.translation: I say: The third division of cleanliness is purification from apparent excretions (al-fuḍūlāt al-ẓāhirah), and these are of two types: filth (awsākh) and detached bodily parts (ajzāʾ).

chapters.title_en: On the Purification of Filth and Moisture: The First Category of External Cleanliness

||| النوع الأول الأوساخ والرطوبات المترشحة وهي ثمانية

الأول ما يجتمع في شعر الرأس من الدرن والقمل فالتنظيف عنه مستحب بالغسل
والترجيل والتدهين إزالة للشعث عنه وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يدهن الشعر
ويرجله غبا ويأمر به (1) ويقول صلى الله عليه وسلم ادهنوا غبا (2) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم من كان له شعرة فليكرمها (3) أي ليصنها عن الأوساخ ودخل
عليه رجل ثائر الرأس أشعث اللحية فقال أما كان لهذا دهن يسكن به شعره ثم
قال يدخل أحدكم كأنه شيطان (4)
الثاني ما يجتمع من الوسخ في معاطف  الأذن والمسح يزيل ما يظهر منه وما
يجتمع في قعر الصماخ فينبغي أن ينظف برفق عند الخروج من الحمام فإن كثرة
ذلك ربما تضر بالسمع
الثالث ما يجتمع في داخل الأنف من الرطوبات المنعقدة الملتصقة بجوانبه
ويزيلها بالاستنشاق والاستنثار
الرابع ما يجتمع على الأسنان وطرف اللسان من القلح فيزيله السواك
والمضمضة وقد ذكرناهما
الخامس ما يجتمع في اللحية من الوسخ والقمل إذا لم يتعهد ويستحب إزالة
ذلك بالغسل والتسريح بالمشط
وفي الخبر المشهور أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان لا يفارقه المشط والمدرى
والمرآة في سفر ولا حضر (5) وهي سنة العرب وفي خبر غريب أنه صلى الله عليه
وسلم كان يسرح لحيته في اليوم مرتين (6) وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم كث اللحية
(7) وكذلك كان أبو بكر وكان عثمان طويل اللحية رقيقها وكان على عريض اللحية
قد ملأت ما بين منكبيه
وفي حديث أغرب منه قالت عائشة رضي الله عنها اجتمع قوم بباب رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم فخرج إليهم فرأيته يطلع في الحب يسوي من رأسه ولحيته
(8) فقلت أوتفعل ذلك يا رسول الله فقال نعم إن الله يحب من عبده أن يتجمل
لإخوانه إذا خرج إليهم والجاهل ربما يظن أن ذلك من حب التزين للناس قياسا
على أخلاق غيره وتشبيها للملائكة بالحدادين وهيهات فقد كان رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم مأمورا بالدعوة وكان من وظائفه أن يسعى في تعظيم أمر نفسه
في قلوبهم كيلا تزدريه نفوسهم ويحسن صورته في أعينهم كيلا تستصغره أعينهم
فينفرهم ذلك ويتعلق المنافقون بذلك في تنفيرهم
وهذا القصد واجب على كل عالم تصدي لدعوة الخلق إلى الله عز وجل وهو أن
يراعي من ظاهره ما لا يوجب نفرة الناس عنه
والاعتماد في مثل هذه الأمور على النية فإنها أعمال في أنفسها تكتسب
الأوصاف من المقصود فالتزين PageV01P137
على هذا القصد محبوب وترك الشعث في اللحية إظهارا للزهد وقلة المبالاة
بالنفس محذور وتركه شغلا بما هو أهم منه محبوب
وهذه أحوال باطنة بين العبد وبين الله  عز وجل
والناقد بصير والتلبيس غير رائج عليه بحال وكم من جاهل يتعاطى هذه الأمور
التفاتا إلى الخلق وهو يلبس على نفسه وعلى غيره ويزعم أن قصده الخير فترى
جماعة من العلماء يلبسون الثياب الفاخرة ويزعمون أن قصدهم إرغام المبتدعة
والمجادلين والتقرب إلى الله تعالى به
وهذا أمر ينكشف يوم تبلى السرائر ويوم يبعثر ما في القبور ويحصل ما في
الصدور فعند ذلك تتميز السبيكة الخالصة من البهرجة فنعوذ بالله من الخزي
يوم العرض الأكبر
السادس وسخ البراجم وهي معاطف ظهور الأنامل كانت العرب لا تكثر غسل ذلك
لتركها غسل اليد عقيب الطعام فيجتمع في تلك الغضون وسخ فأمرهم رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم بغسل البراجم (1)
السابع تنظيف الرواجب (2) أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العرب
بتنظيفها وهي رءوس الأنامل وما تحت الأظفار من الوسخ لأنها كانت لا يحضرها
المقراض في كل وقت فتجتمع فيها أوساخ فوقت لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم قلم الأظفار ونتف الإبط وحلق العانة أربعين يوما (3) لكنه أمر رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتنظيف ما تحت الأظفار (4) وجاء في الأثر أن النبي
صلى الله عليه وسلم استبطأ الوحي فلما هبط عليه جبريل عليه السلام قال له
كيف ننزل عليكم وأنتم لا تغسلون براجمكم ولا تنظفون رواجبكم (5) وقلحا لا
تستاكون مر أمتك بذلك والاف وسخ الظفر والتف وسخ الأذن وقوله عز وجل {فلا
تقل لهما أف} تعبهما أي بما تحت الظفر من الوسخ وقيل لا تتأذ بهما كما
تتأذى بما تحت الظفر
الثامن الدرن الذي يجتمع على جميع البدن برشح العرق وغبار الطريق وذلك
يزيله الحمام ولا بأس بدخول الحمام دخل أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
حمامات الشام وقال بعضهم نعم البيت بيت الحمام يطهر البدن ويذكر النار روي
ذلك عن أبي الدرداء وأبي أيوب الأنصاري رضي الله عنهما
وقال بعضهم بئس البيت بيت الحمام يبدي العورة ويذهب الحياء فهذا تعرض
لآفته وذاك تعرض لفائدته ولا بأس بطلب فائدته عند  الاحتراز من آفته
ولكن على داخل الحمام وظائف من السنن والواجبات فعليه واجبان في عورته
وواجبان في عورة غيره
أما الواجبان في عورته فهو أن يصونها عن نظر الغير ويصونها عن مس الغير
فلا يتعاطى أمرها وإزالة وسخها إلا بيده ويمنع الدلاك من مس الفخذ وما بين
السرة إلى العانة وفي إباحة مس ما ليس بسوءة لإزالة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-س-خ (wasikha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is filth, dirt, or impurity adhering to a surface; denotes both physical grime and moral defilement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the religious sciences, it signifies that which tarnishes the outward form (ẓāhir) and, by extension, impedes the soul's readiness for worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for bodily dirt; metaphorically (majāz) for sin, as in the Quranic {«فلا تقل لهما أف»} where "uff" is linked to the least filth under the nail.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The enumerated items (e.g., "the first," "the second") are governed by a nominal predicate structure (mubtadaʾ-khabar), requiring precise sequential parsing to preserve the author's taxonomic intent.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first category [of external cleanliness] concerns the accumulated filths and seeping moistures, and these are eight in number.

The first is what gathers in the hair of the head from dirt and lice. Cleaning oneself of this is commendable (mustaḥabb) through washing, combing, and oiling, as a removal of dishevelment (shaʿath) from it. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to oil his hair and comb it every other day, and he commanded others to do so. He said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Oil your hair every other day." And he said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever has hair, let him honor it" — meaning, let him protect it from filth. A man entered upon him with disheveled hair and a tangled beard, and he said: "Did this man not have oil with which to settle his hair?" Then he said: "One of you enters as if he were a devil."

The second is what gathers of grime in the folds of the ear. Wiping (al-masḥ) removes what appears of it, but what collects in the depths of the ear canal should be cleaned gently upon leaving the bathhouse (ḥammām), for an excess of this may harm the hearing.

The third is what gathers inside the nose from congealed moistures adhering to its sides. These are removed by snuffing water up (al-istinshāq) and blowing it out (al-istinthār).

The fourth is what gathers on the teeth and the tip of the tongue from film (qalaḥ). This is removed by the toothstick (siwāk) and rinsing the mouth (maḍmaḍah), which we have already mentioned.

The fifth is what gathers in the beard from grime and lice if it is not tended to. It is commendable to remove this by washing and combing with a comb. In the well-known report, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, never parted from his comb, his hair-dresser's iron, and his mirror, whether traveling or at home. This is the custom (sunnah) of the Arabs. In a rare report, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to comb his beard twice a day. His beard was thick, as was that of Abu Bakr. ʿUthman had a long, thin beard, and ʿAli had a broad beard that filled the space between his shoulders.

In a report even rarer than this, ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "A group of people gathered at the door of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He went out to them, and I saw him looking into a mirror, straightening his hair and his beard." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you do this?" He said: "Yes. Indeed, Allah loves that His servant beautify himself for his brothers when he goes out to them." The ignorant one might suppose that this stems from a love of self-adornment before people, drawing an analogy from the character of others and likening the angels to blacksmiths. How far from the truth! For the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was commanded to call [people] to Allah, and among his duties was to strive in magnifying his own station in their hearts, lest their souls disdain him, and to render his image fair in their eyes, lest their eyes belittle him — for that would drive them away, and the hypocrites would seize upon it to repel them further.

This intention is obligatory upon every scholar who undertakes the call of creation to Allah, Mighty and Majestic: namely, that he observe in his outward appearance that which does not cause people to recoil from him. Reliance in such matters is upon the intention (niyyah), for these are acts which in themselves acquire their descriptions from their purpose. Thus, beautification with this intention is beloved, while leaving the beard disheveled as a display of asceticism (zuhd) and carelessness toward oneself is a danger. Leaving it [unattended] out of preoccupation with what is more important is beloved. These are inward states between the servant and Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The critic is discerning, and deception (talbīs) does not pass with him at all. How many an ignorant one engages in these matters with an eye to creation, deceiving himself and others, claiming his intention is good! You see a group of scholars wearing luxurious garments, claiming their intention is to spite the innovators and the disputants, and to draw near to Allah thereby. This is a matter that will be unveiled on the Day when secrets are tested, the Day when what is in the graves is scattered, and what is in the breasts is brought forth. At that moment, the pure ingot will be distinguished from the counterfeit. We seek refuge in Allah from disgrace on the Day of the Great Display.

The sixth is the grime of the knuckle-joints (barājim), which are the folds on the backs of the fingers. The Arabs did not wash these much, due to their neglect of washing the hands after food, so grime would collect in those creases. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded them to wash the knuckle-joints.

The seventh is cleaning the nail-roots (rawājib). The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded the Arabs to clean them — these being the tips of the fingers and the grime under the nails — because they did not have scissors at hand at all times, so filth would accumulate there. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, set a time limit for them for trimming the nails, plucking the armpit hair, and shaving the pubic region: forty days. But he commanded cleaning what is under the nails. It is reported in the tradition (athar) that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, awaited the revelation, and it was delayed. When Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended upon him, he said to him: "How shall we descend upon you when you do not wash your knuckle-joints nor clean your nail-roots?" And [he mentioned] the film (qalaḥ) [on the teeth] that you do not remove with the toothstick — your community was commanded to do this. And "uff" is the grime under the nail, and "tuff" is the grime of the ear. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«فلا تقل لهما أف»} — "So do not say to them 'uff'" — means: do not weary them, even by the grime under the nail. And it is said: do not harm them as you would be harmed by what is under the nail.

The eighth is the scurf that gathers over the entire body from the seepage of sweat and the dust of the road. This is removed by the bathhouse (ḥammām), and there is no harm in entering the bathhouse. The companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered the bathhouses of Syria. Some of them said: "What an excellent house is the bathhouse! It purifies the body and reminds one of the Fire." This is reported from Abu al-Dardā' and Abu Ayyūb al-Anṣārī, may Allah be pleased with them both. Others said: "What an evil house is the bathhouse! It exposes the private parts and removes modesty." This one attends to its harm, and that one attends to its benefit. There is no harm in seeking its benefit while guarding against its harm.

However, upon the one entering the bathhouse are duties from the sunan and the obligations. Upon him are two obligations concerning his own private parts, and two obligations concerning the private parts of others. As for the two obligations concerning his own private parts: he must protect them from the gaze of others, and protect them from the touch of others. He should not handle their affair or remove their filth except with his own hand, and he should prevent the bath-attendant (dallāk) from touching the thigh and what is between the navel and the pubic region. Regarding the permissibility of touching what is not a shameful part (sawʾah) for removing filth, there is some probability, but the more sound analogy (qiyās) is prohibition, for touching the two shameful parts is linked to looking at them in prohibition. Likewise, the rest of the private area — namely, the thighs — should be treated the same.

The two obligations concerning the private parts of others are: he must lower his gaze from them, and he must forbid their exposure, for commanding the good and forbidding the evil (al-nahy ʿan al-munkar) is obligatory. Upon him is the mention [of the prohibition], but acceptance is not upon him. The obligation of mention does not fall from him except for fear of being struck, insulted, or something befalling him that is itself unlawful — for he is not obliged to forbid an unlawful act if doing so would drag him into committing another unlawful act. As for his saying: "I know that this is of no benefit and will not be acted upon" — this is no excuse. Rather, the mention is indispensable, for no heart is free from being affected by hearing the disapproval and sensing the need for caution when sins are named. This has an effect in making the matter ugly in one's eyes and repelling one's soul from it. Thus, it is not permissible to abandon it. For this reason, prudence dictates abandoning entry into the bathhouse at such times, for they are not free of exposed private parts — especially what is below the navel to above the pubic region, for people do not count this as a private part, yet the Sacred Law has attached it to the private parts and made it like their sanctuary. For this reason, it is commendable to empty the bathhouse [of others].

Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith said: "How harsh is a man who owns nothing but a single dirham, which he pays to have the bathhouse emptied for himself." Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, was seen in the bathhouse with his face to the wall, having bound his eyes with a bandage. Some said: "There is no harm in entering the bathhouse, but with two wraps: one for the private parts and one for the head, with which he covers himself and protects his eyes."

As for the sunan, they are ten. The first is the intention (niyyah): that he does not enter for some immediate worldly gain, nor as a plaything following his whim, but rather intends by it the beloved cleanliness, adorning himself for the prayer. Then he gives the bathhouse-keeper his wage before entering, for what he will receive is unknown, as is what the keeper anticipates. Thus, handing over the wage before entry removes the ignorance from one of the two exchange-considerations and pleases his own soul. Then he puts forward his left foot upon entering and says: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I seek refuge in Allah from the filth, the unclean, the wicked, the contaminating, the accursed Satan." Then he enters at a time of solitude, or he makes the effort to have the bathhouse emptied. For if there are none in the bathhouse but the religious and those careful of private parts, still, looking at exposed bodies contains a taint of diminished modesty, and it reminds one of gazing at private parts. Moreover, a person is not free from the exposure of private parts in his movements, by a turn of the edge of his wrap, and the eye falls upon the private part without one knowing. For this reason, Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, bound his eyes. He washes the two sides [of his body] upon entering and does not hasten into the hot chamber until he sweats in the first one. He should not pour water excessively but rather limit himself to what is needed, for that is what is permitted by the contextual indication (qarīnah al-ḥāl). Any excess, if the keeper knew of it, he would resent — especially hot water, for it costs him effort and involves toil. He should recall the heat of the Fire by the heat of the bathhouse, and imagine himself imprisoned in the hot chamber for an hour, and measure it against Hellfire — for it is the house most resembling Hell: fire from below and darkness from above. We seek refuge in Allah from that. Indeed, the intelligent man does not neglect the remembrance of the Hereafter for a single moment, for it is his destiny and his resting place. Thus, in everything he sees — water, fire, or otherwise — he finds a lesson (ʿibrah) and an admonition. For a man looks according to his concern (himmah). When a cloth-merchant, a carpenter, a builder, and a weaver enter a well-appointed, furnished house, if you examine them, you see the cloth-merchant looking at the furnishings, pondering their value; the weaver looking at the garments, pondering their weave; the carpenter looking at the ceiling, pondering how it is constructed; and the builder looking at the walls, pondering how they are made firm and straight. Likewise, the traveler on the path of the Hereafter sees nothing of things but that it becomes for him an admonition and a reminder of the Hereafter. Indeed, he looks at nothing but that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, opens for him a path of reflection. If he looks at darkness, he remembers the gloom of the grave; if he looks at a serpent, he remembers the vipers of Hell; if he looks at an ugly, hideous form, he remembers Munkar and Nakīr and the Zabāniyah; if he hears a terrifying sound, he remembers the Blast of the Trumpet (nafkhat al-ṣūr); if he sees something beautiful, he remembers the bliss of Paradise; if he hears a word of rejection or acceptance in a market or a house, he remembers what will be unveiled of his final affair after the Reckoning — of rejection and acceptance. How fitting it is that this should be the dominant state of the intelligent man's heart, and nothing turns him from it except the pressing necessities of this world. For when he compares the duration of his stay in this world to the duration of his stay in the Hereafter, he deems it insignificant — unless he is among those whose hearts have been made heedless and whose inner sight has been blinded.

Among the sunan is that he does not greet with salām upon entering, and if someone greets him, he does not respond with the words of salām. Rather, he remains silent if another responds, and if he wishes, he says: "May Allah heal you" (ʿāfāka Allāh). There is no harm in his shaking hands with the one entering and saying "May Allah heal you" as an opening of speech. Then he should not speak much in the bathhouse, nor recite the Quran except silently. There is no harm in voicing the seek of refuge (al-istiʿādhah) from Satan. It is disliked (makrūh) to enter the bathhouse between the two evening prayers and near sunset, for that is a time when the devils spread about. There is no harm in another rubbing him down, for this has been transmitted from Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ, who bequeathed that a man who was not among his companions should wash him, saying: "He rubbed me down in the bathhouse once, and I wished to repay him with what would delight him" — and indeed he would delight in that. Evidence for its permissibility is what some companions reported: that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, alighted at a way-station during one of his journeys and slept on his stomach while a black slave massaged his back. I said: "What is this, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The she-camel threw me off." Then, when he finishes with the bathhouse, he thanks Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for this blessing. For it has been said: "Hot water in winter is among the delights about which one will be asked." Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The bathhouse is among the delights that people have newly introduced."

This is from the standpoint of the Sacred Law. As for the standpoint of medicine, it has been said: "The bathhouse after depilation (nūrah) is a safeguard against leprosy." And it is said: "Depilation once a month extinguishes the yellow bile, purifies the complexion, and increases sexual vigor." And it is said: "Urinating in the bathhouse while standing in winter is more beneficial than a draught of medicine." And it is said: "A sleep in summer after the bathhouse equals a draught of medicine." And washing the feet with cold water after leaving the bathhouse is a safeguard against gout. It is disliked to pour cold water over the head upon leaving, and likewise to drink it. This is the ruling for men.

As for women, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is not lawful for a man to let his wife enter the bathhouse." And in the house there is a place for bathing. The well-known ruling is that it is unlawful (ḥarām) for men to enter the bathhouse except with a waist-wrapper (miʾzar), and unlawful for a woman to enter the bathhouse except for one who is postpartum or ill. ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, entered a bathhouse due to an illness that had befallen her. If she enters out of necessity, she should not enter except with a full, ample wrap. And it is disliked for a man to give her the bathhouse fee, for he would thereby be assisting her in what is disliked.

chapters.title_en: The Second Kind: Matters Concerning the Body's Parts — Eight in Number
chapters.arabic_text:
||| النوع الثاني فيما يحدث في البدن من الأجزاء  وهي ثمانية

الأول شعر الرأس ولا بأس بحلقه لمن أراد التنظيف ولا بأس بتركه لمن يدهنه
ويرجله إلا إذا تركه قزعا أي قطعا وهو دأب أهل الشطارة أو أرسل الذوائب على
هيئة أهل الشرف حيث صار ذلك شعارا لهم فإنه إذا لم يكن شريفا كان ذلك
تلبيسا
الثاني شعر الشارب وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم قصوا الشارب وفي لفظ آخر
جزوا الشوارب وفي لفظ آخر حفوا الشوارب وأعفوا اللحى (4) أي اجعلوها حفاف
الشفة أي حولها وحفاف الشيء حوله ومنه {وترى الملائكة حافين من حول العرش}
وفي لفظ آخر احفوا وهذا يشعر بالاستئصال وقوله حفوا يدل على ما دون ذلك
وقال الله عز وجل أن يسئلكموها فيحفكم تبخلوا أي يستقصى عليكم وأما الحلق
فلم يرد
والإحفاء القريب من الحلق نقل عن الصحابة نظر بعض التابعين إلى رجل أحفى
شاربه فقال ذكرتني أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
وقال المغيرة بن شعبة نظر إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد طال
شاربي فقال تعال فقصه لي على سواك (5) ولا بأس بترك سباليه وهما طرفا
الشارب فعل ذلك عمر وغيره لأن ذلك لا يستر الفم ولا يبقى فيه غمر الطعام إذ
لا يصل إليه وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعفوا اللحى أي كثروها وفي الخبر إن
اليهود يعفون شواربهم PageV01P140
ويقصون لحاهم فخالفوهم (1) وكره بعض العلماء الحلق ورآه بدعة
الثالث شعر الإبط ويستحب نتفه في كل أربعين يوما مرة وذلك سهل على من
تعود نتفه في الابتداء فأما  من تعود الحلق فيكفيه الحلق إذ في النتف تعذيب
وإيلام والمقصود النظافة وأن لا يجتمع الوسخ في خللها ويحصل ذلك بالحلق
الرابع شعر العانة ويستحب إزالة ذلك إما بالحلق أو بالنورة ولا ينبغي أن
تتأخر عن أربعين يوما
الخامس الأظفار وتقليمها مستحب لشناعة صورتها إذا طالت ولما يجتمع فيها
من الوسخ قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا هريرة أقلم أظفارك فإن
الشيطان يقعد على ما طال منها (2) ولو كان تحت الظفر وسخ فلا يمنع ذلك صحة
الوضوء لأنه لا يمنع وصول الماءولأنه يتساهل فيه للحاجة لا سيما في أظفار
الرجل وفي الأوساخ التي تجتمع على البراجم وظهور الأرجل والأيدي من العرب
وأهل السواد وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يأمرهم بالقلم وينكر عليهم
ما يرى تحت أظفارهم من الأوساخ ولم يأمرهم بإعادة الصلاة ولو أمر به لكان
فيه فائدة أخرى وهو التغليظ والزجر عن ذلك
ولم أر في الكتب خبرا مرويا في ترتيب قلم الأظفار ولكن سمعت أنه صلى الله
عليه وسلم بدأ بمسبحته اليمنى وختم بإبهامه اليمنى وابتدأ في اليسرى
بالخنصر إلى الإبهام (3) ولما تأملت في هذا خطر لي من المعنى ما يدل على أن
الرواية فيه صحيحة إذ مثل هذا المعنى لا ينكشف ابتداء إلا بنور النبوة وأما
العالم ذو البصيرة فغايته أن يستنبطه من العقل بعد نقل الفعل إليه
فالذي لاح لي فيه والعلم عند الله سبحانه أنه لا بد من قلم أظفار اليد
والرجل واليد أشرف من الرجل فيبدأ بها ثم اليمنى أشرف من اليسرى فيبدأ بها
ثم على اليمنى خمسة أصابع والمسبحة أشرفها إذ هي المشيرة في كلمتي الشهادة
من جملة الأصابع ثم بعدها ينبغي أن يبتدىء بما على يمينها إذ الشرع يستحب
إدارة الطهور وغيره على اليمين وإن وضعت ظهر الكف على الأرض فالإبهام هو
اليمين وإن وضعت بطن الكف فالوسطى هي اليمنى واليد إذا تركت بطبعها كان
الكف مائلا إلى جهة الأرض إذ جهة حركة اليمين إلى اليسار واستتمام  الحركة
إلى اليسار يجعل ظهر الكف عاليا فما يقتضيه الطبع أولى ثم إذا وضعت الكف
على الكف صارت الأصابع في حكم حلقة دائرة فيقتضي ترتيب الدور الذهاب عن
يمين المسبحة إلى أن يعود إلى المسبحة فتقع البداءة بخنصر اليسرى والختم
بإبهامها ويبقى إبهام اليمنى فيختم به التقليم
وإنما قدرت الكف موضوعة على الكف حتى تصير الأصابع كأشخاص في حلقة ليظهر
ترتيبها
وتقدير ذلك أولى من تقدير وضع الكف على ظهر الكف أو وضع ظهر الكف على ظهر
الكف فإن ذلك لا يقتضيه الطبع
وأما أصابع الرجل فالأولى عندي إن لم يثبت فيها نقل أن يبدأ بخنصر اليمنى
ويختم بخنصر اليسرى كما في التخليل فإن المعاني التي ذكرها في اليد لا تتجه
ههنا إذ لا مسبحة في الرجل
وهذه الأصابع في حكم صف واحد ثابت على الأرض فيبدأ من جانب اليمنى فإن
تقديرها حلقة بوضع الأخمص على الأخمص يأباه الطبع بخلاف اليدين
وهذه الدقائق في الترتيب تنكشف بنور النبوة في لحظة واحدة وإنما يطول
التعب علينا
ثم لو سئلنا ابتداء عن الترتيب في ذلك ربما لم يخطر لنا
وإذا ذكرنا فعله صلى الله عليه وسلم PageV01P141
وترتيبه ربما تيسر لنا مما عاينه صلى الله عليه وسلم بشهادة الحكم
وتنبيهه على المعنى استنباط المعنى ولا تظنن أن أفعاله صلى الله عليه وسلم
في جميع حركاته كانت خارجة عن وزن وقانون وترتيب بل جميع الأمور الاختيارية
التي ذكرناها يتردد فيها الفاعل بين قسمين أو أقسام كان لا يقدم على واحد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ل-ق (ḥ-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To shave, remove hair completely; also denotes the orbit or circle of something.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Removal of what is extraneous to the natural form; linked to ritual cleanliness (naẓāfah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for shaving hair; metaphorically used for "exacting fully" (as in {«...يُحْفِكُمْ...»} "He will exact from you").
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "if he leaves it" (إلا إذا تركه) governs a restrictive exception, requiring careful parsing of the apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second kind concerns what occurs in the body from its parts, and these are eight.

The first is the hair of the head. There is no harm in shaving it for one who seeks cleanliness, and no harm in leaving it for one who oils and combs it — except if one leaves it in patches (qazaʿ), i.e., cut in pieces, which is the habit of rogues; or if one lets down long locks (dhawāʾib) in the manner of people of noble rank, when that has become their distinctive emblem. For if one is not noble, this constitutes deception (talbīs).

The second is the hair of the moustache. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Trim the moustache" (qusṣū al-shārib); in another wording: "Clip the moustaches" (juzzū al-shawārib); in yet another: "Shave around the moustaches" (ḥuffū al-shawārib) and "let the beards grow" (aʿfū al-liḥā) — i.e., make them surround the lip, for the surround (ḥifāf) of a thing is its periphery, whence {«وَتَرَى الْمَلَائِكَةَ حَافِّينَ مِنْ حَوْلِ الْعَرْشِ»} "And you see the angels encircling around the Throne." In another wording: "Shave thoroughly" (aḥfū), which suggests complete removal; while his saying "ḥuffū" indicates something less than that. God Almighty said: {«إِن يَسْأَلْكُمُوهَا فَيُحْفِكُمْ تَبْخَلُوا»} "If He asks you for them and then exacts them from you, you would be miserly" — i.e., He would demand everything from you. As for complete shaving, no report has come regarding it.

Al-Iḥfāʾ, which is close to shaving, is transmitted from the Companions. One of the Followers (tābiʿūn) looked at a man who had shaved his moustache thoroughly and said: "You have reminded me of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked at me when my moustache had grown long and said: 'Come, trim it for me on a toothstick (siwāk).'" There is no harm in leaving the two ends (sibālān) — the two tips of the moustache — for ʿUmar and others did this, because they do not cover the mouth nor retain food residue therein, since food does not reach them. His saying ﷺ "let the beards grow" (aʿfū al-liḥā) means "make them abundant." In the report: "The Jews let their moustaches grow and trim their beards, so oppose them." Some scholars disapproved of shaving the beard and deemed it an innovation (bidʿah).

The third is the hair of the armpit. Plucking it is recommended once every forty days. This is easy for one accustomed to plucking from the start; as for one accustomed to shaving, shaving suffices him, for in plucking there is torment and pain. The aim is cleanliness and that no filth accumulate in its interstices, and this is achieved by shaving.

The fourth is the hair of the pubic region. Removing it is recommended, either by shaving or by depilatory lime (nūrah). It should not be delayed beyond forty days.

The fifth is the nails. Trimming them is recommended due to the ugliness of their appearance when long and the filth that gathers beneath them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abū Hurayrah, trim your nails, for Satan sits upon whatever grows long of them." If there is filth beneath the nail, it does not prevent the validity of the ablution (wuḍūʾ), because it does not prevent water from reaching [the skin], and because leniency is granted in this due to necessity — especially regarding the nails of the foot and the dirt that accumulates on the knuckles and the tops of the feet and hands among the Arabs and the people of the villages. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to command them to trim [their nails] and reproach them for the dirt they saw beneath their nails, yet he did not command them to repeat the prayer. Had he commanded that, there would have been another benefit in it — namely, severity and deterrence from that practice.

I have not seen in the books any transmitted report regarding the order of trimming the nails, but I heard that he ﷺ began with his right index finger and ended with his right thumb, and began on the left [hand] with the little finger up to the thumb. When I pondered this, there occurred to me a meaning indicating that the report is sound, for such a meaning is not unveiled initially except by the light of prophecy. As for the insightful scholar, his utmost is to derive it by reason after the action has been transmitted to him.

What became apparent to me therein — and knowledge is with God Almighty — is that one must trim the nails of both hand and foot. The hand is nobler than the foot, so one begins with it; then the right is nobler than the left, so one begins with it. On the right hand there are five fingers, and the index finger (musabbihah) is the noblest of them, for it is the one raised in the two words of the testimony of faith (shahādah) among the fingers. Then after it, one should begin with what is to its right, for the Sacred Law recommends proceeding to the right in purification and other matters. If the back of the hand is placed on the ground, the thumb is the rightmost; if the palm is placed, the middle finger is the rightmost. When the hand is left to its natural disposition, the palm inclines toward the ground, for the direction of the right's movement is toward the left, and completing the movement toward the left makes the back of the hand uppermost. So what nature dictates is more appropriate. Then, if the palm is placed upon the palm, the fingers become like a circular ring, and the order of the circle requires proceeding from the right of the index finger until returning to the index finger — thus the beginning falls upon the left little finger and the ending upon the left thumb, leaving the right thumb to conclude the trimming.

I only estimated the palm placed upon the palm so that the fingers become like persons in a ring, to manifest their order. This estimation is more appropriate than estimating the palm upon the back of the hand or the back upon the back, for that is not dictated by nature.

As for the toes, the more appropriate in my view — if no transmission is established therein — is to begin with the right little toe and end with the left little toe, as in the case of khilāl (passing wet fingers between the toes). For the meanings mentioned regarding the hand do not apply here, since there is no index finger on the foot. These toes are like a single row fixed upon the ground, so one begins from the right side; for estimating them as a ring by placing sole upon sole is rejected by nature, unlike the two hands.

These subtleties of order are unveiled by the light of prophecy in a single moment; it is only upon us that the effort is prolonged. If we were asked at the outset about the order in this matter, perhaps it would not occur to us. But when his action ﷺ and his ordering are mentioned to us, perhaps the derivation of the meaning becomes facilitated for us through what he ﷺ witnessed, by the testimony of wisdom and his indication of the meaning. Do not think that his actions ﷺ in all his movements were outside of measure, law, and order. Rather, all voluntary matters that we have mentioned — the agent wavers between two or more alternatives, and he does not advance upon one specific [option] by mere chance, but by a meaning that necessitates advancement and prioritization. For letting oneself go carelessly, as happens as the nature of beasts, [is blameworthy]; while governing movements by the scales of meanings is the nature of the friends of God (awliyāʾ). The closer a person's movements and thoughts are to governance, and the farther from negligence and being left to no purpose, the higher his rank among the prophets and saints, and the more manifest his proximity to God Almighty. For the one near the Prophet ﷺ is near God Almighty, and the one near God must necessarily be near — so the one near the near one is near in relation to others. We seek refuge in God from having the reins of our movements and stillness in the hand of Satan through the intermediary of caprice (hawā).

Consider the governance of movements in his ﷺ use of kohl (iktiḥāl): he would apply kohl to his right eye three times and to his left twice, beginning with the right due to its nobility. The disparity between the two eyes was so that the total would be odd (witr), for the odd has merit over the even — since God Almighty is Witr (One) and loves the odd. Thus, the servant's action should not be devoid of correspondence to one of God's attributes. For this reason, odd numbers are recommended in cleansing with stones (istijmār).

He did not limit himself to three [in each eye] — which is odd — because the left would then receive only one, and one application generally does not cover the roots of the eyelids with kohl. The right was singled for three because preference is necessary for the odd, and the right is more deserving of increase. If you say: "Why then limit the left to two, which is even?" — the answer is that this is a necessity, for if each were given an odd number, the total would be even, since odd plus odd equals even. Observing the odd in the total act — which is like a single trait — is more beloved than observing it in the individual parts. There is also another aspect: one might apply kohl to each eye three times, by analogy with the ablution (wuḍūʾ), and this has been transmitted in the Ṣaḥīḥ, and it is more appropriate.

Were I to exhaust the subtleties of what he ﷺ observed in his movements, the matter would become lengthy. So measure by what you have heard what you have not heard.

Know that the scholar is not an heir of the Prophet ﷺ unless he has attained all the meanings of the Sacred Law, such that between him and the Prophet ﷺ there remains only one degree — the degree of prophecy — which is the distinguishing degree between the heir and the one inherited from. For the one inherited from is he who acquired the wealth and busied himself in its acquisition and gained power over it; the heir is he who did not acquire it nor gain power over it, but it was transferred to him and he received it from him after its acquisition. Such meanings — despite their ease in relation to the depths and secrets — none can grasp initially except the prophets, and none can derive them by reception after the prophets' indication except the scholars, who are the heirs of the prophets, peace be upon them.

The sixth and seventh are the excess of the navel and the foreskin of the glans. As for the navel, it is cut at birth. As for purification by circumcision (khitān), it is the custom of the Jews on the seventh day after birth; opposing them by delaying until the child's teeth appear is more beloved and farther from danger. He ﷺ said: "Circumcision is a Sunnah for men and an honor for women." One should not exaggerate in the khafḍ (female circumcision). He ﷺ said to Umm ʿAṭiyyah, who used to perform it: "O Umm ʿAṭiyyah, trim but do not overdo (ashimmī wa lā tunhikī), for it is more radiant for the face and more favorable with the husband" — i.e., it preserves more of the face's water and blood, and is better for her intercourse. Observe the consummate eloquence of his ﷺ expression in euphemism, and the radiance of the light of prophecy shining from the interests of the Hereafter — which are the greatest aims of prophecy — to the interests of this world, until there was unveiled to him, though he was unlettered (ummī), concerning this matter of lowly rank what, had negligence occurred regarding it, harm would have been feared. Glory be to Him who sent him as a mercy to the worlds, to gather for them through the blessing of his mission the interests of this world and the religion. May God bless him and grant him peace.

The eighth is what grows long of the beard. We have delayed it only to append to it what pertains to the beard of Sunnahs and innovations, for this is the most fitting place for its mention. They differed regarding what grows long of it. It was said: if a man grasps his beard and removes what exceeds the grip, there is no harm — for Ibn ʿUmar and a group of the Followers did this, and al-Shaʿbī and Ibn Sīrīn deemed it good. Al-Ḥasan and Qatādah disapproved of it, saying: "Leaving it is better as well-being," due to his saying ﷺ "let the beards grow" (aʿfū al-liḥā). The matter in this is lenient, unless it reaches the point of trimming the beard and rounding it from the sides. For excessive length may disfigure the form and unleash the tongues of backbiters toward disparaging it — so there is no harm in guarding against it with this intention.

Al-Nakhaʿī said: "I marvel at an intelligent man with a long beard — how does he not take from his beard and make it between two beards?" For moderation in everything is good. Therefore it was said: "The longer the beard, the more the intellect is tucked up."

وفي اللحية عشر خصال مكروهة وبعضها أشد كراهة من بعض خضابها
بالسواد وتبييضها بالكبريت ونتفها ونتف الشيب منها والنقصان منها
والزيادة وتسريحها تصنعا لأجل الرياء وتركها شعثة إظهارا للزهد والنظر إلى
سوادها عجبا بالشباب وإلى بياضها تكبرا بعلو السن وخضابها بالحمرة والصفرة
من غير نية تشبها بالصالحين
أما الأول  وهو الخضاب بالسواد فهو منهي عنه لقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم خير
شبابكم من تشبه بشيوخكم وشر شيوخكم من تشبه بشبابكم (1) والمراد بالتشبه
بالشيوخ في الوقار لا في تبييض الشعر ونهى عن الخضاب بالسواد (2) وقال هو
خضاب أهل النار (3) وفي لفظ آخر الخضاب بالسواد خضاب الكفار وتزوج رجل على
عهد عمر رضي الله عنه وكان يخضب بالسواد فنصل خضابه وظهرت شيبته فرفعه أهل
المرأة إلى عمر رضي الله عنه فرد نكاحه وأوجعه ضربا وقال غررت القوم
بالشباب ولبست عليهم شيبتك ويقال أول من خضب بالسواد فرعون لعنه الله وعن
ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال يكون في آخر
الزمان قوم يخضبون بالسواد كحواصل الحمام لا يريحون رائحة الجنة (4)
الثاني الخضاب بالصفرة والحمرة وهو جائز تلبيسا للشيب على الكفار في
الغزو والجهاد فإن لم يكن على هذه النية بل للتشبه بأهل الدين فهو مذموم
وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصفرة خضاب المسلمين والحمرة خضاب
المؤمنين (5) وكانوا يخضبون بالحناء للحمرة وبالخلوق والكتم للصفرة وخضب
بعض العلماء بالسواد لأجل الغزو وذلك لا بأس به إذا صحت النية ولم يكن فيه
هوى وشهوة
الثالث تبييضها بالكبريت استعجالا لإظهار علو السن توصلا إلى التوقير
وقبول الشهادة والتصديق بالرواية عن الشيوخ وترفعا عن الشباب وإظهارا لكثرة
العلم ظنا بأن كثرة الأيام تعطيه فضلا وهيهات فلا يزيد كبر السن للجاهل إلا
جهلا فالعلم ثمرة العقل وهي غريزة ولا يؤثر الشيب فيها ومن كانت غريزته
الحمق فطول المدة يؤكد حماقته وقد كان الشيوخ يقدمون الشباب PageV01P143
بالعلم
كان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقدم ابن عباس وهو حديث السن على أكابر
الصحابة ويسأله دونهم
وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ما آتى الله عز وجل عبدا علما إلا شابا
والخير كله في الشباب ثم تلا قوله عز وجل {قالوا سمعنا فتى يذكرهم يقال له
إبراهيم} وقوله تعالى {إنهم فتية آمنوا بربهم وزدناهم هدى} وقوله تعالى
{وآتيناه الحكم صبيا}  وكان أنس رضي الله عنه يقول قبض رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم وليس في رأسه ولحيته عشرون شعرة بيضاء فقيل له يا أبا حمزة فقد
أسن فقال لم يشنه الله بالشيب فقيل أهو شين فقال كلكم يكرهه (1) ويقال إن
يحيى بن أكثم ولي القضاء وهو ابن إحدى وعشرين سنة فقال له رجل في مجلسه
يريد أن يخجله بصغر سنه كم سن القاضي أيده الله فقال مثل سن عتاب بن أسيد
حين ولاه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إمارة مكة وقضاءها فأفحمه (2) وروي
عن مالك رحمه الله أنه قال قرأت في بعض الكتب لا تغرنكم اللحى فإن التيس له
لحية وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء إذا رأيت الرجل طويل القامة صغير الهامة عريض
اللحية فاقض عليه بالحمق ولو كان أمية بن عبد شمس وقال أيوب السختياني
أدركت الشيخ ابن ثمانين سنة يتبع الغلام يتعلم منه
وقال علي بن الحسين من سبق فيه العلم قبلك فهو إمامك فيه وإن كان أصغر
سنا منك وقيل لأبي عمرو بن العلاء أيحسن من الشيخ أن يتعلم من الصغير فقال
إن كان الجهل يقبح به فالتعلم يحسن به وقال يحيى بن معين لأحمد بن حنبل وقد
رآه يمشي خلف بغلة الشافعي يا أبا عبد الله تركت حديث سفيان بعلوه وتمشي
خلف بغلة هذا الفتى وتسمع منه فقال له أحمد لو عرفت لكنت تمشي من الجانب
الآخر إن علم سفيان إن فاتني بعلو أدركته بنزول وإن عقل هذا الشاب إن فاتني
لم أدركه بعلو ولا نزول
الرابع نتف بياضها استنكافا من الشيب وقد نهى عليه السلام عن نتف الشيب
وقال هو نور المؤمن (3) وهو في معنى الخضاب بالسواد وعلة الكراهية ما سبق
والشيب نور الله تعالى والرغبة عنه رغبة عن النور
الخامس نتفها أو نتف بعضها بحكم العبث والهوس وذلك مكروه ومشوه للخلقة
ونتف الفنيكين بدعة وهما جانبا العنفقة
شهد عند عمر بن عبد العزيز رجل كان ينتف فنيكيه فرد شهادته ورد عمر بن
الخطاب  رضي الله عنه وابن أبي ليلى قاضي المدينة شهادة من كان ينتف لحيته
وأما نتفها في أول النبات تشبها بالمرد فمن المنكرات الكبار فإن اللحية
زينة الرجال فإن لله سبحانه ملائكة يقسمون والذي زين بني آدم باللحى وهو من
تمام الخلق وبها يتميز الرجال عن النساء وقيل في غريب التأويل اللحية هي
المراد بقوله تعالى {يزيد في الخلق ما يشاء} قال أصحاب الأحنف بن قيس وددنا
أن نشتري للأحنف لحية ولو بعشرين ألفا وقال شريح القاضي وددت أن لي لحية
ولو بعشرة آلاف وكيف تكره اللحية وفيها تعظيم الرجل والنظر إليه بعين العلم
والوقار والرفع في المجالس وإقبال الوجوه إليه والتقد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ض-ب (kha-ḍa-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To dye, color, or stain; specifically the application of coloring agents to hair or cloth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The outward alteration of appearance; in the religious context, it pertains to the concealment or display of age and status, bearing on intention (niyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to physical dyeing; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the "dyeing" of faith or character, as in "the dye of Allah" (ṣibghat Allāh).
- Root: ش-ي-ب (shay-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Whiteness of hair; old age; the appearance of white hairs as a sign of advancing years.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A divinely ordained marker of human temporality; in the ḥadīth, described as "light" (nūr), signifying dignity and proximity to the afterlife.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical whitening of hair; metaphorical for the wisdom and reverence associated with age, which is not inherently tied to the physical sign.
- Root: ن-ت-ف (n-t-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pluck, pull out, or extract hair from the root.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): An act of altering the created form (taghyīr al-khalq); prohibited when done out of disdain for what Allah has decreed.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal action of plucking; metaphorically, a rejection of divine providence when motivated by vanity or shame.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "if the intention is sound") and exceptions to delineate the boundaries of permissibility (jawāz) versus blameworthiness (dhamm), requiring precise parsing of the protasis and apodosis to determine legal rulings.
chapters.translation:
I say: In the beard there are ten characteristics that are disliked (makrūh), and some are more severely disliked than others: dyeing it black, whitening it with sulfur, plucking it, plucking the white hairs from it, diminishing it, increasing it, combing it with affectation for the sake of ostentation (riyāʾ), leaving it unkempt to display asceticism (zuhd), gazing at its blackness with self-admiration for one's youth, and gazing at its whiteness with pride in advanced age, and dyeing it with red or yellow without the intention of resembling the righteous.

As for the first — namely, dyeing it black — it is prohibited, for the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «The best of your youth are those who resemble your elders, and the worst of your elders are those who resemble your youth.» The intended meaning of resembling the elders is in dignity (waqār), not in the whitening of hair. And he prohibited dyeing with black, saying: «It is the dye of the people of the Fire.» In another wording: «Dyeing with black is the dye of the disbelievers.» A man married during the caliphate of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) while dyeing his beard black; his dye faded and his whiteness appeared, so the woman's family brought him to ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), who annulled his marriage and struck him painfully, saying: "You deceived the people with youth and disguised your whiteness from them." It is said that the first to dye with black was Pharaoh — may Allah curse him. And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «There will come at the end of time a people who dye with black like the crops of pigeons; they will not smell the fragrance of Paradise.»

The second is dyeing with yellow and red, which is permissible as a disguise of whiteness against the disbelievers in raids and jihad. But if it is not with this intention, rather for resemblance to the people of religion, then it is blameworthy. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: «Yellow is the dye of the Muslims, and red is the dye of the believers.» They used to dye with henna for redness and with khilūq and katm for yellowness. Some scholars dyed with black for the sake of raids, and there is no harm in that if the intention is sound and there is no caprice or lust in it.

The third is whitening it with sulfur, hastening to display advanced age as a means to attain reverence, acceptance of testimony, credence in narrating from the elders, self-elevation above youth, and the display of abundant knowledge, supposing that the multitude of days bestows virtue upon one. Far from it! Old age only increases the ignorant in ignorance. For knowledge is the fruit of the intellect, which is an innate disposition (gharīzah), and whiteness of hair has no effect upon it. Whoever's innate disposition is foolishness, the length of time only reinforces his foolishness. The elders used to give precedence to the youth in knowledge. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) used to give precedence to Ibn ʿAbbās, who was of tender age, over the senior Companions, and would ask him rather than them. Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has never given a servant knowledge except in his youth, and all good is in youth." Then he recited the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {«They said: We heard a youth mentioning them, called Ibrāhīm»} and His saying, Exalted: {«Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance»} and His saying, Exalted: {«And We gave him judgment while a child»}. Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was taken, and there were not twenty white hairs in his head and beard." It was said to him: "O Abā Ḥamzah, he has aged." He said: "Allah did not disgrace him with whiteness." It was said: "Is it a disgrace?" He said: "All of you dislike it." It is said that Yaḥyā ibn Aktham was appointed to the judgeship at twenty-one years of age. A man in his assembly said to him, intending to shame him for his youth: "How old is the judge, may Allah support him?" He said: "The age of ʿAttāb ibn Asīd when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) appointed him to the governorship and judgeship of Mecca." Thus he silenced him. It is related from Mālik (may Allah have mercy on him) that he said: "I read in some books: 'Let not the beards deceive you, for the he-goat has a beard.'" Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "If you see a man tall of stature, small of head, and broad of beard, then judge him to be foolish, even if he were Umayyah ibn ʿAbd Shams." Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī said: "I reached an elder of eighty years who followed a young boy to learn from him." ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn said: "Whoever precedes you in knowledge is your imam in it, even if he is younger in age than you." It was said to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: "Is it proper for an elder to learn from a younger one?" He said: "If ignorance is disgraceful for him, then learning is becoming for him." Yaḥyā ibn Muʿīn said to Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, having seen him walking behind the mule of al-Shāfiʿī: "O Abā ʿAbdillāh, you have abandoned the elevated chain of Sufyān and walk behind the mule of this youth, listening to him?" Aḥmad said to him: "If you knew, you would walk on the other side. If the knowledge of Sufyān is lost to me in its elevation, I attain it in its descent; but if the intellect of this youth is lost to me, I cannot attain it by elevation or descent."

The fourth is plucking the white hairs out of disdain for grayness. The Prophet (peace be upon him) prohibited plucking white hairs and said: «It is the light of the believer.» It is in the same category as dyeing with black, and the cause of the dislike is what has preceded. Grayness is the light of Allah, Exalted, and aversion to it is aversion to the light.

The fifth is plucking the beard or part of it out of frivolity and foolishness. That is disliked and disfigures the natural form. Plucking the two side-tufts (al-finīkayn) — which are the two sides of the mustache — is an innovation (bidʿah). A man who plucked his two side-tufts testified before ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, and he rejected his testimony. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ibn Abī Laylā, the judge of Medina, rejected the testimony of one who plucked his beard. As for plucking it at the beginning of its growth to resemble beardless youths, that is among the grave abominations. For the beard is the adornment of men. Allah, Exalted, has angels who divide and distribute, and He who adorned the sons of Adam with beards — it is part of the perfection of creation, and by it men are distinguished from women. It is said in the interpretation of the unusual (gharīb al-taʾwīl) that the beard is what is meant by His saying, Exalted: {«He increases in creation what He wills»}. The companions of al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays said: "We wish we could buy a beard for al-Aḥnaf, even for twenty thousand." Shurayḥ the judge said: "I wish I had a beard, even for ten thousand." How can the beard be disliked, when in it lies the reverence of a man, the gazing upon him with the eye of knowledge and dignity, his elevation in assemblies, the turning of faces toward him, his precedence over the group, and the protection of his honor — for whoever insults a man with a beard alludes to his beard? It has been said that the people of Paradise are beardless youths, except Hārūn, the brother of Moses (peace be upon them both), for he has a beard reaching to his navel, as a particular distinction and honor for him.

The sixth is trimming it in layers, strand upon strand, like the tail feathers, for the adornment of women and affectation. Kaʿb said: "There will be at the end of time a people who trim their beards like the tail of a pigeon and curve their sandals like sickles; those have no share (khalāq) [in the Hereafter]."

The seventh is increasing it, namely, adding to the hair of the two cheeks from the temples — which is hair of the head — until it passes the jawbone and reaches the middle of the cheek. This deviates from the appearance of the people of righteousness.

The eighth is combing it for the sake of people. Bishr said: "In the beard there are two partners: combing it for the sake of people, and leaving it tangled to display asceticism."

The ninth and tenth are gazing at its blackness or its whiteness with the eye of self-admiration (ʿujb). That is blameworthy in all parts of the body, indeed in all character traits and actions, as will be explained later.

This, then, is what we intended to mention of the types of adornment and cleanliness. From three hadiths, there are obtained twelve characteristics of the bodily practices (sunan al-jasad): five pertain to the head — namely, parting the hair of the head, rinsing the mouth (maḍmaḍah), snuffing water into the nose (istinshāq), trimming the mustache, and using the toothstick (siwāk); three pertain to the hand and foot — namely, trimming the nails, washing the finger joints (barājim), and cleaning the knuckles (rawājib); and four pertain to the body — namely, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic region (istihdād), circumcision (khitān), and cleansing with water after relieving oneself (istinjāʾ). The reports have come down concerning all of this collectively. And since the purpose of this book is to address the outward purification (ṭahārah ẓāhirah) rather than the inward, let us confine ourselves to this. Let it be verified that the inward impurities and filths from which one must cleanse are too numerous to be counted. Their detailed exposition will come in the Quarter of the Destroyers (rubʿ al-muhlikāt), along with the definition of the ways to remove them and purify the heart from them, if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

The Book of the Secrets of Purification is completed, by the praise of Allah, Exalted, and His assistance. It will be followed, if Allah, Exalted, wills, by the Book of the Secrets of Prayer. And praise be to Allah alone, and blessings upon our master Muḥammad, and upon every chosen servant.

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
الحمد لله الذي غمر العباد بلطائفه وعمر قلوبهم بأنوار الدين ووظائفه
التي تنزل عن عرش الجلال إلى السماء الدنيا من درجات الرحمة إحدى عواطفه
فارق الملوك مع التفرد بالجلال والكبرياء بترغيب الخلق في السؤال والدعاء
فقال هل من داع فأستجيب له وهل من مستغفر فأغفر له وباين السلاطين بفتح
الباب ورفع الحجاب فرخص للعباد في المناجاة بالصلوات كيفما تقلبت بهم
الحالات في الجماعات والخلوات ولم يقتصر على الرخصة بل تلطف بالترغيب
والدعوة وغيره من ضعفاء الملوك لا يسمح بالخلوة إلا بعد تقديم الهدية
والرشوة فسبحانه ما أعظم شأنه وأقوى سلطانه وأتم لطفه وأعم إحسانه والصلاة
على محمد نبيه المصطفى ووليه المجتبى وعلى آله وأصحابه مفاتيح الهدى
ومصابيح الدجى وسلم تسليما
أما بعد فإن الصلاة عماد الدين وعصام اليقين ورأس القربات وغرة الطاعات
وقد استقصينا في فن الفقه في بسيط المذهب ووسيطه ووجيزه أصولها وفروعها
صارفين جمام العناية إلى تفاريعها النادرة
ووقائعها الشاذة لتكون خزانة للمفتي منها يستمد ومعولا له إليها يفزع
ويرجع
ونحن الآن PageV01P145
في هذا الكتاب نقتصر على ما لا بد للمريد منه من أعمالها الظاهرة
وأسرارها الباطنة وكاشفون من دقائق معانيها الخفية في معاني الخشوع
والإخلاص والنية ما لم تجر العادة بذكره في فن الفقه ومرتبون الكتاب على
سبعة أبواب
الباب الأول في فضائل الصلاة
الباب الثاني في تفضيل الأعمال الظاهرة من الصلاة
الباب الثالث في تفضيل الأعمال الباطنة منها
الباب الرابع في الإمامة والقدوة
الباب الخامس في صلاة الجمعة وأدابها
الباب السادس في مسائل متفرقة تعم بها  البلوى يحتاج المريد إلى معرفتها
الباب السابع في التطوعات وغيرها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of supplication, blessing, and the act of devotional prayer; the second root form (ṣallā) denotes the specific ritual prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ṣalāh signifies the comprehensive act of worship uniting bodily humility (khushūʿ) and spiritual presence (ḥuḍūr), as the "pillar" (ʿimād) of faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "bending" or "inclining" toward God; metaphorically extended to the entire ritual prayer as the supreme act of intimate communion (munājāh).
- Root: خ-ش-و (kh-sh-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of fear, awe, and trembling before majesty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, khushūʿ is the inward state of reverential awe that manifests outwardly in stillness and humility during prayer—distinct from mere bodily composure.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is the physical lowering of the gaze and voice; metaphorical denotes the heart's submission before divine grandeur.
- Root: ن-و-ي (n-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of intention, purpose, and resolve.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Niyyah is the inward orientation (qaṣd) that distinguishes an act of worship from mere habit; it is the soul's pivot for sincerity (ikhlāṣ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is the aim of the heart; metaphorically, it is the "seed" from which the tree of valid worship grows.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Inchoative Predication (al-ibtidāʾ wa al-khabar) — The opening doxology employs nominal sentences (jumal ismiyyah) to establish eternal, stable attributes of God (e.g., "al-ḥamdu lillāh"), contrasting with verbal sentences for contingent acts, thereby signaling ontological priority.
chapters.translation:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to God, who has overwhelmed His servants with His subtle kindnesses and filled their hearts with the lights of religion and its ordinances—which descend from the throne of majesty to the lowest heaven as one of the outpourings of His mercy. He has distinguished Himself from kings, despite His unique possession of majesty and grandeur, by encouraging creation to ask and supplicate, saying: {«Is there any caller that I may answer him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness that I may forgive him?»} And He has set Himself apart from sovereigns by opening the door and lifting the veil, granting His servants license for intimate communion (munājāh) through prayers, in whatever states they may turn about—whether in congregations or in solitude. Nor did He stop at mere permission, but He graciously added encouragement and invitation. The weak among kings do not permit private audience except after the presentation of gifts and bribes—glory be to Him! How great is His affair, how mighty His dominion, how complete His gentleness, how all-encompassing His beneficence!

And blessings upon Muhammad, His chosen Prophet and elect friend, and upon his family and companions—keys of guidance and lamps of darkness—and abundant peace.

To proceed: Know that prayer (ṣalāh) is the pillar of religion (ʿimād al-dīn), the bond of certainty (ʿiṣām al-yaqīn), the foremost of acts of nearness, and the brightest ornament of obedience. We have already exhaustively treated, in the jurisprudence (fiqh) of the school—in its expansive, intermediate, and concise compendia—its principles and branches, directing the fullness of our attention to its rare subdivisions and anomalous cases, so that it might serve as a treasury from which the mufti draws, a support to which he flees and returns.

Now, in this present book, we confine ourselves to what is indispensable for the seeker (murīd) concerning its outward acts and inward mysteries. We shall unveil, from the subtle meanings hidden within the realities of humility (khushūʿ), sincerity (ikhlāṣ), and intention (niyyah), that which custom has not been wont to mention in the art of jurisprudence. And we have arranged the book into seven chapters:

Chapter One: On the Virtues of Prayer.
Chapter Two: On the Excellence of the Outward Acts of Prayer.
Chapter Three: On the Excellence of the Inward Acts Thereof.
Chapter Four: On the Imamate and Following the Leader.
Chapter Five: On the Friday Prayer and Its Etiquettes.
Chapter Six: On Miscellaneous Matters of Widespread Affliction That the Seeker Needs to Know.
Chapter Seven: On Supererogatory Prayers and Other Matters.

chapters.title_en: The First Chapter on the Virtues of Prayer, Prostration, Congregation, the Call to Prayer, and Other Matters
chapters.arabic_text: || الباب الأول في فضائل الصلاة السجود والجماعة والأذان وغيرها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ض-ل (faḍl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus, or superiority; a quality that elevates one thing above another in merit or rank.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, faḍl denotes divine grace or supererogatory merit (faḍīlah) that accrues to acts of worship beyond the obligatory minimum.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "increase" (ziyādah); metaphorically, it signifies moral excellence and religious virtue, not mere quantitative addition.
- Root: ص-ل-و (ṣalāh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning "to supplicate" (duʿāʾ) or "to incline/bend" (mil); also linked to the "second" (muṣallī) in horse racing, implying following in sequence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ṣalāh is the specific ritual worship comprising standing, bowing, prostration, and recitation, established by divine command; its essence is humility (khushūʿ) and remembrance (dhikr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal root is supplication; in the Sharīʿah, it is a technical term (ḥaqīqah sharʿiyyah) for the prescribed ritual, distinct from its lexical generality.
- Root: س-ج-د (sujūd)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lower oneself, to place the forehead on the ground; also used for trees bowing (sujūd al-shajar) in submission.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sujūd is the utmost expression of humility (tawāḍuʿ) and servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) before God; it is the physical culmination of prayer's spiritual state.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is physical prostration; metaphorically, it denotes total submission of the soul to divine will, as in {«وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ»} (Q. 16:49).
- Root: ج-م-ع (jamāʿah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, unite, or assemble; the opposite of dispersion (tafrīqah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Jamāʿah in ritual context is the congregational prayer performed collectively, symbolizing communal unity (ulfah) and mutual support in worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is physical gathering; metaphorically, it signifies the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the community and the spiritual bond formed through shared devotion.
- Root: أ-ذ-ن (adhan)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To listen, hear, or announce; the call to prayer is an announcement (iʿlām) that summons the faithful.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Adhan is the prescribed proclamation of the times of prayer, serving as a public declaration of God's oneness (tawḥīd) and the Prophet's mission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is "to inform" (iʿlām); in religious usage, it is the specific call (nidāʾ) that invites to salvation (falāḥ), as in {«حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاحِ»}.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The phrase "السجود والجماعة والأذان وغيرها" uses the coordinating conjunction (wāw al-ʿaṭf) to link nouns in a series, each governed by the genitive construction (iḍāfah) with "فضائل" (virtues of). The final "وغيرها" (and other matters) functions as a generalizing appositive, extending the enumeration beyond the specified items without altering the syntactic case (all in genitive, majrūr).
chapters.translation: I say: The first chapter concerns the virtues of prayer (ṣalāh), prostration (sujūd), congregational worship (jamāʿah), the call to prayer (adhan), and other related matters. Know that the merits of these acts are established by the Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the scholars (ijmāʿ), and their excellence is rooted in the divine command that elevates them above mere habitual actions. For prayer is the pillar of the religion (ʿimād al-dīn), prostration is the seal of humility before the Almighty, the congregation is the manifestation of unity in obedience, and the call to prayer is the herald that summons hearts to the remembrance of God. These virtues are not mere external forms but are intertwined with the inner realities (ḥaqāʾiq) that purify the soul and draw the servant nearer to his Lord.

chapters.title_en: The Excellence of the Call to Prayer (Faḍīlat al-Adhān)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| فضيلة الأذان

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة يوم القيامة على كثيب من مسك أسود لا
يهولهم حساب ولا ينالهم فزع حتى يفرغ مما بين الناس رجل قرأ القرآن ابتغاء
وجه الله عز وجل وأم بقوم وهم به راضون ورجل أذن في مسجد ودعا إلى الله عز
وجل ابتغاء وجه الله ورجل ابتلي بالرزق في الدنيا فلم يشغله ذلك عن عمل
الآخرة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يسمع نداء المؤذن جن ولا إنس ولا
شيء إلا شهد له يوم القيامة (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يد الرحمن على رأس
المؤذن حتى يفرغ من أذانه (3) وقيل في تفسير قوله عز وجل ومن أحسن قولا ممن
دعا إلى الله وعمل صالحا نزلت في المؤذنين وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا
سمعتم النداء فقولوا مثل ما يقول المؤذن (4) وذلك مستحب إلا في الحيعلتين
فإنه يقول فيهما لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله وفي قوله قد قامت الصلاة أقامها
الله وأدامها ما دامت السموات والأرض وفي التثويب صدقت وبررت ونصحت وعند
الفراغ يقول اللهم رب هذه الدعوة التامة والصلاة القائمة آت محمدا الوسيلة
والفضيلة والدرجة الرفيعة وابعثه المقام المحمود الذي وعدته إنك لا تخلف
الميعاد
وقال سعيد بن المسيب من صلى بأرض فلاة صلى عن يمينه ملك وعن شماله ملك
فإن أذن وأقام صلى وراءه أمثال الجبال من الملائكة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ذ-ن (Adhana)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "announcing" or "proclaiming" by voice; the act of making something known audibly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious usage, the specific summons to congregational worship (ṣalāh), signifying a public declaration of divine oneness and invitation to obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "to inform" or "to make heard"; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to the ritual call, where the voice becomes a symbol of spiritual invitation.
- Root: ك-ث-ب (Kathiba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A raised mound or hill of sand; elevated ground.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatological context, a place of honor and distinction, elevated above the plain of gathering.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal topographical feature; metaphorically, a station of eminence and security on the Day of Resurrection.
- Root: ش-ه-د (Shahida)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bear witness, to testify, to be present.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony that establishes truth; in the hereafter, the act of creation bearing witness to the caller's fidelity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal presence and attestation; metaphorical sense of creation's very existence affirming the caller's sincerity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The construction "لا يسمع... إلا شهد" employs an implicit conditional where the negative universal is followed by an exceptive particle, governing the apodosis as a necessary consequence.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the excellence of the call to prayer (adhān) is established by prophetic traditions and the sayings of the early scholars (āthār).

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Three persons shall be on the Day of Resurrection upon a mound of black musk; neither will the reckoning terrify them, nor will fear reach them, until the judgment among mankind is completed: a man who recited the Quran seeking the Face of God, Mighty and Majestic, and led a people who were well-pleased with him; a man who called to prayer in a mosque and invited to God, Mighty and Majestic, seeking the Face of God; and a man who was tried with provision in this world, yet that did not distract him from the work of the hereafter."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "No jinn, no human, and no thing hears the call of the mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer) except that it bears witness for him on the Day of Resurrection."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "The Hand of the Merciful is upon the head of the mu'adhdhin until he finishes his call to prayer."

And it was said in the interpretation of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ قَوْلًا مِمَّنْ دَعَا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا»} ("And who is better in speech than one who invites to God and works righteousness") — that it was revealed concerning the mu'adhdhins.

And he, peace be upon him, said: "When you hear the call, say the like of what the mu'adhdhin says." This is recommended (mustaḥabb), except in the two hayʿalahs (the phrases "Come to prayer, come to success"), for in them one says: "There is no might and no power except with God." And in his saying "The prayer has been established" (qad qāmat al-ṣalāh), one says: "May God establish it and perpetuate it as long as the heavens and the earth endure." And in the tathwīb (the second call in the dawn prayer: "Prayer is better than sleep"), one says: "You have spoken truthfully, acted righteously, and advised sincerely." And upon finishing, one says: "O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad the means (al-wasīlah), the excellence, and the lofty rank, and raise him to the praiseworthy station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd) which You have promised him; verily, You do not fail in Your promise."

And Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said: "Whoever prays in an empty land, a king (angel) prays on his right and a king on his left; and if he calls to prayer and establishes it, angels like mountains pray behind him."

chapters.title_en: The Excellence of the Prescribed Prayer (Faḍīlat al-Maktūbah)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| فضيلة المكتوبة

قال الله تعالى إن الصلاة كانت على المؤمنين كتابا موقوتا وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم خمس صلوات كتبهن الله على العباد فمن جاء بهن ولم يضيع منهن شيئا
استخفافا بحقهن كان له عند الله عهد أن يدخله الجنة ومن لم يأت بهن فليس له
عند الله عهد إن شاء عذبه وإن شاء أدخله الجنة (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
مثل الصلوات الخمس كمثل نهر عذب غمر بباب أحدكم يقتحم فيه كل يوم خمس  مرات
فما ترون ذلك يبقي من درنه قالوا لا شيء قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
PageV01P146
فإن الصلوات الخمس تذهب الذنوب كما يذهب الماء الدرن (1) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم إن الصلوات كفارة لما بينهن ما اجتنبت الكبائر (2) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم بيننا وبين المنافقين شهود العتمة والصبح لا يستطيعونهما (3)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من لقي الله وهو مضيع للصلاة لم يعبأ الله بشيء من
حسناته (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة عماد الدين فمن تركها فقد هدم
الدين (5) وسئل صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الأعمال أفضل فقال الصلاة لمواقيتها
(6) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من حافظ على الخمس بإكمال طهورها ومواقيتها
كانت له نورا وبرهانا يوم القيامة ومن ضيعها حشر مع فرعون وهامان (7) وقال
صلى الله عليه وسلم مفتاح الجنة الصلاة (8) وقال ما افترض الله على خلقه
بعد التوحيد أحب إليه من الصلاة ولو كان شيء أحب إليه منها لتعبد به
ملائكته فمنهم راكع ومنهم ساجد ومنهم قائم وقاعد (9) وقال النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم من ترك صلاة متعمدا فقد كفر (10) أي قارب أن ينخلع عن الإيمان
بانحلال عروته وسقوط عماده كما يقال لمن قارب البلدة إنه بلغها ودخلها
