||| فضيلة الجمعة

اعلم أن هذا يوم عظيم عظم الله به الإسلام وخصص به المسلمين
قال الله تعالى {إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله
وذروا البيع} فحرم الاشتغال بأمور الدنيا وبكل صارف عن السعي إلى الجمعة
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله عز وجل فرض عليكم الجمعة في يومي هذا في
مقامي هذا (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من ترك الجمعة ثلاثا من غير عذر طبع
الله على قلبه (2) وفي لفظ آخر فقد نبذ الإسلام وراء ظهره (3) واختلف رجل
إلى ابن عباس يسأله عن رجل مات لم يكن يشهد جمعة ولا جماعة فقال في النار
فلم يزل يتردد إليه شهرا يسأله عن ذلك وهو يقول في النار وفي الخبر إن أهل
الكتابين أعطوا يوم الجمعة فاختلفوا فيه فصرفوا عنه وهدانا الله تعالى له
وأخره لهذه الأمة وجعله عيدا لهم فهم أولى الناس به سبقا وأهل الكتابين لهم
تبع (4) وفي حديث أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال أتاني جبريل
عليه السلام في كفه مرآة بيضاء وقال هذه الجمعة يفرضها عليك ربك لتكون لك
عيدا ولأمتك من بعدك قلت فما لنا فيها قال لكم فيها خير ساعة من دعا فيها
بخير قسم له أعطاه الله سبحانه إياه أو ليس له قسم ذخر له ما هو أعظم منه
أو تعوذ من شر مكتوب عليه إلا أعاذه الله عز وجل  من أعظم منه وهو سيد
الأيام عندنا ونحن ندعوه في الآخرة يوم المزيد قلت ولم قال إن ربك عز وجل
اتخذ في الجنة واديا أفيح من المسك أبيض فإذا كان يوم الجمعة نزل تعالى من
عليين على كرسيه فيتجلى لهم حتى ينظروا إلى وجهه الكريم (5) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم خير يوم طلعت عليه الشمس يوم الجمعة فيه خلق آدم عليه السلام
وفيه أدخل الجنة وفيه أهبط إلى الأرض وفيه تيب عليه وفيه مات وفيه تقوم
الساعة وهو عند الله يوم المزيد كذلك تسميه الملائكة في السماء وهو يوم
النظر إلى الله تعالى في الجنة (6) وفي الخبر إن لله عز وجل في كل جمعة
ستمائة ألف عتيق من النار (7) وفي حديث أنس رضي الله عنه أنه صلى الله عليه
وسلم PageV01P178
قال إذا سلمت الجمعة سلمت الأيام (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الجحيم
تسعر في كل يوم قبل الزوال عند استواء الشمس في كبد السماء فلا تصلوا في
هذه الساعة إلا يوم الجمعة فإنه صلاة كله وإن جهنم لا تسعر فيه (2) وقال
كعب إن الله عز وجل فضل من البلدان مكة ومن الشهور رمضان ومن الأيام الجمعة
ومن الليالي ليلة القدر ويقال إن الطير والهوام يلقى بعضها بعضا في يوم
الجمعة فتقول سلام سلام يوم صالح وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من مات يوم
الجمعة أو ليلة الجمعة كتب الله له أجر شهيد ووقي فتنة القبر // حديث من
مات يوم الجمعة كتب الله له أجر شهيد ووقي فتنة القبر أخرجه أبو نعيم في
الحلية من حديث جابر روى الزندي نحوه مختصرا من حديث عبد الله بن عمر وقال
غريب ليس إسناده بمتصل قلت وصله الترمذي الحكيم في النوادر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Gathering, assembling; the day of congregational assembly; the root denotes bringing together dispersed elements into unity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The day divinely designated for the communal assembly of Muslims for worship; carries the theological weight of collective obedience (ṭāʿah) versus individual dispersion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical gathering; metaphorically extended to the spiritual unity of the ummah in submission to the divine command.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Emphasis (Taʾkīd) — Repetition of the subject with intensifying particles (inna, qad) to establish certainty in the listener's mind regarding the sacred status of the day.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that this is a momentous day, one by which God magnified Islam and singled out the Muslims as its exclusive recipients.

God Most High said: {«When the call is proclaimed for the prayer on the day of Friday, hasten earnestly to the remembrance of God, and leave off business»} (Q 62:9). Thus He prohibited engagement in worldly affairs and every distraction that diverts one from hastening to the Friday prayer.

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Verily God, Mighty and Majestic, has made Friday obligatory upon you on this very day of mine, in this very station of mine."

He also said: "Whoever abandons Friday three times without excuse, God seals his heart." In another wording: "He has indeed cast Islam behind his back."

A man repeatedly came to Ibn ʿAbbās asking about a person who died without ever attending Friday prayer or congregational prayer. He replied: "He is in the Fire." The man kept returning to him for a month, asking the same question, and he kept answering: "He is in the Fire."

It is reported in the tradition that the People of the Two Books (Jews and Christians) were given Friday, but they differed concerning it, so they were turned away from it. God guided us to it, and deferred it for this ummah, making it a festival (ʿīd) for them. Thus they are the most deserving of it in precedence, while the People of the Two Books are their followers.

In the ḥadīth of Anas, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me with a white mirror in his hand and said: 'This is Friday, which your Lord makes obligatory upon you, so that it may be a festival for you and for your ummah after you.' I asked: 'What is there in it for us?' He replied: 'In it there is good for you: an hour in which whoever supplicates for good that is apportioned to him, God grants it to him; or if he has no apportioned share, it is stored up for him as something even greater. And whoever seeks refuge from an evil written upon him, God Most High protects him from something even greater than it. It is the master of days with us, and we call it in the Hereafter the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazīd).' I asked: 'Why is that?' He said: 'Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has taken in Paradise a wide valley of white musk. When Friday comes, He descends from ʿIlliyyīn upon His throne, and He manifests Himself to them until they gaze upon His noble Face.'"

The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said: "The best day upon which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam (peace be upon him) was created; on it he was admitted into Paradise; on it he was sent down to the earth; on it his repentance was accepted; on it he died; and on it the Hour will be established. It is, with God, the Day of Increase — thus do the angels name it in the heavens — and it is the day of gazing upon God Most High in Paradise."

It is reported that God Most High frees six hundred thousand souls from the Fire every Friday.

In the ḥadīth of Anas (may God be pleased with him), the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "When Friday is sound, all the days are sound."

He also said: "Verily, the Fire of Hell is kindled every day before noon, when the sun stands at the zenith of the sky. So do not pray at that hour — except on Friday, for it is all prayer, and Hell is not kindled on it."

Kaʿb said: "God Most High favored Mecca among lands, Ramaḍān among months, Friday among days, and the Night of Decree among nights."

It is said that the birds and creeping creatures meet one another on Friday and say: "Peace, peace — a blessed day."

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever dies on Friday or on the night of Friday, God writes for him the reward of a martyr and protects him from the trial of the grave."

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Conditions of the Friday Prayer (Jumuʿah)

||| بيان شروط الجمعة

اعلم أنها تشارك جميع الصلوات في الشروط وتتميز عنها بستة شروط
{الأول} الوقت فإن وقعت تسليمة الإمام في وقت العصر فاتت الجمعة وعليه أن
يتمها ظهرا أربعا والمسبوق إذا وقعت ركعته الأخيرة خارجا من الوقت ففيه
خلاف
الثاني المكان  فلا تصح في الصحاري والبراري وبين الخيام بل لا بد من بقعة
جامعة لأبنية لا تنقل يجمع أربعين ممن تلزمهم الجمعة والقرية فيه كالبلد
ولا يشترط فيه حضور السلطان ولا إذنه ولكن الأحب استئذانه
الثالث العدد فلا تنعقد بأقل من أربعين ذكورا مكلفين أحرارا مقيمين لا
يظعنون عنها شتاء ولا صيفا فإن انفضوا حتى نقص العدد إما في الخطبة أو في
الصلاة لم تصح الجمعة بل لا بد منهم من الأول إلى الآخر
الرابع الجماعة فلو صلى أربعون في قرية أو في بلد متفرقين لم تصح جمعتهم
ولكن المسبوق إذا أدرك الركعة الثانية جاز له الانفراد بالركعة الثانية
وإن لم يدرك ركوع الركعة الثانية اقتدى ونوى الظهر وإذا سلم الإمام تممها
ظهرا
الخامس أن لا تكون الجمعة مسبوقة بأخرى في ذلك البلد
فإن تعذر اجتماعهم في جامع واحد جاز في جامعين وثلاثة وأربعة بقدر الحاجة
وإن لم تكن حاجة فالصحيح الجمعة التي يقع بها التحريم أولا وإذا تحققت
الحاجة فالأفضل الصلاة خلف الأفضل من الإمامين فإن تساويا فالمسجد الأقدم
فإن تساويا ففي الأقرب ولكثرة الناس أيضا فضل يراعى
السادس الخطبتان فهما فريضتان والقيام فيهما فريضة والجلسة بينهما فريضة
وفي الأولى أربع فرائض التحميد وأقله الحمد لله
والثانية الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
والثالثة الوصية بتقوى الله سبحانه وتعالى
والرابعة قراءة آية من القرآن
وكذا فرائض الثانية أربعة إلا أنه يجب فيها الدعاء بدل القراءة
واستماع الخطبتين واجب من الأربعين
وأما السنن فإذا زالت الشمس وأذن المؤذن وجلس الإمام على المنبر انقطعت
الصلاة سوى التحية والكلام لا ينقطع إلا بافتتاح الخطبة
ويسلم الخطيب على الناس إذا أقبل عليهم بوجهه ويردون عليه السلام فإذا
فرغ المؤذن قام مقبلا على الناس بوجهه لا يلتفت يمينا ولا شمالا ويشغل يديه
بقائم السيف أو العنزة والمنبر كي لا يعبث بهما أو يضع إحداهما على الأخرى
ويخطب خطبتين بينهما جلسة خفيفة
ولا يستعمل غريب اللغة ولا يمطط ولا يتغنى
وتكون الخطبة قصيرة بليغة جامعة
ويستحب أن يقرأ آية في الثانية أيضا ولا يسلم من دخل والخطيب يخطب فإن
سلم لم يستحق جوابا والإشارة بالجواب حسن ولا يشمت العاطسين أيضا
هذه شروط الصحة
فأما شروط الوجوب فلا تجب الجمعة إلا على ذكر بالغ عاقل مسلم حر مقيم في
قرية تشتمل على أربعين جامعين PageV01P179
لهذه الصفات أو في قرية من سواد البلد يبلغها نداء البلد من طرف بابها
والأصوات ساكنة والمؤذن رفيع الصوت لقوله تعالى {إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم
الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع} ويرخص لهؤلاء في ترك الجمعة لعذر
المطر والوحل والفزع والمرض والتمريض إذا لم يكن للمريض قيم غيره
ثم يستحب لهم أعني أصحاب الأعذار تأخير الظهر إلى أن يفرغ الناس من
الجمعة فإن حضر الجمعة مريض أو مسافر أو عبد أو امرأة صحت جمعتهم وأجزأت عن
الظهر والله أعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ر-ط (sh-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mark, sign, or stipulation that delimits an act's validity; a binding condition tied to the essence of the ruling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, a sharṭ is that whose absence entails absence of the ruling, though its presence does not necessarily entail the ruling's presence—distinct from the cause (sabab).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes a physical sign (e.g., a banner); here it is metaphorical (majāz) for a legal stipulation that "flags" the act's validity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb) syntactically, mirroring the legal dependency of validity upon the stipulated conditions.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the Friday prayer (Jumuʿah) shares all the general conditions of the [other] prayers, but is distinguished from them by six specific conditions.

{The First} is the time. If the Imam's concluding salutation (taslīmah) falls within the time of the afternoon prayer (ʿAṣr), then the Friday prayer has been missed, and he must complete it as four units of the noon prayer (Ẓuhr). As for the one who is overtaken (masbūq)—if his final unit (rakʿah) falls outside the time, there is a divergence of opinion [among the scholars] concerning him.

{The Second} is the place. It is not valid in open plains, wildernesses, or among tents. Rather, there must be a single locale (buqʿah) that gathers permanent, non-portable structures, accommodating forty persons upon whom the Friday prayer is obligatory. A village in this regard is like a town. The presence of the Sultan or his permission is not a stipulated condition, though seeking his permission is preferable.

{The Third} is the number. It is not validly constituted with fewer than forty free, legally responsible (mukallaf) males, who are settled residents—not departing from it in winter or summer. If they disperse such that the number diminishes—whether during the sermon (khuṭbah) or during the prayer—the Friday prayer is not valid. Rather, [the full forty] must remain from the beginning to the end.

{The Fourth} is the congregation (jamāʿah). If forty [qualified persons] prayed in a village or town while scattered separately, their Friday prayer would not be valid. However, the one overtaken (masbūq)—if he catches the second unit—it is permissible for him to complete the second unit alone. And if he does not catch the bowing (rukūʿ) of the second unit, he follows the Imam [in the remainder] with the intention of the noon prayer (Ẓuhr); when the Imam gives the salutation, he completes it as Ẓuhr.

{The Fifth} is that the Friday prayer must not be preceded by another Friday prayer in that same town. If their gathering in a single congregational mosque becomes impracticable, then it is permissible [to hold it] in two, three, or four mosques, according to the need. If there is no need, then the correct [ruling] is that the Friday prayer [which is valid] is the one by which the opening takbīr (taḥrīmah) is first initiated. When the need is verified, then it is preferable to pray behind the more excellent of the two Imams. If they are equal, then [pray in] the more ancient mosque. If they are equal, then [pray in] the nearest one. The abundance of the people is also a merit that is to be taken into consideration.

{The Sixth} is the two sermons (khuṭbatān). They are two obligations (farīḍatān). Standing during them is an obligation. The sitting between them is an obligation. In the first sermon there are four obligations: (1) the praise of God (taḥmīd), the minimum of which is "Praise be to God" (al-ḥamdu lillāh); (2) the invocation of blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ; (3) the exhortation to the fear of God (taqwā)—Glorified and Exalted is He; and (4) the recitation of a verse from the Qurʾān. Likewise, the obligations of the second sermon are four, except that supplication (duʿāʾ) is required in place of the recitation. Listening to the two sermons is obligatory upon the forty.

As for the Sunnahs [of the Friday prayer]: when the sun has passed its zenith (zawāl), the muezzin gives the call (adhān), and the Imam sits upon the pulpit (minbar), [voluntary] prayer is cut off—except for the greeting of the mosque (taḥiyyah). Speech is not cut off except by the commencement of the sermon. The khaṭīb greets the people with salutation (salām) when he turns his face toward them, and they return the greeting. When the muezzin finishes, he stands facing the people with his face—not turning right or left—and occupies his hands with the shaft of the sword or the staff (ʿanazah) or the pulpit, so that he does not fidget with them, or he places one hand upon the other. He delivers two sermons with a brief sitting between them. He does not employ obscure language, nor does he draw out [his words] in a sing-song manner, nor does he chant melodiously. The sermon should be brief, eloquent, and comprehensive. It is recommended that he also recite a verse in the second sermon. Whoever enters while the khaṭīb is delivering the sermon should not greet [with salām]; if he does greet, he is not entitled to a response—though signaling a response with a gesture is commendable. Nor should he respond to sneezes [with the invocation of mercy] either.

These are the conditions of validity (shurūṭ al-ṣiḥḥah).

As for the conditions of obligation (shurūṭ al-wujūb): the Friday prayer is not obligatory except upon a male, adult, sane, free Muslim, settled in a village comprising forty persons who gather [for the prayer] with these very attributes—or in a village within the outlying districts (sawād) of a town, which the call of the town reaches from its gate-side, with voices stilled and the muezzin raising his voice—due to His saying, Exalted is He: {«إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله وذروا البيع»} ("When the call is proclaimed for the prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trading"). These [residents of outlying districts] are excused from attending the Friday prayer due to the excuse of rain, mud, fear, illness, or nursing the sick—if the patient has no caretaker other than him. Then it is recommended for these—I mean those with valid excuses—to delay the noon prayer (Ẓuhr) until the people have finished the Friday prayer. If a sick person, a traveler, a slave, or a woman attends the Friday prayer, their Friday prayer is valid and suffices them in place of the noon prayer. And God knows best.

chapters.title_en: The Etiquette of Friday (Jumuʿah) Arranged According to Customary Practice, Comprising Ten Principles
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان آداب الجمعة على ترتيب العادة وهي عشر جمل

{الأول} أن يستعد لها يوم الخميس عزما عليها واستقبالا لفضلها فيشتغل
بالدعاء والاستغفار والتسبيح بعد العصر يوم الخميس لأنها ساعة قوبلت
بالساعة المبهمة في يوم الجمعة
قال بعض السلف إن لله عز وجل فضلا سوى أرزاق العباد لا يعطى من ذلك الفضل
إلا من سأله عشية الخميس ويوم الجمعة ويغسل في هذا اليوم ثيابه ويبيضها
ويعد الطيب إن لم يكن عنده ويفرغ قلبه من الأشغال التي تمنعه من البكور إلى
الجمعة وينوي في هذه الليلة صوم يوم الجمعة فإن له فضلا وليكن مضموما إلى
يوم الخميس أو السبت لا مفردا فإنه مكروه ويشتغل بإحياء هذه الليلة بالصلاة
وختم القرآن فلها فضل كثير وينسحب عليها فضل يوم الجمعة
ويجامع أهله في هذه الليلة أو في يوم الجمعة فقد استحب ذلك قوم حملوا
عليه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم رحم الله من بكر وابتكر وغسل واغتسل (1) وهو
حمل الأهل على الغسل وقيل معناه غسل ثيابه فروي بالتخفيف واغتسل لجسده
وبهذا تتم آداب الاستقبال ويخرج من زمرة الغافلين الذين إذا أصبحوا قالوا
ما هذا اليوم  قال بعض السلف أوفى الناس نصيبا من الجمعة من انتظرها ورعاها
من الأمس وأخفهم نصيبا من إذا أصبح يقول أيش اليوم وكان بعضهم يبيت ليلة
الجمعة في الجامع لأجلها
الثاني إذا أصبح ابتدأ بالغسل بعد طلوع الفجر وإن كان لا يبكر فأقربه إلى
الرواح أحب ليكون أقرب عهدا بالنظافة فالغسل مستحب استحبابا مؤكدا وذهب بعض
العلماء إلى وجوبه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم غسل الجمعة واجب على كل محتلم
(2) والمشهور من حديث نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما من أتى الجمعة
فليغتسل (3) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من شهد الجمعة من الرجال والنساء
فليغتسل (4) وكان أهل المدينة إذا تساب المتسابان يقول أحدهما للآخر لأنت
أشر ممن لا يغتسل يوم الجمعة
وقال عمر لعثمان رضي الله عنهما لما دخل وهو يخطب أهذه الساعة منكرا عليه
ترك البكور فقال ما زدت بعد أن سمعت الأذان على أن توضأت وخرجت فقال
والوضوء أيضا وقد علمت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يأمرنا بالغسل
(5) وقد عرف جواز ترك الغسل بوضوء عثمان رضي الله تعالى عنه وبما روي أنه
صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من توضأ يوم الجمعة فبها ونعمت ومن اغتسل فالغسل
أفضل (6) ومن اغتسل للجنابة فليفض الماء على بدنه مرة أخرى PageV01P180
على نية غسل الجمعة فإن اكتفى بغسل واحد أجزأه وحصل له الفضل إذا نوى
كليهما ودخل غسل الجمعة في غسل الجنابة وقد دخل بعض الصحابة على ولده وقد
اغتسل فقال له أللجمعة فقال بل عن الجنابة فقال أعد غسلا ثانيا وروى الحديث
في غسل الجمعة على كل محتلم
وإنما أمره به لأنه لم يكن نواه
وكان لا يبعد أن يقال المقصود النظافة وقد حصلت دون النية ولكن هذا ينقدح
في الوضوء أيضا وقد جعل في الشرع قربة فلا بد من طلب فضلها
ومن اغتسل ثم أحدث توضأ ولم يبطل غسله والأحب أن يحترز عن ذلك
{الثالثة} الزينة وهي مستحبة في هذا اليوم وهي ثلاثة الكسوة والنظافة
وتطييب الرائحة
أما  النظافة فبالسواك وحلق الشعر وقلم الظفر وقص الشارب وسائر ما سبق في
كتاب الطهارة
قال ابن مسعود من قلم أظفاره يوم الجمعة أخرج الله عز وجل منه داء وأدخل
فيه شفاء فإن كان قد دخل الحمام في الخميس أو الأربعاء فقد حصل المقصود
فليتطيب في هذا اليوم بأطيب طيب عنده ليغلب بها الروائح الكريهة ويوصل بها
الروح والرائحة إلى مشام الحاضرين في جواره وأحب طيب الرجال ما ظهر ريحه
وخفي لونه وطيب النساء ما ظهر لونه وخفي ريحه (1) وروي ذلك في الأثر
وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه من نظف ثوبه قل همه ومن طاب ريحه زاد عقله
وأما الكسوة فأحبها البياض من الثياب إذ أحب الثياب إلى الله تعالى البيض
ولا يلبس ما فيه شهرة
ولبس السواد ليس من السنة ولا فيه فضل بل كره جماعة النظر إليه لأنه بدعة
محدثة بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والعمامة مستحبة في هذا اليوم
وروى واثلة بن الأسقع أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الله
وملائكته يصلون على أصحاب العمائم يوم الجمعة (2) فإن أكربه الحر فلا بأس
بنزعها قبل الصلاة وبعدها ولكن لا ينزع في وقت السعي من المنزل إلى الجمعة
ولا في وقت الصلاة ولا عند صعود الإمام المنبر وفي خطبته
الرابع البكور إلى الجامع ويستحب أن يقصد الجامع من فرسخين وثلاث وليبكر
ويدخل وقت البكور بطلوع الفجر وفضل البكور عظيم
وينبغي أن يكون في سعيه إلى الجمعة خاشعا متواضعا ناويا للاعتكاف في
المسجد إلى وقت الصلاة قاصدا للمبادرة إلى جواب نداء الله عز وجل إلى
الجمعة إياه والمسارعة إلى مغفرته ورضوانه وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من
راح إلى الجمعة في الساعة الأولى فكأنما قرب بدنة ومن راح في الساعة
الثانية فكأنما قرب بقرة ومن راح في الساعة الثالثة فكأنما قرب كبشا أقرن
ومن راح في الساعة الرابعة فكأنما أهدى دجاجة ومن راح في الساعة الخامسة
فكأنما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Gathering, assembling, bringing together; the day of assembly (yawm al-jumuʿah) derives its name from the congregation of the people for prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The communal assembly for worship, signifying the unity of the ummah in collective devotion; the Friday prayer is a divinely ordained institution of social-religious cohesion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical gathering; metaphorical extension denotes the spiritual convergence of hearts toward divine mercy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — Sequential clauses linked by fa- (then) to express ordered, cumulative actions, as in the ten-part structure of this section.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now for the exposition of the etiquettes of Friday, arranged according to customary practice, and these comprise ten principles.

**The First Principle:** That one prepare for it on Thursday, resolving upon it and anticipating its excellence. Thus, one occupies oneself with supplication (duʿāʾ), seeking forgiveness (istighfār), and glorification (tasbīḥ) after the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) on Thursday, for that hour corresponds to the indeterminate hour (al-sāʿah al-mubhamah) of Friday. Some of the predecessors (salaf) said: "Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has a bounty distinct from the provisions of His servants, and none is granted of that bounty except he who asks Him on the evening of Thursday and on the day of Friday." On this day, one washes his garments and whitens them, and prepares perfume if he does not possess it. He empties his heart of occupations that would prevent him from going early (bakūr) to the Friday prayer. He intends on this night to fast the day of Friday, for it possesses great merit; however, it should be joined to Thursday or Saturday, not observed alone, for that is disliked (makrūh). He occupies himself with enlivening this night through prayer and completing the recitation of the Qurʾān, for it has abundant merit, and the merit of Friday extends over it. He has intimate relations with his family on this night or on the day of Friday, for a group of scholars deemed this commendable (mustaḥabb), interpreting thereby the Prophet's saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«رحم الله من بكر وابتكر وغسل واغتسل»} — "May Allah have mercy on him who went early, and hastened, and washed, and bathed" — as meaning the washing of one's family, i.e., compelling them to bathe. It is also said the meaning is: he washed his garments — thus it is narrated with lightening (takhfīf) — and bathed his body. With this, the etiquettes of reception are completed, and one exits from the ranks of the heedless who, when morning comes, say: "What is this day?" Some of the predecessors said: "The most complete in portion of Friday is he who awaits it and observes it from yesterday; the least in portion is he who, upon waking, says: 'What day is it today?'" And some of them would spend the night of Friday in the congregational mosque for its sake.

**The Second Principle:** When morning comes, one begins with the bath (ghusl) after the break of dawn. Even if one does not go early, bringing it closer to the time of departure is more beloved, so that it is nearer in time to cleanliness. The bath is strongly recommended (mustaḥabb muʾakkad), and some scholars held it to be obligatory (wājib). The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«غسل الجمعة واجب على كل محتلم»} — "The Friday bath is obligatory upon every one who has reached puberty." The well-known narration from Nāfiʿ on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, states: {«من أتى الجمعة فليغتسل»} — "Whoever comes to the Friday prayer, let him bathe." And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«من شهد الجمعة من الرجال والنساء فليغتسل»} — "Whoever attends the Friday prayer, whether man or woman, let him bathe." The people of Medina, when two men reviled each other, one would say to the other: "You are more evil than one who does not bathe on Friday." ʿUmar said to ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he entered while he was delivering the sermon — censuring him for abandoning the early coming: "What is this hour?" ʿUthmān replied: "I did no more, after hearing the call to prayer (adhān), than perform the ablution (wuḍūʾ) and go out." ʿUmar said: "And the ablution as well? You know that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to command us to bathe." The permissibility of omitting the bath is known from ʿUthmān's ablution, may Allah be pleased with him, and from what is narrated that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«من توضأ يوم الجمعة فبها ونعمت ومن اغتسل فالغسل أفضل»} — "Whoever performs ablution on Friday, that is sufficient and excellent; and whoever bathes, the bath is superior." And whoever bathes for major impurity (janābah) should pour water over his body a second time with the intention of the Friday bath. If he suffices with a single bath, it avails him, and he obtains the merit if he intends both, the Friday bath being subsumed within the bath for janābah. Some of the Companions entered upon his son who had bathed and said to him: "Was it for Friday?" He replied: "Rather, for janābah." He said: "Repeat a second bath," and he narrated the hadith concerning the Friday bath being incumbent upon every one who has reached puberty. He only commanded him to repeat it because he had not intended it. It would not be far-fetched to say that the purpose is cleanliness, and this has been attained without intention; but this consideration arises also regarding ablution, yet it has been made an act of devotion (qurbah) in the Sacred Law, so one must seek its merit. Whoever bathes and then experiences an event requiring ablution performs ablution, and his bath is not nullified; yet it is more beloved to guard against that.

**The Third Principle:** Adornment (zīnah), which is commendable on this day, comprising three things: attire, cleanliness, and perfuming the scent. As for cleanliness, it is through the tooth-stick (siwāk), shaving the hair, trimming the nails, clipping the moustache, and all that has preceded in the Book of Purity (Kitāb al-Ṭahārah). Ibn Masʿūd said: "Whoever trims his nails on Friday, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, expels from him an ailment and introduces into him a healing." If one has entered the bathhouse on Thursday or Wednesday, the purpose has been attained. Let him perfume himself on this day with the finest perfume he possesses, to overcome foul odors and to convey the spirit and fragrance to the nostrils of those present in his vicinity. The most beloved perfume of men is that whose scent is apparent and whose color is hidden; the perfume of women is that whose color is apparent and whose scent is hidden — this is narrated in the tradition. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Whoever cleanses his garment, his worry diminishes; whoever perfumes his scent, his intellect increases." As for attire, the most beloved is white clothing, for the most beloved garments to Allah, Exalted is He, are the white. One should not wear that which is ostentatious (shuhrah). Wearing black is not from the Sunnah, nor does it possess merit; rather, a group deemed looking upon it disliked, for it is an innovation (bidʿah) introduced after the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The turban (ʿimāmah) is commendable on this day. Wāthilah ibn al-Asqaʿ narrated that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«إن الله وملائكته يصلون على أصحاب العمائم يوم الجمعة»} — "Verily, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the wearers of turbans on Friday." If the heat distresses him, there is no harm in removing it before and after the prayer; but he should not remove it during the time of proceeding from his house to the Friday prayer, nor during the prayer itself, nor when the imam ascends the pulpit (minbar) and during his sermon.

**The Fourth Principle:** Going early (bakūr) to the congregational mosque. It is commendable to set out for the mosque from a distance of two or three leagues (farsakh), and to go early. The time of going early begins with the break of dawn, and the merit of going early is immense. One should be, in his proceeding to the Friday prayer, humble (khāshiʿ), submissive, intending seclusion (iʿtikāf) in the mosque until the time of prayer, aiming to hasten in response to the call of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to the Friday prayer, and to race toward His forgiveness and good pleasure. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«من راح إلى الجمعة في الساعة الأولى فكأنما قرب بدنة ومن راح في الساعة الثانية فكأنما قرب بقرة ومن راح في الساعة الثالثة فكأنما قرب كبشا أقرن ومن راح في الساعة الرابعة فكأنما أهدى دجاجة ومن راح في الساعة الخامسة فكأنما أهدى بيضة فإذا خرج الإمام طويت الصحف ورفعت الأقلام واجتمعت الملائكة عند المنبر يستمعون الذكر فمن جاء بعد ذلك فأنما جاء لحق الصلاة ليس له من الفضل شيء»} — "Whoever goes to the Friday prayer in the first hour, it is as if he offered a she-camel; whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he offered a cow; whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he offered a horned ram; whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he offered a hen; whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he offered an egg. When the imam comes out, the scrolls are folded, the pens are lifted, and the angels gather at the pulpit listening to the remembrance. Whoever comes after that comes only for the right of the prayer, having no share of the merit." The first hour is at sunrise, the second until its rising high, the third until its spreading when the feet burn upon the ground, and the fourth and fifth after the forenoon (ḍuḥā) until the zenith (zawāl); its merit is little, and the time of the zenith is the right of the prayer with no merit therein. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«ثلاث لو يعلم الناس ما فيهن لركضوا ركض الإبل في طلبهن الأذان والصف الأول والغدو إلى الجمعة»} — "Three things, if people knew what is in them, they would gallop like camels in seeking them: the call to prayer, the first row, and going early to the Friday prayer." Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The most excellent of them is going early to the Friday prayer." In the report: {«إذا كان يوم الجمعة قعدت الملائكة على أبواب المساجد بأيديهم صحف من فضة وأقلام من ذهب يكتبون الأول فالأول على مراتبهم»} — "When it is Friday, the angels sit at the gates of the mosques, in their hands scrolls of silver and pens of gold, writing down the first and the next in their ranks." And it has come in the report: {«إن الملائكة يتفقدون الرجل إذا تأخر عن وقته يوم الجمعة فيسأل بعضهم بعضا عنه ما فعل فلان وما الذي أخره عن وقته فيقولون اللهم إن كان أخره فقر فأغنه وإن كان أخره مرض فاشفه وإن كان أخره شغل ففرغه لعبادتك وإن كان أخره لهو فأقبل بقلبه إلى طاعتك»} — "The angels check on a man when he is delayed from his time on Friday, asking one another about him: 'What has happened to so-and-so, and what has delayed him from his time?' They say: 'O Allah, if poverty delayed him, enrich him; if illness delayed him, cure him; if occupation delayed him, free him for Your worship; if amusement delayed him, turn his heart toward Your obedience.'" In the first century, one would see before dawn and after the break of dawn the roads filled with people walking in the streets, crowding toward the congregational mosque as on the days of the two festivals (ʿīd), until this practice became extinct. It was said: "The first innovation (bidʿah) to occur in Islam was the abandonment of going early to the congregational mosque." How should Muslims not feel shame before the Jews and Christians, who go early to their synagogues and churches on Saturday and Sunday? And the seekers of this world — how they hasten early to the courtyards of the markets for selling, buying, and profit! Why then do the seekers of the Hereafter not race them? It is said that people will be in their proximity when gazing upon the Face of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, according to the measure of their going early to the Friday prayer. Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, entered the mosque early and saw three men who had preceded him in going early; he was grieved at that and began saying to himself, reproaching himself: "A fourth of four — and what is a fourth of four in going early? It is not far."

**The Fifth Principle:** Concerning the manner of entering. One should not step over the necks of the people (takhṭī al-riqāb), nor pass between their hands. Going early facilitates this for him, for a severe threat has been reported regarding stepping over necks — that he will be made a bridge on the Day of Resurrection over which people will step. Ibn Jurayj narrated, as a mursal report, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while delivering the sermon on Friday, saw a man stepping over the necks of the people until he advanced and sat down. When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished his prayer, he intercepted the man until he met him and said: "O so-and-so, what prevented you from gathering with us today?" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, I did gather with you." The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Did we not see you stepping over the necks of the people?" — indicating thereby that his deed had been rendered void. In a connected (musnad) hadith, he said: {«ما منعك أن تصلي معنا قال أو لم ترني يا رسول الله فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم رأيتك تأنيت وآذيت»} — "What prevented you from praying with us?" He said: "Did you not see me, O Messenger of Allah?" He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "I saw you delaying and harming" — that is, you delayed in going early and harmed those present. Whenever the first row is left vacant and empty, he may step over the necks of the people, for they have squandered their right and abandoned the place of excellence. Al-Ḥasan said: "Step over the necks of those who sit at the gates of the congregational mosques on Friday, for they have no sanctity." If there is none in the mosque except one who is praying, one should not greet him with salām, for it is an imposition of a response in an inappropriate place.

**The Sixth Principle:** That one not pass between the hands of the people, and that he sit wherever he is, near a pillar (usṭuwānah) or a wall, so that they do not pass between his hands — I mean, between the hands of the one praying — for that does not nullify the prayer but is prohibited. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«لأن يقف أربعين عاما خير له من أن يمر بين يدي المصلي»} — "That a man should stand for forty years is better for him than to pass between the hands of the one praying." And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«لأن يكون الرجل رمادا أو رميما تذروه الرياح خير من أن يمر بين يدي المصلي»} — "That a man should be ashes or decayed bones scattered by the winds is better than to pass between the hands of the one praying." It has been narrated in another hadith concerning the passer and the one praying — where he prayed on the road or fell short in repelling — that he said: {«لو يعلم المار بين يدي المصلى والمصلي ما عليهما في ذلك لكان أن يقف أربعين سنة خيرا له من أن يمر بين يديه»} — "If the passer between the hands of the one praying and the one praying knew what is upon them in that, standing for forty years would be better for him than to pass between his hands." The pillar, the wall, and the spread prayer-rug constitute a boundary (ḥadd) for the one praying; whoever crosses it should be repelled. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«ليدفعه فإن أبى فليدفعه فإن أبى فليقاتله فإنه شيطان»} — "Let him repel him; if he refuses, let him repel him; if he refuses, let him fight him, for he is a devil." Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, would repel whoever passed between his hands until he threw him down; sometimes the man would cling to him and complain against him to Marwān, and he would inform him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had commanded him to do so. If he finds no pillar, let him set up before him something of the length of a cubit (dhirāʿ), to serve as a marker of the boundary.

**The Seventh Principle:** That he seek the first row, for its merit is great, as we have narrated. In the hadith: {«من غسل واغتسل وبكر وابتكر ودنا من الإمام واستمع كان ذلك له كفارة لما بين الجمعتين وزيادة ثلاثة أيام»} — "Whoever washes and bathes, goes early and hastens, draws near to the imam and listens, that will be for him an expiation for what is between the two Fridays and an addition of three days." In another wording: {«غفر الله له إلى الجمعة الأخرى»} — "Allah will forgive him until the next Friday." And in some versions it is conditioned: {«ولم يتخط رقاب الناس»} — "and he did not step over the necks of the people." In seeking the first row, one should not neglect three matters. **First:** If he sees near the preacher (khaṭīb) an objectionable thing (munkar) that he is unable to change — such as the imam or another wearing silk, or praying in heavy, distracting armor, or gilded weaponry, or other such things requiring disapproval (inkār) — then staying back is safer for him and more conducive to the composure of his heart. A group of scholars did this, seeking safety. It was said to Bishr ibn al-Ḥārith: "We see you going early yet praying in the last rows." He said: "What is sought is the proximity of hearts, not the proximity of bodies" — indicating thereby that this is nearer to the safety of his heart. Sufyān al-Thawrī looked at Shuʿayb ibn Ḥarb near the pulpit, listening to the sermon of Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr; when he finished the prayer, he said: "Your proximity to this man preoccupied my heart. Are you secure from hearing a word that obliges you to disapprove, yet you do not rise to it?" Then he mentioned what they had introduced of wearing black, and said: "O Abū ʿAbdillāh, is it not in the report: {«ادن واستمع»} — 'Draw near and listen'?" He said: "Woe to you! That is for the rightly-guided, well-directed caliphs. As for these, the farther you are from them and the less you look upon them, the nearer you are to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Saʿīd ibn ʿĀmir said: "I prayed beside Abū al-Dardāʾ, and he kept moving back in the rows until we were in the last row. When we finished praying, I said to him: 'Is it not said that the best of rows is the first?' He said: 'We know that, except that this community is shown mercy and is looked upon among the communities; for when Allah, Exalted is He, looks upon a servant in prayer, He forgives him and those behind him of the people. I only moved back hoping that Allah would forgive me through one of them upon whom He looks.'" Some narrators related that he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say that." Whoever moves back with this intention, as a preference and a display of good character, there is no harm in it. And at this point it is said: "Deeds are but by intentions." **Second:** If the maqṣūrah (the enclosed royal compartment) is not reserved before the preacher and cut off from the mosque for the rulers, then the first row is beloved; otherwise, some scholars disliked entering the maqṣūrah. Al-Ḥasan and Bakr al-Muzanī would not pray in the maqṣūrah, holding that it was reserved for the rulers and was an innovation introduced after the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the mosques, whereas the mosque is open to all people, and this had been appropriated in opposition to the caliphate. Anas ibn Mālik and ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn prayed in the maqṣūrah and did not deem it disliked, seeking proximity. Perhaps the dislike is specific to the state of reservation and prohibition; as for the mere maqṣūrah, when there is no prohibition, no dislike exists. **Third:** The pulpit cuts off some of the rows; the first row is only the single continuous one in the courtyard of the pulpit, while what is on its two sides is cut off. Al-Thawrī used to say: "The first row is that which extends before the pulpit," and this is sound because it is continuous and because the one sitting therein faces the preacher and hears from him. It is not far-fetched to say that the nearest to the qiblah is the first row, without regard to this consideration. Prayer in the markets and open courtyards outside the mosque is disliked. Some of the Companions would strike people and make them stand up from the open courtyards.

**The Eighth Principle:** That one cease the prayer when the imam comes out, and cease speech as well; rather, he occupies himself with responding to the muʾadhdhin, then with listening to the sermon. Some of the common folk have adopted the custom of prostrating when the muʾadhdhins stand up, but no basis for this is established in any tradition (athar) or report (khabar). However, if it coincides with the prostration of recitation (sujūd al-tilāwah), there is no harm in it as supplication, for it is a virtuous time. One does not rule the prohibition of this prostration, for there is no cause for its prohibition. It has been narrated from ʿAlī and ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they said: "Whoever listens and remains silent has two rewards; whoever does not listen and remains silent has one reward; whoever listens and engages in idle talk (laghā) bears two sins; whoever does not listen and engages in idle talk bears one sin." He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«من قال لصاحبه والإمام يخطب أنصت أو مه فقد لغا ومن لغا والإمام يخطب فلا جمعة له»} — "Whoever says to his companion while the imam is delivering the sermon, 'Be silent' or 'Hush,' has engaged in idle talk; and whoever engages in idle talk while the imam is delivering the sermon has no Friday [reward] for him." This indicates that silencing should be by gesture or by casting a pebble, not by speech. In the hadith of Abū Dharr, when he asked Ubayy while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon, "When was this chapter (sūrah) revealed?" — he gestured to him to be silent. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, descended, Ubayy said to him: "Go, for you have no Friday [reward]." Abū Dharr complained of that to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: {«صدق أبي»} — "Ubayy has spoken the truth." Even if one is far from the imam, he should not speak of knowledge or anything else; rather, he should remain silent, for all of that creeps and leads to murmuring until it reaches the listeners. He should not sit in a circle of those who speak. Whoever is unable to listen due to distance should remain silent, for that is what is commendable. And if prayer is disliked during the time of the imam's sermon, speech is even more deserving of dislike. ʿAlī, may Allah honor his face, said: "Prayer is disliked in four hours: after dawn, after the afternoon prayer, at midday, and during prayer while the imam is delivering the sermon."

**The Ninth Principle:** That one observe in the Friday prayer the conditions we have mentioned regarding other prayers. When he hears the imam's recitation, he recites nothing but the Fātiḥah. When he finishes the Friday prayer, he recites "Praise be to Allah" (al-ḥamdu lillāh) seven times before speaking, and "Say: He is Allah, the One" (Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad) and the two refuge-seeking chapters (al-Muʿawwidhatān) seven times each. Some of the predecessors narrated that whoever does this is protected from one Friday to the next, and it is a safeguard for him against the devil. It is commendable to say after the Friday prayer: "O Allah, O Rich, O Praiseworthy, O Beginner, O Restorer, O Merciful, O Loving — enrich me with Your lawful provision (ḥalāl) rather than Your forbidden (ḥarām), and with Your bounty rather than anyone other than You." It is said that whoever persists in this supplication, Allah, Glorified is He, enriches him from His creation and provides for him from whence he does not reckon. Then he prays after the Friday prayer six units (rakʿāt), for Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, narrated that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray two units after the Friday prayer; Abū Hurayrah narrated four; and ʿAlī and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them, narrated six. All are sound, pertaining to different circumstances, and the most complete is the most excellent.

**The Tenth Principle:** That one remain in the mosque until he prays the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr); if he remains until sunset (maghrib), that is even more excellent. It is said: "Whoever prays the afternoon prayer in the congregational mosque has the reward of the pilgrimage (ḥajj); whoever prays the sunset prayer therein has the reward of a pilgrimage and an ʿumrah." If he does not feel secure from ostentation (taṣabbuʿ) and the intrusion of harm upon him through people's gaze upon his seclusion, or if he fears plunging into what does not concern him, then returning to his house is more excellent, remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reflecting upon His graces, thanking Allah, Exalted is He, for His success, fearing his own shortcoming, and watching over his heart and tongue until sunset, so that the noble hour does not escape him. One should not speak in the congregational mosque or other mosques of worldly matters. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«يأتي على الناس زمان يكون حديثهم في مساجدهم أمر دنياهم ليس لله تعالى فيهم حاجة فلا تجالسوهم»} — "A time will come upon people when their discourse in their mosques will be the affairs of their worldly life; Allah, Exalted is He, has no need of them, so do not sit with them."

||| بيان الآداب والسنن الخارجة عن الترتيب السابق الذي يعم جميع النهار

وهي سبعة أمور
الأول: أن يحضر مجالس العلم بكرة أو بعد العصر ولا يحضر مجالس القصاص فلا
خير في كلامهم
ولا ينبغي أن يخلو المريد في جميع يوم الجمعة عن الخيرات والدعوات حتى
توافيه الساعة الشريفة وهو في خير ولا ينبغي أن يحضر الحلق قبل الصلاة وروى
عبد الله بن عمر رضي الله عنهما إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن التحلق
يوم الجمعة قبل الصلاة (2)
إلا أن يكون عالما بالله يذكر بأيام الله ويفقه في دين الله يتكلم في
الجامع بالغداة فيجلس إليه فيكون جامعا بين البكور وبين الاستماع واستماع
العلم النافع في الآخرة أفضل من اشتغاله بالنوافل فقد روى أبو ذر إن حضور
مجلس علم أفضل من صلاة ألف ركعة (3)
قال أنس بن مالك في قوله تعالى فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض
وابتغوا من فضل الله أما إنه ليس بطلب دنيا لكن عيادة مريض وشهود جنازة
وتعلم علم وزيارة أخ في الله عز وجل
وقد سمى الله عز وجل العلم فضلا في مواضع قال تعالى وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم
وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما وقال تعالى ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا يعني العلم
فتعلم العلم في هذا اليوم وتعليمه من أفضل القربات
والصلاة أفضل من مجالس القصاص إذ كانوا يرونه بدعة ويخرجون القصاص من
الجامع بكر ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما إلى مجلسه في  المسجد الجامع فإذا قاص في
موضعه فقال قم عن مجلسي فقال لا أقوم وقد جلست وسبقتك إليه فأرسل ابن عمر
إلى صاحب الشرطة فأقامه، فلو كان ذلك من السنة لما جازت إقامته فقد قال صلى
الله عليه وسلم لا يقيمن أحدكم أخاه من مجلسه ثم يجلس فيه ولكن تفسحوا
وتوسعوا (4)
وكان ابن عمر إذا قام الرجل له من مجلسه لم يجلس فيه حتى يعود إليه
وروى أن قاصا كان يجلس بفناء حجرة عائشة رضي الله عنها فأرسلت إلى ابن
عمر إن هذا قد آذاني بقصصه وشغلني عن سبحتي فضربه ابن عمر حتى كسر عصاه على
ظهره ثم طرده
الثاني: أن يكون حسن المراقبة للساعة الشريفة ففي الخبر المشهور إن في
الجمعة ساعة لايوافقها عبد مسلم يسأل الله عز وجل فيها شيئا إلا أعطاه (5)
وفي خبر آخر لا يصادفها عبد يصلي (6)
واختلف فيها فقيل إنها عند طلوع الشمس وقيل عند الزوال وقيل مع الأذان
وقيل إذا صعد الإمام المنبر وأخذ في الخطبة وقيل إذا قام PageV01P185
الناس إلى الصلاة وقيل آخر وقت العصر أعني وقت الاختيار وقيل قبل غروب
الشمس وكانت فاطمة رضي الله عنها تراعي ذلك الوقت وتأمر خادمتها أن تنظر
إلى الشمس فتؤذنها بسقوطها فتأخذ في الدعاء والاستغفار إلى أن تغرب الشمس
وتخبر بأن تلك الساعة هي المنتظرة وتؤثره عن أبيها صلى الله عليه وسلم
وعليها (1) وقال بعض العلماء هي مبهمة في جميع اليوم مثل ليلة القدر تتوفر
الدواعي على مراقبتها
وقيل إنها تنتقل في ساعات يوم الجمعة كتنقل ليلة القدر وهذا هو الأشبه
وله سر لا يليق بعلم المعاملة ذكره ولكن ينبغي أن يصدق بما قال صلى الله
عليه وسلم إن لربكم في أيام دهركم نفحات ألا فتعرضوا لها (2) ويوم الجمعة
من جملة تلك الأيام فينبغي أن يكون العبد في جميع نهاره متعرضا لها بإحضار
القلب وملازمة الذكر والنزوع عن وساوس الدنيا فعساه يحطى بشيء من تلك
النفحات
وقد قال كعب الأحبار إنها في آخر ساعة من يوم الجمعة  وذلك عند الغروب
فقال أبو هريرة وكيف تكون آخر ساعة وقد سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
يقول لا يوافقها عبد يصلي ولات حين صلاة فقال كعب ألم يقل رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم من قعد ينتظر الصلاة فهو في الصلاة (3) قال بلى قال فذلك
صلاة فسكت أبو هريرة
وكان كعب مائلا إلى أنها رحمة من الله سبحانه للقائمين بحق هذا اليوم
وأوان إرسالها عند الفراغ من تمام العمل
وبالجملة هذا وقت شريف مع وقت صعود الإمام المنبر فليكثر الدعاء فيهما
الثالث يستحب أن يكثر الصلاة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا
اليوم فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من صلى علي في يوم الجمعة ثمانين مرة غفر
الله له ذنوب ثمانين سنة قيل يا رسول الله كيف الصلاة عليك قال تقول اللهم
صل على محمد عبدك ونبيك ورسولك النبي الأمي وتعقد واحدة وإن قلت اللهم صلي
على محمد وعلى آل محمد صلاة تكون لك رضاء ولحقه أداء وأعطه الوسيلة وابعثه
المقام المحمود الذي وعدته واجزه عنا ما هو أهله واجزه أفضل ما جازيت نبيا
عن أمته وصل عليه وعلى جميع إخوانه من النبيين والصالحين يا أرحم الراحمين
(4) تقول هذا سبع مرات فقد قيل من قالها في سبع جمع في كل جمعة سبع مرات
وجبت له شفاعته صلى الله عليه وسلم
وإن أراد أن يزيد أتى بالصلاة المأثورة فقال اللهم اجعل فضائل صلواتك
ونوامي بركاتك وشرائف زكواتك ورأفتك ورحمتك وتحيتك على محمد سيد المرسلين
وإمام المتقين وخاتم النبيين ورسول رب العالمين قائد الخير وفاتح البر ونبي
الرحمة وسيد الأمة اللهم ابعثه مقاما محمودا تزلف به قربه وتقر به عينه
يغبطه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ل-س (J-L-S)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Physical sitting, occupying a place; the act of remaining seated in assembly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious context, sitting in a learning circle (ḥalaqah) as a posture of receptivity to sacred knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for bodily sitting; metaphorical (majāz) for steadfast adherence to a practice or station.
- Root: ق-ص-ص (Q-Ṣ-Ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Narrating stories, recounting tales; tracing a narrative sequentially.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, storytelling (qaṣaṣ) that may deviate from prophetic guidance into embellishment or innovation (bidʿah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for recounting events; metaphorical for the preacher who captivates audiences with tales lacking substantive religious benefit.
- Root: ن-ف-خ (N-F-Kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Breathing, blowing; a gust or emanation of air.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine "breaths" (nafaḥāt) as moments of special mercy and grace that descend upon creation at appointed times.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical blowing; metaphorical for spiritual effusions of divine favor that the servant must actively seek.
- Root: ف-ض-ل (F-Ḍ-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Surplus, excellence, superiority; that which exceeds necessity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Quranic terms, "bounty" (faḍl) often denotes knowledge and divine favor, as in the verse about David.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for excess; metaphorical for divine grace and the merit of virtuous acts over others.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Condition and Exception (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — In the hadith "no servant asks Allah for anything except He gives it," the conditional particle "lā" with the exception clause governs the apodosis, requiring careful parsing of the scope of divine response.
chapters.translation:
I say: Now I shall expound the etiquettes and sunnas that fall outside the preceding order which encompasses the entire day. They are seven matters.

**The First:** That one attend assemblies of knowledge in the early morning or after the afternoon prayer, and not attend the assemblies of storytellers (quṣṣāṣ), for there is no good in their speech. Nor should the seeker (murīd) be devoid, throughout the entire day of Friday, of good deeds and supplications, so that the noble hour overtakes him while he is engaged in goodness. Nor should he attend the learning circles before the prayer. It is narrated that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade forming circles on Friday before the prayer {«نهى عن التحلق يوم الجمعة قبل الصلاة»} — unless one is a knower of Allah who reminds of the days of Allah and imparts understanding in the religion of Allah, speaking in the congregational mosque in the morning, so that one may sit with him, thereby combining early attendance with listening. And listening to knowledge that benefits in the Hereafter is superior to occupying oneself with supererogatory prayers. For Abū Dharr narrated that attending a sitting of knowledge is better than praying one thousand rakʿahs.

Anas ibn Mālik said concerning His saying, the Exalted: {«فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض وابتغوا من فضل الله»} — "And when the prayer is completed, disperse in the land and seek from the bounty of Allah" — "Indeed, it is not the seeking of worldly goods, but rather visiting the sick, attending funerals, learning knowledge, and visiting a brother in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." And Allah, the Exalted, has named knowledge "bounty" (faḍl) in several places. He said, the Exalted: {«وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما»} — "And He taught you what you did not know, and the bounty of Allah upon you is immense." And He said, the Exalted: {«ولقد آتينا داود منا فضلا»} — "And indeed We gave David from Us bounty" — meaning knowledge. Thus, learning knowledge on this day and teaching it is among the most excellent acts of drawing near to Allah.

Prayer is better than the assemblies of storytellers, for the early Muslims deemed storytelling an innovation (bidʿah). They would expel storytellers from the mosque. Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, went early to his place in the congregational mosque, and when a storyteller sat in his spot, he said: "Rise from my place." The man replied: "I will not rise, for I have sat and preceded you to it." So Ibn ʿUmar sent for the chief of police, who removed him. Had this been from the sunnah, it would not have been permissible to remove him, for the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«لا يقيمن أحدكم أخاه من مجلسه ثم يجلس فيه ولكن تفسحوا وتوسعوا»} — "Let none of you remove his brother from his seat and then sit in it, but rather make room and expand." And Ibn ʿUmar, when a man rose from his seat for him, would not sit in it until the man returned to it. It is narrated that a storyteller used to sit in the courtyard of the chamber of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she sent to Ibn ʿUmar: "This man has harmed me with his storytelling and distracted me from my glorification." So Ibn ʿUmar struck him until he broke his staff upon his back, then expelled him.

**The Second:** That one be vigilant in watching for the noble hour. For in the well-known report: {«إن في الجمعة ساعة لا يوافقها عبد مسلم يسأل الله عز وجل فيها شيئا إلا أعطاه»} — "Indeed, in Friday there is an hour in which no Muslim servant asks Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for anything except He gives it to him." And in another report: {«لا يصادفها عبد يصلي»} — "No servant praying will encounter it." There is disagreement concerning it. It is said it is at the rising of the sun; it is said at its zenith; it is said at the call to prayer; it is said when the imam ascends the pulpit and begins the sermon; it is said when the people rise to prayer; it is said it is the last time of the afternoon prayer, meaning the time of choice; and it is said it is before the setting of the sun. Fāṭimah, may Allah be pleased with her, would watch for that time and command her maidservant to look at the sun and alert her at its decline, whereupon she would engage in supplication and seeking forgiveness until the sun set, informing that that hour was the awaited one, and she transmitted it from her father, peace and blessings be upon him and upon her. Some scholars said it is left ambiguous throughout the entire day, like the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), so that motivations are directed toward watching for it. And it is said it shifts among the hours of Friday just as the Night of Decree shifts — and this is the more likely view. It has a secret that is not fitting to mention in the science of practical conduct (ʿilm al-muʿāmalah), but one should affirm the truth of what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«إن لربكم في أيام دهركم نفحات ألا فتعرضوا لها»} — "Indeed, your Lord has breaths (nafaḥāt) in the days of your time — so expose yourselves to them." And Friday is among those days. Thus, the servant should, throughout his entire day, expose himself to them by presence of heart, persistence in remembrance, and withdrawal from the whisperings of the world, so that perhaps he may be granted something of those breaths.

Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: "It is in the last hour of Friday, that is, at sunset." Abū Hurayrah said: "How can it be the last hour, when I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: {«لا يوافقها عبد يصلي»} — 'No servant praying will encounter it' — and that is not a time of prayer?" Kaʿb said: "Did not the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: {«من قعد ينتظر الصلاة فهو في الصلاة»} — 'Whoever sits waiting for prayer is in prayer'?" He replied: "Yes." Kaʿb said: "Then that is prayer." So Abū Hurayrah fell silent. Kaʿb inclined to the view that it is a mercy from Allah, the Exalted, for those who uphold the due of this day, and its time of sending is upon completion of the full work. In sum, this is a noble time, along with the time of the imam's ascent to the pulpit — so let one multiply supplication in both.

**The Third:** It is recommended to multiply blessings upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, on this day. For he said, peace and blessings be upon him: {«من صلى علي في يوم الجمعة ثمانين مرة غفر الله له ذنوب ثمانين سنة»} — "Whoever sends blessings upon me on Friday eighty times, Allah forgives him the sins of eighty years." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how do we send blessings upon you?" He said: "You say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad, Your servant, Your Prophet, and Your Messenger, the unlettered Prophet — and you count one. And if you say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, a blessing that is satisfaction to You, and fulfillment of his due, and grant him the means (al-wasīlah), and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You promised him, and recompense him on our behalf as he deserves, and recompense him with the best You have recompensed any prophet on behalf of his nation, and send blessings upon him and upon all his brothers among the prophets and the righteous, O Most Merciful of the merciful — you say this seven times. For it has been said: whoever says it in seven Fridays, each Friday seven times, his intercession, peace and blessings be upon him, becomes obligatory for him."

And if he wishes to increase, let him come with the transmitted supplication: "O Allah, place the excellences of Your blessings, the growing abundance of Your benedictions, the noble forms of Your purifications, Your tenderness, Your mercy, and Your greeting upon Muḥammad, the master of the messengers, the leader of the God-fearing, the seal of the prophets, the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, the guide to good, the opener of righteousness, the Prophet of mercy, the master of the nation. O Allah, raise him to a praiseworthy station by which You bring him near in proximity, delight his eye, and make the former and latter peoples envy him. O Allah, grant him excellence, superiority, honor, the means, the lofty rank, and the sublime elevated station. O Allah, grant Muḥammad his request, deliver him to his hope, and make him the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted. O Allah, magnify his proof, weigh heavy his scale, make his argument radiant, and raise his degree among the highest of those brought near. O Allah, gather us in his company, make us of the people of his intercession, give us life upon his sunnah, take us in death upon his creed, bring us to his basin, and give us to drink from his cup, neither disgraced, nor regretful, nor doubting, nor altered, nor tempting, nor tempted. Amen, O Lord of the worlds." In general, whatever words of blessing one brings, even the well-known ones in the tashahhud, he is thereby sending blessings. And he should add to it seeking forgiveness, for that too is recommended on this day.

**The Fourth:** Recitation of the Quran — let him multiply it, and let him recite Sūrat al-Kahf specifically. For it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both, that whoever recites Sūrat al-Kahf on the night of Friday, or the day of Friday, is given light from where he recites to Mecca, and is forgiven until the next Friday plus three days, and seventy thousand angels pray for him until morning, and he is cured of illness, abscess, pleurisy, leprosy, and the trial of the Dajjāl. It is recommended to complete the Quran on Friday and its night if one is able. And let his completion be in the two rakʿahs of dawn if he recited at night, or in the two rakʿahs of sunset, or between the call and the iqāmah of Friday — for that has immense merit. The worshippers used to recommend reciting on Friday {«قل هو الله أحد»} one thousand times. It is said that whoever recites it in ten rakʿahs or twenty is better than a full completion of the Quran. And they would send blessings upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, one thousand times, and they would say "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greater" one thousand times. And if one recites the six "musabbiʿāt" on Friday or its night, that is good. It is not narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited specific sūrahs except on Friday and its night: he would recite in the sunset prayer of Friday night {«قل يا أيها الكافرون»} and {«قل هو الله أحد»}, and he would recite in the final night prayer of Friday night Sūrat al-Jumuʿah and Sūrat al-Munāfiqūn. It is narrated that he would recite them in the two rakʿahs of Friday. And he would recite in the dawn prayer of Friday Sūrat Sajdah Luqmān and Sūrat {«هل أتى على الإنسان»}.

**The Fifth:** Prayers — it is recommended that when one enters the mosque, he not sit until he prays four rakʿahs, reciting in them {«قل هو الله أحد»} two hundred times, fifty times in each rakʿah. For it is transmitted from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that whoever does this will not die until he sees his place in Paradise, or it is shown to him. And he should not abandon the two rakʿahs of greeting (taḥiyyah) even if the imam is delivering the sermon, but let him shorten them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, commanded this. And in a rare hadith, he, peace and blessings be upon him, remained silent for the one entering until he prayed them. The Kūfans said: if the imam remains silent for him, he prays them. It is recommended on this day or its night to pray four rakʿahs with four sūrahs: al-Anʿām, al-Kahf, Ṭā Hā, and Yā Sīn. If he does not know them well, let him recite Yā Sīn, Sūrat Sajdah Luqmān, Sūrat al-Dukhān, and Sūrat al-Mulk. And let him not abandon reciting these four sūrahs on Friday night, for in them is abundant merit. And whoever does not know the Quran well, let him recite what he knows — for him it is in the station of a full completion. And let him multiply recitation of Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ. It is recommended to pray the prayer of glorification (ṣalāt al-tasbīḥ), as will come in the chapter on supererogatory acts regarding its manner, because he, peace and blessings be upon him, said to his uncle al-ʿAbbās: "Pray it every Friday." And Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, would not abandon this prayer on Friday after the zenith, and he would inform of the grandeur of its merit. The best is to make one's time: until the zenith for prayer, after the Friday prayer until the afternoon for listening to knowledge, and after the afternoon until sunset for glorification and seeking forgiveness.

**The Sixth:** Charity is recommended specifically on this day, for it is multiplied — except for one who asks while the imam is delivering the sermon, and one who speaks during the imam's speech, for that is disliked. Ṣāliḥ ibn Muḥammad said: A beggar asked on Friday while the imam was delivering the sermon, and he was beside my father. A man gave my father a piece to hand to him, but my father did not take it from him. Ibn Masʿūd said: "When a man asks in the mosque, he has deserved not to be given. And when he asks upon the Quran, do not give him." Some scholars disliked giving charity to beggars in the congregational mosque who step over people's necks, unless one asks standing or sitting in his place without stepping over. Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: Whoever attends Friday, then departs and gives two different kinds of charity, then returns and prays two rakʿahs, perfecting their bowing, prostration, and humility, then says: "O Allah, I ask You by Your name — in the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate — and by Your name of which there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Sustaining, whom neither slumber nor sleep overtakes" — he does not ask Allah, the Exalted, for anything except He gives it to him. Some of the predecessors said: Whoever feeds a poor person on Friday, then goes early and arrives early, and harms no one, then says when the imam concludes the greeting: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate, the Living, the Self-Sustaining, I ask You to forgive me, have mercy on me, and grant me safety from the Fire," then supplicates with whatever occurs to him — it is answered for him.

**The Seventh:** That one make Friday for the Hereafter, refraining on it from all worldly occupations, multiplying devotions (awrād), and not initiating travel on it. For it is narrated that whoever travels on Friday night, his two angels curse him — and it is forbidden after the break of dawn, unless the company would be missed. Some of the predecessors disliked buying water in the mosque from the water-carrier to drink or to give as charity, so as not to be a buyer in the mosque, for buying and selling in the mosque is disliked. They said: there is no harm in giving the piece outside the mosque, then drinking or giving as charity inside. In sum, one should increase on Friday in his devotions and varieties of good deeds. For Allah, the Exalted, when He loves a servant, employs him in virtuous times with the most excellent of deeds; and when He abhors him, He employs him in virtuous times with evil deeds, so that this is more painful in His punishment and more severe in His abhorrence, due to his deprivation of the blessing of the time and his violation of the sanctity of the time. Supplications are recommended on Friday, and their mention will come in the Book of Supplications, Allah willing. And may Allah send blessings upon every chosen servant.

|| الباب السادس في مسائل متفرقة تعم بها البلوى ويحتاج المريد إلى معرفتها

فأما المسائل التي تقع نادرة فقد استقصيناها في كتب الفقه
مسألة الفعل القليل وإن كان لا يبطل الصلاة فهو مكروه إلا لحاجة وذلك في
دفع المار وقتل العقرب التي تخاف ويمكن قتلها بضربة أو ضربتين فإذا صارت
ثلاثة فقد كثرت وبطلت الصلاة وكذلك القملة والبرغوث مهما تأذى بهما كان له
دفعهما وكذلك حاجته إلى الحك الذي يشوش عليه الخشوع
كان معاذ يأخذ القملة والبرغوث في الصلاة
وابن عمر كان يقتل القملة في الصلاة حتى يظهر الدم على يده
وقال النخعي يأخذها ويوهنها ولا شيء  عليه إن قتلها
وقال ابن المسيب يأخذها ويخدرها ثم يطرحها
وقال مجاهد الأحب إلى أن يدعها إلا أن تؤذيه فتشغله عن صلاته فيوهنها قدر
ما لا تؤذي ثم يلقيها
وهذه رخصة وإلا فالكمال الاحتراز عن الفعل وإن قل
ولذلك كان بعضهم لا يطرد الذباب وقال لا أعود نفسي ذلك فأفسد على صلاتي
وقد سمعت أن الفساق بين يدي PageV01P188
الملوك يصبرون على أذى كثير ولا يتحركون
ومهما تثاءب فلا بأس أن يضع يده على فيه وهو الأولى
وإن عطس حمد الله عز وجل في نفسه ولا يحرك لسانه
وإن تجشأ فينبغي أن لا يرفع رأسه إلى السماء وإن سقط رداؤه فلا ينبغي أن
يسويه وكذلك أطراف عمامته فكل ذلك مكروه إلا لضرورة
مسألة الصلاة في النعلين جائزة وإن كان نزع النعلين سهلا وليست الرخصة في
الخف لعسر النزع بل هذه النجاسة معفو عنها
وفي معناها المداس صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في نعليه ثم نزع
فنزع الناس نعالهم فقال لم خلعتم نعالكم قالوا رأيناك خلعت فخلعنا قال صلى
الله عليه وسلم أن جبرائيل عليه السلام أتاني فأخبرني أن بهما خبثا فإذا
أراد أحدكم المسجد فليقلب نعليه ولينظر فيهما فإن رأى خبثا فليمسحه بالأرض
وليصل فيهما (1) وقال بعضهم الصلاة في النعلين أفضل لأنه صلى الله عليه
وسلم قال لم خلعتم نعالكم وهذه مبالغة فإنه صلى الله عليه وسلم سألهم ليبين
لهم سبب خلعه إذ علم أنهم خلعوا على موافقته
وقد روى عبد الله بن السائب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خلع نعليه (2)
فإذن قد فعل كليهما فمن خلع فلا ينبغي أن يضعهما عن يمينه ويساره فيضيق
الموضع ويقطع الصف بل يضعهما بين يديه ولا يتركهما وراءه فيكون قلبه ملتفتا
إليهما
ولعل من رأى الصلاة فيهما أفضل راعي هذا المعنى وهو التفات القلب إليهما
روى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إذا صلى
أحدكم فليجعل نعليه بين رجليه (3) وقال أبو هريرة لغيره اجعلهما بين  رجليك
ولا تؤذ بهما مسلما
ووضعهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على يساره وكان إماما (4) فللإمام
أن يفعل ذلك إذ لا يقف أحد على يساره
والأولى أن لا يضعهما بين قدميه فتشغلانه ولكن قدام قدميه ولعله المراد
بالحديث
وقد قال جبير بن مطعم وضع الرجل نعليه بين قدميه بدعة
مسألة إذا بزق في صلاته لم تبطل صلاته لأنه فعل قليل
وما لا يحصل به صوت لا يعد كلاما وليس على شكل حروف الكلام إلا أنه مكروه
فينبغي أن يحترز منه إلا كما أذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيه إذ روى
بعض الصحابة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى في القبلة نخامة فغضب
غضبا شديدا ثم حكها بعرجون كان في يده وقال ائتوني بعبير فلطخ أثرها
بزعفران ثم التفت إلينا وقال أيكم يحب أن يبزق في وجهه فقلنا لا أحد قال
فإن أحدكم إذا دخل في الصلاة فإن الله عز وجل بينه وبين القبلة (5) وفي لفظ
آخر واجهه الله تعالى فلا يبزقن أحدكم تلقاء وجهه ولا عن يمينه ولكن عن
شماله أو تحت قدمه اليسرى فإن بدرته بادرة فليبصق في ثوبه وليقل به هكذا
ودلك بعضه ببعض
مسألة لوقوف المقتدى سنة وفرض أما السنة فأن يقف الواحد عن يمين الإمام
متأخرا عنه قليلا والمرأة الواحدة تقف خلف الإمام فإن وقفت بجنب الإمام لم
يضر ذلك ولكن خالفت السنة
فإن كان معها رجل PageV01P189
وقف الرجل عن يمين الإمام وهي خلف الرجل
ولا يقف أحد خلف الصف منفردا بل يدخل في الصف أو يجر إلى نفسه واحدا من
الصف
فإن وقف منفردا صحت صلاته مع الكراهية
وأما الفرض
فاتصال الصف وهو أن يكون بين المقتدي والإمام رابطة جامعة فإنهما في
جماعة فإن كانا في مسجد كفى ذلك جامعا لأنه بنى له فلا يحتاج إلى اتصال صف
بل إلى أن يعرف أفعال الإمام صلى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه على ظهر المسجد
بصلاة الإمام
وإذا كان الماموم على فناء  المسجد في طريق أو صحراء مشتركة وليس بينهما
اختلاف بناء مفرق فيكفي القرب بقدر غلوة سهم وكفى بها رابطة إذ يصل فعل
أحدهما إلى الآخر
وإنما يشترط إذا وقف في صحن دار على يمين المسجد أو يساره وبابها لاطىء
في المسجد فالشرط أن يمد صف المسجد في دهليزها من غير انقطاع إلى الصحن
ثم تصح صلاة من في ذلك الصف ومن خلفه دون من تقدم عليه وهكذا حكم الأبنية
