||| القسم الثالث ما يتكرر بتكرر السنين

وهي أربعة صلاة العيدين والتراويح وصلاة رجب وشعبان
الأولى صلاة العيدين وهي سنة مؤكدة وشعار من شعائر الدين وينبغي أن يراعى
فيها سبعة أمور الأول التكبير ثلاثا نسقا فيقول الله أكبر الله أكبر
PageV01P200
الله أكبر كبيرا والحمد لله كثيرا وسبحان الله بكرة وأصيلا لا إله إلا
الله وحده لا شريك له مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون يفتتح بالتكبير
ليلة الفطر إلى الشروع في صلاة العيد وفي العيد الثاني يفتتح التكبير عقيب
الصبح يوم عرفة إلى آخر النهار يوم الثالث عشر وهذا أكمل الأقاويل
ويكبر عقيب الصلوات المفروضة وعقيب النوافل وهو عقيب الفرائض آكد
الثاني إذا أصبح يوم العيد يغتسل ويتزين ويتطيب كما ذكرناه في الجمعة
والرداء والعمامة هو الأفضل للرجال وليجنب الصبيان الحرير والعجائز التزين
عند الخروج
الثالث أن يخرج من طريق ويرجع من طريق آخر (1) هكذا فعل رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم وكان  صلى الله عليه وسلم يأمر بإخراج العواتق وذوات الخدور
(2)
الرابع المستحب الخروج إلى الصحراء إلا بمكة وبيت المقدس فإن كان يوم مطر
فلا بأس بالصلاة في المسجد ويجوز في يوم الصحو أن يأمر الإمام رجلا يصلي
بالضعفة في المسجد ويخرج بالأقوياء مكبرين
الخامس يراعي الوقت فوقت صلاة العيد ما بين طلوع الشمس إلى الزوال
ووقت الذبح للضحايا ما بين ارتفاع الشمس بقدر خطبتين وركعتين إلى آخر
اليوم الثالث عشر
ويستحب تعجيل صلاة الأضحى لأجل الذبح وتأخير صلاة الفطر لأجل تفريق صدقة
الفطر قبلها
هذه سنة رسول الله (3)
السادس في كيفية الصلاة فليخرج الناس مكبرين في الطريق
وإذا بلغ الإمام المصلى لم يجلس ولم يتنفل ويقطع الناس التنفل
ثم ينادي مناد الصلاة جامعة
ويصلي الإمام بهم ركعتين يكبر في الأولى سوى تكبيرة الإحرام والركوع سبع
تكبيرات يقول بين كل تكبيرتين سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله
والله أكبر ويقول وجهت وجهي للذي فطر السموات والأرض عقيب تكبيرة الافتتاح
ويؤخر الاستعاذة إلى ما وراء الثامنة ويقرأ سورة ق في الأولى بعد الفاتحة
واقتربت في الثانية
والتكبيرات الزائدة في الثانية خمس سوى تكبيرتي القيام والركوع
وبين كل تكبيرتين ما ذكرناه
ثم يخطب خطبتين بينهما جلسة ومن فاتته صلاة العيد قضاها
السابع أن يضحي بكبش ضحى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بكبشين أملحين
وذبح بيده وقال بسم الله والله أكبر هذا عني وعمن لم يضح من أمتي (4) وقال
صلى الله عليه وسلم من رأى هلال ذي الحجة وأراد أن يضحي فلا يأخذ من شعره
ولا من أظفاره شيئا (5) قال أبو أيوب الأنصاري كان الرجل يضحي على عهد رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالشاة عن أهل بيته ويأكلون ويطعمون (6)
وله أن يأكل من الضحية بعد ثلاثة أيام فما فوق وردت فيه الرخصة بعد النهي
عنه
وقال سفيان الثوري يستحب أن يصلي بعد عيد الفطر اثنتي عشرة ركعة وبعد عيد
الأضحى ست ركعات (7) وقال هو من السنة
الثانية التراويح وهي عشرون ركعة  PageV01P201
وكيفيتها مشهورة وهي سنة مؤكدة وإن كانت دون العيدين واختلفوا في أن
الجماعة فيها أفضل أم الانفراد وقد خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيها
ليلتين أو ثلاثا للجماعة ثم لم يخرج وقال أخاف أن توجب عليكم (1) وجمع عمر
رضي الله عنه الناس عليها في الجماعة حيث أمن من الوجوب بانقطاع الوحي فقيل
إن الجماعة أفضل لفعل عمر رضي الله عنه ولأن الاجتماع بركة وله فضيلة بدليل
الفرائض ولأنه ربما يكسل في الانفراد وينشط عند مشاهدة الجمع
وقيل الانفراد أفضل لأن هذه سنة ليست من الشعائر كالعيدين فإلحاقها بصلاة
الضحى وتحية المسجد أولى ولم تشرع فيها جماعة
وقد جرت العادة بأن يدخل المسجد جمع معا ثم لم يصلوا التحية بالجماعة
ولقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فضل صلاة التطوع في بيته على صلاته في المسجد
كفضل صلاة المكتوبة في المسجد على صلاته في البيت (2) وروي أنه صلى الله
عليه وسلم قال صلاة في مسجدي هذا أفضل من مائة صلاة في غيره من المساجد
وصلاة في المسجد الحرام أفضل من ألف صلاة في مسجدي وأفضل من ذلك كله رجل
يصلي في زاوية بيته ركعتين لا يعلمهما إلا الله عز وجل (3) وهذا لأن الرياء
والتصنع ربما يتطرق إليه في الجمع ويأمن منه في الوحدة فهذا ما قيل فيه
والمختار أن الجماعة أفضل كما رآه عمر رضي الله عنه
فإن بعض النوافل قد شرعت فيها الجماعة وهذا جدير بأن يكون من الشعائر
التي تظهر
وأما الالتفات إلى الرياء في الجمع والكسل في الإنفراد عدول عن مقصود
النظر في فضيلة الجمع من حيث إنه جماعة وكأن قائله يقول الصلاة خير من
تركها بالكسل والإخلاص خير من الرياء
فلنفرض المسألة فيمن يثق بنفسه أنه لا يكسل لو انفرد ولا يرائي لو حضر
الجمع فأيهما أفضل له فيدور النظر بين بركة الجمع وبين مزيد قوة الإخلاص
وحضور القلب في الوحدة فيجوز أن يكون في تفضيل أحدهما على الآخر تردد ومما
يستحب القنوت ف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ر-ر (K-R-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Repetition, recurrence, return to a prior state or act
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Cyclical reiteration of devotional acts across temporal units (years), distinct from one-time obligations
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal recurrence in time (ḥaqīqah), not metaphorical
- Root: ش-ع-ر (Sh-ʿ-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To know, perceive; shaʿā'ir = ritual marks/signs of a rite
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Outward symbolic observances manifesting religious identity (shaʿā'ir al-dīn)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal as public emblem; metaphorical extension to any conspicuous act of worship
- Root: ض-ح-ي (Ḍ-Ḥ-Y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Forenoon brightness; uḍḥiyah = sacrificial animal offered at forenoon of ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sacrificial offering (qurbān) as act of nearness to God, tied to ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā timing
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the animal and act; metaphorical for self-surrender
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — governing clauses like "whoever sees the crescent... let him not take" and "except in Mecca and Jerusalem," with precise apodosis regulation.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third category comprises prayers that recur with the recurrence of years. These are four: the two Festival Prayers (ṣalāt al-ʿīdayn), the Tarāwīḥ prayer, the prayer of Rajab, and the prayer of Shaʿbān.

**The First: The Two Festival Prayers (ṣalāt al-ʿīdayn)**

These constitute an emphatically confirmed Sunnah (sunnah muʾakkadah) and a ritual emblem among the emblems of religion (shaʿāʾir al-dīn). Seven matters must be observed therein:

**The First Matter: The Takbīr (declaration of God's greatness)** — three consecutive times, saying: "God is Great, God is Great, God is Great, abundantly great; praise be to God, abundantly; glory be to God morning and evening; there is no god but God alone, with no partner, sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers detest it." The Takbīr commences on the night of Fiṭr (end of Ramadan) until the commencement of the Festival Prayer. For the second Festival (al-Aḍḥā), the Takbīr commences immediately after the Dawn Prayer (al-Ṣubḥ) on the Day of ʿArafah until the end of the day of the thirteenth [of Dhū al-Ḥijjah]. This is the most complete of the opinions. One declares the Takbīr after the obligatory prayers and after the supererogatory ones, though it is more emphatic after the obligatory.

**The Second Matter:** When the morning of the Festival arrives, one performs the major ablution (ghusl), adorns oneself, and applies perfume, as we mentioned regarding Friday. The cloak (ridāʾ) and turban are preferable for men. Young boys should be kept away from silk, and elderly women from excessive adornment when going out.

**The Third Matter:** One should go out by one route and return by another. Thus did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) act. He (peace and blessings be upon him) used to command that unmarried girls and women secluded behind curtains be brought out [for the prayer].

**The Fourth Matter:** It is recommended to go out to open ground (al-ṣaḥrāʾ), except in Mecca and Jerusalem. If it is a rainy day, there is no harm in praying in the mosque. On a clear day, it is permissible for the imam to appoint a man to lead the weak in prayer at the mosque, while he goes out with the strong, declaring the Takbīr.

**The Fifth Matter:** Observing the time. The time of the Festival Prayer is between sunrise and zenith (al-zawāl). The time of slaughtering the sacrificial animals (al-ḍaḥāyā) is between the rising of the sun by the measure of two sermons and two units of prayer, until the end of the thirteenth day. It is recommended to hasten the Aḍḥā prayer for the sake of the slaughter, and to delay the Fiṭr prayer for the sake of distributing the alms of Fiṭr (ṣadaqat al-fiṭr) before it. This is the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).

**The Sixth Matter: Concerning the Manner of the Prayer.** The people should go out declaring the Takbīr on the way. When the imam reaches the place of prayer (al-muṣallā), he does not sit nor perform supererogatory prayers, and the people cease their supererogatory prayers. Then a caller announces: "The prayer is gathering (al-ṣalātu jāmiʿah)." The imam leads them in two units. In the first unit, besides the opening Takbīr (takbīrat al-iḥrām) and the Takbīr of bowing (al-rukūʿ), he declares seven Takbīrs. Between every two Takbīrs he says: "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Great." He says, immediately after the opening Takbīr: "I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth (fāṭir al-samāwāt wa al-arḍ)." He delays the seeking of refuge (al-istiʿādhah) until after the eighth [Takbīr]. He recites Sūrat Qāf in the first unit after the Fātiḥah, and "Iqtarabat" (Sūrat al-Qamar) in the second. The additional Takbīrs in the second unit are five, besides the two Takbīrs of standing and bowing. Between every two Takbīrs, [he says] what we have mentioned. Then he delivers two sermons with a sitting between them. Whoever misses the Festival Prayer makes it up.

**The Seventh Matter:** One should offer a sacrificial ram (kabsh). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sacrificed two horned rams, slaughtered them with his own hand, and said: "In the name of God, and God is Great. This is on behalf of me and on behalf of whoever of my community has not sacrificed." He (peace and blessings be upon him) also said: "Whoever sees the crescent of Dhū al-Ḥijjah and intends to sacrifice, let him not take anything from his hair nor from his nails." Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī said: "A man would sacrifice on behalf of his household a single sheep during the era of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and they would eat and feed others." One may eat from the sacrificial animal after three days and beyond; the license (rukhṣah) was reported after the prohibition thereof. Sufyān al-Thawrī said: "It is recommended to pray twelve units after the Fiṭr Festival and six units after the Aḍḥā Festival." He said: "This is from the Sunnah."

**The Second: The Tarāwīḥ Prayer**

It consists of twenty units. Its manner is well-known. It is an emphatically confirmed Sunnah, though below the two Festivals in rank. They differed as to whether congregation therein is superior or individual performance. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came out for it for two or three nights for the congregation, then ceased coming out, saying: "I fear that it would be made obligatory upon you." ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) gathered the people upon it in congregation when safety from obligation was assured by the cessation of revelation. It is said that congregation is superior — for the act of ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him), because gathering is a blessing possessing virtue, as evidenced by the obligatory prayers, and because one might become sluggish in solitude while being energized upon witnessing the congregation.

It is also said that individual performance is superior, because this is a Sunnah not among the ritual emblems like the two Festivals; likening it to the forenoon prayer (al-ḍuḥā) and the mosque-greeting prayer (taḥiyyat al-masjid) is more fitting, and no congregation was legislated for it. Custom has it that people enter the mosque together, yet they do not perform the greeting prayer in congregation. And for his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "The virtue of supererogatory prayer in one's house over his prayer in the mosque is like the virtue of the obligatory prayer in the mosque over his prayer in the house." It is also narrated that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a hundred prayers in other mosques, and a prayer in the Sacred Mosque is better than a thousand prayers in my mosque. Better than all that is a man who prays two units in a corner of his house, known to none but God, Mighty and Majestic." This is because ostentation (al-riyāʾ) and affectation (al-taṣannuʿ) might creep into the congregation, while one is safe from them in solitude. This is what has been said on the matter.

The chosen position is that congregation is superior, as ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) saw it. For some supererogatory prayers have had congregation legislated for them, and this one is worthy of being among the emblems that are made manifest. As for the concern about ostentation in congregation and sluggishness in solitude, that is a deviation from the intended consideration of the virtue of congregation qua congregation. It is as if its proponent says: "Prayer is better than abandoning it out of sluggishness, and sincerity is better than ostentation." Let us then frame the question for one who is confident of himself that he would not be sluggish if alone, nor ostentatious if he attended the congregation — which is better for him? The consideration then turns between the blessing of congregation and the greater strength of sincerity and presence of heart in solitude. It is conceivable that there be hesitation in preferring one over the other. Among the recommended matters is the Qunūt (supplication of standing) in the Witr prayer during the latter half of Ramadan.

**As for the Prayer of Rajab:** It has been narrated with an chain of transmission (isnād) from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "There is no one who fasts the first Thursday of Rajab, then prays between the Evening Prayer (al-ʿishāʾ) and the Night Prayer (al-ʿatamah) twelve units, separating every two units with a salutation (taslīmah), reciting in each unit the Opening of the Book once, 'Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree' (Innā anzalnāhu fī laylat al-qadr) three times, and 'Say: He is God, One' (Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad) twelve times. When he finishes his prayer, he sends blessings upon me seventy times, saying: 'O God, send blessings upon Muḥammad, the Unlettered Prophet, and upon his family.' Then he prostrates and says in his prostration seventy times: 'Most Holy, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit (al-rūḥ).' Then he raises his head and says seventy times: 'Lord, forgive, have mercy, and pardon what You know; indeed, You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous.' Then he prostrates another prostration and says therein the like of what he said in the first prostration. Then he asks for his need in his prostration, for it shall be fulfilled." The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "No one prays this prayer except that God the Exalted forgives him all his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea, the number of sand grains, the weight of mountains, and the leaves of trees; and he will intercede on the Day of Resurrection for seven hundred of his household who have merited the Fire." This is a recommended prayer (mustaḥabbah). We have only mentioned it in this category because it recurs with the recurrence of years, even though its rank does not reach the rank of the Tarāwīḥ and the Festival Prayer — for this prayer was transmitted by single narrators (āḥād). However, I have seen the people of Jerusalem, all of them, persistently observing it and not permitting its abandonment, so I wished to mention it.

**As for the Prayer of Shaʿbān:** On the night of the fifteenth thereof, one prays one hundred units, every two units with a salutation, reciting in each unit after the Fātiḥah "Say: He is God, One" eleven times. If he wishes, he may pray ten units, reciting in each unit after the Fātiḥah one hundred times "Say: He is God, One." This too is narrated among the collection of prayers. The predecessors (al-salaf) used to pray this prayer and called it the Prayer of Goodness (ṣalāt al-khayr); they would gather for it, and perhaps they prayed it in congregation. It is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: "Thirty of the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) told me that whoever prays this prayer on this night, God looks upon him seventy looks, and grants him for every look seventy needs, the least of which is forgiveness."

chapters.title_en: The Fourth Division of Supererogatory Prayers: Those Tied to Incidental Causes, Not to Fixed Times

||| القسم الرابع من النوافل ما يتعلق بأسباب عارضة ولا يتعلق بالمواقيت

وهي تسعة: صلاة الخسوف والكسوف والاستسقاء وتحية المسجد وركعتي الوضوء
وركعتين بين الأذان والإقامة وركعتين عند الخروج من المنزل والدخول فيه
ونظائر ذلك فنذكر منها ما يحضرنا الآن
الأولى صلاة الخسوف قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الشمس والقمر
آيتان من آيات الله لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم ذلك فافزعوا
إلى ذكر الله والصلاة (2) قال ذلك لما مات ولده إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم
وكسفت الشمس فقال الناس إنما كسفت لموته
والنظر في كيفيتها ووقتها أما الكيفية فإذا كسفت الشمس في وقت الصلاة فيه
مكروهة أو غير مكروهة نودي الصلاة جامعة وصلى الإمام بالناس في المسجد
ركعتين وركع في كل ركعة ركوعين أوائلهما أطول من أواخرهما
ولا يجهر فيقرأ في الأولى من قيام الركعة الأولى الفاتحة والبقرة وفي
الثانية الفاتحة وآل عمران وفي الثالثة الفاتحة وسورة النساء وفي الرابعة
الفاتحة وسورة المائدة أو مقدار ذلك من القرآن من حيث أراد ولو اقتصر على
الفاتحة في كل قيام أجزأه ولو اقتصر على سور قصار فلا بأس
ومقصود التطويل دوام الصلاة إلى الإنجلاء
ويسبح في الركوع الأول قدر مائة آية وفي الثاني قدر ثمانين وفي الثالث
قدر سبعين وفي الرابع قدر خمسين
وليكن السجود على قدر الركوع في كل ركعة
ثم يخطب خطبتين بعد الصلاة بينهما جلسة ويأمر الناس بالصدقة والعتق
والتوبة
وكذلك يفعل بخسوف القمر إلا أنه يجر فيها لأنها ليلية
فأما وقتها فعند ابتداء الكسوف إلى تمام الإنجلاء ويخرج وقتها بأن تغرب
الشمس كاسفة
وتفوت صلاة خسوف القمر بأن يطلع قرص الشمس إذ يبطل سلطان الليل ولا تفوت
بغروب القمر خاسفا لأن الليل كله سلطان القمر فإن انجلى في أثناء الصلاة
أتمها مخففة
ومن أدرك الركوع الثاني مع الإمام فقد فاتته تلك الركعة لأن الأصل هو
الركوع الأول
الثانية صلاة الاستسقاء فإذا غارت الأنهار وانقطعت الأمطار أو إنهارت
قناة فيستحب للإمام أن  يأمر الناس أولا بصيام ثلاثة أيام وما أطاقوا من
الصدقة والخروج من المظالم والتوبة من المعاصي ثم يخرج بهم في اليوم الرابع
وبالعجائز والصبيان متنظفين في ثياب بذلة واستكانة متواضعين بخلاف العيد
وقيل يستحب PageV01P203
إخراج الدواب لمشاركتها في الحاجة ولقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لولا صبيان
رضع ومشايخ ركع وبهائم رتع لصب عليكم العذاب صبا (1) ولو خرج أهل الذمة
أيضا متميزين لم يمنعوا فإذا اجتمعوا في المصلى الواصل من الصحراء نودي
الصلاة جامعة فصلى بهم الإمام ركعتين مثل صلاة العيد بغير تكبير ثم يخطب
خطبتين وبينهما جلسة خفيفة وليكن الاستغفار معظم الخطبتين وينبغي في وسط
الخطبة الثانية أن يستدبر الناس ويستقبل القبلة ويحول رداءه في هذه الساعة
تفاؤلا بتحويل الحال (2) هكذا فعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيجعل
أعلاه أسفله وما على اليمين على الشمال وما على الشمال وما على اليمين
وكذلك يفعل الناس ويدعون في هذه الساعة سرا ثم يستقبلهم فيختم الخطبة
ويدعون أرديتهم محولة كما هي حتى ينزعوها متى نزعوا الثياب
ويقول في الدعاء اللهم إنك أمرتنا بدعائك ووعدتنا إجابتك فقد دعوناك كما
أمرتنا فأجبنا كما وعدتنا اللهم فامنن علينا بمغفرة ما قارفنا وإجابتك في
سقيانا وسعة أرزاقنا
ولا بأس بالدعاء أدبار الصلوات في الأيام الثلاثة قبل الخروج ولهذا
الدعاء آداب وشروط باطنة من التوبة ورد المظالم وغيرها وسيأتي ذلك في كتاب
الدعوات
الثالثة صلاة الجنائز وكيفيتها مشهورة وأجمع دعاء مأثور ما روي في الصحيح
عن عوف بن مالك قال رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى على جنازة فحفظت
من دعائه اللهم اغفر له وارحمه وعافه واعف عنه وأكرم نزله ووسع مدخله
واغسله بالماء والثلج والبرد ونقه من الخطايا كما ينقى الثوب الأبيض من
الدنس وأبدله دارا خيرا من داره وأهلا خيرا من أهله وزوجا خيرا من زوجه
وأدخله الجنة وأعذه من عذاب القبر ومن عذاب النار (3) حتى قال عوف تمنيت أن
أكون أنا ذلك الميت
ومن أدرك التكبيرة الثانية فينبغي أن يراعي ترتيب الصلاة  في نفسه ويكبر
مع تكبيرات الإمام فإذا سلم الإمام قضى تكبيرة الذي فات كفعل المسبوق فإنه
لو بادر التكبيرات لم تبق للقدوة في هذه الصلاة معنى فالتكبيرات هي الأركان
الظاهرة وجدير بأن تقام مقام الركعات في سائر الصلوات هذا هو الأوجه عندي
وإن كان غيره محتملا
والأخبار الواردة في فضل صلاة الجنازة وتشييعها مشهورة فلا نطيل بإيرادها
وكيف لا يعظم فضلها وهي من فرائض الكفايات وإنما تصير نفلا في حق من لم
تتعين عليه بحضور غيره ثم ينال بها فضل فرض الكفاية وإن لم يتعين لأنهم
بجملتهم قاموا بما هو فرض الكفاية وأسقطوا الحرج عن غيرهم فلا يكون ذلك
كنفل لا يسقط به فرض عن أحد ويستحب طلب كثرة الجمع تبركا بكثرة الهمم
والأدعية واشتماله على ذي دعوة مستجابة لما روى
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-س-ف (kha-sa-fa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be eclipsed, to become dark, to lose light; the veiling of a celestial body's light.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A cosmic sign (āyah) indicating divine power, not a natural phenomenon independent of God's will.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the celestial event; metaphorical for the darkening of one's state or fortune.
- Root: س-ق-ي (sa-qa-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To give to drink, to water; the act of seeking rain (istisqā') as a supplication for divine provision.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A communal plea for mercy (raḥmah) through collective humility and repentance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for quenching thirst; metaphorical for spiritual nourishment and divine grace.
- Root: خ-ي-ر (kha-ya-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To choose, to prefer; the act of seeking the better option.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istikhārah as a submission of one's will to divine decree (qadar), acknowledging human ignorance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for selection; metaphorical for entrusting the outcome to God's omniscience.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnā') — Governing the syntactic relationship between conditions (e.g., "if you see this") and their apodoses, ensuring precise legal and ritual implications.
chapters.translation:
I say: The fourth division of supererogatory prayers pertains to incidental causes and is not tied to fixed times. These are nine: the prayer of the solar eclipse (khusūf), the lunar eclipse (kusūf), the prayer for rain (istisqā'), the greeting of the mosque (taḥiyyat al-masjid), the two rakʿahs after ablution (wuḍū'), the two rakʿahs between the call to prayer (adhān) and the commencement (iqāmah), the two rakʿahs upon leaving the home and entering it, and similar practices. We shall mention what is present to us now.

The first is the prayer of the eclipse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: {«إن الشمس والقمر آيتان من آيات الله لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم ذلك فافزعوا إلى ذكر الله والصلاة»} — "The sun and the moon are two signs among the signs of God; they are not eclipsed for the death of anyone nor for his life. So when you see that, hasten to the remembrance of God and prayer." He said this when his son Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, died, and the sun was eclipsed, so the people said, "It was only eclipsed for his death."

As for its modality (kayfiyyah) and its time: Regarding the modality, when the sun is eclipsed at a time when prayer is disliked (makrūh) or not disliked, the call is made, "Prayer is gathering" (al-ṣalātu jāmiʿah). The imam leads the people in the mosque in two rakʿahs, bowing twice in each rakʿah, with the first bowings being longer than the latter ones. He does not recite aloud. In the first rakʿah, he recites from the standing of the first bowing the Fātiḥah and al-Baqarah; in the second, the Fātiḥah and Āl ʿImrān; in the third, the Fātiḥah and Sūrat al-Nisā'; and in the fourth, the Fātiḥah and Sūrat al-Mā'idah — or the equivalent amount of the Qur'an from wherever he wishes. If he limits himself to the Fātiḥah in each standing, it suffices him; and if he limits himself to short sūrahs, there is no harm. The purpose of prolongation is the continuation of the prayer until the eclipse clears.

He glorifies (subḥān) in the first bowing to the extent of one hundred verses, in the second to the extent of eighty, in the third to the extent of seventy, and in the fourth to the extent of fifty. The prostration should be proportionate to the bowing in each rakʿah. Then he delivers two sermons (khuṭbah) after the prayer, with a sitting between them, and commands the people to give charity, to free slaves, and to repent. Likewise is done for the lunar eclipse, except that he recites aloud in it, because it is nocturnal.

As for its time: It is from the beginning of the eclipse until its complete clearing. Its time exits when the sun sets while still eclipsed. The prayer of the lunar eclipse is missed when the disk of the sun rises, for the dominion of the night is nullified; it is not missed by the moon setting while eclipsed, because the entire night is the dominion of the moon. If the eclipse clears during the prayer, he completes it in a lightened manner. Whoever catches the second bowing with the imam has missed that rakʿah, for the foundational element is the first bowing.

The second is the prayer for rain (istisqā'). When rivers dry up, rains cease, or a canal collapses, it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the imam to first command the people to fast for three days, to give as much charity as they can, to restore wrongs (maẓālim), and to repent from sins. Then he goes out with them on the fourth day, along with the elderly women and children, in a state of cleanliness, wearing humble garments, with meekness and humility — contrary to the Festival prayer (ʿĪd). It is said that it is recommended to bring out the livestock to share in the need, due to his saying, peace be upon him: "Were it not for suckling infants, kneeling elders, and grazing beasts, punishment would have been poured upon you." If the People of the Covenant (ahl al-dhimmah) also go out, distinguished, they are not prevented. When they gather at the prayer place (muṣallā) adjoining the open desert, the call is made, "Prayer is gathering." The imam leads them in two rakʿahs like the Festival prayer, without the extra takbīrs, then delivers two sermons with a light sitting between them. The seeking of forgiveness (istighfār) should be the predominant part of the two sermons. In the middle of the second sermon, he should turn his back to the people and face the qiblah, and turn his cloak (ridā') at that moment, as an omen of the transformation of the state — thus did the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, act. He makes its upper part lower, what is on the right to the left, and what is on the left to the right. The people do likewise and supplicate secretly at that moment. Then he faces them and concludes the sermon, while they keep their cloaks turned until they remove them when they remove their garments.

He says in the supplication: "O God, You have commanded us to supplicate You and promised us Your response. We have supplicated You as You commanded us, so respond to us as You promised us. O God, bestow upon us forgiveness for what we have committed, and Your response in our rain, and the abundance of our provisions." There is no harm in supplication after the obligatory prayers during the three days before going out. This supplication has inner etiquettes and conditions — repentance, restoration of wrongs, and others — which will come in the Book of Supplications (Kitāb al-Daʿawāt).

The third is the funeral prayer (ṣalāt al-janāzah). Its modality is well-known. The most comprehensive transmitted supplication is what is related in the Ṣaḥīḥ from ʿAwf ibn Mālik, who said: "I saw the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, pray over a funeral, and I memorized from his supplication: {«اللهم اغفر له وارحمه وعافه واعف عنه وأكرم نزله ووسع مدخله واغسله بالماء والثلج والبرد ونقه من الخطايا كما ينقى الثوب الأبيض من الدنس وأبدله دارا خيرا من داره وأهلا خيرا من أهله وزوجا خيرا من زوجه وأدخله الجنة وأعذه من عذاب القبر ومن عذاب النار»} — 'O God, forgive him, have mercy on him, grant him well-being, pardon him, honor his resting place, widen his entrance, wash him with water, snow, and hail, purify him from sins as a white garment is purified from filth, and give him a better home than his home, a better family than his family, a better spouse than his spouse. Admit him to Paradise and protect him from the punishment of the grave and the punishment of the Fire.'" — until ʿAwf said: "I wished that I myself were that deceased person."

Whoever catches the second takbīr should observe the order of the prayer in himself and say the takbīr with the imam's takbīrs. When the imam gives the salutation, he makes up the takbīr he missed, like the one who is preceded (masbūq). For if he hastened the takbīrs, there would remain no meaning for following (iqtidā') in this prayer. The takbīrs are the apparent pillars (arkān), and it is fitting that they stand in place of the bowings in other prayers. This is the most correct view in my opinion, even if another is possible.

The reports concerning the virtue of the funeral prayer and following the bier are well-known, so we will not prolong by citing them. How could its virtue not be great, given that it is among the communal obligations (farā'iḍ al-kifāyāt)? It only becomes supererogatory for one upon whom it is not individually incumbent due to the presence of others. Then he attains the virtue of the communal obligation even if not individually incumbent, because they all together fulfilled what is a communal obligation and removed the burden from others. Thus it is not like a supererogatory act that removes no obligation from anyone. It is recommended to seek a large gathering, seeking blessing in the multitude of intentions and supplications, and its inclusion of one whose supplication is answered — as related by Kurayb from Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with him, that a son of his died, and he said: "O Kurayb, see how many people have gathered for him." He said: "I went out and found people gathered for him, and I informed him." He said: "Do you say they are forty?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Bring him out, for I heard the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, say: {«ما من رجل مسلم يموت فيقوم على جنازته أربعون رجلا لا يشركون بالله شيئا إلا شفعهم الله عز وجل فيه»} — 'There is no Muslim man who dies, and forty men stand over his funeral, not associating anything with God, except that God, Mighty and Majestic, accepts their intercession for him.'" When one follows the funeral and reaches the graves, or enters the cemetery, he says: "Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of these abodes, from among the believers and Muslims. May God have mercy on those who have preceded us and those who will come after. And we, God willing, shall join you."

It is preferable not to depart until the deceased is buried. When the grave is leveled over the deceased, he stands over it and says: "O God, Your servant has returned to You, so be kind to him and have mercy on him. O God, make the earth spacious for his sides, open the gates of heaven to his soul, and accept him from You with a good word. O God, if he was virtuous, multiply his virtue; and if he was sinful, overlook him."

The fourth is the greeting of the mosque (taḥiyyat al-masjid) — two rakʿahs or more, a confirmed Sunnah (sunnah mu'akkadah), such that it is not dropped even if the imam is delivering the sermon on Friday, despite the confirmed obligation to listen attentively to the preacher. If one occupies himself with an obligatory prayer or a make-up prayer, the greeting is fulfilled thereby and the virtue is attained, for the purpose is that the beginning of one's entry should not be devoid of worship specific to the mosque, fulfilling the right of the mosque. For this reason, it is disliked to enter the mosque without ablution. If one enters for passage or sitting, let him say: "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest" — saying it four times. It is said that this equals two rakʿahs in virtue.

The school of al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, holds that the greeting is not disliked in the disliked times — namely, after the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr), after the dawn prayer (ṣubḥ), at the time of zenith (zawāl), and at the times of sunrise and sunset — due to what is related that he, peace be upon him, prayed two rakʿahs after the ʿaṣr, and it was said to him: "Did you not forbid us from this?" He said: "These are two rakʿahs I used to pray after the ẓuhr, and the delegation occupied me from them." This hadith yields two benefits. One: the dislike is confined to a prayer with no cause, and among the weakest causes is the making up of supererogatory prayers, since scholars differ on whether supererogatory prayers are made up. If one does what he missed, is it a make-up? If the dislike is removed by the weakest of causes, then a fortiori it is removed by entering the mosque, which is a strong cause. For this reason, the funeral prayer when present, and the eclipse and rain prayers, are not disliked in these times, because they have causes.

The second benefit: the making up of supererogatory prayers, for the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, made up that prayer, and we have in him a good example. ʿĀ'ishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "When the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was overcome by sleep or illness and did not stand for the night prayer, he prayed twelve rakʿahs at the beginning of the day." The scholars have said: Whoever is in prayer and misses responding to the caller to prayer (mu'adhdhin), when he finishes, he makes it up and responds, even if the caller has fallen silent. There is no meaning now to the saying of one who says that this is like the first and is not made up — for if it were so, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, would not have prayed it in the disliked time.

Indeed, whoever has a regular devotion (wird) and an excuse prevents him from it should not grant himself license to abandon it, but rather make it up at another time, so that his soul does not incline toward ease and comfort. Making it up is good as a means of striving against the soul (mujāhadat al-nafs), and because he, peace be upon him, said: {«أحب الأعمال إلى الله تعالى أدومها وإن قل»} — "The most beloved of deeds to God Almighty is the most constant, even if little." The intent is that one should not slacken in the constancy of his deed. ʿĀ'ishah, may God be pleased with her, related from the Prophet, peace be upon him, that he said: "Whoever worships God, Mighty and Majestic, with a worship, then abandons it out of weariness, God, Mighty and Majestic, will abhor him." Let him beware of falling under this threat. The verification of this report is that God Almighty abhors him for abandoning it out of weariness; were it not for the abhorrence and distancing, weariness would not have been given sway over him.

The fifth is two rakʿahs after ablution, recommended, because ablution is an act of drawing near (qurbah), and its purpose is prayer. Events (ḥadath) are incidental, and perhaps an event may occur before prayer, nullifying the ablution and wasting the effort. Thus hastening to two rakʿahs is the fulfillment of the purpose of ablution before its loss. This is known from the hadith of Bilāl, when he, peace be upon him, said: "I entered Paradise and saw Bilāl there, so I said to Bilāl: 'By what did you precede me to Paradise?' Bilāl said: 'I know nothing except that I do not perform ablution without praying two rakʿahs immediately after it.'"

The sixth is two rakʿahs upon entering the home and upon leaving it. Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, related that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: "When you leave your home, pray two rakʿahs that will protect you from an evil exit; and when you enter your home, pray two rakʿahs that will protect you from an evil entry." In the meaning of this is every matter begun that has significance. Thus two rakʿahs are reported upon entering the state of iḥrām, two rakʿahs at the beginning of a journey, and two rakʿahs upon returning from a journey in the mosque before entering the house — all of this is transmitted from the action of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. Some of the righteous, when they ate a meal, prayed two rakʿahs; when they drank a drink, prayed two rakʿahs; and likewise for every matter they initiated.

The beginnings of matters should be blessed with the remembrance of God, Mighty and Majestic, and they are of three degrees. Some are repeated frequently, like eating and drinking, which begin with the name of God, Mighty and Majestic. He, peace be upon him, said: {«كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فهو أبتر»} — "Every matter of importance not begun with the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate, is cut off." The second is what is not frequently repeated but has significance, like the marriage contract and the beginning of counsel and consultation. It is recommended therein to begin with praise of God (taḥmīd), so the one giving in marriage says: "Praise be to God, and blessings upon the Messenger of God, peace be upon him — I give you my daughter in marriage." The one accepting says: "Praise be to God, and blessings upon the Messenger of God, peace be upon him — I accept the marriage." It was the custom of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, at the beginning of delivering a message, counsel, and consultation, to precede with the taḥmīd. The third is what is not repeated often, and when it occurs it endures and has significance — like travel, purchasing a new house, entering iḥrām, and the like. It is recommended to precede it with two rakʿahs. The least of this is leaving the home and entering it, for it is a kind of short journey.

The seventh is the prayer of seeking guidance (ṣalāt al-istikhārah). Whoever is resolved upon a matter and does not know its outcome, nor knows whether the good is in abandoning it or in proceeding with it, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, commanded him to pray two rakʿahs, reciting in the first the Fātiḥah and {«قل يا أيها الكافرون»} — "Say: O disbelievers" — and in the second the Fātiḥah and {«قل هو الله أحد»} — "Say: He is God, the One." When he finishes, he supplicates and says: "O God, I seek Your guidance through Your knowledge, and I seek Your power through Your might, and I ask You from Your great bounty, for You are able and I am not able, and You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O God, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my worldly life, the outcome of my affair, its immediate and its future, then decree it for me, bless me in it, and make it easy for me. And if You know that this matter is evil for me in my religion, my worldly life, the outcome of my affair, its immediate and its future, then turn me away from it and turn it away from me, and decree for me the good wherever it may be, for You are capable of all things." This was related by Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: "The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, used to teach us the istikhārah in all matters as he taught us a sūrah from the Qur'an." He, peace be upon him, said: "When one of you is resolved upon a matter, let him pray two rakʿahs, then mention the matter and supplicate with what we have mentioned." Some of the sages said: "Whoever is given four things is not denied four things: whoever is given gratitude is not denied increase; whoever is given repentance is not denied acceptance; whoever is given istikhārah is not denied the choice of good; and whoever is given consultation is not denied correctness."

The eighth is the prayer of need (ṣalāt al-ḥājah). Whoever is straitened in his affair, and a need touches him for the rectification of his religion and his worldly life, for a matter that has become difficult for him, let him pray this prayer. It is related from Wahīb ibn al-Ward that he said: "Among the supplications that are not rejected is that the servant prays twelve rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah the Mother of the Book (Fātiḥah), the Throne Verse (āyat al-kursī), and {«قل هو الله أحد»}. When he finishes, he falls into prostration and says: 'Glory be to Him who donned might and spoke with it. Glory be to Him who wrapped Himself in majesty and honored Himself with it. Glory be to Him who enumerated all things in His knowledge. Glory be to Him to whom glorification is due alone. Glory be to the Possessor of favor and bounty. Glory be to the Possessor of might and generosity. Glory be to the Possessor of length. I ask You by the strongholds of might from Your Throne, and the utmost of mercy from Your Book, and by Your greatest name, Your most high majesty, and Your complete and universal words, which no righteous or wicked person can surpass, to send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad.' Then he asks his need, in which there is no disobedience, and he will be answered, God willing, Mighty and Majestic." Wahīb said: "It has reached us that it was said: 'Do not teach it to your foolish ones, lest they use it to cooperate in disobeying God, Mighty and Majestic.'"

The ninth is the prayer of glorification (ṣalāt al-tasbīḥ). This prayer is transmitted in a specific manner, and it is not restricted to a time or a cause. It is recommended that one not let a week pass without it once, or a month once. ʿIkrimah related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with him, that he, peace be upon him, said to al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: "Shall I not give you? Shall I not grant you? Shall I not bestow upon you something that, if you do it, God will forgive you your sin — its first and its last, its old and its new, its error and its deliberate, its secret and its public? You pray four rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah the Fātiḥah and a sūrah. When you finish the recitation in the first rakʿah while standing, you say: 'Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest' — fifteen times. Then you bow and say it while bowing ten times. Then you raise from the bowing and say it standing ten times. Then you prostrate and say it ten times. Then you raise from prostration and say it sitting ten times. Then you prostrate and say it while prostrating ten times. Then you raise from prostration and say it ten times. That is seventy-five in each rakʿah. You do that in four rakʿahs. If you can pray it once every day, do so; if not, then once every Friday; if not, then once every month; if not, then once every year." In another narration, he says at the beginning of the prayer: "Glory be to You, O God, and with Your praise; blessed is Your name; exalted is Your majesty; sanctified are Your names; and there is no god but You." Then he glorifies fifteen times before the recitation and ten after the recitation, and the rest as previously — ten and ten. He does not glorify after the final prostration while sitting. This is the most excellent, and it is the choice of Ibn al-Mubārak. The total from the two narrations is three hundred glorifications. If he prays it by day, then with one salutation; if by night, then with two salutations is better, as it is reported that the night prayer is two by two. If he adds after the glorification the saying: "There is no might and no power except with God, the Most High, the Magnificent," it is good, for that is reported in some narrations. These are the transmitted prayers.

None of these supererogatory prayers is recommended in the disliked times, except the greeting of the mosque and what we have mentioned after the greeting — the two rakʿahs of ablution, the prayer of travel, leaving the home, and istikhārah — no, because the prohibition is emphasized, and these causes are weak, not reaching the degree of the eclipse, the rain prayer, and the greeting. I have seen some Sufis praying the two rakʿahs of ablution in the disliked times, and this is extremely far, because ablution is not a cause for prayer; rather, prayer is the cause for ablution. One should perform ablution in order to pray, not pray because he performed ablution. Every person in a state of minor impurity (muḥdith) who wishes to pray in a disliked time has no way except to perform ablution and pray, so no meaning remains for the dislike. He should not intend the two rakʿahs of ablution as he intends the two rakʿahs of the greeting. Rather, when he performs ablution, he prays two rakʿahs as voluntary worship (taṭawwu'), so that his ablution is not left idle — as Bilāl used to do. It is pure voluntary worship occurring immediately after ablution. The hadith of Bilāl does not indicate that ablution is a cause like the eclipse or the greeting, such that one intends the two rakʿahs of ablution. It is impossible to intend ablution by the prayer; rather, one should intend the prayer by the ablution. How could it be coherent for one to say in his ablution, "I perform ablution for my prayer," and in his prayer, "I pray for my ablution"? Rather, whoever wishes to guard his ablution from idleness in a disliked time should intend a make-up prayer, if it is permissible that there be on his responsibility a prayer that was affected by a defect due to some cause — for making up prayers in disliked times is not disliked. As for the intention of voluntary worship, there is no basis for it.

In the prohibition of disliked times, there are three important matters. One: guarding against resembling the worshippers of the sun. Two: guarding against the spreading of devils, for he, peace be upon him, said: {«إن الشمس لتطلع ومعها قرن الشيطان فإذا طلعت قارنها وإذا ارتفعت فارقها فإن استوت قارنها فإذا زالت فارقها فإذا تضيفت للغروب قارنها فإذا غربت فارقها»} — "The sun rises with a horn of the devil beside it; when it rises, he accompanies it; when it ascends, he separates from it; when it reaches its zenith, he accompanies it; when it declines, he separates from it; when it inclines toward setting, he accompanies it; and when it sets, he separates from it." He forbade prayers in these times and pointed to this as the cause. Three: the travelers of the path to the Hereafter do not cease to be constant in prayers at all times, and constancy in a single pattern of worship breeds weariness. Whenever one is prevented from it for an hour, zeal increases and motivations are stirred, for man is eager for what he is prevented from. In the suspension of these times is an increase of incitement and a spur to await the passing of the time. Thus these times are designated for glorification (tasbīḥ) and seeking forgiveness (istighfār), guarding against weariness through constancy, and seeking relief by transitioning from one type of worship to another. In novelty and renewal there is pleasure and zeal, while in continuing upon one thing there is burden and weariness. For this reason, prayer was not made mere prostration, nor mere bowing, nor mere standing; rather, the acts of worship were arranged from diverse actions and varied remembrances, for the heart perceives from each of them a new pleasure upon transitioning to it. Had one persisted upon a single thing, weariness would hasten to him.

Since these are important matters in the prohibition against engaging in the disliked times — besides other secrets that human power cannot fathom, and God and His Messenger know best — these important matters are not abandoned except for causes that are important in the Law, such as making up prayers, the rain prayer, the eclipse prayer, and the greeting of the mosque. As for what is weaker than these, one should not oppose the purpose of the prohibition with it. This is the most correct view in our opinion, and God knows best.

The Book of the Secrets of Prayer from the Book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences is completed. It will be followed, God willing, by the Book of the Secrets of Almsgiving (Zakāh). With the praise of God, His aid, and His good success. And praise be to God alone, and His blessings upon the best of His creation, Muḥammad, and upon his family and companions, with abundant peace.

chapters.title_en: The Book of the Mysteries of Alms-Tax (Zakāh)
chapters.arabic_text:
| كتاب أسرار الزكاة

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله الذي أسعد وأشقى وأمات وأحيا وأضحك
وأبكى وأوجد وأفنى وأفقر وأغنى وأضر وأقنى الذي خلق الحيوان من نطفة تمنى
ثم تفرد عن الخلق بوصف الغنى ثم خصص بعض عباده بالحسنى فأفاض عليهم من نعمة
ما أيسر به من شاء واستغنى وأحوج إليه من أخفق في رزقه وأكدى إظهارا
للامتحان والابتلا
ثم جعل الزكاة للدين أساسا ومبنى وبين أن  بفضله تزكى من عباده من تزكى
ومن غناه زكى ماله من زكى والصلاة على محمد المصطفى سيد الورى وشمس الهدى
وعلى آله واصحابه المخصوصين بالعلم والتقى
أما بعد فإن الله تعالى جعل الزكاة إحدى مباني الإسلام وأردف بذكرها
الصلاة التي هي أعلى الأعلام فقال تعالى {وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة}
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم بني الإسلام على خمس شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن
محمدا عبده ورسوله وإقام الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة (2) وشدد الوعيد على
المقصرين فيها فقال {والذين يكنزون الذهب والفضة ولا ينفقونها في سبيل الله
فبشرهم بعذاب أليم} ومعنى الإنفاق في سبيل الله إخراج حق الزكاة قال
PageV01P208
الأحنف بن قيس كنت في نفر من قريش فمر أبو ذر فقال بشر الكانزين بكي في
ظهورهم يخرج من جنوبهم وبكي في أقفائهم يخرج من جباههم
وفي رواية أنه يوضع على حلمة ثدي أحدهم فيخرج من نغض كتفيه ويوضع على نغض
كتفيه حتى يخرج من حلمة ثدييه يتزلزل وقال أبو ذر انتهيت إلى رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم وهو جالس في ظل الكعبة فلما رآني قال هم الأخسرون ورب
الكعبة فقلت ومن هم قال الأكثرون أموالا إلا من قال هكذا وهكذا من بين يديه
ومن خلفه وعن يمينه وعن شماله وقليل ما هم ما من صاحب إبل ولا بقر ولا غنم
لا يؤدي زكاتها إلا جاءت يوم القيامة أعظم ما كانت وأسمنه تنطحه بقرونها
وتطؤه بأظلافها كلما نفدت أخراها عادت عليه أولاها حتى يقضى بين الناس (1)
وإذا كان هذا التشديد مخرجا في الصحيحين فقد صار من مهمات الدين الكشف عن
أسرار الزكاة وشروطها الجلية والخفية ومعانيها الظاهرة والباطنة مع
الاقتصار على ما لا يستغنى عن معرفته مؤدي الزكاة وقابضها وينكشف ذلك في
أربعة فصول
الفصل الأول في أنواع الزكاة وأسباب وجوبها
الثاني آدابها وشروطها الباطنة والظاهرة
الثالث في القابض وشروط استحقاقه وآداب قبضه
الرابع في صدقة التطوع وفضلها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ك-و (Zāy-Kāf-Wāw)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, increase, purification; the core sense of thriving and cleansing—as a plant thrives (zakā al-zarʿ) and a soul is purified from defilement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qurʾān, zakāh denotes both the obligatory alms and the spiritual purification it effects; it is the act that causes the soul to grow in merit and the wealth to be blessed, linked to divine grace (tazkiyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage is botanical/economic growth; metaphorical (majāz) usage is the purification of the self and wealth through giving—the transfer of surplus as a divine ordinance.
- Root: ك-ن-ز (Kāf-Nūn-Zāy)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To amass and hoard treasure (kanz); the root implies concealment and accumulation of wealth without disbursement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Qurʾānic threat against "those who hoard gold and silver" (al-kānizūn), the term is restricted to those who withhold the obligatory right (ḥaqq) of God from wealth—not mere possession.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: storing treasure; metaphorical: withholding the due alms, since the harm lies in the refusal to expend, not in the storing itself.
- Root: خ-ل-ف (Khā-Lām-Fā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To succeed, come after, or fail (akhfaqa); the root carries the sense of trailing behind and disappointment in seeking provision.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine alternation of states—wealth and poverty—as a test (imtiḥān); the one who "fails" (akhfaqa) in sustenance is made needy to manifest divine wisdom in trial.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to miss the mark in seeking; metaphorical: the divinely ordained disparity of provision as an instrument of probation.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Inceptive Clauses (al-Ibtidāʾ) — The opening doxology (khuṭbah) employs nominal sentences (jumal ismiyyah) with the predicate as a fresh assertion (faṣl), establishing the divine attributes as permanent states, not contingent events; the subsequent conditional and relative clauses (ṣilah) are governed by the principle of taʿlīq, where the apodosis is suspended on the protasis for rhetorical emphasis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Praise belongs to God, who made some fortunate and some wretched, who causes death and gives life, who makes to laugh and makes to weep, who brings into existence and annihilates, who impoverishes and enriches, who harms and benefits. He created the living being from a drop of fluid that is emitted (nutfah), then He alone, to the exclusion of all creation, is characterized by self-sufficiency (ghinā). He then singled out certain of His servants for the most beautiful reward (al-ḥusnā), and poured upon them from His bounty—making easy the means of livelihood for whomsoever He willed, who then became independent, and making needy whomsoever He caused to fail in his provision and to be disappointed, as a manifestation of trial and testing (imtiḥān wa ibtilāʾ).

Then He made the alms-tax (zakāh) a foundation and a structure for the religion, and He made clear that by His grace is purified whoever is purified among His servants, and from His riches is purified the wealth of whoever gives alms. And blessings be upon Muḥammad, the Chosen One, the master of all creatures, the sun of guidance, and upon his family and companions, who are distinguished by knowledge and piety.

To proceed: God—exalted is He—made the alms-tax one of the pillars of Islam, and He coupled its mention with the prayer (ṣalāh), which is the loftiest of the symbols of faith. He said—exalted is He: {«And establish the prayer and give the alms-tax»} (Q 2:43). And the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger, the establishment of prayer, and the giving of alms-tax." And He intensified the threat against those who fall short in it, saying: {«And those who hoard gold and silver and do not expend them in the way of God—give them tidings of a painful chastisement»} (Q 9:34). The meaning of "expending in the way of God" is the discharge of the obligatory right of the alms-tax.

Al-Aḥnaf ibn Qays said: I was among a group of Quraysh when Abū Dharr passed by and said: "Give tidings to the hoarders of a branding iron that will be applied to their backs, emerging from their sides, and a branding iron applied to their napes, emerging from their foreheads." In another narration: "It will be placed on the nipple of one of their breasts, and it will emerge from the cartilage of his shoulder-blades; and it will be placed on the cartilage of his shoulder-blades until it emerges from the nipples of his breasts, while he trembles violently."

And Abū Dharr said: I came upon the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—while he was sitting in the shade of the Kaʿbah. When he saw me, he said: "They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah!" I said: "Who are they?" He said: "Those who are most abundant in wealth—except for the one who gives from before him, from behind him, from his right, and from his left—and few they are!" And he said: "There is no owner of camels, cattle, or sheep who does not pay their alms-tax, but they will come on the Day of Resurrection in their most enormous and fattest state, goring him with their horns and trampling him with their hooves. Whenever the last of them has passed, the first of them returns upon him, until judgment is rendered among the people."

Now, since this severe threat is transmitted in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (of Bukhārī and Muslim), it has become among the most important matters of the religion to unveil the mysteries of the alms-tax, its conditions both manifest and hidden, and its meanings both outward and inward—while confining ourselves to what the payer of alms and the receiver of alms cannot dispense with knowing. This will be disclosed in four chapters:

Chapter One: On the kinds of alms-tax and the causes of its obligation.
Chapter Two: On its etiquettes and its conditions, both inward and outward.
Chapter Three: On the receiver, the conditions of his eligibility, and the etiquettes of his receiving.
Chapter Four: On voluntary almsgiving (ṣadaqat al-taṭawwuʿ) and its merit.

chapters.title_en: The First Chapter on the Types of Alms (Zakāh), the Causes of Their Obligation, and the Categories of Alms According to Their Objects
chapters.arabic_text: || الفصل الأول في أنواع الزكاة وأسباب وجوبها والزكوات باعتبار متعلقاتها ستة أنواع  زكاة النعم والنقدين والتجارة وزكاة الركاز والمعادن وزكاة المعشرات وزكاة الفطر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ك-و (Z-K-W)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, increase, purification; in legal terms, the obligatory due that purifies wealth and causes it to flourish.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Zakāh as a purifying act of worship (ʿibādah) that cleanses the soul from avarice and the wealth from impurity, linked to Quranic usage {«خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا»}.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of growth and blessing; metaphorical (majāz) in the legal obligation, as it is a cause for increase in divine reward.
- Root: ن-ع-م (N-ʿ-M)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Livestock, specifically camels, cattle, sheep, and goats; also denotes grace and bounty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic context, the term is restricted to grazing animals (sāʾimah) that are pastured for most of the year, as opposed to working animals.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the animals themselves; metaphorical for the divine grace that necessitates gratitude through alms.
- Root: ر-ك-ز (R-K-Z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Buried treasure; from the root meaning to plant or fix in the earth; also used for a mine (maʿdin) as a fixed deposit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Rikāz refers to pre-Islamic buried hoards (kanz) and minerals extracted from the earth, both subject to a one-fifth (khums) levy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for what is fixed in the ground; metaphorical for the obligation that is fixed upon the finder.
- Root: ع-ش-ر (ʿ-Sh-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The tenth part; ʿushr (tithe) on agricultural produce.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The tenth levied on lands watered by rain or natural sources, as opposed to half-tenth on irrigated lands.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the numerical fraction; metaphorical for the entire category of agricultural dues.
- Root: ف-ط-ر (F-Ṭ-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Breaking the fast; also creation or origination (fiṭrah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Zakāt al-Fiṭr is the alms of breaking the fast of Ramaḍān, obligatory on every Muslim, free or slave, male or female, young or old, as a purification for the faster.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the act of breaking fast; metaphorical for the alms tied to that occasion.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The enumeration of six types after the general statement "six types" is a clarifying apposition (badal), where each item is syntactically coordinated by wa (and), establishing a comprehensive division without redundancy.
chapters.translation: I say: The first chapter concerns the types of alms (zakāh), the causes of their obligation, and the alms, considered with respect to their objects (mutaʿallaqāt), are six types: the alms of livestock (zakat al-naʿam), of the two precious metals (al-naqdayn) — namely gold and silver — and of trade goods (al-tijārah); the alms of buried treasure (al-rikāz) and of mines (al-maʿādin); the alms of tithed produce (al-muʿashsharāt) — that is, agricultural yields subject to the tenth or half-tenth; and the alms of breaking the fast (zakāt al-fiṭr). These six categories exhaust the objects upon which alms are due, and their causes of obligation vary between the growth of wealth, the passage of a lunar year (ḥawl), and the specific occasions ordained by the Law (al-Sharʿ).

chapters.title_en: The First Type: Zakāh on Grazing Livestock (Zakāt al-Naʿam)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| النوع الأول زكاة النعم

ولا تجب هذه الزكاة وغيرها إلا على حر مسلم
ولا يشترط البلوغ بل تجب في مال الصبي والمجنون هذا شرط من عليه
وأما المال فشروطه خمسة أن يكون نعما سائمة باقية حولا نصابا كاملا
مملوكا على الكمال
الشرط الأول كونه نعما فلا زكاة إلا في الإبل والبقر والغنم
أما الخيل والبغال والحمير والمتولد من بين الظباء والغنم فلا زكاة فيها
الثاني السوم فلا زكاة في معلوفة وإذا أسيمت في وقت وعلفت في وقت تظهر
بذلك مؤنتها فلا زكاة فيها
الثالث الحول قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا زكاة في مال حتى يحول
عليه الحول (2) ويستثنى من هذا نتاج الحول
الرابع كمال الملك والتصرف فتجب الزكاة في الماشية المرهونة لأنه الذي
حجر على نفسه فيه ولا تجب في الضال والمغصوب إلا إذا عاد بجميع نمائه فيجب
زكاة ما مضى عند عوده ولو كان عليه دين يستغرق ماله فلا زكاة عليه فإنه ليس
غنيا به إذ الغنى ما يفضل عن الحاجة
الخامس كمال النصاب
أما الإبل فلا شيء فيها حتى تبلغ خمسا ففيها جذعة من الضأن والجذعة هي
التي تكون في السنة الثانية أو ثنية من المعز وهي التي تكون في السنة
الثالثة
وفي عشر شاتان وفي خمس عشرة ثلاث شياه
وفي عشرين أربع شياه
وفي خمس وعشرين بنت مخاض وهي التي في السنة الثانية فإن لم يكن في ماله
بنت مخاض فابن لبون ذكر وهو الذي في السنة الثالثة يؤخذ إن كان قادرا على
شرائها وفي ست وثلاثين ابنة لبون
ثم إذا بلغت ستا وأربعين ففيها حقة وهي التي في السنة الرابعة
فإذا صارت إحدى وستين ففيها جذعة وهي التي في السنة الخامسة
فإذا صارت ستا وسبعين ففيها بنتا لبون
فإذا صارت إحدى وتسعين ففيها حقتان
فإذا صارت إحدى وعشرين ومائة ففيها ثلاث بنات لبون
فإذا صارت مائة وثلاثين فقد استقر الحساب ففي كل  خمسين حقة وفي كل أربعين
بنت لبون PageV01P209
وأما البقر فلا شيء فيها حتى تبلغ ثلاثين ففيها تبيع وهو الذي في السنة
الثانية
ثم في أربعين مسنة وهي التي في السنة الثالثة
ثم في ستين تبيعان
واستقر الحساب بعد ذلك
ففي كل أربعين مسنة
وفي كل ثلاثين تبيع
وأما الغنم فلا زكاة فيها حتى تبلغ أربعين ففيها شاة جذعة من الضأن أو
ثنية من المعز
ثم لا شيء فيها حتى تبلغ مائة وعشرين وواحدة ففيها شاتان
إلى مائتي شاة وواحدة فيها ثلاث شياه إلى أربعمائة ففيها أربع شياه
ثم استقر الحساب في كل مائة شاة
وصدقة الخليطين كصدقة المالك الواحد في النصاب فإذا كان بين رجلين أربعون
من الغنم ففيها شاة
وإن كان بين ثلاثة نفر مائة شاة وعشرون ففيها شاة واحدة
على جميعهم
وخلطة الجوار كخلطة الشيوع ولكن يشترط أن يريحا معا ويسقيا معا ويحلبا
معا ويسرحا معا ويكون المرعى معا ويكون إنزاء الفحل معا
وأن يكونا جميعا من أهل الزكاة ولا حكم للخلطة مع الذمي والمكاتب
ومهما نزل في واجب الإبل عن سن إلى سن فهو جائز ما لم يجاوز بنت مخاض في
النزول
ولكن تضم إليه جبران السن لسنة واحدة شاتين أو عشرين درهما
ولسنتين أربع شياه أو أربعين درهما
وله أن يصعد في السن ما لم يجاوز الجذعة في الصعود ويأخذ الجبران من
الساعين من بيت المال
ولا تؤخذ في الزكاة مريضة إذا كان بعض المال صحيحا ولو واحدة
ويؤخذ من الكرائم كريمة ومن اللئام لئيمة
ولا يؤخذ من المال الأكولة ولا الماخض ولا الربا ولا الفحل ولا غراء
المال
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ك-و (Z-K-W)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, increase, purification; zakāh as that which purifies wealth through disbursement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Obligatory alms as a purifying act (taṭhīr) of the soul and property, tied to divine command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is growth; metaphorical (majāz) usage denotes the fixed charitable due, as it "grows" the remainder in blessing.
- Root: س-و-م (S-W-M)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pasturing freely; livestock left to graze on unowned land.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Condition for zakāh—distinguishing free-grazing (sāʾimah) from stall-fed (maʿlūfah) animals.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: grazing; technical: the legal category triggering zakāh obligation.
- Root: ح-و-ل (Ḥ-W-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Turning, passing of time; a full lunar year.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The temporal condition (ḥawl) for zakāh liability on accumulated wealth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: revolution of time; legal: completion of one year.
- Root: ن-ص-ب (N-Ṣ-B)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Setting up, erecting; a fixed limit or threshold.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The minimum quantum (niṣāb) below which no zakāh is due.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: erected mark; technical: the taxable minimum.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clauses with Implied Apodosis (Sharṭ maʿa ḥadhf al-jawāb) — In phrases like "If it reaches five, then therein is a jadhaʿah," the apodosis is a nominal sentence indicating obligation, governed by the conditional particle.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first type is the zakāh on grazing livestock.

This zakāh and others are not obligatory except upon a free Muslim. Puberty is not a condition; rather, it is obligatory upon the wealth of a minor and an insane person—this is the condition pertaining to the one upon whom it is due.

As for the wealth itself, its conditions are five: that it be grazing livestock, that it remain (in one's possession) for a full year, that it reach a complete niṣāb, and that it be owned in full.

The first condition: that it be livestock (naʿam). Thus, no zakāh is due except upon camels, cattle, and sheep/goats. As for horses, mules, donkeys, and what is produced from the crossing of gazelles and sheep, there is no zakāh upon them.

The second: free grazing (sawm). There is no zakāh upon stall-fed animals. If they are grazed at one time and fed at another, such that their maintenance cost becomes apparent, then there is no zakāh upon them.

The third: the passing of the year (ḥawl). The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: {«لَا زَكَاةَ فِي مَالٍ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ»} — "There is no zakāh upon wealth until a year has passed over it." Excepted from this is the offspring born within the year (natāj al-ḥawl).

The fourth: completeness of ownership and disposal. Zakāh is obligatory upon mortgaged livestock, because the owner has only restricted himself therein. It is not obligatory upon a lost animal or a usurped one, unless it returns with all its increase—then zakāh for the elapsed period is due upon its return. Even if one has a debt that consumes all his wealth, no zakāh is due upon him, for he is not wealthy by it, since wealth (ghinā) is what exceeds one's need.

The fifth: completeness of the niṣāb.

As for camels: nothing is due until they reach five. Then therein is one jadhaʿah of sheep—the jadhaʿah being one in its second year—or one thaniyyah of goats, which is one in its third year.

In ten: two sheep.
In fifteen: three sheep.
In twenty: four sheep.
In twenty-five: a bint makhāḍ—that which is in its second year. If one does not possess a bint makhāḍ, then a ibn labūn male—that which is in its third year—is taken, if he is able to purchase it.
In thirty-six: a bint labūn.

Then when they reach forty-six, therein is a ḥiqqah—that which is in its fourth year.
When they become sixty-one, therein is a jadhaʿah—that which is in its fifth year.
When they become seventy-six, therein are two bint labūn.
When they become ninety-one, therein are two ḥiqqahs.
When they become one hundred and twenty-one, therein are three bint labūn.
When they reach one hundred and thirty, the reckoning is settled: for every fifty, one ḥiqqah; and for every forty, one bint labūn.

As for cattle: nothing is due until they reach thirty. Then therein is a tabīʿ—that which is in its second year.
Then in forty: a musinnah—that which is in its third year.
Then in sixty: two tabīʿs.
The reckoning is settled after that: for every forty, a musinnah; and for every thirty, a tabīʿ.

As for sheep/goats: no zakāh is due until they reach forty. Then therein is one sheep—a jadhaʿah of sheep or a thaniyyah of goats.
Then nothing is due until they reach one hundred and twenty-one. Then therein are two sheep.
Up to two hundred and one: therein are three sheep.
Up to four hundred: therein are four sheep.
Then the reckoning is settled: for every hundred, one sheep.

The zakāh of two partners (khalīṭayn) is like that of a single owner regarding the niṣāb. Thus, if forty sheep are between two men, one sheep is due therein. If one hundred and twenty sheep are between three persons, one sheep is due upon all of them collectively.

Partnership by proximity (khilṭat al-jiwār) is like partnership by common ownership (khilṭat al-shuyūʿ), but with the condition that they pasture together, water together, milk together, send out to graze together, share the same pasture, and that the stallion's covering be done together. Both must be among those liable for zakāh—there is no effect of partnership with a dhimmī or a mukātab.

Whenever one descends in the obligatory (age) category of camels from one age to a lower age, it is permissible, so long as he does not descend below a bint makhāḍ. However, he must add a compensation for the age difference (jubrān al-sinn) for one year: two sheep or twenty dirhams; for two years: four sheep or forty dirhams. He may also ascend in age, so long as he does not ascend above a jadhaʿah, and he takes the compensation from the collectors (sāʿīn) from the treasury (bayt al-māl).

A sick animal is not taken in zakāh if part of the wealth is healthy—even if only one. From the choice animals, a choice one is taken; from the inferior ones, an inferior one. The milch ewe (akūlah), the pregnant one (mākhiḍ), the breeding ram (rabā), the stud (faḥl), and the choicest of the wealth (ghirāʾ al-māl) are not taken.

chapters.title_en: The Second Type: The Alms-Tithe on Irrigated and Rain-Fed Crops (Zakāt al-Muʿsharāt)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| النوع الثاني زكاة المعشرات

فيجب العشر في كل مستنبت مقتات بلغ ثمانمائة من ولا شيء فيما دونها ولا
في الفواكه والقطن ولكن في الحبوب التي تقتات وفي التمر والزبيب
ويعتبر أن تكون ثمانمائة من تمرا أو زبيبا لا رطبا وعنبا ويخرج ذلك بعد
التجفيف
ويكمل مال أحد الخليطين بمال الآخر في خلطة الشيوع كالبستان المشترك بين
ورثة  لجميعهم ثمانمائة من من زبيب فيجب على جميعهم ثمانون منا من زبيب بقدر
حصصهم
ولا يعتبر خلطة الجوار فيه
ولا يكمل نصاب الحنطة بالشعير
ويكمل نصاب الشعير بالسلت فإنه نوع منه هذا قدر الواجب إن كان يسقى بسيح
أو قناة فإن كان يسقى بنضح أو دالية فيجب نصف العشر فإن اجتمعا فالأغلب
يعتبر
وأما صفة الواجب فالتمر والزبيب اليابس والحب اليابس بعد التنقية
ولا يؤخذ عنب ولا رطب إلا إذا حلت بالأشجار آفة وكانت المصلحة في قطعها
قبل تمام الإدراك فيؤخذ الرطب فيكال تسعة للمالك وواحد للفقير
ولا يمنع من هذه القسمة قولنا إن القسمة بيع بل يرخص في مثل هذا للحاجة
ووقت الوجوب أن يبدو الصلاح في الثمار وأن يشتد الحب
ووقت الأداء بعد الجفاف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ش-ر (ʿ-sh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The tenth part; the tithe levied on agricultural produce.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The obligatory share (ḥaqq) ordained on produce of the earth, tied to the divine command of purifying wealth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the tenth; metaphorical (majāz) for the entire obligatory due, as the term extends to half-tenth.
- Root: ق-و-ت (q-w-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sustenance; that which preserves life and is stored for subsistence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The staple foodstuff (qūt) that meets the essential need of the body, distinguishing it from luxury fruits.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for edible grains and dates; metaphorical for any stored provision.
- Root: خ-ل-ط (kh-l-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Mixing, blending; co-ownership in a shared property.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legal commingling (khilṭah) of shares that unites the owners for the purpose of completing the nisāb.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical mixing; metaphorical for legal unity of interest, as in joint inheritance.
- Root: س-ق-ي (s-q-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Irrigation; watering by natural or artificial means.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The mode of watering determines the rate of due—natural (unpaid) versus artificial (paid) irrigation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the act of watering; metaphorical for the cause that determines the legal obligation.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The particle "in" (if) introduces a condition whose apodosis is governed by the protasis, as in "in kāna yusqā... fa-yajibu" (if it is watered... then half-tithe is due), requiring precise parsing of the conditional structure.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second type is the alms-tithe on irrigated and rain-fed crops (zakāt al-muʿsharāt).

Thus, the full tithe is obligatory on every cultivated staple foodstuff (mūqitat) that reaches eight hundred mann (in weight); nothing is due on what is less than that, nor on fruits and cotton. Rather, it applies to grains that are staple foods, and to dried dates and raisins. It is required that the eight hundred mann be of dried dates or raisins, not fresh dates or fresh grapes, and it is extracted after drying.

The wealth of one of two partners is completed by the wealth of the other in a commingling of common ownership (khilṭat al-shuyūʿ)—such as a shared orchard among heirs. If all of them together possess eight hundred mann of raisins, then eighty mann of raisins is obligatory upon all of them, in proportion to their shares. Commingling by mere adjacency (khilṭat al-jiwār) is not considered therein.

Nor is the nisāb of wheat completed by barley. But the nisāb of barley is completed by spelt (sult), for it is a species of it. This is the extent of the obligatory due if the crop is watered by a flowing channel (sayḥ) or an underground conduit (qanāt). But if it is watered by a water-wheel (naḍḥ) or a bucket-lift (dāliyah), then half of the tithe is obligatory. If both modes are combined, then the predominant one is considered.

As for the description of the obligatory due: it is dried dates, dried raisins, and dried grain, after purification (tanqiyah). Neither fresh grapes nor fresh dates are taken, except when a blight afflicts the trees and the benefit lies in cutting them before full ripening. Then the fresh dates are taken and measured out, giving nine parts to the owner and one to the poor. This division is not prevented by our statement that division is a sale; rather, it is permitted in such a case due to necessity.

The time of obligation is when the fruit begins to ripen (budūw al-ṣalāḥ) and when the grain hardens. The time of payment is after drying.

chapters.title_en: The Third Type: Alms on the Two Precious Metals (Gold and Silver)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| النوع الثالث زكاة النقدين

فإذا تم الحول على وزن مائتي درهم بوزن مكة نقرة خالصة ففيها خمسة دراهم
وهو ربع العشر وما زاد فبحسابه ولو درهما
ونصاب الذهب عشرون مثقالا خالصا بوزن مكة ففيها ربع العشر وما زاد
فبحسابه وإن نقص من النصاب حبة فلا زكاة
وتجب على من معه دراهم مغشوشة إذا كان فيها هذا المقدار من النقرة
الخالصة
وتجب الزكاة في التبر وفي الحلي المحظور كأواني الذهب والفضة ومراكب
الذهب للرجال
ولا تجب في الحلي المباح
وتجب في الدين الذي هو على ملىء ولكن تجب عند الاستيفاء وإن كان مؤجلا
فلا تجب إلا عند حلول الأجل
PageV01P210
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ك-و (Z-K-W)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, increase, purification; the obligatory alms (zakāh) that purifies wealth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Zakāh as a divinely ordained right (ḥaqq) in wealth, effecting spiritual purification and communal equity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of growth and blessing; metaphorical extension to the obligatory due that causes the remainder to thrive.
- Root: ن-ص-ب (N-Ṣ-B)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To set up, erect; the threshold (niṣāb) as the fixed limit at which obligation commences.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The legally defined minimum quantum of wealth triggering the duty, rooted in the notion of standing firm (naṣaba) as a criterion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: erecting a marker; metaphorical: the established measure for liability.
- Root: ح-و-ل (Ḥ-W-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The turning of time; the completion of a lunar year (ḥawl) as the period of possession.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The full cycle of the year, signifying stability and continuity of ownership.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the revolution of time; metaphorical: the lapse of the full year as a condition for obligation.
- Root: ت-ب-ر (T-B-R)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pure uncoined gold or silver; raw bullion (tibr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Unworked metal, distinct from coined currency, yet equally subject to zakāh.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: ore or nugget; metaphorical: any unminted precious metal held for value.
- Root: ح-ل-ي (Ḥ-L-Y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ornament, adornment (ḥilyah); jewelry.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Decorative items; their legal status depends on permissibility of use (mubāḥ) versus prohibition (maḥẓūr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: adornment; metaphorical: the legal ruling attached to the object's permitted or forbidden employment.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Completion of Time (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The sentence «فإذا تم الحول» establishes a temporal-condition construction where the completion of the year (ḥawl) is the protasis, and the obligation of five dirhams is the apodosis, governed by the particle 'idhā' indicating a definite future condition.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third type is the alms on the two precious metals (zakāh al-naqdayn).

When a full year (ḥawl) has elapsed upon the weight of two hundred dirhams, by the Meccan weight, of pure silver (naqrah khāliṣah), then upon it is five dirhams — and that is one-quarter of the tenth (rubʿ al-ʿushr). Whatever exceeds that is reckoned proportionally, even if it be a single dirham. The niṣāb of gold is twenty mithqāls of pure gold, by the Meccan weight; upon it is one-quarter of the tenth, and whatever exceeds is reckoned proportionally. If the niṣāb is deficient by even a single grain (ḥabbah), then no zakāh is due.

Zakāh is obligatory upon one who possesses debased dirhams (maghshūshah) if within them there is this amount of pure silver (al-naqrah al-khāliṣah).

Zakāh is obligatory upon raw bullion (al-tibr) and upon prohibited ornaments (al-ḥily al-maḥẓūr), such as vessels of gold and silver, and gold mounts for men. It is not obligatory upon permissible ornaments (al-ḥily al-mubāḥ).

Zakāh is obligatory upon a debt owed by a solvent debtor (malīʾ), but it becomes obligatory only upon its recovery (istīfāʾ). If the debt is deferred (muʾajjal), then it is not obligatory except upon the arrival of its term (ḥulūl al-ajal).

chapters.title_en: The Fourth Kind: Zakāh on Trade Goods
chapters.arabic_text:
||| النوع الرابع زكاة التجارة

وهي كزكاة النقدين وإنما ينعقد الحول من وقت ملك النقد الذي به اشترى
البضاعة إن كان النقد نصابا فإن كان ناقصا أو اشترى بعرض على نية التجارة
فالحول من وقت الشراء
وتؤدى الزكاة من نقد البلد وبه يقوم
فإن كان ما به الشراء نقدا وكان نصابا كاملا كان التقويم به أولى من نقد
البلد
ومن نوى التجارة من مال قنية فلا ينعقد الحول بمجرد نيته حتى يشتري به
شيئا ومهما قطع نية التجارة قبل تمام الحول سقطت الزكاة
والأولى أن تؤدى زكاة  تلك السنة وما كان من ربح في السلعة في آخر الحول
وجبت الزكاة فيه بحول رأس المال ولم يستأنف له حولا كما في النتاج
وأموال الصيارفة لا ينقطع حولها بالمبادلة الجارية بينهم كسائر التجارات
وزكاة ربح مال القراض على العامل وإن كان قبل القسمة هذا هو الأقيس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ك-و (Z-K-W)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, increase, purification; zakāh as that which purifies wealth through prescribed disbursement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Obligatory alms tied to surplus wealth (māl al-namāʾ), signifying both spiritual purification and material increment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "growth" (numuww) applied to wealth; metaphorical extension to ritual purification of the soul.
- Root: ح-و-ل (Ḥ-W-L)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Turning, passing of time; the annual cycle (ḥawl) marking zakāh liability.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Completion of a lunar year as a legal condition (sharṭ) for obligation, not intrinsic to the wealth itself.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Temporal metaphor — the "turning" of the year over the asset.
- Root: ق-و-م (Q-W-M)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Standing, establishing value; taqwīm as valuation of goods in monetary terms.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Assessment of market worth to determine zakāh threshold (niṣāb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "erecting" a price; metaphorical for fixing equivalence in exchange.
