Sleep overcame me, and behold, the two figures descended in their form. One called to his companion and repeated the very same words, then said: 'Do you know what our Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed this night?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'He has bestowed upon each of the six one hundred thousand.' I awoke with a joy beyond description."

And from him also, may God be pleased with him, he said: "I performed the pilgrimage in a certain year. When I had completed my rites (manāsik), I reflected upon the one whose pilgrimage is not accepted, and I said: 'O God, I have bestowed my pilgrimage and made its reward for the one whose pilgrimage You have not accepted.' He said: 'Then I saw the Lord of Might in a dream — glorified be His Majesty — and He said to me: "O ʿAlī, are you being generous with Me, while I created generosity and the generous? I am the Most Generous of the generous and the Most Munificent of the munificent, and more worthy of munificence and generosity than all the worlds. I have bestowed upon everyone whose pilgrimage I did not accept, for the sake of the one whose pilgrimage I accepted."'"

chapters.title_en: The Virtue of the Sacred House and Exalted Mecca
chapters.arabic_text:
||||  فضيلة البيت ومكة المشرفة

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله عز وجل قد وعد هذا البيت أن يحجه كل سنة
ستمائة ألف فإن نقصوا أكملهم الله عز وجل من الملائكة (3) وإن الكعبة تحشر
كالعروس المزفوفة وكل من حجها يتعلق بأستارها يسعون حولها حتى تدخل الجنة
فيدخلون معها وفي الخبر إن الحجر الأسود ياقوتة من يواقيت الجنة وإنه يبعث
يوم القيامة له عينان ولسان ينطق PageV01P241
به يشهد لكل من استلمه بحق وصدق (1) وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقبله كثيرا
(2) وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم سجد عليه وكان يطوف على الراحلة فيضع
المحجن عليه ثم يقبل طرف المحجن (3) وقبله عمر رضي الله عنه ثم قال إني
لأعلم أنك حجر لا تضر ولا تنفع (4) ولولا أني رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم يقبلك ما قبلتك ثم بكى حتى علا نشيجه فالتفت إلى ورائه فرأى عليا كرم
الله وجهه ورضي الله عنه فقال يا أبا الحسن ههنا تسكب العبرات وتستجاب
الدعوات فقال علي رضي الله عنه يا أمير المؤمنين بل هو يضر  وينفع قال وكيف
قال إن الله تعالى لما أخذ الميثاق على الذرية كتب عليهم كتابا ثم ألقمه
هذا الحجر فهو يشهد للمؤمن بالوفاء ويشهد على الكافر بالجحود قيل فذلك هو
معنى قول الناس عند الاستلام اللهم إيمانا بك وتصديقا بكتابك ووفاء بعهدك
وروي عن الحسن البصري رضي الله عنه أن صوم يوم فيها بمائة ألف يوم وصدقة
درهم بمائة ألف درهم وكذلك كل حسنة بمائة الف ويقال طواف سبعة أسابيع أيام
يعدل عمرة وثلاث عمر تعدل حجة
وفي الخبر الصحيح عمرة في رمضان كحجة معي (5) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
أنا أول من تنشق عنه الأرض ثم آتي أهل البقيع فيحشرون معي ثم آتي أهل مكة
فأحشر بين الحرمين (6)
وفي الخبر إن آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قضى مناسكه لقيته الملائكة
فقالوا بر حجك يا آدم لقد حججنا هذا البيت قبلك بألفي عام (7)
وجاء في الأثر إن الله عز وجل ينظر في كل ليلة إلى أهل الأرض فأول من
ينظر إليه أهل الحرم وأول من ينظر إليه من أهل الحرم أهل المسجد الحرام فمن
رآه طائفا غفر له ومن رآه مصليا غفر له ومن رآه قائما مستقبل الكعبة غفر له
وكوشف بعض الأولياء رضي الله عنهم قال إني رأيت الثغور كلها تسجد لعبادان
ورايت عبادان ساجدة لجدة
ويقال لا تغرب الشمس من يوم إلا ويطوف بهذا البيت رجل من الأبدال ولا
يطلع الفجر من ليلة إلا طاف به واحد من الأوتاد وإذا انقطع ذلك كان سبب
رفعه من الأرض فيصبح الناس وقد رفعت الكعبة لا يرى الناس لها أثرا وهذا إذا
أتى عليها سبع سنين لم يحجها أحد ثم يرفع القرآن من المصاحف فيصبح الناس
فإذا الورق أبيض يلوح ليس فيه حرف ثم ينسخ القرآن من القلوب فلا يذكر منه
كلمة ثم يرجع الناس إلى الأشعار والأغاني وأخبار الجاهلية ثم يخرج الدجال
وينزل عيسى عليه السلام فيقتله والساعة عند ذلك بمنزلة الحامل المقرب التي
تتوقع ولادتها
وفي الخبر استكثروا  من الطواف بهذا البيت قبل أن يرفع فقد هدم مرتين
ويرفع في الثالثة (8)
وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال قال
PageV01P242
الله تعالى إذا أردت أن أخرب الدنيا بدأت ببيتي فخربته ثم أخرب الدنيا
على أثره (1)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ي-ت (bayt)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The dwelling or shelter; in sacred usage, the Kaʿbah as the primordial house of worship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The House of God as the focal point of pilgrimage (ḥajj) and divine covenant (mīthāq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical structure; metaphorical for the sanctuary of divine mercy.
- Root: ح-ج-ج (ḥajj)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To repair, intend, or visit repeatedly; the pilgrimage as a deliberate journey.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ritual of pilgrimage as an act of devotion fulfilling a divine command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the annual rite; metaphorical for the soul's journey toward God.
- Root: ط-و-ف (ṭawāf)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To encircle or circumambulate; the act of going around the Kaʿbah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The circumambulation as a symbol of the soul's orientation toward the divine presence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical rite; metaphorical for perpetual devotion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Temporal Clauses (al-sharṭ wa al-jazāʾ) — The text employs conditional constructions (e.g., "if they are deficient") and temporal clauses (e.g., "when the sun sets") to structure prophetic reports and eschatological warnings.
chapters.translation: I say: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Verily, God Almighty has promised this House that six hundred thousand will perform the pilgrimage to it every year; if they are deficient, God Almighty will complete them from the angels." And the Kaʿbah will be gathered forth like a bride adorned for her wedding, and every one who has performed the pilgrimage to it will cling to its curtains, hastening around it, until it enters Paradise, and they enter with it. And in the report: "The Black Stone is a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and it will be raised on the Day of Resurrection having two eyes and a speaking tongue, by which it will bear witness for every one who touched it in truth and sincerity." The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to kiss it frequently. And it is narrated that he prostrated upon it, and he used to circumambulate upon his mount, placing his crooked staff upon it, then kissing the tip of the staff. And ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) kissed it, then said: "I know well that you are a stone that neither harms nor benefits; were it not that I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) kissing you, I would not kiss you." Then he wept until his sobbing rose high, and he turned behind him and saw ʿAlī (may God honor his face and be pleased with him), and he said: "O Abū al-Ḥasan, here tears are poured forth and supplications are answered." ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) said: "O Commander of the Faithful, rather it harms and benefits." He said: "How so?" He said: "When God Almighty took the covenant upon the progeny, He wrote upon them a writ, then He fed it to this Stone; so it bears witness for the believer to his fidelity and bears witness against the disbeliever to his denial." It was said: That is the meaning of the people's saying at the touching: "O God, in faith in You, and affirmation of Your Book, and fidelity to Your covenant." And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī (may God be pleased with him) that fasting a day therein equals a hundred thousand days, and giving a dirham in charity equals a hundred thousand dirhams, and likewise every good deed equals a hundred thousand. And it is said: A circumambulation of seven circuits in those days equals an ʿumrah, and three ʿumrahs equal a ḥajj. And in the authentic report: "An ʿumrah in Ramaḍān equals a ḥajj with me." And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "I am the first from whom the earth will be split open, then I will come to the people of al-Baqīʿ, and they will be gathered with me; then I will come to the people of Mecca, and I will be gathered between the two sanctuaries." And in the report: When Adam (peace be upon him) had completed his rites, the angels met him and said: "May your pilgrimage be blessed, O Adam; we have performed the pilgrimage to this House before you by two thousand years." And it has come in the tradition that God Almighty looks every night upon the people of the earth, and the first He looks upon are the people of the Sanctuary, and the first He looks upon from the people of the Sanctuary are the people of the Sacred Mosque. Whomsoever He sees circumambulating, He forgives him; whomsoever He sees praying, He forgives him; whomsoever He sees standing facing the Kaʿbah, He forgives him. And some of the saints (may God be pleased with them) were unveiled to, and he said: "I saw all the frontier towns prostrating to ʿAbbādān, and I saw ʿAbbādān prostrating to Jeddah." And it is said: The sun does not set on any day except that a man from the substitutes (abdāl) circumambulates this House, and the dawn does not break on any night except that one of the pegs (awtād) has circumambulated it. And when that ceases, it will be the cause of its being raised from the earth, and the people will wake to find the Kaʿbah raised, with no trace of it visible to them. And this will be when seven years pass without anyone performing the pilgrimage to it. Then the Qurʾān will be raised from the codices, and the people will wake to find the pages white and gleaming, with no letter in them. Then the Qurʾān will be erased from the hearts, and not a word of it will be remembered. Then the people will return to poetry, songs, and tales of the Age of Ignorance. Then the Dajjāl will emerge, and Jesus (peace be upon him) will descend and kill him. And the Hour at that time will be like a pregnant woman near term, awaiting her delivery. And in the report: "Perform much circumambulation of this House before it is raised; for it has been demolished twice, and it will be raised the third time." And it is narrated from ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: God Almighty said: "When I intend to destroy the world, I begin with My House and destroy it, then I destroy the world after it."

chapters.title_en: The Virtue of Residing in Mecca (May Allah Protect It) and the Disapproval of It
chapters.arabic_text:
|||| فضيلة المقام بمكة حرسها الله تعالى وكراهيته

كره الخائفون المحتاطون من العلماء المقام بمكة لمعان ثلاثة
الأول خوف التبرم والأنس بالبيت فإن ذلك ربما يؤثر في تسكين حرقة القلب
في الاحترام وهكذا كان عمر رضي الله عنه يضرب الحجاج إذا حجوا ويقول يا أهل
اليمن يمنكم ويا أهل الشام شامكم ويا أهل العراق عراقكم ولذلك هم عمر رضي
الله عنه بمنع الناس من كثرة الطواف وقال خشيت أن يأنس الناس بهذا البيت
الثاني تهييج الشوق بالمفارقة لتنبعث داعية العودة فإن الله تعالى جعل
البيت مثابة للناس وأمنا أي يثوبون ويعودون إليه مرة بعد أخرى ولا يقضون
منه وطرا
وقال بعضهم تكون في بلد وقلبك مشتاق إلى مكة متعلق بهذا البيت خير لك من
أن تكون فيه وأنت متبرم بالمقام وقلبك في بلد آخر
وقال بعض السلف كم من رجل بخراسان هو أقرب إلى هذا البيت ممن يطوف به
ويقال إن لله تعالى عبادا تطوف بهم الكعبة تقربا إلى الله عز وجل
الثالث الخوف من ركوب الخطايا والذنوب بها فإن ذلك مخطر وبالحري أن يورث
مقت الله عز وجل لشرف الموضع
وروي عن وهيب بن الورد المكي قال كنت ذات ليلة في الحجر أصلي فسمعت كلاما
بين الكعبة والأستار يقول إلى الله أشكو ثم إليك يا جبرائيل ما ألقى من
الطائفين حولي من تفكرهم في الحديث ولغوهم ولهوهم لئن لم ينتهوا عن ذلك
لأنتفضن انتفاضة يرجع كل حجر مني إلى الجبل الذي قطع منه
وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه ما من بلد يؤاخذ فيه العبد بالنية قبل العمل
إلا مكة وتلا قوله تعالى ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم نذقه من عذاب أليم أي أنه
على مجرد الإرادة
ويقال إن السيئات تضاعف بها كما تضاعف الحسنات وكان ابن عباس رضي الله
عنه يقول الاحتكار بمكة من الإلحاد في الحرم وقيل الكذب أيضا وقال ابن عباس
لأن أذنب سبعين ذنبا بركية أحب إلي من أن أذنب ذنبا واحدا بمكة وركية منزل
بين مكة والطائف والخوف ذلك انتهى بعض المقيمين إلى أن لم يقض حاجته في
الحرم بل كان يخرج إلى الحل عند قضاء الحاجة
وبعضهم أقام شهرا وما وضع جنبه على الأرض
وللمنع من الإقامة كره بعض العلماء أجور دور مكة ولا تظنن أن كراهة
المقام يناقض فضل البقعة لأن هذه كراهة علتها ضعف الخلق وقصورهم عن القيام
بحق الموضع فمعنى قولنا إن ترك المقام به أفضل أي بالإضافة إلى مقام مع
التقصير والتبرم أما أن يكون أفضل من المقام مع الوفاء بحقه فهيهات وكيف لا
ولما عاد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى مكة استقبل الكعبة وقال إنك
لخير أرض الله عز وجل وأحب بلاد الله تعالى إلي ولولا أني أخرجت منك لما
خرجت (2) وكيف لا والنظر إلى البيت عبادة والحسنات فيها مضاعفة كما ذكرناه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ص-د (qaṣada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intentional aim or direction toward a goal; the core sense of deliberate pursuit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, qaṣd denotes the volitional orientation of the heart, distinguishing purposeful acts from mere habit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to physical direction; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to moral and spiritual intention, as in "intending" a place's sanctity.
- Root: خ-و-ف (khawf)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Fear or apprehension arising from anticipated harm; a state of emotional trepidation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, khawf is a pious caution (waraʿ) that motivates avoidance of sin, distinct from mere worldly dread.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: fear of a tangible threat; metaphorical: reverential awe before divine majesty, as in the fear of failing to honor sacred precincts.
- Root: أ-ن-س (anisa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Familiarity, sociability, or becoming accustomed; the opposite of estrangement (waḥshah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In spiritual discourse, uns (familiarity) can dull the heart's fervent longing (shawq), reducing reverence to routine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: companionship; metaphorical: the soul's complacency with the sacred, which diminishes its awe.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — In sentences like "if they do not desist, I will shake," the protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (result), requiring precise temporal and modal alignment to convey causal necessity.
chapters.translation:
I say: The cautious and God-fearing scholars have disapproved of residing in Mecca (may Allah protect it) for three reasons.

The first is the fear of becoming weary and overly familiar with the House, for this may extinguish the burning ardor of the heart in reverence. Thus ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) used to strike the pilgrims when they performed the Hajj, saying: "O people of Yemen, return to your Yemen! O people of Syria, return to your Syria! O people of Iraq, return to your Iraq!" For this reason, ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) intended to prevent people from excessive circumambulation, saying: "I fear that the people will become overly familiar with this House."

The second is the stirring of longing (shawq) through separation, so that the impulse to return is aroused. For Allah (the Exalted) has made the House a place of return (mathābah) for mankind and a sanctuary, meaning they return to it again and again, and never satisfy their desire for it. Some of them said: "That you be in a land while your heart yearns for Mecca, attached to this House, is better for you than being in it while weary of residence, with your heart in another land." Some of the predecessors (salaf) said: "How many a man in Khurasan is closer to this House than one who circumambulates it!" And it is said that Allah (the Exalted) has servants whom the Kaʿbah circumambulates, drawing near to Allah (the Mighty and Majestic).

The third is the fear of committing sins and offenses there, for that is perilous and likely to incur Allah's wrath (the Mighty and Majestic) due to the nobility of the place. It is narrated from Wahb ibn al-Ward al-Makkī that he said: "One night I was in the Ḥijr praying, and I heard speech between the Kaʿbah and the curtains: 'To Allah I complain, then to you, O Gabriel, of what I suffer from those circumambulating around me—their heedless talk, their idle chatter, and their play. If they do not desist from this, I will shake with such a shaking that every stone of me will return to the mountain from which it was hewn.'"

Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "There is no land in which a servant is taken to task for intention before action except Mecca." And he recited the saying of the Exalted: {«وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ»} (And whoever intends therein deviation with injustice, We shall make him taste a painful punishment) — that is, upon mere intention.

It is said that sins are multiplied there just as good deeds are multiplied. Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "Hoarding in Mecca is a form of deviation (ilḥād) in the Sanctuary." It was also said: "And lying likewise." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "That I commit seventy sins in Rukkah is dearer to me than that I commit one sin in Mecca." Rukkah is a waystation between Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif. Such was the fear that some residents reached the point of not relieving themselves in the Sanctuary, but would go out to the profane land (al-ḥill) when needing to answer the call of nature. Some of them stayed a month without laying their side upon the ground.

And because of this prohibition on residence, some scholars disapproved of renting out houses in Mecca. Do not think that the disapproval of residence contradicts the virtue of the place, for this disapproval has as its cause the weakness of creatures and their shortcoming in fulfilling the right of the place. Thus, our saying that abandoning residence there is better means: in comparison to a residence accompanied by shortcoming and weariness. As for it being better than residence with full fulfillment of its right—far from it! And how could it not be? When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) returned to Mecca, he faced the Kaʿbah and said: "Indeed, you are the best of Allah's lands and the most beloved of Allah's cities to me. Had I not been expelled from you, I would not have left you." And how could it not be so, when gazing upon the House is an act of worship, and good deeds therein are multiplied, as we have mentioned.

chapters.title_en: The Virtue of the Noble City (Madīnah) Over All Other Lands
chapters.arabic_text:
|||| فضيلة المدينة الشريفة على سائر البلاد

ما بعد مكة بقعة أفضل من مدينة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فالأعمال
فيها أيضا مضاعفة قال صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة في مسجدي هذا خير من ألف
صلاة فيما سواه إلا المسجد الحرام (3) وكذلك كل عمل بالمدينة بألف
PageV01P243
وبعد مدينته الأرض المقدسة فإن الصلاة فيها بخمسمائة صلاة فيما سواها إلا
المسجد الحرام وكذلك سائر الأعمال
وروى ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال صلاة في مسجد المدينة
بعشرة آلاف صلاة وصلاة في المسجد الأقصى بألف صلاة وصلاة في المسجد الحرام
بمائة ألف صلاة (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من صبر على شدتها ولأوائها كنت
له شفيعا يوم القيامة (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من استطاع أن يموت
بالمدينة فليمت فإنه لن يموت بها أحد إلا كنت له شفيعا يوم القيامة (3) وما
بعد هذه البقاع الثلاث فالمواضع فيها متساوية إلا الثغور فإن المقام بها
للمرابطة فيها فيه فضل عظيم
ولذلك قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تشد الرحال إلا إلى ثلاثة مساجد المسجد
الحرام ومسجدي هذا والمسجد الأقصى (4) وقد ذهب بعض العلماء إلى الاستدلال
بهذا الحديث في المنع من الرحلة لزيارة المشاهد وقبور العلماء والصلحاء وما
تبين لي أن الأمر كذلك بل الزيارة مأمور بها قال صلى الله عليه وسلم كنت
نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور فزوروها ولا تقولوا هجرا (5) والحديث إنما ورد في
المساجد وليس في معناها المشاهد لأن المساجد بعد المساجد الثلاثة متماثلة
ولا بلد إلا وفيه مسجد فلا معنى للرحلة إلى مسجد آخر وأما المشاهد فلا
تتساوى بل بركة زيارتها على قدر درجاتهم عند الله عز وجل نعم لو كان في
موضع لا مسجد فيه فله أن يشد الرحال إلى موضع فيه مسجد وينتقل إليه بالكلية
إن شاء ثم ليت شعري هل يمنع هذا القائل من شد الرحال إلى قبور الأنبياء
عليهم السلام مثل إبراهيم وموسى ويحيى وغيرهم عليهم السلام فالمنع من ذلك
في غاية الإحالة فإذا جوز هذا فقبور الأولياء والعلماء والصلحاء في معناها
فلا يبعد أن يكون ذلك من أغراض الرحلة كما أن زيارة العلماء في الحياة من
المقاصد هذا في الرحلة أما المقام فالأولى بالمريد أن يلازم مكانه إذا لم
يكن قصده من السفر استفادة العلم مهما سلم له حاله في وطنه فإن لم يسلم
فيطلب من المواضع ما هو أقرب إلى الخمول وأسلم للدين وأفرغ للقلب وأيسر
للعبادة فهو أفضل المواضع له قال صلى الله عليه وسلم البلاد بلاد الله عز
وجل والخلق عباده فأي موضع رأيت فيه رفقا فأقم واحمد الله تعالى (6) وفي
الخبر من بورك له في شيء فليلزمه ومن جعلت معيشته في شيء فلا ينتقل عنه حتى
يتغير عليه (7) وقال أبو نعيم رأيت سفيان الثوري وقد جعل جرابه على كتفه
وأخذ نعليه بيده فقلت إلى أين يا أبا عبد الله قال إلى بلد  أملأ فيه جرابي
بدرهم
وفي حكاية أخرى بلغني عن قرية فيها رخص أقيم فيها قال فقلت وتفعل هذا يا
أبا عبد الله فقال نعم إذا سمعت برخص في بلد فاقصده فإنه أسلم لدينك وأقل
لهمك وكان يقول هذا زمان سوء لا يؤمن فيه على الخاملين فكيف PageV01P244
بالمشهورين هذا زمان تنقل يتنقل الرجل من قرية إلى قرية يفر بدينه من
الفتن
ويحكى عنه أنه قال والله ما أدري أي البلاد أسكن فقيل له خراسان فقال
مذاهب مختلفة وآراه فاسدة قيل فالشام قال يشار إليك بالأصابع أراد الشهرة
قيل فالعراق قال بلد الجبابرة قيل مكة قال مكة تذيب الكيس والبدن وقال له
رجل غريب عزمت على المجاورة بمكة فأوصني قال أوصيك بثلاث لا تصلين في الصف
الأول ولا تصحبن قرشيا ولا تظهرن صدقة وإنما كره الصف الأول لأنه يشتهر
فيفتقد إذا غاب فيختلط بعمله التزين والتصنع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ض-ل (faḍala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus; superiority in rank or merit; that which exceeds the measure of another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Excellence (faḍīlah) as a divinely conferred distinction elevating one locus or act above another in reward (thawāb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to intrinsic merit; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to places as vessels of multiplied recompense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Tafḍīl (Elative Construction) — the pattern "afʿalu min" (better than) governs comparative superiority, requiring the second term to be a genus or class, as in "afḍal min" (better than) with "sāʾir al-bilād" (all other lands).
chapters.translation:
I say: After Makkah, there is no spot more excellent than the city of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Thus, deeds therein are also multiplied. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in other than it, except the Sacred Mosque {«صلاة في مسجدي هذا خير من ألف صلاة فيما سواه إلا المسجد الحرام»}." Likewise, every deed in Madīnah is [multiplied] by a thousand.

And after his city, [the most excellent is] the Holy Land (al-arḍ al-muqaddasah), for prayer therein is [equivalent to] five hundred prayers in other than it, except the Sacred Mosque; and similarly for all other deeds.

Ibn ʿAbbās narrated from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "A prayer in the Mosque of Madīnah is [worth] ten thousand prayers; a prayer in al-Masjid al-Aqṣā is [worth] a thousand prayers; and a prayer in the Sacred Mosque is [worth] one hundred thousand prayers {«صلاة في مسجد المدينة بعشرة آلاف صلاة وصلاة في المسجد الأقصى بألف صلاة وصلاة في المسجد الحرام بمائة ألف صلاة»}." And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever endures its hardship and its severity (laʾwāʾihā), I shall be an intercessor (shafīʿ) for him on the Day of Resurrection {«من صبر على شدتها ولأوائها كنت له شفيعا يوم القيامة»}." And he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever is able to die in Madīnah, let him die [there], for none will die therein except that I shall be an intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection {«من استطاع أن يموت بالمدينة فليمت فإنه لن يموت بها أحد إلا كنت له شفيعا يوم القيامة»}."

Beyond these three places, all locations are equal [in merit], except the frontier outposts (al-thughūr), for residing therein for the purpose of ribāṭ (frontier vigilance) carries a great virtue.

For this reason, he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Do not set out on journeys (lā tushadd al-riḥāl) except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, this mosque of mine, and al-Masjid al-Aqṣā {«لا تشد الرحال إلا إلى ثلاثة مساجد المسجد الحرام ومسجدي هذا والمسجد الأقصى»}." Some scholars have used this hadith as evidence to prohibit travel for visiting the shrines (mashāhid), the graves of scholars, and the righteous. But it has not become clear to me that the matter is so; rather, visitation (ziyārah) is commanded. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "I had forbidden you from visiting graves, so visit them, and do not utter indecent speech {«كنت نهيتكم عن زيارة القبور فزوروها ولا تقولوا هجرا»}." The hadith [prohibiting travel] was only reported concerning mosques, and shrines are not equivalent to them in meaning, because mosques—beyond the three [excepted]—are all alike, and there is no town without a mosque therein; thus there is no point in traveling to another mosque. As for shrines, they are not equal; rather, the blessing of visiting them is proportionate to their [occupants'] degrees with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Yes, if one were in a place with no mosque therein, he may set out to a place containing a mosque and relocate to it entirely, if he wishes.

Then, would that I knew—does this [prohibiting] speaker forbid setting out to the graves of the prophets, peace be upon them, such as Ibrāhīm, Mūsā, Yaḥyā, and others, peace be upon them? Forbidding that would be utterly impossible (fī ghāyat al-iḥālah). And if he permits this, then the graves of the awliyāʾ (friends of Allah), the scholars, and the righteous are equivalent to them in meaning. Thus, it is not far-fetched that this be among the purposes of travel, just as visiting scholars during their lifetime is among the [legitimate] aims.

This concerns travel. As for residence (al-maqām), the better course for the seeker (al-murīd) is to remain in his place if his purpose in traveling is not the acquisition of knowledge, as long as his condition is sound in his homeland. But if it is not sound, then let him seek among places that which is closer to obscurity (al-khumūl), safer for his religion, more freeing for his heart, and easier for worship—for that is the most excellent place for him. He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "The lands are the lands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the creatures are His servants; so wherever you see ease (rifq) for yourself, take up residence there and praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic {«البلاد بلاد الله عز وجل والخلق عباده فأي موضع رأيت فيه رفقا فأقم واحمد الله تعالى»}." And in the report: "Whoever is blessed in a thing, let him adhere to it; and whoever's livelihood is made [easy] in a thing, let him not move from it until it changes for him {«من بورك له في شيء فليلزمه ومن جعلت معيشته في شيء فلا ينتقل عنه حتى يتغير عليه»}."

Abū Nuʿaym said: I saw Sufyān al-Thawrī having placed his saddlebag (jirābuhu) on his shoulder and taken his sandals in his hand, so I said: "Where to, O Abā ʿAbdillāh?" He said: "To a land in which I may fill my saddlebag with a dirham." In another anecdote: It reached me that he said concerning a village in which prices were low (rukhaṣ): "I shall reside therein." He said: So I said: "And would you do this, O Abā ʿAbdillāh?" He said: "Yes. When you hear of low prices in a land, seek it out, for it is safer for your religion and less for your concern (hamm)." And he used to say: "This is an evil time (zamān sawʾ) in which the obscure are not safe—how then [can] the famous [be safe]? This is a time of moving about; a man moves from village to village, fleeing with his religion from tribulations (fitan)."

And it is narrated from him that he said: "By Allah, I do not know which land I should inhabit." So it was said to him: "Khurāsān." He said: "Divergent sects (madhāhib mukhtalifah) and corrupt opinions (ārāʾ fāsidah)." It was said: "Al-Shām." He said: "One is pointed at with fingers"—meaning fame (al-shuhrah). It was said: "Al-ʿIrāq." He said: "A land of tyrants (al-jabābirah)." It was said: "Makkah." He said: "Makkah melts away the intellect (al-kays) and the body (al-badan)." And a stranger said to him: "I have resolved to take up permanent residence (al-mujāwarah) in Makkah, so advise me." He said: "I advise you with three things: Do not pray in the first row, do not keep company with a Qurashī, and do not display your charity (ṣadaqah)." He only disliked the first row because it brings fame; thus, if one is absent, he is missed, and adornment (al-tazayyun) and affectation (al-taṣannuʿ) become mixed into his deeds.

chapters.title_en: Section 114 — The Second Chapter on the Conditions for the Obligation of Hajj, the Validity of Its Pillars, Its Duties, and Its Prohibitions
chapters.arabic_text:
||| الفصل الثاني في شروط وجوب الحج وصحة أركانه وواجباته ومحظوراته

أما الشرائط فشرط صحة الحج اثنان الوقت والإسلام فيصح حج الصبي ويحرم
بنفسه إن كان مميزا ويحرم عنه وليه إن كان صغيرا ويفعل به ما يفعل في الحج
من الطواف والسعي وغيره
وأما الوقت فهو شوال وذو القعدة وتسع من ذي الحجة إلى طلوع الفجر من يوم
النحر فمن أحرم بالحج في غير هذه المدة فهي عمرة وجميع السنة وقت العمرة
ولكن من كان معكوفا على النسك أيام منى فلا ينبغي أن يحرم بالعمرة لأنه لا
يتمكن من الاشتغال عقيبه لاشتغاله بأعمال منى
وأما شروط وقوعه عن حجة الإسلام فخمسة الإسلام والحرية والبلوغ والعقل
والوقت
فإن أحرم الصبي أو العبد ولكن عتق العبد وبلغ الصبي بعرفة أو بمزدلفة
وعاد إلى عرفة قبل طلوع الفجر أجزأهما عن حجة الإسلام لأن الحج عرفة وليس
عليهما دم إلا شاة
وتشترط هذه الشرائط في وقوع العمرة عن فرض الإسلام إلا الوقت وأما شروط
وقوع الحج نفلا عن الحر البالغ فهو بعد براءة ذمته عن حجة الإسلام فحج
الإسلام متقدم ثم  القضاء لمن أفسده في حالة الوقوف ثم النذر ثم النيابة ثم
النفل وهذا الترتيب مستحق وكذلك يقع وإن نوى خلافه
وأما شروط لزوم الحج فخمسة البلوغ والإسلام والعقل والحرية والاستطاعة
ومن لزمه فرض الحج لزمه فرض العمرة ومن أراد دخول مكة لزيارة أو تجارة
ولم يكن حطابا لزمه الإحرام على قول ثم يتحلل بعمل عمرة أو حج
وأما الاستطاعة فنوعان أحدهما المباشرة وذلك له أسباب أما في نفسه
فبالصحة وأما في الطريق فبأن تكون خصبة آمنة بلا بحر مخطر ولا عدو قاهر
وأما في المال فبأن يجد نفقة ذهابه وإيابه إلى وطنه كان له أهل أو لم يكن
لأن مفارقة الوطن شديدة وأن يملك نفقة من تلزمه نفقته في هذه المدة وأن
يملك ما يقضي به ديونه وأن يقدر على راحلة أو كرائها بمحمل أو زاملة إن
استمسك على الزاملة
وأما النوع الثاني فاستطاعة المغضوب بماله وهو أن يستأجر من يحج عنه بعد
فراغ الأجير عن حجة الإسلام لنفسه ويكفي نفقة الذهاب بزاملة في هذا النوع
والابن إذا عرض طاعته على الأب الزمن صار به مستطيعا ولو عرض ماله لم يصر
به مستطيعا لأن الخدمة بالبدن فيها شرف للولد وبذل المال فيه منة على
الوالد
ومن استطاع لزمه الحج وله التأخير ولكنه فيه على خطر فإن تيسر له ولو في
آخر عمره سقط عنه
وإن مات قبل الحج لقي الله عز وجل عاصيا بترك الحج وكان الحج في تركته
يحج عنه وإن لم يوص كسائر ديونه
وإن استطاع في سنة فلم يخرج مع الناس وهلك ماله في تلك السنة قبل حج
الناس ثم مات لقي الله عز وجل ولا حج عليه
ومن مات ولم يحج مع اليسار فأمره شديد عند الله تعالى قال عمر رضي الله
عنه لقد هممت أن أكتب في الأمصار بضرب الجزية على من لم يحج ممن يستطيع
إليه سبيلا
وعن سعيد بن جبير وإبراهيم النخعي ومجاهد وطاوس لو علمت رجلا غنيا وجب
عليه الحج ثم مات  قبل أن يحج ما صليت عليه وبعضهم كان له جار موسر فمات ولم
يحج فلم يصل عليه
وكان ابن عباس يقول من مات ولم يزك ولم يحج سأل الرجعة إلى الدنيا وقرأ
قوله عز وجل رب أرجعون لعلي أعمل صالحا فيما تركت {قال}
PageV01P245
الحج
وأما الأركان التي لا يصح الحج بدونها فخمسة الإحرام والطواف والسعي بعده
والوقوف بعرفة والحلق بعده على قول وأركان العمرة كذلك إلا الوقوف
والواجبات المجبورة بالدم ست الإحرام من الميقات فمن تركه وجاوز الميقات
محلا فعليه شاة والرمي فيه الدم قولا واحدا وأما الصبر بعرفة إلى غروب
الشمس والمبيت بمزدلفة والمبيت بمنى وطواف الوداع فهذه الأربعة يجبر تركها
بالدم على أحد القولين وفي القول الثاني فيها دم على وجه الاستحباب
وأما وجوه أداء الحج والعمرة فثلاثة
الأول الإفراد وهو الأفضل وذلك أن يقدم الحج وحده فإذا فرغ خرج إلى الحل
فأحرم واعتمر وأفضل الحل لإحرام العمرة الجعرانة ثم التنعيهم ثم الحديبية
وليس على المفرد دم إلا أن يتطوع
الثاني القران وهو أن يجمع فيقول لبيك بحجة وعمرة معا فيصير محرما بهما
ويكفيه أعمال الحج وتندرج العمرة تحت الحج كما يندرج الوضوء تحت الغسل إلا
أنه إذا طاف وسعى قبل الوقوف بعرفة فسعيه محسوب من النسكين وأما طوافه فغير
محسوب لأن شرط الطواف الفرض في الحج أن يقع بعد الوقوف وعلى القارن دم شاة
إلا أن يكون مكيا فلا شيء عليه لأنه لم يترك ميقاته إذ ميقاته مكة
الثالث التمتع وهو أن يجاوز الميقات محرما بعمرة ويتحلل بمكة ويتمتع
بالمحظورات إلى وقت الحج ثم يحرم بالحج ولا يكون متمتعا إلا بخمس شرائط
أحدها أن لا يكون من حاضري المسجدد الحرام وحاضره من كان منه على مسافة
لا تقصر فيها الصلاة
الثاني أن يقدم العمرة على الحج
الثالث أن تكون عمرته في أشهر الحج
الرابع أن لا يرجع إلى ميقات الحج ولا إلى مثل مسافته لإحرام الحج
الخامس أن يكون حجه وعمرته عن شخص واحد فإذا وجدت هذه  الأوصاف كان متمتعا
ولزمه دم شاة فإن لم يجد فصيام ثلاثة أيام في الحج
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش ر ط (sh-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mark, sign, or stipulation that delimits a matter; a condition binding an act's validity or obligation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A stipulated prerequisite (sharṭ) that renders an act sound (ṣaḥīḥ) or obligatory (wājib) in the divine law (Sharʿ); distinct from the essence (dhāt) of the act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes a fixed boundary; metaphorically, a legal condition that restricts permissibility or obligation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Structure (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (sharṭ) governs the apodosis (jawāb), as in "if he enters iḥrām outside this period, it is ʿumrah," where the legal consequence is syntactically tied to the condition.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second chapter concerns the conditions for the obligation of Hajj, the validity of its pillars, its duties, and its prohibitions.

As for the conditions [of validity], the conditions for the soundness of Hajj are two: time and Islam. Thus, the Hajj of a boy is valid, and he enters iḥrām himself if he is discerning (mumayyiz); but his guardian enters iḥrām on his behalf if he is a young child, and he performs on him what is performed in Hajj — the circumambulation (ṭawāf), the running (saʿy), and other rites.

As for the time, it is Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and the first nine [days] of Dhū al-Ḥijjah up to the dawn of the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr). Whoever enters iḥrām for Hajj outside this period, it is [deemed] ʿumrah; and the entire year is the time for ʿumrah. However, whoever is detained by the rites during the days of Minā should not enter iḥrām for ʿumrah, for he cannot occupy himself with it afterward due to his engagement in the works of Minā.

As for the conditions for its counting as the Hajj of Islam (ḥijjat al-Islām), they are five: Islam, freedom, puberty, reason, and time. If a boy enters iḥrām, or a slave [does so], but the slave is emancipated and the boy reaches puberty at ʿArafah or at Muzdalifah, and he returns to ʿArafah before dawn, it suffices for both as the Hajj of Islam, because Hajj is ʿArafah; and upon them is no [obligatory] blood [sacrifice] except a sheep. These conditions are required for the ʿumrah to count as the obligatory [ʿumrah] of Islam, except the time. As for the conditions for Hajj to count as supererogatory (nafl) for a free adult, it is after his liability is cleared of the Hajj of Islam. Thus, the Hajj of Islam comes first, then the make-up (qaḍāʾ) for one who corrupts it during the standing [at ʿArafah], then the vow (nadhr), then the deputyship (niyābah), then the supererogatory. This order is obligatory, and it so occurs even if one intends otherwise.

As for the conditions for the binding obligation (luzūm) of Hajj, they are five: puberty, Islam, reason, freedom, and capacity (istitāʿah). Whoever is bound by the obligatory Hajj is bound by the obligatory ʿumrah. Whoever wishes to enter Mecca for visitation or trade, and is not a woodcutter [i.e., a frequent entrant], is bound to enter iḥrām according to one opinion, then he exits [iḥrām] by performing the rites of ʿumrah or Hajj.

As for capacity (istitāʿah), it is of two types. One is direct [personal] capacity, and it has causes: regarding oneself, it is sound health; regarding the road, it is that it be fertile and safe, without a perilous sea or an overwhelming enemy; regarding wealth, it is that he find the provisions for his going and his returning to his homeland — whether he has a family or not, for leaving one's homeland is severe — and that he possess [enough] to support those whose maintenance is incumbent upon him during this period, and that he possess [enough] to settle his debts, and that he be able [to obtain] a mount (rāḥilah) or its hire, with a howdah (maḥmil) or a saddle-bag (zāmilah), if he can hold himself steady on the saddle-bag.

As for the second type, it is the capacity of one who is obstructed by his wealth, namely that he hires someone to perform Hajj on his behalf, after the hired agent has completed the Hajj of Islam for himself. In this type, the provision for the going with a saddle-bag suffices. And the son, if he offers his service to his paralyzed father, becomes thereby capable; but if he offers his wealth, he does not become capable thereby, because service with the body carries honor for the son, whereas expending wealth carries a favor (minnah) over the parent.

Whoever becomes capable, Hajj is binding upon him, and he may delay it, but he is thereby in peril. If it becomes feasible for him — even at the end of his life — it is dropped from him. But if he dies before [performing] Hajj, he meets God, Mighty and Majestic, as a disobedient one for abandoning Hajj, and Hajj is [executed] from his estate — it is performed on his behalf even if he did not bequeath it, like his other debts.

If he becomes capable in a year but does not go out with the people, and his wealth perishes in that year before the people's Hajj, then he dies, he meets God, Mighty and Majestic, with no Hajj upon him. Whoever dies without performing Hajj despite affluence, his matter is severe with God, Exalted is He. ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "I nearly wrote to the provinces to impose the jizyah upon whoever did not perform Hajj among those able to find a way to it." It is reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, Mujāhid, and Ṭāwūs: "If I knew a wealthy man upon whom Hajj was obligatory, then he died before performing Hajj, I would not pray over him." And some of them had a wealthy neighbor who died without performing Hajj, so he did not pray over him. Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: "Whoever dies without paying zakāh and without performing Hajj will ask for return to the world," and he recited the saying of God, Exalted is He: {«رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ لَعَلِّي أَعْمَلُ صَالِحًا فِيمَا تَرَكْتُ»} — "My Lord, return me, that I may do righteous deeds in what I have left behind" (Q 23:99–100).

As for the pillars (arkān) without which Hajj is not sound, they are five: the iḥrām, the circumambulation (ṭawāf), the running (saʿy) after it, the standing at ʿArafah (wuqūf), and the shaving (ḥalq) after it, according to one opinion. The pillars of ʿumrah are likewise, except the standing. The duties (wājibāt) that are compensated by blood [sacrifice] are six: the iḥrām from the mīqāt — whoever abandons it and passes the mīqāt in a non-sacred state owes a sheep; the stoning (ramy), in which blood is [due] by unanimous opinion; and as for remaining at ʿArafah until sunset, the overnight stay at Muzdalifah, the overnight stay at Minā, and the farewell circumambulation (ṭawāf al-wadāʿ) — these four have their abandonment compensated by blood according to one of the two opinions, and in the second opinion, blood is [due] for them by way of recommendation (istiḥbāb).

As for the modes of performing Hajj and ʿumrah, they are three.

The first is ifrād (separation), and it is the most virtuous. That is, one presents Hajj alone; when he finishes, he goes out to the ḥill (the non-sacred precinct) and enters iḥrām and performs ʿumrah. The most virtuous place in the ḥill for the iḥrām of ʿumrah is al-Jiʿrānah, then al-Tanʿīm, then al-Ḥudaybiyyah. Upon the one performing ifrād is no blood [sacrifice] unless he volunteers.

The second is qirān (conjoining), which is that one combines, saying: "Here I am (labbayk) for a Hajj and an ʿumrah together," thus becoming in iḥrām for both. The works of Hajj suffice him, and the ʿumrah is subsumed under the Hajj, just as the ablution (wuḍūʾ) is subsumed under the full bath (ghusl). However, if he circumambulates and runs before the standing at ʿArafah, his running is counted for both rites, but his circumambulation is not counted, because the condition of the obligatory circumambulation in Hajj is that it occur after the standing. Upon the one performing qirān is a sheep [as blood], unless he is a Meccan, in which case nothing is upon him, for he did not abandon his mīqāt, since his mīqāt is Mecca.

The third is tamattuʿ (enjoyment), which is that one passes the mīqāt in iḥrām for ʿumrah, exits [iḥrām] in Mecca, and enjoys the [previously] prohibited things until the time of Hajj, then enters iḥrām for Hajj. One is not a mutamattiʿ except with five conditions: first, that he not be among the residents of the Sacred Mosque (ḥāḍirī al-masjid al-ḥarām) — and its resident is one who is at a distance from it within which prayer is not shortened; second, that he present the ʿumrah before the Hajj; third, that his ʿumrah be in the months of Hajj; fourth, that he not return to the mīqāt of Hajj, nor to a place of equivalent distance, for the iḥrām of Hajj; fifth, that his Hajj and his ʿumrah be for one person. When these attributes are found, he is a mutamattiʿ, and a sheep is incumbent upon him. If he does not find [a sheep], then fasting three days during the Hajj before the Day of Sacrifice — whether separated or consecutive — and seven [days] when he returns to his homeland. If he does not fast the three until he returns to his homeland, he fasts the ten consecutively or separately. The substitute for the blood of qirān and tamattuʿ is the same. The most virtuous is ifrād, then tamattuʿ, then qirān.

As for the prohibitions (maḥẓūrāt) of Hajj and ʿumrah, they are six.

The first is wearing [the sewn garments]: the shirt, the trousers, the socks, and the turban. Rather, one should wear a waist-wrapper (izār) and a cloak (ridāʾ) and sandals. If he does not find sandals, then [he may wear] short boots (mukʿabayn). If he does not find a waist-wrapper, then trousers. There is no harm in the belt and in seeking shade in the howdah, but he should not cover his head, for his iḥrām is in the head. As for the woman, she may wear all sewn garments, provided she does not cover her face with what touches it, for her iḥrām is in her face.

The second is perfume (ṭīb). Let him avoid everything that the rational people count as perfume. If he perfumes himself or wears [sewn garments], a sheep is upon him.

The third is shaving and clipping the nails; in both is the ransom (fidyah), namely a sheep. There is no harm in kohl, entering the bathhouse, bloodletting (faṣd), cupping (ḥijāmah), and combing the hair.

The fourth is sexual intercourse (jimāʿ), which corrupts [the Hajj] before the first exit [from iḥrām] (al-taḥallul al-awwal), and in it is a camel (badanah), or a cow, or seven sheep. If it occurs after the first exit, a camel is incumbent upon him, but his Hajj is not corrupted.

The fifth is the preliminaries of intercourse, such as the kiss and the touching that breaks ritual purity with women, for it is prohibited, and in it is a sheep. Likewise in masturbation (istimnāʾ). Marriage and giving in marriage are prohibited, but there is no blood [sacrifice] in them, for they do not contract.

The sixth is killing the game of the land (ṣayd al-barr) — namely, what is edible, or what is generated from the lawful and the unlawful. If one kills game, upon him is its equivalent from livestock, with consideration given to similarity in form. The game of the sea is lawful, and there is no compensation in it.

chapters.title_en: The Second Chapter on the Ordering of Outward Acts from the Journey’s Commencement to Its Return, Comprising Ten Summations
chapters.arabic_text: || الباب الثاني في ترتيب الأعمال الظاهرة من أول السفر إلى الرجوع وهي عشر جمل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ت-ب (r-t-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ordering, arranging, setting in sequence; a rank or station (martabah) implying fixed gradation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, tartīb denotes the divinely sanctioned sequence of acts (tartīb al-aʿmāl) that mirrors the hierarchical order of causes and purposes in worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical arrangement in time or space; metaphorical (majāz) — the moral or spiritual precedence of one duty over another.
- Root: س-ف-ر (s-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To uncover, reveal; also journeying (safar) as the act of traversing land, from the idea of uncovering the horizon.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Safar in religious context is a permissible worldly act that becomes an occasion for spiritual discipline (riyāḍah) and reflection on divine signs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical travel; metaphorical — the soul’s journey toward God, as in the Qur’anic {«سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ»} (travel in the land), which implies both outward and inward movement.
- Root: ج-م-ل (j-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A totality, a comprehensive sum; also beauty (jamāl) as harmonious completeness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Jumlah here denotes a complete category or division of rulings, not a mere enumeration — each jumlah is a self-contained unit of legal-theological ordering.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a gathered aggregate; metaphorical — a conceptual whole whose parts are mutually entailed, like the limbs of a single body.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Tafsīr (Coordination by Explication) — The phrase “wa-hiya ʿashru jumal” is a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) functioning as an explicative appositive (badal) to the preceding clause, clarifying that the “ordering” (tartīb) consists precisely of ten comprehensive divisions, not an additional item.
chapters.translation: I say: The second chapter concerns the ordering of the outward acts (al-aʿmāl al-ẓāhirah) from the very commencement of the journey (safar) until the return (rujūʿ) — and these acts comprise ten comprehensive summations (jumal).
