chapters.arabic_text:
||| الجملة الأولى في السير من أول الخروج إلى الإحرام

وهي ثمانية الأولى في المال فينبغي أن يبدأ بالتوبة ورد المظالم وقضاء
الديون وإعداد النفقة لكل من تلزمه نفقته إلى وقت الرجوع ويرد ما عنده من
الودائع ويستصحب من المال الحلال الطيب ما يكفيه لذهابه وإيابه من غير
PageV01P246
تقتير بل على وجه يمكنه معه التوسع في الزاد والرفق بالضعفاء والفقراء
ويتصدق بشيء قبل خروجه ويشتري  لنفسه دابة قوية على الحمل لا تضعف أو
يكتريها فإن اكترى فليظهر للمكاري كل ما يريد أن يحمله من قليل أو كثير
ويحصل رضاه فيه
الثانية في الرفيق ينبغي أن يلتمس رفيقا صالحا محبا للخير معينا عليه إن
نسي ذكره وإن ذكر أعانه وإن جبن شجعه وإن عجز قواه وإن ضاق صدره صبره
ويودع رفقاءه المقيمين وإخوانه وجيرانه فيودعهم ويلتمس أدعيتهم فإن الله
تعالى جاعل في أدعيتهم خيرا والسنة في الوداع أن يقول أستودع الله دينك
وأمانتك وخواتيم عملك (1) وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لمن أراد السفر في
حفظ الله وكنفه زودك الله التقوى وغفر ذنبك ووجهك للخير أينما كنت (2)
الثالثة في الخروج من الدار ينبغي إذا هم بالخروج أن يصلي ركعتين أولا
يقرأ في الأولى بعد الفاتحة قل يا أيها الكافرون وفي الثانية الإخلاص فإذا
فرغ رفع يديه ودعا الله سبحانه عن إخلاص صاف ونية صادقة وقال اللهم أنت
الصاحب في السفر وأنت الخليفة في الأهل والمال والولد والأصحاب احفظنا
وإياهم من كل آفة وعاهة اللهم إنا نسألك في مسيرنا هذا البر والتقوى ومن
العمل ما ترضى اللهم إنا نسألك أن تطوي لنا الأرض وتهون علينا السفر وأن
ترزقنا في سفرنا سلامة البدن والدين والمال وتبلغنا حج بيتك وزيارة قبر
نبيك محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم إنا نعوذ بك من وعثاء السفر وكآبة
المنظر وسوء المنقلب في الأهل والمال والولد والأصحاب اللهم اجعلنا وإياهم
في جوارك ولا تسلبنا وإياهم نعمتك ولا تغير ما بنا وبهم من عافيتك
الرابعة إذا حصل على باب الدار قال بسم الله توكلت على الله ولا حول ولا
قوة إلا بالله أعوذ بالله رب أعوذ بك أن أضل أو أضل أو أذل أو أذل أو أزل
أو أزل أو أظلم أو أظلم أو أجهل أو يجهل علي اللهم إني لم أخرج أشرا ولا
بطرا ولا رياء ولا سمعة بل خرجت اتقاء سخطك وابتغاء مرضاتك وقضاء فرضك
واتباع سنة نبيك وشوقا إلى لقائك فإذا  مشى قال اللهم بك انتشرت وعليك توكلت
وبك اعتصمت وإليك توجهت اللهم أنت ثقتي وأنت رجائي فاكفني ما أهمني وما لا
أهتم به وما أنت أعلم به مني عز جارك وجل ثناؤك ولا إله غيرك اللهم زودني
التقوى واغفر لي ذنبي ووجهني للخير أينما توجهت ويدعو بهذا الدعاء في كل
منزل يدخل عليه
الخامسة في الركوب فإذا ركب الراحلة يقول بسم الله وبالله والله أكبر
توكلت على الله ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم ما شاء الله كان
وما لم يشأ لم يكن سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين وإنا إلى ربنا
لمنقلبون اللهم إني وجهت وجهي إليك وفوضت أمري كله إليك وتوكلت في جميع
أموري عليك أنت حسبي ونعم الوكيل
فإذا استوى على الراحلة واستوت تحته قال سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله
إلا الله والله أكبر سبع مرات وقال الحمد لله الذي هدانا لهذا وما كنا
لنهتدي لولا أن هدانا الله اللهم أنت الحامل على الظهر وأنت المستعان على
الأمور
السادسة في النزول والسنة أن لا ينزل حتى يحمى النهار ويكون أكثر سيره
بالليل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم بالدلجة فإن الأرض تطوي بالليل ما لا
تطوي بالنهار (3) وليقلل نومه بالليل حتى يكون PageV01P247
عونا على السير
ومهما أشرف على المنزل فليقل اللهم رب السموات السبع وما أظللن ورب
الأرضين السبع وما أقللن ورب الشياطين وما أضللن ورب الرياح وما ذرين ورب
البحار وما جرين أسالك خير هذا المنزل وخير أهله وأعوذ بك من شره وشر ما
فيه اصرف عني شر شرارهم
فإذا نزل المنزل صلى ركعتين فيه ثم قال أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات التي لا
يجاوزهن بر ولا فاجر من شر ما خلق
فإذا جن عليه الليل يقول يا أرض ربي وربك الله أعوذ بالله من شرك وشر ما
فيك وشر ما دب عليك أعوذ بالله من شر كل أسد وأسود وحية وعقرب ومن شر ساكن
البلد ووالد وما ولد وله ما  سكن في الليل والنهار وهو السميع العليم
السابعة في الحراسة ينبغي أن يحتاط بالنهار فلا يمشي منفردا خارج القافلة
لأنه ربما يغتال أو ينقطع ويكون بالليل متحفظا عند النوم فإن نام في ابتداء
الليل افترش ذراعه وإن نام في آخر الليل نصب ذراعه نصبا وجعل رأسه في كفه
هكذا كان ينام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سفره (1) لأنه ربما استثقل
النوم فتطلع الشمس وهو لا يدري فيكون ما يفوته من الصلاة أفضل مما يناله من
الحج والأحب في الليل أن يتناوب الرفيقان في الحراسة فإن نام أحدهما حرس
الآخر (2) فهو السنة فإن قصده عدو أو سبع في ليل أو نهار فليقرأ آية الكرسي
وشهد الله والإخلاص والمعوذتين وليقل بس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ي-ر (s-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Movement upon the earth, traversing a path; the act of journeying with deliberate purpose.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The soul's progression toward God through physical travel, mirroring spiritual wayfaring (sulūk).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical movement; metaphorical (majāz) for the heart's journey toward divine proximity.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — Sequential clauses linked by "ثم" and "فـ" to structure a graded series of obligatory and recommended acts, each building upon the prior.
chapters.translation:
I say: This section comprises eight matters concerning the journey from the moment of departure until the assumption of iḥrām.

**The First Matter: Concerning Wealth.** One should begin with repentance (tawbah), restoring what is owed to others (mazālim), settling debts, and preparing provisions for every person whose maintenance is obligatory upon him until the time of his return. He must return any deposits (wadāʾiʿ) in his possession. He should take with him lawful, pure wealth sufficient for his going and coming — not with miserliness, but in a manner that permits him to be generous with his provisions and kind to the weak and the poor. He should give charity before his departure. He should purchase for himself a mount strong enough to bear the load without weakening, or else hire one. If he hires, let him disclose to the hireman everything he intends to carry, whether little or much, and secure his full consent therein.

**The Second Matter: Concerning the Companion.** One should seek a righteous companion who loves goodness and assists in it — one who reminds him if he forgets, aids him if he remembers, emboldens him if he shows cowardice, strengthens him if he weakens, and bears patiently with him if his breast becomes constricted. He should bid farewell to his resident companions, brothers, and neighbors, seeking their supplications, for God the Exalted places good in their prayers. The Sunnah in bidding farewell is to say: "I entrust to God your religion, your trustworthiness, and the seal of your deeds." The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say to one intending travel: "In God's protection and His care. May God provide you with piety, forgive your sin, and direct you toward goodness wherever you may be."

**The Third Matter: Concerning Leaving the House.** When he resolves to depart, he should first pray two rakʿahs — reciting in the first, after the Fātiḥah, {«Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn»} and in the second {«al-Ikhlāṣ»}. When he finishes, he raises his hands and supplicates God with pure sincerity and truthful intention, saying: "O God, You are the Companion in travel and the Successor over family, wealth, children, and companions. Protect us and them from every affliction and malady. O God, we ask You in this journey of ours for righteousness and piety, and for deeds pleasing to You. O God, we ask You to fold the earth for us, to ease our travel, to grant us in our journey soundness of body, religion, and wealth, and to convey us to the pilgrimage of Your House and the visitation of the grave of Your Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him). O God, we seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, the gloom of the scene, and the evil return concerning family, wealth, children, and companions. O God, place us and them in Your protection, do not strip us and them of Your grace, and do not change the well-being You have bestowed upon us and them."

**The Fourth Matter: When He Reaches the Door of the House.** He says: "In the name of God. I place my trust in God. There is no might and no power except through God. I seek refuge with God. O Lord, I seek refuge in You from leading astray or being led astray, from humiliating or being humiliated, from slipping or being slipped, from wronging or being wronged, from acting ignorantly or being treated with ignorance. O God, I have not gone out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation — rather, I have gone out fearing Your displeasure, seeking Your good pleasure, fulfilling Your obligation, following the Sunnah of Your Prophet, and yearning for the vision of You." When he walks, he says: "O God, by You I have spread forth, upon You I rely, by You I hold fast, and toward You I direct myself. O God, You are my trust and You are my hope. Suffice me what concerns me, what does not concern me, and what You know better than I. Mighty is Your protection, glorious is Your praise, and there is no god but You. O God, provide me with piety, forgive me my sin, and direct me toward goodness wherever I turn." He repeats this supplication at every station he enters.

**The Fifth Matter: Concerning Riding.** When he mounts the riding beast, he says: "In the name of God, and through God. God is Greatest. I place my trust in God. There is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent. What God wills comes to be; what He does not will does not come to be. Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, though we were not capable of mastering it, and to our Lord we shall surely return. O God, I have turned my face toward You, entrusted my entire affair to You, and relied upon You in all my matters. You are my sufficiency, and the best of guardians." When he is seated firmly upon the mount and it is steady beneath him, he says: "Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest" — seven times — then says: "Praise be to God who has guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had God not guided us. O God, You are the Carrier upon the back, and You are the Helper in all affairs."

**The Sixth Matter: Concerning Alighting.** The Sunnah is not to alight until the day has become hot, and to make the greater part of his travel by night. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Travel by night, for the earth is folded by night in a way it is not folded by day." Let him minimize his sleep at night so that it becomes an aid to the journey. Whenever he draws near a station, let him say: "O God, Lord of the seven heavens and what they overshadow, Lord of the seven earths and what they carry, Lord of the devils and what they lead astray, Lord of the winds and what they scatter, Lord of the seas and what they flow — I ask You for the good of this station and the good of its people, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is within it. Turn away from me the evil of its wicked ones." When he alights at the station, he prays two rakʿahs therein, then says: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of God, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can transgress, from the evil of what He has created." When night falls upon him, he says: "O earth, my Lord and your Lord is God. I seek refuge in God from your evil, the evil of what is within you, and the evil of what creeps upon you. I seek refuge in God from the evil of every lion, serpent, scorpion, and from the evil of the dweller of the land, and from a parent and what he begets. To Him belongs what dwells in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

**The Seventh Matter: Concerning Vigilance.** One should be cautious by day, not walking alone outside the caravan, for he might be waylaid or cut off. By night, he should be guarded when sleeping. If he sleeps at the beginning of the night, he makes his arm a pillow; if he sleeps at the end of the night, he props his arm upright and places his head in his palm — thus did the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sleep on his journeys — for he might fall into heavy sleep, and the sun might rise while he is unaware, and what he misses of prayer would be better than what he attains of pilgrimage. It is preferable at night for the two companions to take turns guarding — if one sleeps, the other keeps watch — for this is the Sunnah. If an enemy or a wild beast approaches him, by night or by day, let him recite the Āyat al-Kursī, {«Shahida Allāhu»}, al-Ikhlāṣ, and the two Muʿawwidhatān, and say: "In the name of God. What God wills. There is no power except through God. God suffices me. I place my trust in God. What God wills — none brings good but God. What God wills — none repels evil but God. God suffices me and suffices. God hears whoever calls upon Him. There is no limit beyond God and no refuge apart from God. God has decreed: {«I shall prevail, I and My messengers»} — indeed, God is Strong, Mighty. I fortify myself with God the Magnificent, and I seek succor from the Living who never dies. O God, guard us with Your eye that never sleeps, and shelter us with Your pillar that cannot be assailed. O God, have mercy upon us through Your power over us, so that we perish not — and You are our trust and our hope. O God, incline toward us the hearts of Your male and female servants with gentleness and mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."

**The Eighth Matter:** Whenever he ascends a rise in the road, it is recommended to say "Allāhu Akbar" three times, then say: "O God, to You belongs the honor upon every height, and to You belongs all praise in every state." Whenever he descends, he glorifies (subḥān). Whenever he fears loneliness on his journey, he says: "Glory be to God, the King, the Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit. You have veiled the heavens with might and dominion."

chapters.title_en: The Second Section on the Etiquette of Iḥrām from the Mīqāt to Entering Mecca
chapters.arabic_text:
||| الجملة الثانية في آداب الإحرام من الميقات إلى دخول مكة

وهي خمسة الأول أن يغتسل وينوي به غسل الإحرام أعني إذا انتهى إلى
الميقات المشهور الذي يحرم الناس منه ويتمم غسله بالتنظيف ويسرح لحيته
ورأسه ويقلم أظفاره ويقص شاربه ويستكمل النظافة التي ذكرناها في الطهارة
الثاني أن يفارق الثياب المخيطة ويلبس  ثوبي الإحرام فيرتدي ويتزر بثوبين
أبيضين فالأبيض هو أحب الثياب إلى الله عز وجل ويتطيب في ثيابه وبدنه ولا
بأس بطيب يبقي جرمه بعد الإحرام فقد رؤي بعض المسك على مفرق رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم بعد الإحرام مما كان استعمله قبل الإحرام (3)
الثالث أن يصبر بعد لبس الثياب حتى تنبعث به راحلته إن كان راكبا أو يبدأ
بالسير إن كان راجلا فعند ذلك ينوي الإحرام بالحج أو بالعمرة PageV01P248
قرانا أو إفرادا كما أراد
ويكفي مجرد النية لانعقاد الإحرام ولكن السنة أن يقرن بالنية لفظ التلبية
فيقول لبيك اللهم لبيك لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك لا
شريك لك وإن زاد قال لبيك وسعديك والخير كله بيديك والرغباء إليك لبيك بحجة
حقا تعبدا ورقا اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد
الرابع إذا انعقد إحرامه بالتلبية المذكورة فيستحب أن يقول اللهم إني
أريد الحج فيسره لي وأعني على أداء فرضه وتقبله مني اللهم إني نويت أداء
فريضتك في الحج فاجعلني من الذين استجابوا لك وآمنوا بوعدك واتبعوا أمرك
واجعلني من وفدك الذين رضيت عنهم وارتضيت وقبلت منهم اللهم فيسر لي أداء ما
نويت من الحج اللهم قد أحرم لك لحمي وشعري ودمي وعصبي ومخي وعظامي وحرمت
على نفسي النساء والطيب ولبس المخيط ابتغاء وجهك والدار الآخرة
ومن وقت الإحرام حرم عليه المحظورات الستة التي ذكرناها من قبل فليجتنبها
الخامس يستحب تجديد التلبية في دوام الإحرام خصوصا عند اصطدام الرفاق
وعند اجتماع الناس وعند كل صعود وهبوط وعند كل ركوب ونزول رافعا بها صوته
بحيث لا يبح حلقه ولا ينبهر فإنه لا ينادي أصم ولا غائبا (1) كما ورد في
الخبر
ولا بأس برفع الصوت بالتلبية في المساجد الثلاثة فإنها مظنة المناسك أعني
المسجد الحرام ومسجد الخيف ومسجد الميقات وأما سائر المساجد فلا بأس فيها
بالتلبية من غير رفع صوت وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أعجبه شيء قال لبيك
إن العيش عيش الآخرة (2)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing the entire body with water, whether obligatory or supererogatory; the root denotes the act of cleansing that removes physical impurity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual context, it signifies the purification of the outward form (ẓāhir) as a precondition for the sanctity (ḥurma) of iḥrām, mirroring the inward purification of intention (niyya).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to water-washing; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the soul's cleansing from heedlessness.
- Root: ن-و-ي (n-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intent, purpose, resolution; the root implies a settled determination in the heart that distinguishes an act from mere movement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The theological linchpin of worship (ʿibādāt); niyya is the differentiator between habitual acts (ʿādāt) and devotional acts (qurubāt), and it is the very substance of iḥrām's validity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the heart's resolve; metaphorical when the tongue articulates it, for the tongue merely declares what the heart has already sealed.
- Root: ل-ب-ي (l-b-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To respond, to answer a call; the doubled form (labbayka) intensifies the response, implying repeated and continuous compliance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The talbiya is the verbal covenant (ʿahd) of the pilgrim, affirming God's absolute unity (tawḥīd) and the pilgrim's servitude (ʿubūdiyya) in response to the divine summons of Abraham.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal as a response to a caller; metaphorical in the ritual context, where it signifies the soul's answer to God's primordial command, "And proclaim the pilgrimage to mankind" {«وَأَذِّن فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ»}.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When the author says "أعني إذا انتهى إلى الميقات" (i.e., when he reaches the mīqāt), the particle "أعني" introduces an explicative apposition that restricts and specifies the preceding general statement, a construction Sībawayh treats as a parenthetical clarification that does not disturb the syntactic flow of the main clause.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second section concerns the etiquette of iḥrām from the mīqāt to the entry into Mecca. These are five.

The first: That he perform the major ablution (ghusl), intending thereby the bath of iḥrām — that is, when he reaches the well-known mīqāt from which the people assume iḥrām — and he completes his bath with cleansing, combing his beard and head, trimming his nails, clipping his moustache, and perfecting the cleanliness which we have already mentioned in the Book of Purification.

The second: That he part with sewn garments and don the two garments of iḥrām, wrapping himself in the lower garment (izār) and the upper drape (ridāʾ), both white — for white is the most beloved of garments to God, Mighty and Majestic. He may apply perfume to his garments and body, and there is no harm in a fragrance whose substance remains after iḥrām, for some musk was observed on the parting of the hair of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, after iḥrām, from what he had used before iḥrām.

The third: That he wait after donning the garments until his mount rises with him if he is riding, or he begins to walk if he is on foot. At that moment he intends iḥrām for the pilgrimage (ḥajj) or for the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumra), whether as a combined pilgrimage (qirān) or as a single one (ifrād), as he wishes. The mere intention suffices for the contraction of iḥrām, but the Sunna is to couple the intention with the utterance of the talbiya, saying: "Here I am, O God, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Verily, praise and grace are Yours, and the dominion. You have no partner." If he adds, he says: "Here I am, and at Your service. All good is in Your hands, and the supplication is to You. Here I am, for a true pilgrimage, in worship and servitude. O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad."

The fourth: When his iḥrām is contracted by the aforementioned talbiya, it is recommended that he say: "O God, verily I desire the pilgrimage, so make it easy for me, assist me in performing its obligation, and accept it from me. O God, verily I have intended to perform Your obligation in the pilgrimage, so make me among those who responded to You, believed in Your promise, and followed Your command. Make me among Your guests (wafd) with whom You were pleased, whom You accepted, and from whom You received. O God, make easy for me the performance of what I have intended of the pilgrimage. O God, verily I have consecrated to You my flesh, my hair, my blood, my sinews, my marrow, and my bones, and I have made unlawful to myself women, perfume, and the wearing of sewn garments, seeking Your Face and the Abode of the Hereafter."

From the time of iḥrām, the six prohibitions which we mentioned previously become unlawful for him, so let him avoid them.

The fifth: It is recommended to renew the talbiya throughout the duration of iḥrām, especially at the meeting of companions, at the gathering of people, at every ascent and descent, and at every mounting and dismounting, raising his voice with it — yet not to the point of hoarsening his throat nor exhausting his breath, for he is not calling a deaf one nor an absent one, as has come in the report.

There is no harm in raising the voice with the talbiya in the three mosques, for they are the places of the rites (manāsik) — namely, the Sacred Mosque, the Mosque of al-Khayf, and the Mosque of the Mīqāt. As for other mosques, there is no harm in the talbiya therein without raising the voice. And it was the practice of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that when something pleased him, he would say: "Here I am, verily the true life is the life of the Hereafter."

chapters.title_en: The Third Discourse on the Etiquette of Entering Mecca until the Circumambulation
chapters.arabic_text:
||| الجملة الثالثة في  آداب دخول مكة إلى الطواف

وهي ستة الأول أن يغتسل بذي طوى لدخول مكة
والاغتسالات المستحبة المسنونة في الحج تسعة
الأول للإحرام من الميقات ثم لدخول مكة ثم لطواف القدوم ثم للوقوف بعرفة
ثم للوقوف بمزدلفة ثم ثلاثة أغسال لرمي الجمار الثلاث ولا غسل لرمي جمرة
العقبة ثم لطواف الوداع ولم ير الشافعي رضي الله عنه في الجديد الغسل لطواف
الزيارة ولطواف الوداع فتعود إلى سلعة
الثاني أن يقول عند الدخول في أول الحرم وهو خارج مكة اللهم هذا حرمك
وأمنك فحرم لحمي ودمي وشعري وبشري على النار وآمني من عذابك يوم تبعث عبادك
واجعلني من أوليائك وأهل طاعتك
الثالث أن يدخل مكة من جانب الأبطح وهو ثنية كدا بفتح الكاف عدل رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من جادة الطريق إليها (3) فالتأسي به أولى وإذا
خرج خرج من ثنية كدى بضم الكاف وهي الثنية السفلى والأولى هي العليا
الرابع إذا دخل مكة وانتهى إلى راس الردم فعنده يقع بصره على البيت فليقل
لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر اللهم أنت السلام ومنك السلام ودارك دار السلام
تباركت يا ذا الجلال والإكرام اللهم إن هذا بيتك عظمته وكرمته وشرفته اللهم
فزده تعظيما وزده تشريفا وتكريما وزده مهابة وزد من حجه برا وكرامة اللهم
افتح لي أبواب رحمتك وأدخلني جنتك وأعذني من الشيطان الرجيم
الخامس إذا دخل المسجد الحرام فليدخل من باب بني شيبة وليقل بسم الله
وبالله ومن الله وإلى وفي سبيل الله وعلى ملة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
فإذا قرب من البيت قال الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى اللهم
PageV01P249
صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك وعلى إبراهيم خليلك وعلى جميع أنبيائك ورسلك
وليرفع يديه وليقل اللهم إني أسألك في مقامي هذا في أول مناسكي أن تتقبل
توبتي وأن تتجاوز عن خطيئتي وتضع عني وزري الحمد لله الذي بلغني بيته
الحرام الذي جعله مثابة للناس وأمنا وجعله مباركا وهدى للعالمين اللهم إني
عبدك والبلد بلدك والحرم حرمك  والبيت بيتك جئتك أطلب رحمتك وأسألك مسألة
المضطر الخائف من عقوبتك الراجي لرحمتك الطالب مرضاتك
السادس أن تقصد الحجر الأسود بعد ذلك وتمسه بيدك اليمنى وتقبله وتقول
اللهم أمانتي اديتها وميثاقي وفيته اشهد لي بالموافاة فإن لم يستطيع
التقبيل وقف في مقابلته ويقول ذلك ثم لا يعرج على شيء دون الطواف وهو طواف
القدوم إلا أن يجد الناس في المكتوبة فيصلي معهم ثم يطوف
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ-س-ل (gh-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Washing the body with water; ritual purification by ablution of the whole form.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ceremonial cleansing (ghusl) as a Sunnah-commended act of physical and spiritual preparation for sacred rites.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal washing (ḥaqīqah) versus metaphorical purification of the soul from sins (majāz).
- Root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mountain pass or defile (thaniyyah); bending or folding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A geographical landmark associated with prophetic practice (taʾassī), not a ritual obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal topographical term; used here as a specific site for emulation, not metaphor.
- Root: ط-و-ف (t-w-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Circling around; encompassing movement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ritual circumambulation of the Kaʿbah (ṭawāf), a pillar of pilgrimage.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical circling; metaphorically, the soul's orbit around divine presence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with In (إن) — The protasis (condition) and apodosis (result) are parsed with the verb in the jussive or indicative as context demands; here, "if he cannot kiss" (فإن لم يستطع) governs a permissible alternative action, showing juristic flexibility in ritual.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third discourse concerns the etiquette of entering Mecca up to the circumambulation. These are six in number.

The first is that he perform the major ablution (ghusl) at Dhū Ṭuwā for entering Mecca. The commendable and Sunnah-recommended ablutions during the pilgrimage are nine: the first for the state of consecration (iḥrām) from the miqāt; then for entering Mecca; then for the circumambulation of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm); then for the standing at ʿArafāt; then for the standing at Muzdalifah; then three ablutions for the three stone-throwings (ramy al-jimār), with no ablution for the throwing of the ʿAqabah pillar; then for the farewell circumambulation (ṭawāf al-wadāʿ). Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, did not hold in the new opinion (al-jadīd) that ablution is required for the circumambulation of visitation (ṭawāf al-ziyārah) or the farewell circumambulation, so the matter reverts to the preferred view (salʿah).

The second is that he say upon entering the beginning of the Sacred Precinct (al-ḥaram), while still outside Mecca: "O God, this is Your sanctuary and Your place of security, so make my flesh, my blood, my hair, and my skin forbidden to the Fire, and grant me security from Your punishment on the day You resurrect Your servants, and make me among Your friends and the people of Your obedience."

The third is that he enter Mecca from the side of al-Abṭaḥ, which is the pass of Kudā (with the opening of the kāf). The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, deviated from the main road to it, so emulating him is more virtuous. When he departs, he should exit from the pass of Kudā (with the damma on the kāf), which is the lower pass, while the first is the upper one.

The fourth is that when he enters Mecca and reaches the head of the embankment (raʾs al-radm), where his gaze falls upon the House, he should say: "There is no god but God, and God is greatest. O God, You are Peace, and from You is peace, and Your abode is the Abode of Peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. O God, this is Your House; You have magnified it, honored it, and ennobled it. O God, increase it in majesty, increase it in honor and veneration, increase it in awe, and increase in honor and nobility whoever performs the pilgrimage to it. O God, open for me the doors of Your mercy, admit me into Your Paradise, and protect me from the accursed Satan."

The fifth is that when he enters the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Ḥarām), he should enter through the Gate of Banī Shaybah and say: "In the name of God, and with God, and from God, and to God, and in the path of God, and upon the creed of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace." When he draws near to the House, he should say: "Praise be to God, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen. O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, and upon Abraham, Your intimate friend, and upon all Your prophets and messengers." He should raise his hands and say: "O God, I ask You in this station of mine, at the beginning of my rites, that You accept my repentance, that You overlook my transgression, and that You remove from me my burden. Praise be to God who has conveyed me to His Sacred House, which He has made a place of return for mankind and a security, and made it blessed and a guidance for the worlds. O God, I am Your servant, the land is Your land, the sanctuary is Your sanctuary, and the House is Your House. I have come to You seeking Your mercy, and I ask You with the asking of one distressed, fearful of Your punishment, hoping for Your mercy, and seeking Your good pleasure."

The sixth is that he then make for the Black Stone, touch it with his right hand, kiss it, and say: "O God, I have fulfilled my trust and fulfilled my covenant; bear witness to me for the meeting." If he is unable to kiss it, he stands opposite it and says this. Then he should not turn aside to anything before the circumambulation, which is the circumambulation of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm), unless he finds the people in the obligatory prayer, in which case he prays with them, and then circumambulates.

chapters.title_en: The Fourth Discourse: On the Circumambulation (Ṭawāf)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| الجملة الرابعة في الطواف

فإذا أراد افتتاح الطواف إما للقدوم وإما لغيره فينبغي أن يراعي أمورا
ستة
الأول أن يراعي شروط الصلاة من طهارة الحدث والخبث في الثوب والبدن
والمكان وستر العورة
فالطواف بالبيت صلاة ولكن الله سبحانه أباح فيه الكلام وليضطبع قبل
ابتداء الطواف وهو أن يجعل وسط ردائه تحت إبطه اليمنى ويجمع طرفيه على
منكبه الأيسر فيرخي طرفا وراء ظهره وطرفا على صدره ويقطع التلبية عند
ابتداء الطواف ويشتغل بالأدعية التي سنذكرها
الثاني إذا فرغ من الاضطباع فليجعل البيت على يساره وليقف عند الحجر
الأسود وليتنح عنه قليلا ليكون الحجر قدامه فيمر بجميع الحجر بجميع بدنه في
ابتداء طوافه
وليجعل بينه وبين البيت قدر ثلاث خطوات ليكون قريبا من البيت فإنه أفضل
ولكيلا يكون طائفا على الشاذروان فإنه من البيت وعند الحجر الأسود قد يتصل
الشاذروان بالأرض ويلتبس به والطائف عليه لا يصح طوافه لأنه طائف في البيت
والشاذروان هو الذي فضل عن عرض جدار البيت بعد أن ضيق أعلى الجدار ثم من
هذا الموقف يبتدىء الطواف
الثالث أن يقول قبل مجاوزة الحجر بل في ابتداء الطواف بسم الله والله
أكبر اللهم إيمانا بك وتصديقا بكتابك ووفاء بعهدك واتباعا لسنة نبيك محمد
صلى الله عليه وسلم ويطوف
فأول ما يجاوز الحجر ينتهي إلى باب البيت فيقول اللهم هذا البيت بيتك
وهذا الحرم حرمك وهذا الأمن أمنك وهذا مقام العائذ بك من النار
وعند ذكر المقام يشير بعينه إلى مقام إبراهيم عليه السلام اللهم إن بيتك
عظيم ووجهك كريم وأنت أرحم الراحمين فأعذني من النار  ومن الشيطان الرجيم
وحرم لحمي ودمي على النار وآمني من أهوال يوم القيامة واكفني مؤنة الدنيا
والآخرة
ثم يسبح الله تعالى ويحمده حتى يبلغ الركن العراقي فعنده يقول اللهم إني
أعوذ بك من الشرك الشك والكفر والنفاق والشقاق وسوء الأخلاق وسوء المنظر في
الأهل والمال والولد
فإذا بلغ الميزاب قال اللهم أظلنا تحت عرشك يوم لا ظل إلا ظلك اللهم
اسقني بكأس محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم شربة لا أظمأ بعدها أبدا
فإذا بلغ الركن الشامي قال اللهم اجعله حجا مبرورا وسعيا مشكورا وذنبا
مغفورا وتجارة لن تبور يا عزيز يا غفور رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم إنك
أنت الأعز الأكرم فإذا بلغ الركن اليماني قال اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الكفر
وأعوذ بك من الفقر ومن عذاب القبر ومن فتنة المحيا والممات وأعوذ بك من
الخزي في الدنيا والآخرة ويقول بين الركن اليماني والحجر الأسود اللهم ربنا
آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا برحمتك فتنة القبر وعذاب النار
فإذا بلغ الحجر الأسود قال اللهم اغفر لي برحمتك أعوذ برب هذا الحجر من
الدين والفقر وضيق الصدر وعذاب القبر وعند ذلك قد تم شوط واحد فيطوف كذلك
سبعة أشواط فيدعو بهذه الأدعية في كل شوط
الرابع أن يرمل في ثلاثة أشواط ويمشي في الأربعة الأخر
PageV01P250
على الهيئة المعتادة
ومعنى الرمل الإسراع في المشي مع تقارب الخطا وهو دون العدو وفوق المشي
المعتاد
والمقصود منه ومن الاضطباع إظهار الشطارة والجلادة والقوة هكذا كان القصد
أولا قطعا لطمع الكفار وبقيت تلك السنة (1) والأفضل الرمل مع الدنو من
البيت فإن لم يمكنه للزحمة فالرمل مع البعد أفضل فيخرج إلى حاشية المطاف
وليرمل ثلاثا ثم ليقرب إلى البيت في المزدحم وليمش أربعا
وإن أمكنه استلام الحجر في كل شوط فهو الأحب وإن منعه الزحمة أشار باليد
وقبل يده وكذلك استلام الركن اليماني يستحب من سائر الأركان
وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يستلم الركن اليماني (2) ويقبله (3)
ويضع خده عليه (4) ومن  أراد تخصيص الحجر بالتقبيل واقتصر في الركن اليماني
على الاستلام أغنى عن اللمس باليد فهو أولى
الخامس إذا تم الطواف سبعا فليأت الملتزم وهو بين الحجر والباب وهو موضع
استجابة الدعوة وليلتزق بالبيت وليتعلق بالأستار وليلصق بطنه بالبيت وليضع
عليه خده الأيمن وليبسط عليه ذراعيه وكفيه وليقل اللهم يا رب البيت العتيق
أعتق رقبتي من النار وأعذني من الشيطان الرجيم وأعذني من كل سوء وقنعني بما
رزقتني وبارك لي فيما آتيتني اللهم إن هذا البيت بيتك والعبد عبدك وهذا
مقام العائذ بك من النار اللهم اجعلني من أكرم وفدك عليك ثم ليحمد الله
كثيرا في هذا الموضع وليصل على رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى جميع الرسل
كثيرا وليدع بحوائجه الخاصة وليستغفر من ذنوبه
كان بعض السلف في هذا الموضع يقول لمواليه تنحوا عني حتى أقر لربي بذنوبي
السادس إذا فرغ من ذلك ينبغي أن يصلي خلف المقام ركعتين يقرأ في الأولى
قل يا أيها الكافرون وفي الثانية الإخلاص وهما ركعتا الطواف
قال الزهري مضت السنة أن يصلي لكل سبع ركعتين (5) وإن قرن بين أسابيع
وصلى ركعتين جاز (6) فعل ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكل أسبوع طواف
وليدع بعد ركعتي الطواف وليقل اللهم يسر لي اليسرى وجنبني العسرى واغفر
لي في الآخرة والأولى واع
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To go around, encircle, encompass; the act of circling a thing, derived from the notion of encompassing movement around a center.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the sacred law, the specific devotional act of encircling the Kaʿbah seven times, a rite of pilgrimage (manāsik) embodying the soul's orientation toward the Divine House.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical encircling; metaphorical (majāz) for encompassing obedience and devotion, as the heart circumambulates the remembrance of God.
- Root: ض-ط-ب-ع (ḍ-ṭ-b-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To place something under the armpit (iḍṭibāʿ); the act of baring the right shoulder by passing the upper garment beneath the right armpit and casting its ends over the left shoulder.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A ritual state (hayʾah) of the pilgrim (muḥrim) during ṭawāf, symbolizing readiness and vigor in service.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal bodily posture; metaphorically, the casting off of indolence in approaching the Divine.
- Root: ر-م-ل (r-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To hasten with short, quick steps; the rapid gait with a slight trotting motion, distinct from running (ʿadw) and ordinary walking.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A Prophetic practice (sunnah) in the first three circuits, manifesting physical prowess and dispelling the enemy's hope.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the gait; metaphorical for spiritual alacrity in the pursuit of worship.
- Root: ل-ز-م (l-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cling, adhere, or cleave to something; the place of clinging (multazam) between the Black Stone and the Door.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The sacred spot where supplication is answered; the act of pressing the body against the Kaʿbah in humble entreaty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical clinging; metaphorical for the soul's desperate attachment to Divine mercy.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Condition and Consequence (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The opening conditional clause "فإذا أراد" (when he intends) governs a sequence of imperative and apodictic statements, each introduced by "فينبغي" or "فليفعل," establishing a structured ritual protocol with precise syntactic coordination.
chapters.translation:
I say: When the pilgrim intends to commence the circumambulation (ṭawāf)—whether for the arrival (qudūm) or for another purpose—he should observe six matters.

**The First:** That he observe the conditions of prayer (shurūṭ al-ṣalāh): purity from ritual impurity (ḥadath) and from filth (khabath) in the garment, the body, and the place, and the covering of the private parts (satr al-ʿawrah). For the circumambulation of the House is a prayer, but God—glorified be He—has permitted speech therein. And he should perform the iḍṭibāʿ before beginning the ṭawāf, which is to place the middle of his cloak (ridāʾ) beneath his right armpit, gather its two ends upon his left shoulder, letting one end hang behind his back and the other upon his chest. And he should cease the talbiyah at the commencement of the ṭawāf and occupy himself with the supplications (adʿiyah) which we shall mention.

**The Second:** When he has finished the iḍṭibāʿ, let him place the House on his left side and stand at the Black Stone (al-Ḥajar al-Aswad). Let him draw back slightly from it so that the Stone is before him, and he passes by the entire Stone with his entire body at the beginning of his circuit. And let him place between himself and the House a distance of about three steps, so that he is near the House—for that is more virtuous—and so that he does not circumambulate upon the Shādhrawān, for it is part of the House. At the Black Stone, the Shādhrawān may connect with the ground and become confused with it; and the one who circumambulates upon it, his ṭawāf is not valid, because he is circumambulating within the House. The Shādhrawān is that which remains from the width of the House's wall after the upper part of the wall was narrowed. Then from this standing place he begins the ṭawāf.

**The Third:** That he say before passing the Stone—rather, at the commencement of the ṭawāf: "In the name of God, and God is Most Great. O God, in faith in You, and in affirmation of Your Book, and in fulfillment of Your covenant, and in following the Sunnah of Your Prophet Muḥammad—may God's peace and blessings be upon him." Then he circumambulates. When he first passes the Stone, he reaches the Door of the House and says: "O God, this House is Your House, and this Sanctuary is Your Sanctuary, and this security is Your security, and this is the station of the one seeking refuge in You from the Fire." And at the mention of the station (maqām), he gestures with his eye toward the Station of Abraham (maqām Ibrāhīm)—peace be upon him. "O God, Your House is great, and Your Face is noble, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. So protect me from the Fire, and from the accursed Satan. And make my flesh and my blood forbidden to the Fire, and grant me security from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, and spare me the burden of this world and the Hereafter."

Then he glorifies God—exalted be He—and praises Him until he reaches the Iraqi Corner (al-Rukn al-ʿIrāqī). At it he says: "O God, I seek refuge in You from polytheism (shirk), doubt (shakk), disbelief (kufr), hypocrisy (nifāq), discord (shiqāq), evil character (sūʾ al-akhlāq), and evil appearance in family, wealth, and offspring."

When he reaches the Water Spout (al-Mīzāb), he says: "O God, shade us beneath Your Throne on the Day when there is no shade but Your shade. O God, give me to drink from the cup of Muḥammad—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—a drink after which I shall never thirst."

When he reaches the Syrian Corner (al-Rukn al-Shāmī), he says: "O God, make it an accepted pilgrimage (ḥajjan mabrūran), a thanked endeavor (saʿyan mashkūran), a forgiven sin (dhanban maghfūran), and a commerce that will never perish (tijāratan lan tabūr). O Mighty, O Forgiving. O Lord, forgive and have mercy, and overlook what You know. Indeed, You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous."

When he reaches the Yemeni Corner (al-Rukn al-Yamānī), he says: "O God, I seek refuge in You from disbelief, and I seek refuge in You from poverty, and from the punishment of the grave, and from the trial of life and death, and I seek refuge in You from disgrace in this world and the Hereafter."

And between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone he says: "O God, our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us—by Your mercy—from the trial of the grave and the punishment of the Fire."

When he reaches the Black Stone, he says: "O God, forgive me by Your mercy. I seek refuge in the Lord of this Stone from debt, poverty, constriction of the breast, and the punishment of the grave." At that point, one circuit (shawṭ) is completed. He circumambulates thus seven circuits, reciting these supplications in every circuit.

**The Fourth:** That he hasten (yarmul) in three circuits and walk in the remaining four in the customary manner. The meaning of ramal is hastening in walking with close steps—it is below running (ʿadw) and above customary walking. The intent of it and of the iḍṭibāʿ is to manifest vigor (shaṭārah), robustness (jalādah), and strength (quwwah). Thus was the original intent—decisively—to cut off the hope of the disbelievers, and that Sunnah remained. The more virtuous is the ramal with proximity to the House; but if that is not possible due to crowding, then the ramal at a distance is more virtuous, so he goes out to the edge of the circumambulation area (al-Maṭāf). Let him hasten three circuits, then draw near to the House in the crowd, and walk four.

If he is able to touch the Black Stone (istilām) in every circuit, that is most beloved. If the crowd prevents him, he gestures with his hand and kisses it. Likewise, touching the Yemeni Corner is recommended above the other corners. It is narrated that the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—used to touch the Yemeni Corner and kiss it and place his cheek upon it. And whoever wishes to single out the Stone for kissing and restricts himself to touching (istilām) at the Yemeni Corner—that suffices over touching by hand, and it is more appropriate.

**The Fifth:** When he completes the ṭawāf of seven circuits, let him come to the Multazam—which is between the Stone and the Door—and it is a place where supplication is answered. Let him cling to the House, hang upon the curtains (astār), press his belly against the House, place his right cheek upon it, and spread his arms and palms upon it. And let him say: "O God, O Lord of the Ancient House (al-Bayt al-ʿAtīq), free my neck from the Fire, and protect me from the accursed Satan, and protect me from every evil, and make me content with what You have provided me, and bless me in what You have given me. O God, this House is Your House, and the servant is Your servant, and this is the station of the one seeking refuge in You from the Fire. O God, make me among the most honored of Your guests before You." Then let him praise God abundantly in this place, and send blessings upon His Messenger—peace and blessings be upon him—and upon all the messengers abundantly, and let him supplicate for his specific needs, and seek forgiveness for his sins.

Some of the Salaf used to say at this place to their attendants: "Withdraw from me, until I confess my sins to my Lord."

**The Sixth:** When he finishes this, he should pray two units (rakʿatayn) behind the Station (Maqām). He recites in the first {«قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ»} ("Say: O disbelievers") and in the second {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} ("Say: He is God, the One"). These are the two units of the ṭawāf. Al-Zuhrī said: "The Sunnah has been established that one prays two units for every seven circuits." And if he combines multiple sets of seven and prays two units, that is permissible—the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—did so. And every set of seven is a ṭawāf.

And let him supplicate after the two units of the ṭawāf, saying: "O God, ease for me the easy way, and turn me away from the hard way, and forgive me in the Hereafter and the First. And guard me with Your graces (alṭāf) so that I do not disobey You, and aid me in Your obedience by Your success-giving (tawfīq). And turn me away from Your disobediences, and make me among those who love You, and love Your angels and Your messengers, and love Your righteous servants. O God, make me beloved to Your angels and Your messengers, and to Your righteous servants. O God, just as You guided me to Islam, so establish me upon it with Your graces and Your guardianship (wilāyah), and employ me in obedience to You and obedience to Your Messenger, and save me from the misguiding trials (muḍillāt al-fitan)."

Then let him return to the Stone, touch it, and conclude the ṭawāf with it. The Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Whoever circumambulates the House seven times and prays two units, for him is the reward of freeing a slave." This is the manner (kayfiyyah) of the ṭawāf.

The obligatory (wājib) portion of it, after the conditions of prayer, is: to complete the number of circuits—seven—around the entire House; to begin at the Black Stone; to place the House on his left; to circumambulate within the Mosque and outside the House—not upon the Shādhrawān nor within the Ḥijr; and to maintain continuity (muwālāh) between the circuits, not separating them in an unusual manner. Beyond this, all is Sunnah and prescribed forms (hayʾāt).

||| الجملة الخامسة في السعي

فإذا فرغ من الطواف فليخرج من باب الصفا وهو في محاذاة الضلع الذي بين
الركن اليماني والحجر فإذا خرج من ذلك الباب وانتهى إلى الصفا وهو جبل
فيرقى فيه درجات في حضيض الجبل بقدر قامة الرجل رقى رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم حتى بدت له الكعبة (2)
وابتداء السعي من أصل الجبل كاف وهذه الزيادة مستحبة ولكن بعض تلك الدرج
مستحدثة فينبغي أن لا يخلفها وراء ظهره فلا يكون متمما للسعي وإذا ابتدأ من
ههنا سعى بينه وبين المروة سبع مرات
وعند رقية في الصفا ينبغي أن يستقبل البيت ويقول الله أكبر الله أكبر
الحمد لله على ما هدانا الحمد لله بمحامده كلها على جميع نعمه كلها لا إله
إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت بيده الخير وهو
على كل شيء قدير لا إله إلا الله وحده صدق وعده ونصر عبده وأعز جنده وهزم
الأحزاب وحده لا إله إلا الله مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون لا إله إلا
الله مخلصين له الدين الحمد لله رب العالمين فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين
تصبحون وله الحمد في السموات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون يخرج الحي من الميت
ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك تخرجون ومن آياته أن
خلقكم من تراب ثم إذا أنتم بشر تنتشرون اللهم إني أسألك إيمانا دائما
ويقينا صادقا وعلما نافعا وقلبا خاشعا ولسانا ذاكرا وأسألك العفو والعافية
والمعافاة الدائمة في الدنيا والآخرة ويصلي على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
ويدعو الله عز وجل بما شاء من حاجته عقيب هذا الدعاء
ثم ينزل ويبتدىء السعي وهو يقول رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم إنك أنت
الأعز الأكرم اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار
ويمشي على هينة حتى ينتهي إلى الميل الأخضر وهو أول ما يلقاه  إذا نزل من
الصفا وهو على زاوية المسجد الحرام فإذا بقي بينه وبين محاذاة الميل ستة
أذرع أخذ في السير السريع وهو الرمل حتى ينتهي إلى الميلين الأخضرين
ثم يعود إلى الهينة فإذا انتهى إلى المروة صعدها كما صعد الصفا وأقبل
بوجهه على الصفا ودعا بمثل ذلك الدعاء وقد حصل السعي مرة واحدة فإذا عاد
إلى الصفا حصلت مرتان يفعل ذلك سبعا ويرمل في موضع الرمل في كل مرة ويسكن
في موضع السكون كما سبق وفي كل نوبة يصعد الصفا والمروة فإذا فعل ذلك فقد
فرغ من طواف القدوم والسعي وهما سنتان
والطهارة مستحبة للسعي وليست بواجبة بخلاف الطواف وإذا سعى فينبغي أن لا
يعيد السعي بعد الوقوف ويكتفي بهذا ركنا فإنه ليس من شروط السعي أن يتأخر
عن الوقوف وإنما ذلك شرط في طواف الركن نعم شرط كل سعي أن يقع بعد طواف أي

chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ع-ي (Sa-ʿAyn-Yā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to strive, exert effort, or run briskly" — the root denotes purposeful movement toward a goal, whether physical or metaphorical.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual context, saʿy is the sacred pacing between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, symbolizing earnest seeking (ṭalab) and devotion; it is a divinely ordained act of worship, not mere locomotion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = rapid walking; metaphorical (majāz) = striving in deeds or supplication. Here, the term is used literally for the physical rite, but its spiritual import is the exertion of the soul.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause Sequencing (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The text uses "fa-idhā" (فإذا) to link completed actions (e.g., finishing ṭawāf) to subsequent obligations, with the jawāb (apodosis) indicating the resultant command or recommended act.
chapters.translation:
I say: When the pilgrim has completed the circumambulation (ṭawāf), let him exit through the Gate of al-Ṣafā, which lies in alignment with the side between the Yamānī Corner and the Black Stone. When he has exited through that gate and reached al-Ṣafā — which is a mountain — he ascends upon its steps at the mountain's base to the height of a man's stature, for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) ascended until the Kaʿbah became visible to him.

The commencement of the saʿy from the mountain's base is sufficient, and this additional ascent is recommended (mustaḥabb). However, some of those steps are newly constructed, so he should not leave them behind his back, lest he fail to complete the saʿy properly. When he begins from this point, he paces between it and al-Marwah seven times.

Upon ascending al-Ṣafā, he should face the House (the Kaʿbah) and say: "God is Greater, God is Greater. Praise be to God for guiding us. Praise be to God with all His praises, for all His blessings. There is no god but God alone, with no partner; to Him belongs sovereignty and to Him belongs praise; He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good, and He is powerful over all things. There is no god but God alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and honored His soldiers; He alone defeated the confederates. There is no god but God, sincere to Him in religion, even if the disbelievers detest it. There is no god but God, sincere to Him in religion. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. So glorified be God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning; and to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at the afternoon and when you reach the noonday. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death; and thus shall you be brought forth. And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then behold, you are humans spreading abroad. O God, I ask You for enduring faith, truthful certainty, beneficial knowledge, a humble heart, and a tongue that remembers You; and I ask You for pardon, well-being, and perpetual protection in this world and the Hereafter." Then he sends blessings upon Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and supplicates to God Almighty with whatever needs he wishes, following this prayer.

Then he descends and begins the saʿy, saying: "O Lord, forgive and have mercy, and overlook what You know; indeed, You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous. O God, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the torment of the Fire." He walks at a leisurely pace until he reaches the first green marker, which is the first thing he encounters upon descending from al-Ṣafā, located at the corner of the Sacred Mosque. When there remains between him and the alignment of the marker six cubits, he begins rapid pacing — which is the ramal — until he reaches the two green markers. Then he returns to a leisurely pace. When he reaches al-Marwah, he ascends it as he ascended al-Ṣafā, turns his face toward al-Ṣafā, and supplicates with a similar prayer. Thus, one saʿy is completed. When he returns to al-Ṣafā, two are completed. He does this seven times, performing the ramal in its designated place each time and slowing in its designated place as previously mentioned. In each round, he ascends al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah. When he has done this, he has completed the ṭawāf of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm) and the saʿy — both of which are Sunnah.

Ritual purity (ṭahārah) is recommended for the saʿy but not obligatory, unlike the ṭawāf. If he has performed the saʿy, he should not repeat it after the standing at ʿArafāt (wuqūf); rather, he suffices with this as a pillar (rukn), for it is not a condition of the saʿy that it be delayed until after the wuqūf. That condition applies only to the circumambulation of the pillar (ṭawāf al-rukn). Indeed, the condition for every saʿy is that it occur after a circumambulation, whichever circumambulation it may be.

||| الجملة السادسة في الوقوف وما قبله

الحاج إذا انتهى يوم عرفة إلى عرفات يتفرغ لطواف القدوم ودخول مكة قبل
الوقوف وإذا وصل قبل ذلك بأيام فطاف طواف القدوم فيمكث محرما إلى اليوم
السابع من ذي الحجة فيخطب الإمام بمكة خطبة بعد الظهر عند الكعبة ويأمر
الناس بالاستعداد للخروج إلى منى يوم التروية والمبيت بها وبالغدو منها إلى
عرفة لإقامة فرض الوقوف بعد الزوال إذ وقت الوقوف من الزوال إلى طلوع الفجر
الصادق من يوم النحر فينبغي أن يخرج إلى منى ملبيا ويستحب له المشي من مكة
في المناسك إلى انقضاء حجته إن قدر عليه والمشي من مسجد إبراهيم عليه
السلام إلى الموقف أفضل وآكد
فإذا انتهى إلى منى قال اللهم هذه منى فامنن علي بما مننت به على أوليائك
وأهل طاعتك وليمكث هذه الليلة بمنى وهو مبيت منزل لا يتعلق به نسك فإذا
أصبح يوم عرفة صلى الصبح فإذا طلعت الشمس على ثبير سار إلى عرفات ويقول
اللهم أجعلها خير غدوة غدوتها قط واقربها من رضوانك وأبعدها من سخطك اللهم
إليك غدوت وإياك  رجوت وعليك اعتمدت ووجهك أردت فاجعلني ممن تباهي به اليوم
من هو خير مني وأفضل
فإذا أتى عرفات فليضرب خباءه بنمرة قريبا من المسجد فثم ضرب رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم قبته (1) ونمرة هي بطن عرنة دون الموقف ودون عرفة
وليغتسل للوقوف فإذا زالت الشمس خطب الإمام خطبة وجيزة وقعد وأخذ المؤذن في
المؤذن في الأذان والإمام في الخطبة الثانية ووصل الإقامة بالأذان وفرغ
الإمام مع تمام إقامة المؤذن ثم جمع بين الظهر والعصر بأذان وإقامتين وقصر
الصلاة وراح إلى الموقف فليقف بعرفة ولا يقفن في وادي عرنة وأما مسجد
إبراهيم عليه السلام فصدره في الوادي وأخرياته من عرفة فمن وقف في صدر
المسجد لم يحصل له الوقوف بعرفة
ويتميز مكان عرفة من المسجد بصخرات كبار فرشت ثم
والأفضل أن يقف عند الصخرات بقرب الإمام مستقبلا للقبلة راكبا وليكثر من
أنواع التحميد والتسبيح والتهليل والثناء على الله عز وجل والدعاء والتوبة
ولا يصوم في هذا اليوم ليقوى على المواظبة على الدعاء
ولا يقطع التلبية يوم عرفة بل الأحب أن يلبي تارة ويكب على الدعاء أخرى
وينبغي أن لا ينفصل من طرف عرفة إلا بعد الغروب ليجمع في عرفة بين الليل
والنهار وإن أمكنه الوقوف يوم الثامن ساعة عند إمكان الغلط في الهلال فهو
الحزم وبه الأمن من الفوات
ومن فاته الوقوف حتى طلع الفجر يوم النحر فقد فاته الحج فعليه أن يتحلل
عن إحرامه بأعمال العمرة ثم يريق دما لأجل الفوات ثم يقضي العام الآتي
وليكن أهم اشتغاله في هذا اليوم الدعاء ففي مثل تلك البقعة ومثل ذلك الجمع
ترجى إجابة الدعوات
والدعاء المأثور عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (2) وعن السلف
PageV01P253
في يوم عرفة أول ما يدعو به فليقل لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له
الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير
اللهم اجعل في قلبي نورا وفي سمعي نورا وفي بصري نورا وفي لساني  نورا
اللهم اشرح لي صدري ويسر لي أمري وليقل
اللهم رب الحمد لك الحمد كما تقول وخيرا مما نقول لك صلاتي ونسكي ومحياي
ومماتي وإليك مآبي وإليك ثوابي
اللهم إني أعوذ بك من وساوس الصدر وشتات الأمر وعذاب القبر
اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر ما يلج في الليل ومن شر ما يلج في النهار ومن شر
ما تهب به الرياح ومن شر بوائق الدهر
اللهم إني أعوذ بك من تحول عافيتك وفجأة نقمتك وجميع سخطك
اللهم اهدني بالهدى واغفر لي في الآخرة والأولى يا خير مقصود وأسنى منزول
به وأكرم مسئول ما لديه أعطني العشية أفضل ما أعطيت أحدا من خلقك وحجاج
بيتك يا أرحم الراحمين
اللهم يا رفيع الدرجات ومنزل البركات ويا فاطر الأرضين والسموات ضجت إليك
الأصوات بصنوف اللغات يسألونك الحاجات وحاجتي إليك أن لا تنساني في دار
البلاء إذا نسيني أهل الدنيا
اللهم إنك تسمع كلامي وترى مكاني وتعلم سري وعلانيتي ولا يخفى عليك شيء
من أمري أنا البائس الفقير المستغيث المستجير الوجل المشفق المعترف بذنه
أسألك مسألة المسكين وأبتهل إليك ابتهال المذنب الذليل وأدعوك دعاء الخائف
الضرير دعاء من خضعت لك رقبته وفاضت لك عبرته وذل لك جسده ورغم لك أنفه
اللهم لا تجعلني بدعائك رب شقيا وكن بي رءوفا رحيما يا خير المسئولين
وأكرم المعطين
إلهي من مدح لك نفسه فإني لائم نفسي
إلهي أخرست المعاصي لساني فما لي وسيلة عن عمل ولا شفيع سوى الأمل
إلهي إني أعلم أن ذنوبي لم تبق لي عندك جاها ولا للاعتذار وجها ولكنك
أكرم الأكرمين
إلهي إن لم أكن أهلا أن أبلغ رحمتك فإن رحمتك أهل أن تبلغني ورحمتك وسعت
كل شيء وأنا شيء
إلهي إن ذنوبي وإن كانت عظاما ولكنها صغار في جنب عفوك فاغفرها لي يا
كريم
إلهي أنت أنت وأنا أنا أنا العواد إلى الذنوب وأنت العواد إلى المغفرة
إلهي إن كنت لا ترحم إلا أهل طاعتك فإلى من يفزع المذنبون
إلهي تجنبت عن  طاعتك عمدا وتوجهت إلى معصيتك قصدا فسبحا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ق-ف (w-q-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Standing still, halting, cessation of motion; the ritual pause at ʿArafāt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The devotional halt (wuqūf) as the essential pillar (rukn) of Ḥajj, signifying the soul's stillness before its Lord.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical standing; metaphorical (majāz) for the heart's attentive pause in supplication.
- Root: ن-م-ر (n-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A place name; the valley of ʿUranah adjacent to ʿArafāt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The site of the Prophet's ﷺ tent, marking the boundary between the permitted standing-place and the forbidden valley.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal toponym; rhetorically distinguishes the precise limits of the ritual precinct.
- Root: ث-ب-ر (th-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mountain at ʿArafāt; root sense of remaining, persisting.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The hill from whose sunrise the pilgrim departs, symbolizing enduring resolve.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal geographic reference; majāz for the moment of divine mercy descending.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — "If the standing is missed until dawn... then the Ḥajj is missed" (fa-in fāta... fa-qad fāta), governing legal consequence with precise protasis-apodosis structure.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Sixth Discourse concerns the Standing (al-wuqūf) and what precedes it.

When the pilgrim reaches ʿArafāt on the Day of ʿArafah, he should devote himself to the circumambulation of arrival (ṭawāf al-qudūm) and entering Mecca before the Standing. If he arrives several days earlier and performs the arrival circumambulation, he remains in the state of iḥrām until the seventh day of Dhū al-Ḥijjah. Then the imam delivers a sermon in Mecca after the noon prayer (ẓuhr) at the Kaʿbah, commanding the people to prepare for departure to Minā on the Day of Tarwiyah, to spend the night there, and to set out from it to ʿArafāt to fulfill the obligatory Standing after the sun's decline (zawāl). For the time of the Standing extends from the sun's decline to the dawn of the true morning on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Naḥr). Thus, he should depart to Minā uttering the talbiyah. It is recommended (mustaḥabb) for him to walk from Mecca through the rites (manāsik) until the completion of his Ḥajj, if he is able; and walking from the Mosque of Abraham (upon him be peace) to the Standing-place is more virtuous and more emphatic.

When he reaches Minā, he says: "O Allah, this is Minā, so bestow upon me what You have bestowed upon Your friends and the people of Your obedience." He should spend this night at Minā—a night of lodging (mabīt manzil) to which no ritual act is attached. When morning comes on the Day of ʿArafah, he prays the dawn prayer (ṣubḥ). When the sun rises upon Mount Thabīr, he proceeds to ʿArafāt, saying: "O Allah, make this the best morning journey I have ever undertaken, the nearest to Your good pleasure, and the farthest from Your wrath. O Allah, to You I have set out, upon You I have relied, and Your Face I have sought. So make me among those with whom You boast today—one better and more excellent than I."

When he arrives at ʿArafāt, let him pitch his tent at Namirah, near the mosque, for there the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pitched his dome. Namirah is the hollow of ʿUranah, below the Standing-place and below ʿArafāt. Let him perform the ritual bath (ghusl) for the Standing. When the sun declines, the imam delivers a brief sermon, then sits, and the muezzin begins the call to prayer (adhān) while the imam delivers the second sermon, joining the iqāmah to the adhān, and the imam finishes precisely as the muezzin completes the iqāmah. Then he combines the noon (ẓuhr) and afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayers with one adhān and two iqāmahs, shortening the prayers, and proceeds to the Standing-place. Let him stand at ʿArafāt, but let him not stand in the valley of ʿUranah. As for the Mosque of Abraham (upon him be peace), its front portion lies in the valley while its rear portions are within ʿArafāt; so whoever stands in the front of the mosque has not achieved the Standing at ʿArafāt.

The boundary of ʿArafāt is distinguished from the mosque by large stones laid out there. The most virtuous act is to stand near the stones, close to the imam, facing the qiblah, mounted, and to multiply the varieties of praise (taḥmīd), glorification (tasbīḥ), declaration of divine unity (tahlīl), eulogy of Allah Almighty, supplication (duʿāʾ), and repentance (tawbah). He should not fast on this day, so as to gain strength for persevering in supplication.

He should not cease the talbiyah on the Day of ʿArafah; rather, it is most beloved that he utter the talbiyah at one time and devote himself to supplication at another. He should not depart from the edge of ʿArafāt until after sunset, so as to combine in ʿArafāt both the night and the day. If he can stand on the eighth day for an hour, given the possibility of error in sighting the crescent moon, that is prudence (ḥazm), and through it he is secure from missing the rite.

Whoever misses the Standing until dawn breaks on the Day of Sacrifice has missed the Ḥajj entirely. He must then dissolve his iḥrām through the rites of ʿUmrah, shed a sacrificial animal (dam) for the missed rite, and make up the Ḥajj in the following year. Let his foremost occupation on this day be supplication, for in such a place and amid such a gathering, the answering of prayers is hoped for.

The supplication transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from the pious predecessors (al-salaf) for the Day of ʿArafah—the first thing he should say—is: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and dies not; in His hand is all good, and He is powerful over all things. O Allah, place in my heart light, in my hearing light, in my sight light, and in my tongue light. O Allah, expand my breast for me and ease my affair for me." And let him say:

"O Allah, Lord of all praise, to You is all praise as You say, and better than what we say. To You is my prayer, my sacrifice, my living, and my dying; to You is my return, and to You is my reward.

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the breast, the scattering of affairs, and the torment of the grave.

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil that enters by night and the evil that enters by day, from the evil that the winds carry, and from the calamities of time.

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the withdrawal of Your well-being, the suddenness of Your retribution, and all of Your wrath.

O Allah, guide me with guidance, and forgive me in the Hereafter and the First. O Best of all sought objects, O Most Exalted of all destinations, O Most Generous of all asked—grant me this evening the best of what You have granted any of Your creatures and the pilgrims of Your Sacred House, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

O Allah, O Raiser of degrees and Sender of blessings, O Originator of the earths and the heavens—voices have clamored to You in diverse languages, asking You their needs. And my need of You is that You not forget me in the abode of trial when the people of this world forget me.

O Allah, You hear my speech, see my place, and know my secret and my public; nothing of my affair is hidden from You. I am the wretched one, the poor one, the imploring one, the seeking-refuge one, the fearful one, the apprehensive one, the one confessing his sin. I ask You with the asking of the destitute, I implore You with the imploring of the guilty and abased, and I call upon You with the call of the fearful and humble—the call of one whose neck has bowed to You, whose tears have flowed for You, whose body has been humbled before You, and whose nose has been rubbed in the dust for You.

O Allah, do not make me wretched through my supplication to You, O Lord, and be kind and merciful to me, O Best of those who are asked and Most Generous of those who give.

My God—whoever praises You for himself, I indeed blame my own soul.

My God—sins have silenced my tongue, so I have no means through deeds nor any intercessor save hope.

My God—I know that my sins have left me no standing with You, nor any face for excuse; but You are the Most Generous of the generous.

My God—if I am not worthy to attain Your mercy, then Your mercy is worthy to attain me; and Your mercy encompasses all things, and I am a thing.

My God—though my sins be great, they are small beside Your pardon, so forgive them for me, O Generous One.

My God—You are You, and I am I. I am the one who returns to sins, and You are the One who returns to forgiveness.

My God—if You show mercy only to the people of Your obedience, then to whom shall the sinners flee?

My God—I shunned Your obedience deliberately and turned to Your disobedience intentionally. Glory be to You! How great is Your proof against me, and how generous is Your pardon toward me! By the obligation of Your proof upon me, the severance of my excuse before You, my poverty toward You, and Your richness apart from me—forgive me, O Best of those whom a caller has called, and Most Excellent of those whom a hopeful one has hoped. By the sanctity of Islam and the covenant of Muḥammad ﷺ, I seek intercession with You; so forgive me all my sins, and turn me from this standing-place of mine with my needs fulfilled. Grant me what I have asked, and realize my hope in what I have wished.

My God—I have called upon You with the supplication You taught me, so do not deprive me of the hope You made known to me.

My God—what will You do this evening with a servant who confesses his sin to You, humbled in his abasement before You, submissive in his offense, imploring You concerning his deed, repentant to You from his transgression, seeking Your forgiveness for his wrong, beseeching You for pardon from it, asking You for the success of his needs, and hoping in You at his standing-place despite the abundance of his sins? O Refuge of every living thing and Protector of every believer—whoever does well wins through Your mercy, and whoever errs perishes through his own error.

O Allah—to You we have set out, in Your courtyard we have alighted, upon You we have placed our hope, what is with You we have sought, to Your beneficence we have exposed ourselves, Your mercy we have hoped for, from Your chastisement we have feared, to You with the heavy burdens of sins we have fled, and to Your Sacred House we have performed the pilgrimage. O You who owns the needs of the askers and knows the consciences of the silent—O You who has no lord invoked alongside Him, no creator above Him to be feared, no vizier to be approached, and no chamberlain to be bribed—O You who increases not in generosity and munificence with the abundance of asking, nor in favor and beneficence with the abundance of needs.

O Allah—You have appointed for every guest a hospitality, and we are Your guests, so make our hospitality from You the Garden (al-Jannah).

O Allah—for every delegation there is a gift, for every visitor an honor, for every asker a grant, for every hopeful one a reward, for every seeker of what is with You a recompense, for every one seeking mercy from You a mercy, for every desirous one toward You a nearness, and for every one seeking intercession with You a pardon. We have come as a delegation to Your Sacred House, stood at these great rites, and witnessed these noble stations, hoping for what is with You—so do not disappoint our hope.

Our God—You have continued Your blessings until souls were reassured by the succession of Your favors; You have manifested Your signs until the mute spoke with Your proof; You have multiplied Your graces until Your friends confessed their shortcoming before Your right; You have displayed Your verses until the heavens and the earths declared Your evidences; and You have subdued by Your power until everything bowed to Your might and faces were humbled before Your greatness. When Your servants do evil, You forbear and grant respite; when they do good, You bestow favor and accept; when they disobey, You conceal; when they sin, You pardon and forgive; when we call, You answer; when we cry out, You hear; when we turn to You, You draw near; and when we turn away from You, You call us back.

Our God—You have said in Your clear Book to Muḥammad, the Seal of the Prophets: {«Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them»} [Q 8:38]. So You were pleased with them through their affirmation of the word of divine unity after denial. And we bear witness to You of unity in humility, and to Muḥammad of prophethood in sincerity. So forgive us, through this testimony, our former offenses, and do not make our portion therein less than the portion of those who entered into Islam.

Our God—You have loved drawing near to You through the freeing of those whom our right hands possess, and we are Your servants, and You are more worthy of bestowing favor—so free us.

You have commanded us to give charity to our poor, and we are Your poor, and You are more worthy of graciousness—so give charity to us.

You have enjoined upon us pardon for those who wrong us, and we have wronged ourselves, and You are more worthy of generosity—so pardon us.

Our Lord, forgive us and have mercy upon us; You are our Protector. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us by Your mercy from the chastisement of the Fire.

Let him multiply the supplication of al-Khaḍir (upon him be peace), which is to say: "O You whom no affair distracts from another affair, no hearing from another hearing, and to whom voices are not confused; O You whom questions do not confound and languages do not differ; O You whom the importunity of the insistent does not weary and the asking of the askers does not annoy—make us taste the coolness of Your pardon and the sweetness of intimate communion with You."

Let him supplicate with whatever occurs to him, and let him seek forgiveness for himself, for his parents, and for all believing men and believing women. Let him be persistent in supplication and magnify his request, for nothing is too great for Allah. Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: "He is at ʿArafāt—O Allah, do not turn back the multitude on my account." And Bakr al-Muzanī said: A man remarked, "When I looked upon the people of ʿArafāt, I thought they had indeed been forgiven—were it not that I was among them."

chapters.title_en: The Seventh Discourse on the Remaining Rites of Pilgrimage After the Standing: The Overnight Stay, the Stoning, the Sacrifice, the Shaving, and the Circumambulation

||| الجملة السابعة في بقية أعمال الحج بعد الوقوف من المبيت والرمي والنحر والحلق والطواف

فإذا أفاض من عرفة بعد غروب الشمس فينبغي أن يكون على السكينة والوقار
وليجتنب وجيف الخيل وإيضاع الإبل كما يعتاده بعض الناس فإن رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم نهى عن وجيف الخيل وإيضاع الإبل وقال اتقوا الله وسيروا
سيرا جميلا لا تطأوا ضعيفا ولا تؤذوا  مسلما (1)
فإذا بلغ المزدلفة اغتسل لها لأن المزدلفة من الحرم فليدخله بغسل وإن قدر
على دخوله ماشيا فهو أفضل وأقرب إلى توقير الحرم ويكون في الطريق رافعا
صوته بالتلبية فإذا بلغ المزدلفة قال اللهم إن هذه مزدلفة جمعت فيها ألسنة
مختلفة تسألك حوائج مؤتنفه فاجعلني ممن دعاك فاستجبت له وتوكل عليك فكفيته
ثم يجمع بين المغرب والعشاء بمزدلفة في وقت العشاء قاصرا له بأذان وإقامتين
ليس بينهما نافلة ولكن يجمع نافلة المغرب والعشاء والوتر بعد الفريضتين
ويبدأ بنافلة المغرب ثم بنافلة العشاء كما في الفريضتين فإن ترك النوافل في
السفر خسران ظاهر وتكليف إيقاعها في الأوقات إضرار وقطع للتبعية بينهما
وبين الفرائض فإذا جاز أن يؤدي النوافل مع الفرائض بتيمم واحد بحكم التبعية
فبأن يجوز أداؤهما على حكم الجمع بالتبعية أولى ولا يمنع من هذا مفارقة
النفل للفرض في جواز أدائه على الراحلة لما أو مأنا إليه من التبعية
والحاجة
ثم يمكث تلك الليلة PageV01P255
بمزدلفة وهو مبيت نسك ومن خرج منها في النصف الأول من الليل ولم يبت
فعليه دم وإحياء هذه الليلة الشريفة من محاسن القربات لمن يقدر عليه ثم إذا
انتصف الليل يأخذ في التأهب للرحيل ويتزود الحصى منها ففيها أحجار رخوة
فليأخذ سبعين حصاة فإنها قدر الحاجة ولا بأس بأن يستظهر بزيادة فربما يسقط
منه بعضها ولتكن الحصى خفافا بحيث يحتوي عليه أطراف البراجم
ثم ليغلس بصلاة الصبح وليأخذ في المسير حتى إذا انتهى إلى المشعر الحرام
وهو آخر المزدلفة فيقف ويدعو إلى الإسفار ويقول اللهم بحق المشعر الحرام
والبيت الحرام والشهر الحرام والركن والمقام أبلغ روح محمد منا التحية
والسلام وأدخلنا دار السلام يا ذا الجلال والإكرام ثم يدفع منها قبل طلوع
الشمس حتى ينتهي إلى موضع يقال له وادي محسر فيستحب له أن يحرك دابته حتى
يقطع عرض الوادي وإن كان راجلا أسرع في المشي
ثم إذا أصبح يوم النحر خلط التلبية بالتكبير فيلبي تارة ويكبر أخرى
فينتهي إلى منى ومواضع الجمرات وهي ثلاثة فيتجاوز  الأولى والثانية فلا شغل
له معهما يوم النحر حتى ينتهي إلى جمرة العقبة وهي على يمين مستقبل القبلة
في الجادة والمرمى مرتفع قليلا في سفح الجبل وهو ظاهر بمواقع الجمرات ويرمي
جمرة العقبة بعد طلوع الشمس بقدر رمح وكيفيته أن يقف مستقبلا القبلة وإن
استقبل الجمرة فلا بأس ويرمي سبع حصيات رافعا يده ويبدل التلبية بالتكبير
ويقول مع كل حصاة الله أكبر على طاعة الرحمن ورغم الشيطان اللهم تصديقا
بكتابك واتباعا لسنة نبيك فإذا رمى قطع التلبية والتكبير إلا التكبير عقيب
فرائض الصلوات من ظهر يوم النحر إلى عقيب الصبح من آخر أيام التشريق ولا
يقف في هذا اليوم للدعاء بل يدعو في منزله
وصفة التكبير أن يقول الله أكبر الله أكبر الله أكبر كبيرا والحمد لله
كثيرا وسبحان الله بكرة وأصيلا لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له مخلصين له
الدين ولو كره الكافرون لا إله إلا الله وحده صدق وعده ونصر عبده وهزم
الأحزاب وحده لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر ثم ليذبح الهدي إن كان معه
والأولى أن يذبح بنفسه وليقل بسم الله والله أكبر اللهم منك وبك وإليك تقبل
مني كما تقبلت من خليلك إبراهيم والتضحية بالبدن أفضل ثم بالبقر ثم بالشاة
والشاة أفضل من مشاركة ستة في البدنة أو البقرة والضأن أفضل من المعز قال
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خير الأضحية الكبش الأقرن والبيضاء أفضل من
الغبراء والسوداء (1) وقال أبو هريرة البيضاء أفضل في الأضحى من دم سوداوين
وليأكل منه إن كانت من هدي التطوع ولا يضحين بالعرجاء والجدعاء والعضباء
والجرباء والشرقاء والخرقاء والمقابلة والمدابرة والعجفاء والجدع في الأنف
والأذن للقطع منهما والعضب في القرن وفي نقصان القوائم والشرقاء المشقوقة
الأذن من فوق والخرقاء من أسفل والمقابلة المخروقة في الأذن من قدام
والمدابرة من خلف والعجفاء المهزولة التي لا تنقى أي لا مخ فيها من الهزال
ثم ليحلق بعد ذلك والسنة أن يستقبل القبلة ويبتدىء بمقدم رأسه فيحلق الشق
الأيمن إلى العظمين  المشرفين على القفا ثم ليحلق الباقي ويقول اللهم أثبت
لي بكل شعرة حسنة وامح عني بها سيئة وارفع لي بها عندك درجة والمرأة تقصر
الشعر والأصلع يستحب له إمرار الموسى على رأسه ومهما حلق بعد رمي الجمرة
فقد حصل له التحلل الأول وحل له كل المحذورات إلا النساء والصيد

- Root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Tranquility, stillness, repose; the opposite of agitation and haste.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The settled composure of the soul that accompanies reverential awe (sakīnah) in devotional acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical stillness; metaphorical for the inner calm mandated in sacred precincts.
- Root: ر-م-ي (r-m-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Casting, throwing, pelting with stones.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ritual stoning (ramy al-jamarāt) as an act of symbolic repulsion of Satan and obedience to divine command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of throwing; metaphorically signifies the casting away of base desires.
