chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Following in succession; recitation as sequential tracing of words
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tilāwah implies both oral recitation and obedient following of what is recited
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = following; metaphorical (majāz) = reciting with reverent compliance
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — series of coordinated clauses each amplifying the preceding, requiring precise particle linkage (wa, fa, thumma) for logical sequence
chapters.translation:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

Praise be to Allah, who conferred His favor upon His servants through His sent Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and His revealed Book, unto which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it — a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy — until the path of reflection widened for people of intellect through what it contains of narratives and reports, and through it the way of the upright course and the straight path became clear, by what it details of rulings and distinguishes between the lawful and the unlawful. It is the illumination and the light; through it is deliverance from delusion; in it is healing for what lies in breasts. Whoever opposes it among the tyrants, Allah crushes him; whoever seeks knowledge in other than it, Allah leads him astray. It is the firm rope of Allah, His manifest light, the trustworthy handhold, and the most faithful refuge. It encompasses the little and the much, the small and the great. Its wonders never cease, and its marvels never end. Its benefits cannot be circumscribed by any limit among people of knowledge, nor does frequency of repetition wear it out among people of recitation. It is that which guided the former and the latter. When the jinn heard it, they did not delay in turning to their people as warners, {«فقالوا إنا سمعنا قرآنا عجبا يهدي إلى الرشد فآمنا به ولن نشرك بربنا أحدا»} — "They said: Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Quran that guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord." Thus, whoever believes in it has been granted success; whoever speaks by it has spoken truth; whoever clings to it has been guided; whoever acts by it has triumphed. And He, exalted, said: {«إنا نحن نزلنا الذكر وإنا له لحافظون»} — "Indeed, We have sent down the Remembrance, and indeed We are its Preserver." Among the means of its preservation in hearts and codices is the continuity of its recitation and perseverance in its study, along with the fulfillment of its etiquettes and conditions, and the safeguarding of what it contains of inward works and outward etiquettes. This necessarily requires its exposition and detailing, and its aims unfold in four chapters:

Chapter One: On the virtue of the Quran and its people.
Chapter Two: On the etiquettes of recitation in the outward.
Chapter Three: On the inward works during recitation.
Chapter Four: On understanding the Quran and its interpretation by personal opinion and otherwise.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف ض ل (faḍl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus, or superiority in rank or quality; a bounty that exceeds what is due.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, faḍl denotes divine grace (faḍl Allāh) as an unmerited bestowal, distinct from justice (ʿadl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for surplus; metaphorical (majāz) for honor and excellence conferred by God.
- Root: ذ م م (dhamm)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Censure, blame, or dispraise—the opposite of praise (madḥ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, dhamm is the moral-legal judgment of reproach attached to an act or omission, often paired with ʿiqāb (punishment).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for verbal blame; metaphorical for the state of deserving reproach.
- Root: ق ص ر (qaṣr)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Shortening, failing to reach the full extent, or being deficient in capacity or effort.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious contexts, taqṣīr denotes negligence in fulfilling obligatory or recommended acts—falling short of the due measure.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical shortening; metaphorical for moral and spiritual deficiency in devotion.
- Root: ت ل و (tilāwah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Following, reciting, or reading sequentially—one thing following another in order.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tilāwah of the Qur’an implies both recitation and obedient following of its commands, as the reciter “follows” the text in heart and deed.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for vocal recitation; metaphorical for internalized adherence and practice.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase “wa-ahlihī” (and its people) is an appositive clarifying the scope of faḍl, linking the merit of the Qur’an to those who uphold it, without a new syntactic clause.
chapters.translation: I say: The first chapter concerns the merit of the Qur’an and its people, and the blame of those who fall short in its recitation.

||| فضيلة القرآن

قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من قرأ القرآن ثم رأى أن أحدا أوتي أفضل مما أوتي
فقد استصغر ما عظمه الله
PageV01P272
تعالى (1)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما من شفيع أفضل منزلة عند الله تعالى من القرآن
لا نبي ولا ملك ولا غيره (2)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لو كان القرآن في إهاب ما مسته النار (3)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل عبادة أمتي تلاوة القرآن (4)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أيضا إن الله عز وجل قرأ طه ويس قبل أن يخلق
الخلق بألف عام فلما سمعت الملائكة القرآن قالت طوبى لأمة ينزل عليهم هذا
وطوبى لأجواف تحمل هذا وطوبى لألسنة تنطق بهذا (5)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خيركم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه (6)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول الله تبارك وتعالى من شغله قراءة القرآن عن
دعائي ومسألتي أعطيته أفضل ثواب الشاكرين (7)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة يوم القيامة على كثيب من مسك أسود لا
يهولهم فزع ولا ينالهم حساب حتى يفرغ ما بين الناس رجل قرأ القرآن ابتغاء
وجه الله عز وجل والخ أم به قوما وهم به راضون (8)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أهل القرآن أهل الله وخاصته (9)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن القلوب تصدأ كما يصدأ الحديد فقيل يا رسول
الله وما جلاؤها فقال تلاوة القرآن وذكر الموت (10)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لله أشد أذنا إلى قارىء القرآن من صاحب القينة
إلى قينته (11)
الآثار قال أبو أمامة الباهلي اقرءوا القرآن ولا تغرنكم هذه المصاحف
المعلقة فإن الله لا يعذب قلبا هو وعاء للقرآن
وقال ابن مسعود إذا أردتم العلم فانثروا القرآن فإن فيه علم  الأولين
والآخرين
وقال أيضا اقرءوا القرآن فإنكم تؤجرون عليه بكل حرف منه عشر حسنات أما
إني لا أقول الحرف ألم ولكن الألف حرف واللام حرف والميم حرف
وقال أيضا لا يسأل أحدكم عن نفسه إلا القرآن فإن كان يحب القرآن ويعجبه
فهو يحب الله سبحانه ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن كان يبغض القرآن فهو
يبغض الله سبحانه ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم
وقال عمرو بن العاص كل آية في القرآن درجة في الحنة ومصباح في بيوتكم
وقال أيضا من قرأ القرآن فقد أدرجت النبوة بين جنبيه إلا أنه لا يوحى إليه
وقال أبو هريرة PageV01P273
إن البيت الذي يتلى فيه القرآن اتسع بأهله وكثر خيره وحضرته الملائكة
وخرجت منه الشياطين وإن البيت الذي لايتلى فيه كتاب الله عز وجل ضاق بأهله
وقل خيره وخرجت منه الملائكة وحضرته الشياطين
وقال أحمد بن حنبل رأيت الله عز وجل في المنام فقلت يا رب ما أفضل ما
تقرب به المتقربون إليك قال بكلامي يا أحمد قال قلت يا رب بفهم أو بغير فهم
قال بفهم وبغير فهم
وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي إذا سمع الناس القرآن من الله عز وجل يوم
القيامة فكأنهم لم يسمعوه قط
وقال الفضيل بن عياض ينبغي لحامل القرآن أن لا يكون له إلى أحد حاجة ولا
إلى الخلفاء فمن دونهم فينبغي أن تكون حوائج الخلق إليه
وقال أيضا حامل القرآن حامل راية الإسلام فلا ينبغي أن يلهو مع من يلهو
ولا يسهو مع من يسهو ولا يلغو مع من يلغو تعظيما لحق القرآن
وقال سفيان الثوري إذا قرأ الرجل القرآن قبل الملك بين عينيه
وقال عمرو بن ميمون من نشر مصحفا حين يصلي الصبح فقرأ منه مائة آية رفع
الله عز وجل له مثل عمل جميع أهل الدنيا
ويروى أن خالد بن عقبة جاء إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال اقرأ
علي القرآن فقرأ عليه إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان وإيتاء ذي القربى الآية
فقال له  فأعاد فقال والله إن له لحلاوة وإن عليه لطلاوة وإن أسفله لمورق
وإن أعلاه لمثمر وما يقول هذا بشر (1)
وقال الحسن والله ما دون القرآن من غنى ولا بعده من فاقة
وقال الفضيل من قرأ خاتمة سورة الحشر حين يصبح ثم مات من يومه ختم له
بطابع الشهداء ومن قرأها حين يمسي ثم مات من ليلته ختم له بطابع الشهداء
وقال القاسم بن عبد الرحمن قلت لبعض النساك ما ههنا أحد نستأنس به فمد
يده إلى المصحف ووضعه على حجره وقال هذا
وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه ثلاث يزدن في الحفظ ويذهبن البلغم
السواك والصيام وقراءة القرآن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ض-ل (faḍl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Superabundance, excess of goodness; precedence in rank and merit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Excellence (faḍīlah) as a divinely conferred surplus of honor, distinct from justice (ʿadl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in reference to God's bounty; metaphorical when applied to acts of worship as their inherent worth.
- Root: ت-ل-و (tilāwah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Following, tracing; recitation as sequential articulation of words.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Recitation (tilāwah) of the Qur'an as obedient following of its commands, not mere utterance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for vocal recitation; metaphorical for internalized compliance.
- Root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥifẓ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Guarding, preserving; retaining in memory.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Qur'an as preserved (maḥfūẓ) in hearts and the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for memory retention; metaphorical for safeguarding one's conduct by the Qur'an.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — coordinating nouns in series (e.g., "no prophet, no angel, no other") without repeating the particle, each standing as an independent explicative of the preceding category.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the merits of the Qur'an are vast beyond enumeration, and its excellences are too numerous for counting. We shall cite, by way of blessing, a selection of the prophetic traditions (aḥādīth) and the reports of the Companions and the Successors (āthār) concerning its virtue, that the heart may be stirred to its recitation and the soul may be roused to its veneration.

The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever recites the Qur'an and then sees that someone has been given something better than what he has been given, has indeed deemed small what God—exalted is He—has deemed great."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "There is no intercessor of nobler station before God—exalted is He—than the Qur'an: neither a prophet, nor an angel, nor any other."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Were the Qur'an to be within a hide, the Fire would not touch it."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "The most excellent act of worship of my community is the recitation of the Qur'an."

And he, peace be upon him, also said: "Verily God—mighty and majestic is He—recited Ṭāhā and Yāsīn a thousand years before He created the creation. When the angels heard the Qur'an, they said: 'Blessed (ṭūbā) be a community upon whom this is sent down, and blessed be the bellies that carry this, and blessed be the tongues that utter this.'"

And he, peace be upon him, said: "The best of you is he who learns the Qur'an and teaches it."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "God—blessed and exalted is He—says: 'Whoever is occupied by the recitation of the Qur'an from supplicating Me and asking of Me, I shall give him the most excellent reward of the thankful.'"

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Three persons on the Day of Resurrection shall be upon a mound of black musk, neither the Great Terror shall frighten them, nor shall any reckoning reach them, until the judgment among mankind is finished: a man who recited the Qur'an seeking the Face of God—mighty and majestic is He—and a man who led a people with it, and they were well-pleased with him."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "The people of the Qur'an are the people of God and His elect."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "Verily hearts rust just as iron rusts." It was said: "O Messenger of God, what is their polish?" He said: "The recitation of the Qur'an and the remembrance of death."

And he, peace be upon him, said: "God listens more intently to the reciter of the Qur'an than the master of a songstress listens to his songstress."

The Reports (Āthār): Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī said: "Recite the Qur'an, and let not these hanging codices deceive you, for God shall not torment a heart that is a vessel for the Qur'an."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "If you desire knowledge, then scatter the Qur'an, for in it is the knowledge of the ancients and the later ones."

He also said: "Recite the Qur'an, for you are rewarded for it for every letter of it ten good deeds. Verily I do not say that 'alif-lām-mīm' is a letter, but rather the 'alif' is a letter, the 'lām' is a letter, and the 'mīm' is a letter."

He also said: "Let none of you ask about himself except through the Qur'an: if he loves the Qur'an and it pleases him, then he loves God—glorified is He—and His Messenger, peace be upon him; and if he detests the Qur'an, then he detests God—glorified is He—and His Messenger, peace be upon him."

ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: "Every verse in the Qur'an is a degree in Paradise and a lamp in your houses."

He also said: "Whoever recites the Qur'an has indeed enfolded prophethood between his two sides, except that revelation is not sent down to him."

Abū Hurayrah said: "Verily the house in which the Qur'an is recited expands with its people, its good increases, the angels attend it, and the devils depart from it. And the house in which the Book of God—mighty and majestic is He—is not recited narrows upon its people, its good diminishes, the angels depart from it, and the devils attend it."

Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal said: "I saw God—mighty and majestic is He—in a dream, and I said: 'O Lord, what is the most excellent thing by which those who draw near draw near to You?' He said: 'By My Speech, O Aḥmad.' I said: 'O Lord, with understanding or without understanding?' He said: 'With understanding and without understanding.'"

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī said: "When the people hear the Qur'an from God—mighty and majestic is He—on the Day of Resurrection, it will be as though they had never heard it before."

Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: "It behooves the bearer of the Qur'an that he have no need of anyone, nor of the caliphs nor those below them; rather, the needs of the creation should be directed to him."

He also said: "The bearer of the Qur'an is the bearer of the banner of Islam; it behooves him not to sport with those who sport, nor to be heedless with those who are heedless, nor to indulge in frivolity with those who indulge in frivolity, in veneration of the right of the Qur'an."

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: "When a man recites the Qur'an, the angel stands between his eyes."

ʿAmr ibn Maymūn said: "Whoever spreads open a muṣḥaf at the time of the morning prayer and recites from it one hundred verses, God—mighty and majestic is He—raises for him the like of the deeds of all the people of the world."

It is related that Khālid ibn ʿUqbah came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and said: "Recite the Qur'an to me." So he recited to him: {«Verily God commands justice, excellence, and giving to the near of kin»} — the verse. He said to him: "Repeat it." So he repeated it, and he said: "By God, it has sweetness, and upon it is beauty, and its lower part is verdant, and its upper part is fruitful, and no human says this."

Al-Ḥasan said: "By God, there is no wealth apart from the Qur'an, nor any poverty after it."

Al-Fuḍayl said: "Whoever recites the closing of Sūrat al-Ḥashr in the morning and then dies that day, is sealed with the seal of the martyrs; and whoever recites it in the evening and then dies that night, is sealed with the seal of the martyrs."

Al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: "I said to one of the ascetics: 'There is no one here with whom we may find companionship.' So he stretched his hand to the muṣḥaf, placed it upon his lap, and said: 'This.'"

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may God be well-pleased with him, said: "Three things increase retention and drive away phlegm: the toothstick (siwāk), fasting, and the recitation of the Qur'an."

chapters.title_en: On the Condemnation of the Recitation of the Negligent
chapters.arabic_text:
||| في ذم تلاوة الغافلين

قال أنس بن مالك رب تال للقرآن والقرآن يلعنه وقال ميسرة الغريب هو
القرآن في جوف الفاجر وقال أبو سليمان الداراني الزبانية أسرع إلى حملة
القرآن الذين يعصون الله عز وجل منهم إلى عبدة الأوثان حين عصوا الله
سبحانه بعد القرآن
وقال بعض العلماء إذا قرأ ابن آدم القرآن ثم خلط ثم عاد فقرأ قيل له مالك
ولكلامي وقال ابن الرماح ندمت على استظهاري القرآن لأنه بلغني أن أصحاب
القرآن يسألون عما يسأل عنه الأنبياء يوم القيامة
وقال ابن مسعود ينبغي لحامل القرآن أن يعرف بليله إذا الناس ينامون
وبنهاره إذا الناس يفرطون وبحزنه إذا الناس يفرحون وببكائه إذا الناس
يضحكون وبصمته إذا الناس يخوضون وبخشوعه إذا الناس يختالون وينبغي لحامل
القرآن أن يكون مستكينا لينا ولاينبغي له أن يكون جافيا ولا مماريا ولا
صياحا ولا صخابا ولا حديدا
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أكثر منافقي هذه الأمة قراؤها (2) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم اقرأ القرآن ما نهاك فإن لم ينهك فلست تقرؤه (3) وقال صلى الله
عليه وسلم ما آمن بالقرآن من استحل محارمه (4) وقال بعض السلف PageV01P274
إن العبد ليفتتح سورة فتصلي عليه الملائكة حتى يفرغ منها وإن العبد
ليفتتح سورة فتلعنه حتى يفرغ منها فقيل له وكيف ذلك فقال إذا أحل حلالها
وحرم حرامها صلت  عليه وإلا لعنته
وقال بعض العلماء إن العبد ليتلو القرآن فيلعن نفسه وهو لا يعلم يقول
{ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين} وهو ظالم نفسه ألا لعنة الله على الكاذبين
وهو منهم
وقال الحسن إنكم اتخذتم قراءة القرآن مراحل وجعلتم الليل جملا فأنتم
تركبونه فتقطعون به مراحله وإن من كان قبلكم رأوه رسائل من ربهم فكانوا
يتدبرونها بالليل وينفذونها بالنهار
وقال ابن مسعود أنزل القرآن عليهم ليعملوا به فاتخذوا دراسته عملا إن
أحدكم ليقرأ القرآن من فاتحته إلى خاتمته ما يسقط منه حرفا وقد أسقط العمل
به
وفي حديث ابن عمر وحديث جندب رضي الله عنهما لقد عشنا دهرا طويلا وأحدنا
يؤتى الإيمان قبل القرآن فتنزل السورة على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فيتعلم
حلالها وحرامها وآمرها وزاجرها وما ينبغي أن يقف عنده منها
ثم لقد رأيت رجالا يؤتى أحدهم القرآن قبل الإيمان فيقرأ ما بين فاتحة
الكتاب إلى خاتمته لا يدري ما آمره ولا زاجره ولا ما ينبغي أن يقف عنده منه
ينثره نثر الدقل (1) وقد ورد في التوراة يا عبدي أما تستحي مني يأتيك كتاب
من بعض إخوانك وأنت في الطريق تمشي فتعدل عن الطريق وتقعد لأجله وتقرؤه
وتتدبره حرفا حرفا حتى لا يفوتك شيء منه وهذا كتابي أنزلته إليك انظر كم
فصلت لك فيه من القول وكم كررت عليك فيه لتتأمل طوله وعرضه ثم أنت معرض عنه
أفكنت أهون عليك من بعض إخوانك يا عبدي يقعد إليك بعض إخوانك فتقبل عليه
بكل وجهك وتصغي إلى حديثه بكل قلبك فإن تكلم متكلم أو شغلك شاغل عن حديثه
أومأت إليه أن كف وها أنا ذا مقبل عليك ومحدث لك وأنت معرض بقلبك عني
أفجعلتني أهون عندك من بعض إخوانك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ت-ل-ا (t-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Following, reciting sequentially, tracing letters in order
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Recitation as an act of obedient following (tilāwah) that entails compliance with what is recited
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is sequential reading; metaphorical sense is the "following" of commands — hence the reciter who disobeys is a reciter only in name
- Root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Expulsion, distancing, cursing with deprivation of mercy
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divine curse (laʿnah) as removal from divine proximity — applied here to the reciter who betrays the Book's purpose
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: verbal imprecation; metaphorical: the Quran's own testimony against the disobedient reciter on the Day of Judgment
- Root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Carrying, bearing, undertaking a burden
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "Carrier of the Quran" (ḥāmil al-Qurʾān) as one entrusted with its weight of obligation, not merely its memorization
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical carrying; metaphorical: bearing the covenant of acting upon it
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (al-takhṣīṣ bi-al-taqdīm) — the fronting of "the Quran" in "the Quran curses him" (wa-al-Qurʾānu yalʿanuhu) restricts the cursing to the Quran itself, emphasizing that the very Book becomes an active agent against its negligent reciter.
chapters.translation:
I say: In condemnation of the recitation of the negligent ones.

Anas ibn Mālik said: "Many a reciter of the Quran — and the Quran curses him." And Maysarah al-Gharīb said: "It is the Quran in the belly of the wicked man." And Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "The Zabāniyah (the stern angels of punishment) are swifter to seize the carriers of the Quran who disobey God Almighty than they are to seize the idol-worshippers — because they disobeyed God, Glorified be He, after the Quran [had come to them]."

And some scholars said: "When the son of Adam recites the Quran, then mixes [it with disobedience], then returns to recite — it is said to him: 'What is between you and My speech?'" And Ibn al-Rimmāḥ said: "I regretted having memorized the Quran, for it reached me that the people of the Quran will be questioned concerning what the prophets are questioned about on the Day of Resurrection."

And Ibn Masʿūd said: "It befits the carrier of the Quran to be known by his night [vigil] when people sleep, and by his day [fasting] when people are negligent, and by his sorrow when people rejoice, and by his weeping when people laugh, and by his silence when people engage in idle talk, and by his humility when people strut with pride. And it befits the carrier of the Quran to be meek and gentle; it does not befit him to be coarse, nor contentious, nor clamorous, nor loud-voiced, nor sharp-tempered."

And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The majority of the hypocrites of this community are its reciters." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Recite the Quran as long as it forbids you; if it does not forbid you, then you are not reciting it." And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "He has not believed in the Quran who makes lawful its prohibitions." And some of the Salaf said: "Indeed, a servant opens a sūrah, and the angels pray for him until he finishes it; and indeed, a servant opens a sūrah, and it curses him until he finishes it." It was said to him: "How is that?" He said: "If he treats its lawful as lawful and its unlawful as unlawful, it prays for him; otherwise, it curses him."

And some scholars said: "Indeed, a servant recites the Quran and curses himself without knowing. He says: {«A curse of God be upon the wrongdoers»} — and he is a wrongdoer to his own soul. {«A curse of God be upon the liars»} — and he is among them."

And al-Ḥasan said: "You have taken the recitation of the Quran as stages [to traverse], and you have made the night a camel; you ride it and cut through its stages upon it. But those before you saw it as letters from their Lord; they would ponder them by night and execute them by day."

And Ibn Masʿūd said: "The Quran was sent down to them to act upon it, so they took its study as their [sole] work. Indeed, one of you recites the Quran from its opening to its end, not dropping a single letter from it — yet he has dropped acting upon it entirely."

And in the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar and the ḥadīth of Jundub, may God be pleased with them both: "We lived for a long time, and one of us would be given faith before the Quran. Then a sūrah would be sent down upon Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and he would learn its lawful and its unlawful, its commands and its prohibitions, and what he ought to pause at within it. Then I have seen men to whom one of them is given the Quran before faith; he recites from the opening of the Book to its end, not knowing its commands, nor its prohibitions, nor what he ought to pause at within it — he scatters it as one scatters unripe dates."

And it has been related in the Torah: "O My servant, are you not ashamed of Me? A letter comes to you from one of your brothers while you are walking on the road, and you turn aside from the road, and you sit down for its sake, and you read it and ponder it letter by letter, so that nothing of it escapes you. And this is My Book, which I have sent down to you. Look at how much speech I have detailed for you in it, and how many times I have repeated to you in it, so that you might contemplate its length and its breadth — and then you turn away from it. Am I then more insignificant to you than one of your brothers? O My servant, one of your brothers sits with you, and you turn your whole face toward him, and you incline with all your heart to his speech. If a speaker speaks or an occupier occupies you from his speech, you gesture to him to be silent. And here I am, turning toward you and speaking to you — while you turn your heart away from Me. Have you then made Me more insignificant to you than one of your brothers?"

chapters.title_en: The Second Book on the Outward Etiquettes of Recitation — Ten Principles
chapters.arabic_text:
|| الباب الثاني في ظاهر آداب التلاوة وهي عشرة

الأول في حال القارىء وهو أن يكون على الوضوء واقعا على هيئة الأدب
والسكون إما قائما وإما جالسا مستقبل القبلة مطرقا رأسه غير متربع ولا
متكىء ولا جالس على هيئة التكبر ويكون جلوسه  وحده كجلوسه بين يدي أستاذه
وأفضل الأحوال أن يقرأ في الصلاة قائما وأن يكون في المسجد فذلك من أفضل
الأعمال
فإن قرأ على غير وضوء وكان مضطجعا في الفراش فله أيضا فضل ولكنه دون ذلك
قال الله تعالى الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في

chapters.translation:
I say: The second book concerns the outward etiquettes of recitation, and they are ten.

**The First: Concerning the State of the Reciter** — namely, that he be in a state of ritual purity (wuḍūʾ), assuming a posture of propriety and tranquility, either standing or sitting, facing the qiblah, with head bowed, neither cross-legged, nor reclining, nor seated in a posture of arrogance. His sitting alone should be like his sitting before his teacher. The most excellent of states is that he recite within the prayer standing, and that he be in the mosque — for that is among the most virtuous of deeds.

If he recites without ritual purity, lying upon his bed, he also obtains merit, but it is inferior to that. God Most High says: {«الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ويتفكرون في خلق السموات والأرض»} — "Those who remember God standing, sitting, and upon their sides, and reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth." Thus He praised all, but gave precedence to standing in remembrance, then sitting, then remembrance while reclining.

ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him) said: "Whoever recites the Qurʾān standing in prayer has for every letter one hundred good deeds; whoever recites it sitting in prayer has for every letter fifty good deeds; whoever recites it outside prayer in a state of ritual purity has twenty-five good deeds; and whoever recites it without ritual purity has ten good deeds." Whatever is done by standing at night is more excellent, for it is more conducive to the heart's emptiness. Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī (may God be pleased with him) said: "The abundance of prostration by day is not [as virtuous] as the prolongation of standing at night."

**The Second: Concerning the Measure of the Qurʾān [to be recited]** — For reciters have varying customs regarding abundance and abbreviation. Among them are those who complete the entire Qurʾān once in a day and night; some twice; and some reached three times. Among them are those who complete it once a month. The most appropriate reference point in such estimations is the saying of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): "Whoever recites the Qurʾān in less than three [days] has not comprehended it." This is because exceeding that prevents him from measured recitation (tartīl). ʿĀʾishah (may God Most High be pleased with her), upon hearing a man reciting the Qurʾān hastily and carelessly, said: "This one has neither recited the Qurʾān nor kept silent." The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar (may God be pleased with them both) to complete the Qurʾān every seven days. Likewise, a group of the Companions (may God be pleased with them) used to complete the Qurʾān every Friday — such as ʿUthmān, Zayd ibn Thābit, Ibn Masʿūd, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb (may God be pleased with them all).

Thus, in completion there are four degrees: completion in a day and night — which a group disapproved; completion every month, i.e., one-thirtieth part daily — as if this were an exaggeration in abbreviation, just as the first was an exaggeration in abundance. Between these two lie two moderate degrees: one is once a week, and the second is twice a week, approximating three.

The most beloved [practice] is that one complete one recitation by night and one by day, making his daytime completion on Monday in the two units of the dawn prayer or after them, and his nighttime completion on the night of Friday in the two units of the sunset prayer or after them — so that he begins the first part of the day and the first part of the night with his completion. For the angels (peace be upon them) pray for him: if his completion is at night, [they pray] until morning; if by day, until evening — so that its blessing encompasses the entire night and day.

The detailed ruling on the measure of recitation is this: if one is among the worshippers traversing the path of [outward] works, he should not fall short of two completions per week. If he is among those traversing through works of the heart and varieties of reflection, or among those occupied with disseminating knowledge, there is no harm in restricting himself to once a week. If he is penetrating in reflection upon the meanings of the Qurʾān, he may suffice with once a month, due to his great need for frequent repetition and deep contemplation.

**The Third: Concerning the Method of Division** — As for one who completes the Qurʾān once a week, he divides it into seven portions (aḥzāb). The Companions (may God be pleased with them) divided it into portions. It is narrated that ʿUthmān (may God be pleased with him) used to begin on the night of Friday with al-Baqarah through al-Māʾidah; on the night of Saturday with al-Anʿām through Hūd; on the night of Sunday with Yūsuf through Maryam; on the night of Monday with Ṭāhā through Ṭā-Sīn-Mīm [al-Shuʿarāʾ] of Moses and Pharaoh; on the night of Tuesday with al-ʿAnkabūt through Ṣād; on the night of Wednesday with Tanzīl [al-Sajdah] through al-Raḥmān; and he would complete on the night of Thursday.

Ibn Masʿūd divided it into sections not following this arrangement. It is said that the portions of the Qurʾān are seven: the first portion is three sūrahs; the second is five sūrahs; the third is seven sūrahs; the fourth is nine sūrahs; the fifth is eleven sūrahs; the sixth is thirteen sūrahs; and the seventh is al-Mufaṣṣal from Qāf to its end. Thus did the Companions (may God be pleased with them) divide it, and they used to recite it accordingly. There is a report concerning this from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). This was before the fifths, tenths, and thirtieths were devised — whatever is other than this is an innovation (muḥdath).

**The Fourth: Concerning Writing** — It is recommended to beautify the writing of the Qurʾān and make it clear. There is no harm in vowel-pointing and marking with red or other colors, for these are adornment and clarification, and a deterrent from error and mispronunciation (laḥn) for the reader. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn used to disapprove of the fifths, tenths, and thirtieths. It is narrated from al-Shaʿbī and Ibrāhīm the disapproval of red vowel-pointing and taking payment for it. They used to say: "Strip the Qurʾān bare." The presumption concerning these [scholars] is that they disapproved of opening this door out of fear that it would lead to introducing additions, as a sealing of the door, and out of eagerness to guard the Qurʾān against whatever change might befall it. When it does not lead to a prohibited matter, and the affair of the community has settled upon what yields increased knowledge, there is no harm in it. Nor does its being an innovation prevent this — for how many an innovation is good, as was said concerning the establishment of congregational [prayers] in Tarāwīḥ: it is among the innovations of ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him), and it is a good innovation (bidʿah ḥasanah). The blameworthy innovation is only that which clashes with the ancient Sunnah or nearly leads to its alteration.

Some of them used to say: "I recite from the muṣḥaf that is vowel-pointed, but I do not point it myself." Al-Awzāʿī narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr: "The Qurʾān was bare in the muṣḥafs. The first thing they introduced in it was the pointing on the bāʾ and tāʾ." They said: "There is no harm in it, for it is a light for it." Then after that they introduced large dots at the ends of verses, and they said: "There is no harm in it; by it the head of the verse is known." Then after that they introduced the ornamental medallions and opening headings.

Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī said: "I asked al-Ḥasan about pointing the muṣḥafs in red." He said: "And what is its pointing?" I said: "They grammatically inflect the word in Arabic." He said: "As for the grammatical inflection of the Qurʾān, there is no harm in it." Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ said: "I entered upon Ibn Sīrīn and saw him reciting from a vowel-pointed muṣḥaf, though he had disapproved of pointing." It is said that al-Ḥajjāj was the one who introduced this: he summoned the reciters until they counted the words of the Qurʾān and its letters, equalized its portions, and divided it into thirty parts and other divisions.

**The Fifth: Concerning Measured Recitation (Tartīl)** — It is recommended in the manner of the Qurʾān, for we shall explain that the purpose of recitation is reflection, and tartīl assists in that. For this reason, Umm Salamah (may God be pleased with her) described the recitation of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and behold, she described a recitation clearly articulated letter by letter. Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with him) said: "That I recite al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān, measuring them out and reflecting upon them, is more beloved to me than that I recite the entire Qurʾān hastily." He also said: "That I recite Idhā Zulzilat and al-Qāriʿah, reflecting upon them, is more beloved to me than that I recite al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān with rapidity."

Mujāhid was asked about two men who entered the prayer, their standing being equal, except that one recited only al-Baqarah while the other recited the entire Qurʾān. He said: "They are equal in reward."

Know that tartīl is recommended not merely for reflection — for even a non-Arab who does not understand the meaning of the Qurʾān is recommended to employ tartīl and deliberateness in recitation, because that is closer to reverence and respect, and more impactful upon the heart than hasty, careless recitation.

**The Sixth: Concerning Weeping** — Weeping is recommended with recitation. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Recite the Qurʾān and weep; if you do not weep, then feign weeping." He (peace and blessings be upon him) also said: "He is not of us who does not chant the Qurʾān with a beautiful voice." Ṣāliḥ al-Murrī said: "I recited the Qurʾān to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in a dream, and he said to me: 'O Ṣāliḥ, this is recitation — but where is the weeping?'" Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both) said: "When you recite a prostration verse of Sūrat Subḥān [al-Isrāʾ], do not hasten to prostrate until you weep; if your eye does not weep, then let your heart weep." The way of feigning weeping is to bring sorrow into one's heart, for from sorrow weeping arises. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The Qurʾān was revealed with sorrow; when you recite it, then show sorrow." The manner of bringing about sorrow is to reflect upon what it contains of threats, warnings, covenants, and pledges; then to reflect upon one's own shortcomings in its commands and prohibitions — then one will inevitably grieve and weep. If sorrow and weeping do not come to one as they come to the possessors of pure hearts, then let him weep over the loss of sorrow and weeping — for that is among the greatest of calamities.

**The Seventh: Concerning Observing the Rights of the Verses** — When one passes by a prostration verse, he prostrates. Likewise, if he hears it from another, he prostrates when the reciter prostrates. He does not prostrate except in a state of ritual purity. In the Qurʾān there are fourteen prostrations; in Sūrat al-Ḥajj there are two; and there is no prostration in Sūrat Ṣād. The minimum is that he prostrate by placing his forehead upon the ground. The most complete is that he say the takbīr, prostrate, and supplicate in his prostration with what befits the verse he recited — such as reciting the saying of God Most High: {«خرّوا سجدا وسبحوا بحمد ربهم وهم لا يستكبرون»} — "They fell prostrate and glorified the praise of their Lord, and they do not wax arrogant" — and then saying: "O God, make me among those who prostrate to Your face, who glorify Your praise, and I seek refuge in You from being among the arrogant against Your command or against Your friends." And when he recites His saying: {«ويخرون للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا»} — "And they fall upon their chins weeping, and it increases them in humility" — he says: "O God, make me among those who weep unto You, humble before You." Likewise for every prostration. The conditions of prayer are required for this prostration: covering the nakedness, facing the qiblah, and purity of garment and body from both ritual impurity and filth.

If one is not in a state of ritual purity upon hearing, then when he purifies himself he prostrates. It has been said regarding its completeness that he says the takbīr raising his hands for its consecration (taḥrīm), then says the takbīr for descending to prostration, then says the takbīr for rising, then gives the salutation. Some added the tashahhud — but there is no basis for this except analogy with the prostration of prayer, which is far-fetched, for the command came concerning prostration, so let one follow the command therein. The takbīr for descending is closest to the beginning; whatever is beyond that is remote.

Then, the one praying behind an imam should prostrate when the imam prostrates, and he does not prostrate for his own recitation if he is a follower.

**The Eighth: Concerning What to Say at the Beginning and During Recitation** — At the start of his recitation, one should say: "I seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan. {«رب أعوذ بك من همزات الشياطين وأعوذ بك رب أن يحضرون»} — 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they attend me.'" Let him recite "Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabb al-nās" and Sūrat al-Ḥamd. At the completion of his recitation, let him say: "God Most High has spoken the truth, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) has conveyed. O God, benefit us by it and bless us in it. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and I seek forgiveness from God, the Living, the Self-Subsisting."

During recitation, if he passes by a verse of glorification, he glorifies and magnifies; if he passes by a verse of supplication and seeking forgiveness, he supplicates and seeks forgiveness; if he passes by a verse of hope, he asks; if he passes by a verse of fear, he seeks refuge. He does this with his tongue or with his heart, saying: "Glory be to God; we seek refuge in God; O God, provide us; O God, have mercy on us." Ḥudhayfah said: "I prayed with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he began Sūrat al-Baqarah. He did not pass by a verse of mercy but that he asked, nor by a verse of punishment but that he sought refuge, nor by a verse of transcendence but that he glorified." When he finished, he said what he used to say — may the blessings and peace of God be upon him — at the completion of the Qurʾān: "O God, have mercy on me through the Qurʾān, and make it for me a leader, a light, a guidance, and a mercy. O God, remind me from it what I have forgotten, and teach me from it what I am ignorant of, and provide me its recitation in the hours of the night and the ends of the day, and make it a proof for me, O Lord of the worlds."

**The Ninth: Concerning Raising the Voice in Recitation** — There is no doubt that one must raise his voice to the extent that he hears himself, for recitation is the articulation of sound through letters, and sound is indispensable. Its minimum is what one hears himself; if he does not hear himself, his prayer is not valid.

As for raising the voice so that others hear, it is beloved in one respect and disliked in another. That which indicates the recommendation of secrecy is what is narrated that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The merit of secret recitation over open recitation is like the merit of secret charity over open charity." In another wording: "The one who recites aloud is like the one who gives charity openly, and the one who recites secretly is like the one who gives charity secretly." In the general report: "The work done in secret is preferred over that done openly by seventy-fold." Likewise his saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "The best of provision is what suffices, and the best of remembrance is the hidden one." And in the report: "Let none of you raise his voice over another in recitation between the sunset and night prayers."

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab heard one night in the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz raising his voice in recitation during his prayer, and he had a beautiful voice. He said to his servant: "Go to this one praying and command him to lower his voice." The servant said: "The mosque is not ours, and the man has a share in it." So Saʿīd raised his voice and said: "O you who prays! If you seek God Almighty by your prayer, then lower your voice; but if you seek the people, then they will avail you nothing against God." ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz fell silent and shortened his bowing. When he gave the salutation, he took his sandals and departed — and he was at that time the governor of Medina.

That which indicates the recommendation of raising the voice is what is narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) heard a group of his Companions raising their voices in the night prayer and approved of that. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When one of you rises at night to pray, let him raise his voice in recitation, for the angels and the inhabitants of the house listen to his recitation and pray with his prayer."

He (peace and blessings be upon him) passed by three of his Companions (may God be pleased with them) in differing states. He passed by Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) while he was lowering his voice, and asked him about that. He said: "The One whom I privately address hears me." He passed by ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) while he was raising his voice, and asked him about that. He said: "I wake the drowsy and drive away Satan." He passed by Bilāl while he was reciting verses from this sūrah and verses from that sūrah, and asked him about that. He said: "I mix the good with the good." He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "All of you have done well and hit the mark."

The manner of reconciling these reports is that secrecy is further from ostentation (riyāʾ) and affectation, so it is more excellent for one who fears that for himself. But if one does not fear that, and there is nothing in raising the voice that disturbs the time of another worshipper, then raising the voice is more excellent — because the work in it is greater; because its benefit also extends to others, and the good that is transitive is more excellent than the good that is intransitive; because it awakens the heart of the reciter and gathers his attention toward reflection, directing his hearing to it; because it repels sleep by raising the voice; because it increases his vigor for recitation and diminishes his laziness; because by his raising his voice he may hope to awaken a sleeper, thus becoming the cause of his revival; and because a heedless idler may see him and be energized by his energy, yearning for service. Whenever any of these intentions is present, raising the voice is more excellent.

If these intentions are combined, the reward is multiplied. By the multiplicity of intentions do the works of the righteous grow pure and their rewards multiply. If in a single work there are ten intentions, there are in it ten rewards. For this reason we say that reciting the Qurʾān from the muṣḥafs is more excellent — for it adds to the work the act of looking, contemplating the muṣḥaf, and carrying it, thus increasing the reward by reason of it. It has been said that a completion from the muṣḥaf is [worth] seven [completions], because looking at the muṣḥaf is itself an act of worship. ʿUthmān (may God be pleased with him) wore out two muṣḥafs due to his frequent recitation from them. Many of the Companions used to recite from the muṣḥafs and disliked that a day should pass without their looking into the muṣḥaf.

One of the jurists of Egypt entered upon al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) at dawn, with a muṣḥaf before him. Al-Shāfiʿī said to him: "Your reflection has distracted you from the Qurʾān. I pray the night prayer and place the muṣḥaf before me, and I do not close it until morning."

**The Tenth: Concerning Beautifying Recitation and Measuring It** — By modulating the voice without excessive elongation that alters the composition — for that is Sunnah. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Adorn the Qurʾān with your voices." He (peace be upon him) said: "God has not listened to anything as He listens to a beautiful voice in recitation of the Qurʾān." He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "He is not of us who does not chant the Qurʾān." It was said he meant thereby being free from need [of others], and it was said he meant melodious chanting and the modulation of tones — and this latter is closer according to the people of language.

It is narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was one night waiting for ʿĀʾishah (may God be pleased with her), and she was delayed. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "What detained you?" She said: "O Messenger of God, I was listening to the recitation of a man — I have never heard a more beautiful voice than his." He (peace and blessings be upon him) stood and listened to him for a long time, then returned and said: "This is Sālim, the freed slave of Abū Ḥudhayfah. Praise be to God who has placed in my community one like him." He (peace and blessings be upon him) also listened one night to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, with Abū Bakr and ʿUmar (may God be pleased with them both) present. They stood for a long time, then he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever wishes to recite the Qurʾān fresh and tender as it was revealed, let him recite it according to the recitation of Ibn Umm ʿAbd." He (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Ibn Masʿūd: "Recite to me." He said: "O Messenger of God, shall I recite to you when upon you it was revealed?" He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "I love to hear it from another." So he recited while the eyes of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) overflowed with tears.

He (peace and blessings be upon him) listened to the recitation of Abū Mūsā and said: "This one has been given a pipe from the pipes of the family of David." When that reached Abū Mūsā, he said: "O Messenger of God, had I known that you were listening, I would have embellished it for you with the finest embellishment." Haytham the reciter saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in a dream. He said: "He said to me: 'Are you Haytham, who adorns the Qurʾān with his voice?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'May God reward you with good.'"

In the report: The Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), when they gathered, would command one of them to recite a sūrah from the Qurʾān. ʿUmar used to say to Abū Mūsā (may God be pleased with them both): "Remind us of our Lord." So he would recite before him until the time of prayer was nearly midway, and it would be said: "O Commander of the Believers, the prayer, the prayer!" He would say: "Are we not in prayer?" — alluding to the saying of God Almighty: {«ولذكر الله أكبر»} — "And the remembrance of God is greater." He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever listens to a verse from the Book of God Almighty, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection." In the report: "Ten good deeds are written for him." However great the reward of listening, since the reciter is the cause of it, he is a partner in the reward — unless his intention is ostentation and affectation.

فهم أصل الكلام ثم التعظيم ثم حضور القلب ثم التدبر ثم التفهم ثم التخلي
عنموانع الفهم ثم التخصيص ثم التأثر ثم الترقي ثم التبري
فالأول فهم عظمة الكلام وعلوه وفضل الله سبحانه وتعالى ولطفه بخلقه في
نزوله  عن عرش جلاله إلى درجة إفهام خلقه
فلينظر كيف لطف بخلقه في إيصال معاني كلامه الذي هو صفة قديمة قائمة
بذاته إلى أفهام خلقه وكيف تجلت لهم تلك الصفة في طي حروف وأصوات هي صفات
البشر إذ يعجز البشر عن الوصول إلى فهم صفات الله عز وجل إلا بوسيلة صفات
نفسه
ولولا استتار كنه جلالة كلامه بكسوة الحروف لما ثبت لسماع الكلام عرش ولا
ثري ولتلاشي ما بينهما من عظمة سلطانه وسبحات نوره ولولا تثبيت الله عز وجل
لموسى عليه السلام لما أطاق لسماع كلامه كما لم يطق الجبل مبادي تجليه حيث
صار دكا ولا يمكن تفهيم عظمة الكلام إلا بأمثلة على حد فهم الخلق
ولهذا عبر بعض العارفين عنه فقال إن كل حرف من كلام الله عز وجل في اللوح
المحفوظ أعظم من جبل قاف وإن الملائكة عليهم السلام لو اجتمعت على الحرف
الواحد أن يقلوه ما أطاقوه حتى يأتي إسرافيل عليه السلام وهو ملك اللوح
فيرفعه فيقله بإذن الله عز وجل ورحمته لا بقوته وطاقته ولكن الله عز وجل
طوقه ذلك واستعمله به ولقد تألق بعض الحكماء في التعبير عن وجه اللطف في
إيصال معاني الكلام مع علو درجته إلى فهم الإنسان وتثبيته مع قصور رتبته
وضرب له مثلا لم يقصر فيه وذلك أنه دعا PageV01P280
بعض الملوك حكيم إلى شريعة الأنبياء عليهم السلام فسأله الملك عن أمور
فأجاب بما لا يحتمله فهمه فقال الملك أرأيت ما تأتي به الأنبياء إذا ادعت
أنه ليس بكلام الناس وأنه كلام الله عز وجل فيكف يطيق الناس حمله فقال
الحكيم إنا رأينا الناس لما أرادوا أن يفهموا بعض الدواب والطير ما يريدون
من تقديمها وتأخيرها وإقبالها وإدبارها ورأوا الدواب يقصر تمييزها عن فهم
كلامهم الصادر عن أنوار عقولهم مع حسنه وتزيينه وبديع نظمه فنزلوا إلى درجة
تمييز البهائم وأوصلوا مقاصدهم إلى بواطن البهائم بأصوات يضعونها لائقة بهم
من النقر والصفير والأصوات القريبة من أصواتها لكي يطيقوا حملها وكذلك
الناس يعجزون عن حمل  كلام الله عز وجل بكنهه وكمال صفاته فصاروا بما
تراجعوا بينهم من الأصوات التي سمعوا بها الحكمة كصوت النقر والصفير الذي
سمعت به الدواب من الناس
ولم يمنع ذلك معاني الحكمة المخبوءة في تلك الصفات من أن شرف الكلام أي
الأصوات لشرفها وعظم لتعظيمها فكان الصوت للحكمة جسدا ومسكنا والحكمة للصوت
نفسا وروحا
فكما أن أجساد البشر تكرم وتعز لمكان الروح فكذلك أصوات الكلام تشرف
للحكمة التي فيها
والكلام على المنزلة رفيع الدرجة قاهر السلطان نافذ الحكم في الحق
والباطل وهو القاضي العدل والشاهد المرتضى يأمر وينهى ولا طاقة للباطل أن
يقوم قدام كلام الحكمة كما لا يستطيع الظل أن يقول قدام شعاع الشمس ولا
طاقة للبشر أن ينفذوا غور الحكمة كما لا طاقة لهم أن ينفذوا بأبصارهم ضوء
عين الشمس ولكنهم ينالون من ضوء عين الشمس ما تحيا به أبصارهم ويستدلون به
على حوائجهم فقط
فالكلام كالملك المحجوب الغائب وجهه النافذ أمره وكالشمس الغزيرة الظاهرة
مكنون عنصرها وكالنجوم الزهرة التي قد يهتدى بها من لا يقف على سيرها فهو
مفتاح الخزائن النفيسة وشراب الحياة الذي من شرب منه لم يمت ودواء الأسقام
الذي من سقي منه لم يسقم فهذا الذي ذكره الحكيم نبذة من تفهيم معنى الكلام
والزيادة عليه لا تليق بعلم المعاملة فينبغي أن يقتصر عليه
الثاني التعظيم للمتكلم فالقارئ عند البداية بتلاوة القرآن ينبغي أن يحضر
في قلبه عظمة المتكلم ويعلم أن ما يقرؤه ليس من كلام البشر وأن في تلاوة
كلام الله عز وجل غاية الخطر فإنه تعالى قال {لا يمسه إلا المطهرون} وكما
أن ظاهر جلد المصحف وورقه محروس عن ظاهر بشرة اللامس إلا إذا كان متطهرا
فباطن معناه أيضا بحكم عزه وجلاله محجوب عن باطن القلب إلا إذا كان متطهرا
عن كل رجس ومستنيرا بنور التعظيم والتوقير وكما لا يصلح لمس جلد المصحف كل
يد فلا يصلح لتلاوة حروفه كل لسان ولا لنيل معانيه كل قلب ولمثل هذا
التعظيم كان عكرمة بن أبي جهل  إذا نشر المصحف غشى عليه ويقول هو كلام ربي
هو كلام ربي فتعظيم الكلام تعظيم المتكلم ولن تحضره عظمة المتكلم ما لم
يتفكر في صفاته وجلاله وأفعاله فإذا حضر بباله العرش والكرسي والسموات
والأرض وما بينهما من الجن والإنس والدواب والأشجار وعلم أن الخالق لجميعها
والقادر عليها والرازق لها واحد وأن الكل في قبضة قدرته مترددون بين فضله
ورحمته وبين نقمته وسطوته إن أنعم فبفضله وإن عاقب فبعدله وأنه الذي يقول
هؤلاء إلى الجنة ولا أبالي وهؤلاء إلى النار ولا أبالي وهذا غاية العظمة
والتعالي فبالتفكر في أمثال هذا يحضر تعظيم المتكلم ثم تعظيم الكلام
