واستعملني به صالحا تقبله مني (1) اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية وحسن
اليقين والمعافا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Calling, invoking, summoning; the act of supplication directed toward God
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Duʿāʾ as the essence of worship (ʿibādah), the creature's acknowledgment of need (iftiqār) before the Creator
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal petition; metaphorical (majāz) — any act of worship expressing dependence
- Root: و-ر-د (wa-ra-da)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Arriving at water; the daily portion of devotional recitation
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Awrād as the disciplined schedule of remembrance (dhikr) and supplication
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — approaching a watering place; metaphorical — the soul's regular approach to divine grace
- Root: ح-ر-ث (ḥa-ra-tha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Tilling the soil, cultivating for harvest
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥarth al-ākhirah — sowing deeds in this world to reap in the Hereafter (Quranic usage: {«مَن كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الْآخِرَةِ»})
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — agriculture; metaphorical — the acquisition of deeds as seeds for eternal reward
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿa-fa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Erasing, pardoning, obliterating the trace of an offense
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿAfw as divine pardon that removes the very record of sin
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — effacing a mark; metaphorical — God's obliteration of guilt
- Root: ق-ب-ض (qa-ba-ḍa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Seizing, grasping, taking hold
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qabḍ as God's taking of the soul at death; also constriction as divine decree
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical seizure; metaphorical — God's sovereign taking of life
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "If you are among the seekers..." (fa-in kunta...) establishes a protasis whose apodosis is the imperative "say" (fa-qul), governing the entire sequence of supplications that follow.
chapters.translation:
I say: Chapter Four — Concerning supplications transmitted from the Prophet (peace be upon him) and from his Companions (may God be pleased with them), with their chains of transmission omitted, selected from the totality of what Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī, Ibn Khuzaymah, and Ibn Mundhir (may God have mercy on them) compiled.

Know that it is recommended for the aspirant (murīd), when he awakens, that his most beloved of daily litanies (awrād) be supplication, as will be mentioned in the Book of Litanies. For if you are among the seekers of the tillage of the Hereafter (ḥarth al-ākhirah), following the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) in what he supplicated with, then say at the opening of your supplications (1) and at the conclusions of your prayers (2):

"Glory be to my Lord, the Exalted, the Most High, the Bestower — there is no god but God alone, with no partner; to Him belongs sovereignty and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things powerful."

And say: "I am well-pleased with God as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad (peace be upon him) as Prophet" — three times.

And say: "O God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, Lord of all things and their Sovereign, I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and the evil of Satan and his polytheism." (4)

And say: "O God, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion and my worldly life, my family and my wealth. O God, cover my faults, calm my fears, and forgive my stumbles. And protect me from before me and from behind me, from my right and from my left, and from above me; and I seek refuge in You from being treacherously seized from beneath me." (1)

"O God, do not entrust me to Your cunning, do not turn me over to other than You, do not strip away from me Your covering, do not make me forget Your remembrance, and do not make me among the heedless." (2)

And say: "O God, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me, and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin — so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You." (3) — three times.

And say: "O God, grant me well-being in my body, grant me well-being in my hearing, grant me well-being in my sight — there is no god but You." (4) — three times.

And say: "O God, I ask You for contentment after the decree, and the coolness of life after death, and the delight of gazing upon Your noble Face, and longing for Your meeting — without harmful adversity or misleading trial. And I seek refuge in You from committing injustice or suffering injustice, from transgressing or having transgression committed against me, or from earning an error or a sin You will not forgive." (5)

"O God, I ask You for steadfastness in the matter and resolve upon right guidance. And I ask You for gratitude for Your favor and excellence in Your worship. And I ask You for a humble, sound heart, and upright character, and a truthful tongue, and accepted deeds. And I ask You for the good of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know — for You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen." (6)

"O God, forgive me what I have advanced and what I have deferred, what I have concealed and what I have declared, and what You know better than I — for You are the Advancer and You are the Deferrer, and You are over all things powerful, and over every unseen thing a Witness." (7)

"O God, I ask You for faith that does not revert, and bliss that does not perish, and the eternal delight of the eye, and the companionship of Your Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the highest of the everlasting Garden." (8)

"O God, I ask You for the good things, and the doing of good deeds, and the abandonment of evil deeds, and love of the poor. I ask You for Your love, and the love of those who love You, and the love of every deed that draws me near to Your love — and that You turn toward me in repentance, forgive me, and have mercy on me. And if You intend a trial for a people, then take me to Yourself untried." (9)

"O God, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive so long as life is good for me, and take me in death when death is good for me. I ask You for fear of You in the unseen and the witnessed, and the word of justice in contentment and anger, and moderation in wealth and poverty, and the delight of gazing upon Your Face, and longing for Your meeting. And I seek refuge in You from harmful adversity and misleading trial. And O God, adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us guides, rightly guided." (1)

"O God, apportion to us from Your fear that which will serve as a barrier between us and Your acts of disobedience, and from Your obedience that which will convey us to Your Garden, and from certainty that which will make the calamities of this world and the Hereafter light upon us." (2)

"O God, fill our faces with shame before You, and our hearts with awe of You, and settle within our souls from Your majesty that which will subdue our limbs to Your service. And make You, O God, more beloved to us than anyone other than You, and make us more fearful of You than of anyone other than You." (3)

"O God, make the beginning of this day of ours rectitude, its middle success, and its end triumph. O God, make its beginning mercy, its middle grace, and its end honor and forgiveness." (4)

"Praise be to God, before Whose majesty everything has humbled itself, before Whose might everything has submitted, before Whose sovereignty everything has bowed, and before Whose power everything has yielded. And praise be to God, before Whose awe everything has grown still, Whose wisdom has manifested everything, and before Whose grandeur everything has become small." (5)

"O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, the wives of Muhammad and his progeny; and bless Muhammad and his family, his wives and his progeny, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham among the worlds — indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious." (6)

"O God, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, Your Prophet, and Your Messenger — the unlettered Prophet, Your trustworthy Messenger — and grant him the praiseworthy station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd) which You promised him on the Day of Judgment." (7)

"O God, make us among Your righteous friends (awliyāʾ), Your successful party (ḥizb), and Your righteous servants. Employ us for that which pleases You from us, grant us success in what You love from us, and dispose us by Your good choice for us." (8)

"We ask You for the comprehensive goods, their openings and their conclusions; and we seek refuge in You from the comprehensive evils, their openings and their conclusions." (9)

"O God, by Your power over me, turn toward me in repentance — indeed You are the Acceptor of Repentance, the Merciful. And by Your forbearance toward me, pardon me — indeed You are the Forgiving, the Forbearing. And by Your knowledge of me, be gentle with me — indeed You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. And by Your sovereignty over me, make me master of my soul and do not give it dominion over me — indeed You are the Sovereign, the Compeller." (10)

"Glory be to You, O God, and by Your praise — there is no god but You. I have done evil and wronged my soul, so forgive me my sin — indeed You are my Lord, and none forgives sins but You." (11)

"O God, inspire me with my right guidance (rushd) and protect me from the evil of my soul." (12)

"O God, provide me with lawful sustenance for which You will not punish me, and make me content with what You have provided me, and employ me in it righteously that You may accept it from me." (1)

"O God, I ask You for pardon and well-being, and excellence of certainty, and preservation (muʿāfāh) in this world and the Hereafter." (2)

"O You Whom sins do not harm and Whom forgiveness does not diminish — grant me what does not harm You, and give me what does not diminish You. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims. You are our Protector in this world and the Hereafter — cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. You are our Guardian, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the Best of forgivers. And write for us good in this world and in the Hereafter — indeed we have turned to You. Our Lord, upon You we rely, and to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the wrongdoing people. Our Lord, make us not a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord — indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise. Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excess in our affairs, and make firm our feet and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and place not in our hearts any rancor toward those who believe — our Lord, indeed You are Kind, Merciful. Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith — up to His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: {«إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ»} (Indeed, You do not fail the promise). Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err — our Lord, to the end of the Surah." (3)

"My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and have mercy on them as they raised me when I was small. And forgive the believing men and the believing women, the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the living among them and the dead." (4)

"My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and overlook what You know — and You are the Most Exalted, the Most Generous, and You are the Best of the merciful, and You are the Best of forgivers. And indeed to God we belong, and indeed to Him we return. And there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent. And God suffices us, and He is the Best Disposer of affairs. And may God send blessings upon Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets, and upon his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace." (5)

chapters.title_en: The Varieties of Divinely-Transmitted Seeks of Refuge (Istiʿādhah) from the Prophet ﷺ
chapters.arabic_text:
||| أنواع الاستعاذة المأثورة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

اللهم إني أعوذ بك من البخل وأعوذ بك من الجبن وأعوذ بك من أن أرد إلى
ارذل العمر وأعوذ بك من فتنة الدنيا وأعوذ بك من عذاب القبر (6) اللهم إني
أعوذ بك من طبع يهدي إلى طمع ومن طمع في غير مطمع ومن PageV01P321
طمع حيث لا مطمع (1) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من علم لا ينفع وقلب لا يخشع
ودعاء لا يسمع ونفس لا تشبع وأعوذ بك من الجوع فإنه بئس الضجيع ومن الخيانة
فإنها بئست البطانة ومن الكسل والبخل والجبن والهرم ومن أن أرد إلى ارذل
العمر ومن فتنة الدجال وعذاب القبر ومن فتنة المحيا والممات اللهم إنا
نسألك قلوبا أواهة مخبتة منيبة في سبيلك اللهم إني أسألك عزائم مغفرتك
وموجبات رحمتك والسلامة من كل إثم والغنيمة من كل بر والفوز بالجنة والنجاة
من النار (2) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من التردي وأعوذ بك من الغم والغرق والهدم
وأعوذ بك من أن أموت في سبيلك مدبرا وأعوذ بك من أن أموت في تطلب الدنيا
(3) اللهم إني أعوذ بك شر ما علمت ومن شر ما لم أعلم (4) اللهم جنبني
منكرات الأخلاق والأعمال والأدواء والأهواء (5) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من جهد
البلاء ودرك الشقاء وسوء القضاء وشماتة الأعداء (6) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من
الكفر والدين والفقر وأعوذ بك من عذاب جهنم وأعوذ بك من فتنة الدجال (7)
اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شر سمعي وبصري وشر لساني وقلبي وشر منيي (8) اللهم
إني أعوذ بك من جار السوء في دار المقامة فإن جار البادية يتحول (9) اللهم
إني أعوذ بك من القسوة والغفلة والعيلة والذلة والمسكنة  وأعوذ بك من الكفر
والفقر والفسوق والشقاق والنفاق وسوء الأخلاق وضيق الأرزاق والسمعة والرياء
وأعوذ بك من الصمم والبكم والعمى والجنون والجذام والبرص وسيىء الأسقام
(10) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من زوال نعمتك ومن تحول عافيتك ومن فجأة نقمتك ومن
جميع سخطك (11) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من عذاب النار وفتنة النار وعذاب القبر
وشر فتنة الغنى وشر فتنة الفقر وشر فتنة PageV01P322
المسيح الدجال وأعوذ بك من المغرم والمأثم (1) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من نفس
لا تشبع وقلب لا يخشع وصلاة لا تنفع ودعوة لا تستجاب وأعوذ بك من شر الغم
وفتنة الصدر (2) اللهم إني أعوذ بك من غلبة الدين وغلبة العدو وشماتة
الأعداء (3) وصلى الله على محمد وعلى كل عبد مصطفى من كل العالمين آمين
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of clinging, seeking protection, and attaching oneself to a sanctuary (maljaʾ) for safety from harm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, istiʿādhah signifies the creature's existential acknowledgment of utter dependence upon the Creator's sovereign guardianship (ḥifẓ) against both worldly and eschatological evils.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) as seeking shelter; metaphorically (majāz) it denotes the soul's flight from every contingent cause to the Necessary Being alone.
- Root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Trial, tribulation, and the burning test that discriminates the sincere from the corrupt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes the divinely-ordained probationary affliction (miḥnah) that refines faith, including the supreme trial of the Dajjāl.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of smelting gold in fire; metaphorical sense of any seductive allure that diverts the heart from obedience.
- Root: خ-ن-ث (kh-n-th) [variant reading of خيانة, kh-y-n]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Treachery, breach of trust, and covert betrayal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The violation of the covenant (mīthāq) between the servant and his Lord, manifesting in unfaithfulness to divine commands.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: concealing goods entrusted; metaphorical: the soul's concealment of its true rebellious intent behind a façade of piety.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The repeated "wa-aʿūdhu bika" (and I seek refuge in You) functions as an anaphoric coordinate (maʿṭūf) that re-establishes the governing verb's scope over each new object, preserving the supplicatory rhythm and grammatical independence of each clause.
chapters.translation:
I say: These are the varieties of seeking refuge (istiʿādhah) transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ:

"O Allah, I seek refuge in You from miserliness, and I seek refuge in You from cowardice, and I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most decrepit age [of senility], and I seek refuge in You from the trial of this world, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a nature that leads to covetousness, and from covetousness in that which is not a legitimate object of desire, and from covetousness where there is no object of desire. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from knowledge that does not benefit, and a heart that does not humble itself, and a supplication that is not heard, and a soul that is not satisfied; and I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is an evil bedfellow, and from treachery, for it is an evil companion, and from laziness, miserliness, cowardice, and senility, and from being returned to the most decrepit age, and from the trial of the Dajjāl, and the punishment of the grave, and from the trial of life and death. O Allah, we ask You for hearts that are penitent (awwāhah), humbly submissive (mukhbitah), and returning unto Your path. O Allah, I ask You for the firm resolutions of Your forgiveness, and the causes of Your mercy, and safety from every sin, and the gain of every good, and victory with Paradise, and deliverance from the Fire. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from falling into a pit, and I seek refuge in You from grief, drowning, and collapse [of a structure], and I seek refuge in You from dying in Your path while fleeing, and I seek refuge in You from dying in pursuit of this world. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I know, and from the evil of what I do not know. O Allah, keep me away from the abominable qualities of character, deeds, ailments, and passions. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of tribulation, the attainment of misery, the evil of divine decree, and the gloating of enemies. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief, debt, and poverty, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hellfire, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of the Dajjāl. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my hearing and my sight, the evil of my tongue and my heart, and the evil of my seminal fluid. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from an evil neighbor in the abode of permanent residence, for the neighbor of the desert may move away. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from hardness of heart, heedlessness, destitution, humiliation, and abasement; and I seek refuge in You from disbelief, poverty, wickedness, discord, hypocrisy, evil character, constricted provisions, seeking reputation, and ostentation; and I seek refuge in You from deafness, muteness, blindness, madness, leprosy, vitiligo, and evil ailments. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the withdrawal of Your favor, the transition of Your well-being, the suddenness of Your retribution, and from all of Your wrath. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the Fire, the trial of the Fire, the punishment of the grave, the evil of the trial of wealth, the evil of the trial of poverty, the evil of the trial of the Messiah the Dajjāl; and I seek refuge in You from debt and sin. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from a soul that is not satisfied, a heart that does not humble itself, a prayer that does not benefit, and a supplication that is not answered; and I seek refuge in You from the evil of grief and the trial of the breast. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the dominance of debt, the dominance of the enemy, and the gloating of enemies."

And may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, and upon every chosen servant from among all the worlds. Āmīn.

chapters.arabic_text:
|| الباب الخامس في الأدعية المأثورة عند حدوث كل حادث من الحوادث

إذا أصبحت وسمعت الأذان فيستحب لك جواب المؤذن وقد ذكرناه وذكرنا أدعية
دخول الخلاء والخروج منه وأدعية الوضوء في كتاب الطهارة فإذا خرجت إلى
المسجد فقل اللهم اجعل في قلبي نورا وفي لساني نورا واجعل في سمعي نورا
واجعل في بصري نورا واجعل خلفي نورا وأمامي نورا واجعل من فوقي نورا اللهم
أعطني (4) نورا وقل أيضا اللهم إني أسألك بحق السائلين عليك وبحق ممشاي هذا
إليك (5) فإني لم أخرج أشرا ولا بطرا ولا رياء ولا سمعة خرجت اتقاء سخطك
وابتغاء مرضاتك فأسألك أن تنقذني من النار وأن تغفر لي ذنوبي إنه لا يغفر
الذنوب إلا أنت
فإن خرجت من المنزل لحاجة فقل بسم الله رب أعوذ بك أن أظلم أو أظلم أو
أجهل أو يجهل علي (6) بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله
العلي العظيم بسم الله التكلان على الله (7)
فإذا انتهيت إلى المسجد تريد دخوله فقل اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد
وسلم اللهم اغفر لي جميع ذنوبي وافتح لي أبواب رحمتك (8) وقدم رجلك اليمنى
في الدخول فإذا رأيت في المسجد من يبيع أو يبتاع فقل لا أربح الله تجارتك
(9) وإذا رأيت من ينشد ضالة في المسجد فقل لا ردها الله عليك أمر به رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (10) فإذا صليت ركعتي الصبح فقل بسم الله اللهم
إني أسألك رحمة من عندك تهدي بها قلبي الدعاء إلى آخره (11) PageV01P323
كما أوردناه عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
فإذا ركعت فقل في ركوعك اللهم لك ركعت ولك خشعت وبك آمنت ولك أسلمت وعليك
توكلت أنت ربي خشع سمعي وبصري ومخي وعظمي وعصبي وما استقلت به قدمي لله رب
العالمين (1) وإن أحببت فقل سبحان ربي العظيم ثلاث مرات (2) أو سبوح قدوس
رب الملائكة والروح (3) فإذا رفعت رأسك من الركوع فقل سمع الله لمن حمده
ربنا لك الحمد ملء السموات وملء الأرض وملء ما شئت من شيء بعد أهل الثناء
والمجد أحق ما قال العبد وكلنا لك عبد لا مانع لما أعطيت ولا معطي لما منعت
ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد (4) وإذا سجدت فقل اللهم لك سجدت وبك آمنت ولك
أسلمت سجد وجهي للذي خلقه وصوره وشق سمعه وبصره فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين
اللهم سجد لك سوادي وخيالي وآمن بك فؤادي أبوء بنعمتك علي وأبوء بذنبي وهذا
ما جنيت على نفسي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (5) أو تقول سبحان
ربي الأعلى ثلاث مرات (6) فإذا فرغت من الصلاة فقل اللهم أنت السلام ومنك
السلام تباركت يا ذا الجلال والإكرام (7) وتدعو بسائر الأدعية التي ذكرناها
فإذا قمت من المجلس وأردت دعاء يكفر لغو المجلس فقل سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك
أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت أستغفرك وأتوب إليك عملت سوءا وظلمت نفسي فاغفر لي
فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت (8)
فإذا دخلت السوق فقل لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك وله الحمد
يحيي ويميت وهو حي لا يموت بيده الخير وهو على كل شيء قدير (9) بسم الله
اللهم إني أسألك خير هذه السوق وخير ما فيها اللهم إني أعوذ بك من شرها  وشر
ما فيها اللهم إني أعوذ بك أن أصيب فيها يمينا فاجرة أو صفقة خاسرة (10)
فإن كان عليك دين فقل اللهم اكفني بحلالك عن حرامك وأغنني بفضلك عمن سواك
(11)
فإذا لبست ثوبا جديدا فقل اللهم كسوتني هذا الثوب فلك الحمد أسألك من
خيره وخير ما صنع له وأعوذ بك من شره وشر ما صنع له (12)
وإذا PageV01P324
رأيت شيئا من الطيرة تكرهه فقل اللهم لا يأتي بالحسنات إلا أنت ولا يذهب
بالسيئات إلا أنت ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله (1)
وإذا رأيت الهلال فقل اللهم أهله علينا بالأمن والإيمان والبر والسلامة
والإسلام والتوفيق لما تحب وترضى والحفظ عمن تسخط ربي وربك الله (2) ويقول
هلال رشد وخير آمنت بخالقك (3) اللهم إني أسألك خير هذا الشهر وخير القدر
وأعوذ بك من شر يوم الحشر (4) وتكبر قبله أولا ثلاثا
وإذا هبت الريح فقل اللهم إني أسألك خير هذه الريح وخير ما فيها وخير ما
أرسلت به ونعوذ بك من شرها وشر ما فيها ومن شر ما أرسلت به (5)
وإذا بلغك وفاة أحد فقل إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون وإنا إلى ربنا لمنقلبون
اللهم اكتبه في المحسنين واجعل كتابه في عليين واخلفه على عقبه في الغابرين
اللهم لا تحرمنا أجره ولا تفتنا بعده واغفر لنا وله (6)
وتقول عند التصدق {ربنا تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم}
وتقول عند الخسران {عسى ربنا أن يبدلنا خيرا منها إنا إلى ربنا راغبون}
وتقول عند ابتداء الأمور ربنا آتنا من لدنك رحمة وهيىء لنا من أمرنا رشدا
رب اشرح لي صدري ويسر لي أمري
وتقول عند النظر إلى السماء ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا سبحانك فقنا عذاب
النار تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجا وجعل فيها سراجا وقمرا منيرا
وإذا سمعت صوت الرعد فقل سبحان من يسبح الرعد بحمده والملائكة من خيفته
(7)
فإن رأيت الصواعق فقل اللهم لا تقتلنا بغضبك ولا تهلكنا بعذابك وعافنا
قبل ذلك (8) قاله ك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Calling, invoking, summoning; the act of supplication as a direct address to another
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Supplication (duʿāʾ) as the essence of worship—the creature's acknowledgment of need (iftiqār) before the Creator, distinct from mere request
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of vocal calling; metaphorical (majāz) when denoting the heart's orientation toward God without utterance
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dhakara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Remembrance, mention, recollection; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Remembrance (dhikr) as the highest act of worship—presence of heart (ḥuḍūr al-qalb) with God, the very marrow of devotion
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for verbal mention; metaphorical for the heart's vigilant awareness that repels heedlessness (ghaflah)
- Root: ق-ض-ي (qaḍā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Decree, judgment, completion; the execution of a determined matter
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine decree (qaḍāʾ) as the primordial determination; destiny (qadar) as the detailed unfolding of causes and effects
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for judicial verdict; metaphorical for the causal nexus wherein supplication itself is a decreed cause for repelling affliction
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The phrase "If you say X, then say Y" establishes a syntactic parallelism where the protasis (condition) governs the apodosis (response), mirroring the causal linkage between human action and divine response.
chapters.translation:
I say: This is the fifth chapter concerning the transmitted supplications to be uttered upon the occurrence of every event among events.

When you rise in the morning and hear the call to prayer (adhān), it is commendable (mustaḥabb) for you to respond to the caller—and we have already mentioned this, along with the supplications for entering and exiting the privy and those for ablution, in the Book of Purification. When you depart toward the mosque, say: "O Allah, place light in my heart, and light upon my tongue, and place light in my hearing, and light in my sight, and place light behind me, and light before me, and light above me. O Allah, grant me light." And also say: "O Allah, I ask You by the right of those who ask of You, and by the right of this my walking unto You—for I have not come out in insolence, nor in vanity, nor for show, nor for reputation. I have come out fearing Your wrath and seeking Your good pleasure. So I ask You to deliver me from the Fire and to forgive me my sins—verily, none forgives sins but You."

If you depart from your home for a need, say: "In the name of Allah. O Lord, I seek refuge in You from wronging or being wronged, from acting ignorantly or being treated with ignorance. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. There is no might and no power except with Allah, the Exalted, the Magnificent. In the name of Allah; upon Allah do I rely."

When you arrive at the mosque intending to enter it, say: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and grant him peace. O Allah, forgive me all my sins and open for me the gates of Your mercy." And advance your right foot upon entering. If you see in the mosque one who sells or buys, say: "May Allah not profit your trade." And if you see one who announces a lost item in the mosque, say: "May Allah not return it to you"—this was commanded by the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. When you have prayed the two units of the dawn prayer, say: "In the name of Allah. O Allah, I ask You for mercy from Your presence whereby You guide my heart"—the supplication to its end, as we have transmitted it from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, peace be upon him.

When you bow (rukūʿ), say in your bowing: "O Allah, to You I have bowed, and to You I have humbled myself, and in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted, and upon You I have relied. You are my Lord. My hearing, my sight, my brain, my bones, my nerves, and all that my feet carry have humbled themselves to Allah, Lord of the worlds." And if you wish, say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent" three times, or "Most Glorious, Most Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit." When you raise your head from bowing, say: "Allah hears him who praises Him. Our Lord, to You is all praise—filling the heavens, filling the earth, and filling whatever You will beyond that. O Possessor of praise and glory, most worthy of what the servant says—and all of us are Your servants. There is no preventer of what You give, nor giver of what You withhold, and the wealth of the wealthy avails nothing against You." When you prostrate (sujūd), say: "O Allah, to You I have prostrated, and in You I have believed, and to You I have submitted. My face has prostrated before Him who created it, fashioned it, and opened its hearing and sight—so blessed be Allah, the Best of creators. O Allah, to You prostrated my darkness and my shadow, and in You believed my heart. I acknowledge Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin. This is what I have wrought against my soul, so forgive me—for none forgives sins but You." Or you may say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High" three times. When you have finished the prayer, say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor." And supplicate with the rest of the supplications we have mentioned.

When you rise from a gathering and desire a supplication that expiates the idle talk of the session, say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise. I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance. I have done evil and wronged my soul, so forgive me—for none forgives sins but You."

When you enter the marketplace, say: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion, and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and dies not. In His hand is all good, and He is powerful over all things. In the name of Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this market and the good of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from striking therein a false oath or a losing bargain." If you have a debt upon you, say: "O Allah, suffice me with Your lawful provision against Your forbidden, and enrich me by Your bounty from all besides You."

When you don a new garment, say: "O Allah, You have clothed me with this garment, so to You is the praise. I ask You for its good and the good of that for which it was made, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of that for which it was made."

When you see something of ill omen (ṭiyarah) that you dislike, say: "O Allah, none brings good things but You, and none removes evil things but You. There is no might and no power except with Allah."

When you see the crescent moon, say: "O Allah, bring it upon us with security and faith, with well-being and safety, with Islam and success toward what You love and are pleased with, and with protection from what You abhor. My Lord and your Lord is Allah." And say: "A crescent of guidance and good—I believe in your Creator. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this month and the good of the decree, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of the Day of Gathering." And pronounce the takbīr (Allāhu akbar) three times before it.

When the wind blows, say: "O Allah, I ask You for the good of this wind, and the good of what is in it, and the good of what it has been sent with. And I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil of what is in it, and the evil of what it has been sent with."

When news of someone's death reaches you, say: "Verily, to Allah we belong, and to Him we return, and to our Lord we shall be turned. O Allah, write him among the doers of good, and place his record in ʿIlliyyīn, and compensate his progeny after him among those who remain. O Allah, deprive us not of his reward, nor try us after him, and forgive us and him."

And say upon giving charity: {«رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ»} ("Our Lord, accept from us; verily You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing").

And say upon loss: {«عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَا أَنْ يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ»} ("Perhaps our Lord will give us better than it in exchange; verily, to our Lord we are desirous").

And say at the commencement of affairs: "Our Lord, grant us from Your presence mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance. My Lord, expand for me my breast and ease for me my task."

And say upon looking at the sky: {«رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ»} ("Our Lord, You have not created this in vain—glory be to You—so protect us from the punishment of the Fire"). {«تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجًا وَقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا»} ("Blessed is He who placed in the heaven constellations and placed therein a lamp and an illuminating moon").

When you hear the sound of thunder, say: "Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels from His awe."

If you see lightning bolts, say: "O Allah, do not kill us with Your wrath, nor destroy us with Your punishment, but grant us well-being before that." This was said by Kaʿb.

When the sky rains, say: "O Allah, a wholesome watering and a beneficial downpour. O Allah, make it a rain of mercy, and do not make it a rain of punishment."

When you become angry, say: "O Allah, forgive me my sin, and remove the rage of my heart, and deliver me from the accursed Satan."

When you fear a people, say: "O Allah, verily we place You against their throats, and we seek refuge in You from their evils."

When you go forth to battle, say: "O Allah, You are my support and my helper, and by You I fight."

When your ear rings, send blessings upon Muhammad, peace be upon him, and say: "May Allah mention with good the one who mentioned me with good."

When you see the response to your supplication, say: "Praise be to Allah, by whose might and majesty good deeds are perfected." And when it is delayed, say: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance."

When you hear the call to the sunset prayer (maghrib), say: "O Allah, this is the coming of Your night, the departure of Your day, the voices of Your callers, and the presence of Your prayers. I ask You to forgive me."

When distress afflicts you, say: "O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant, the son of Your maidservant. My forelock is in Your hand; Your judgment is executed upon me; Your decree is just concerning me. I ask You by every name that is Yours—by which You have named Yourself, or revealed in Your Book, or taught to any of Your creation, or kept hidden in the knowledge of the unseen with You—that You make the Qurʾān the spring of my heart, the light of my breast, the dispeller of my grief, and the remover of my sorrow and distress." The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "No servant is afflicted with sorrow and says this, except that Allah removes his distress and gives him joy in its place." It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we not learn it?" He said: "Yes, it behooves whoever hears it to learn it."

When you feel pain in your body or the body of another, treat it with the ruqyah (incantation) of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. When a person complained of a sore or wound, he would place his index finger on the ground, then raise it and say: "In the name of Allah. The dust of our earth, with the saliva of one of us, heals our sick one by the permission of our Lord." And when you feel pain in your body, place your hand upon the aching part and say "In the name of Allah" three times, and say seven times: "I seek refuge in the might of Allah and His power from the evil of what I find and fear."

When calamity befalls you, say: "There is no god but Allah, the Exalted, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Noble Throne."

If you intend to sleep, perform ablution first, then recline upon your right side facing the qiblah. Then pronounce the takbīr thirty-four times, the tasbīḥ thirty-three times, and the taḥmīd thirty-three times. Then say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your wrath, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. O Allah, I cannot attain full praise of You, even if I strove—but You are as You have praised Yourself. O Allah, in Your name I live and I die. O Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of everything and its Sovereign, Cleaver of the seed and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qurʾān—I seek refuge in You from the evil of every possessor of evil, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. You are the First, so nothing is before You; You are the Last, so nothing is after You; You are the Manifest, so nothing is above You; You are the Hidden, so nothing is beneath You. Settle my debt and enrich me against poverty. O Allah, You created my soul, and You take it—to You belongs its death and its life. O Allah, if You cause it to die, forgive it; and if You give it life, protect it. O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. In Your name, my Lord, I have laid down my side, so forgive me my sin. O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the Day You gather Your servants. O Allah, I have submitted my soul to You, and turned my face to You, and entrusted my affair to You, and leaned my back upon You—in desire and in fear of You. There is no refuge and no deliverance from You except to You. I believe in Your Book which You have revealed, and in Your Prophet whom You have sent."

And let this be the last of your supplications, for the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, commanded this. And let him say before that: "O Allah, awaken me in the hours most beloved to You, and employ me in the deeds most beloved to You, that draw me near to You in closeness and distance me from Your wrath in distance. I ask You, so You give me; I seek Your forgiveness, so You forgive me; I call upon You, so You respond to me."

When you awaken from your sleep at morning, say: "Praise be to Allah who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the resurrection. We have entered the morning, and the dominion belongs to Allah—and greatness and sovereignty belong to Allah, and might and power belong to Allah. We have entered the morning upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah) of Islam, upon the word of sincerity, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and upon the creed of our father Abraham, a ḥanīf, and he was not of the polytheists. O Allah, by You we enter the morning, and by You we enter the evening; by You we live, and by You we die, and to You is the final return. O Allah, I ask You to raise us in this day toward every good, and I seek refuge in You from committing evil therein or bringing it upon a Muslim—for You have said: {«وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُمْ بِالنَّهَارِ ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ لِيُقْضَىٰ أَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى»} ("And He it is who takes you by night and knows what you have committed by day; then He raises you therein that a term appointed may be fulfilled"). O Allah, Cleaver of the dawn, Maker of the night a repose, and the sun and the moon a reckoning—I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is in it. In the name of Allah; whatever Allah wills—there is no power except with Allah. Whatever Allah wills—every blessing is from Allah. Whatever Allah wills—all good is in the hand of Allah. Whatever Allah wills—none repels evil but Allah. I am content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad, peace be upon him, as Prophet. Our Lord, upon You we rely, to You we turn in repentance, and to You is the final return."

And when he enters the evening, he says the same, except that he says: "We have entered the evening," and adds: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah and all His names from the evil of what He has created and brought forth, from the evil of every possessor of evil, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. Verily, my Lord is upon a straight path." Its chain of transmission is sound (jayyid). Muslim has from the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayrah concerning the supplication at sleep: "I seek refuge in You from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold." And al-Ṭabarānī has it in his supplications from the ḥadīth of Abū al-Dardāʾ.

When he looks into a mirror, he says: "Praise be to Allah who proportioned my creation and balanced it, honored the form of my face and beautified it, and made me among the Muslims."

When you purchase a servant, a boy, or an animal, take hold of its forelock and say: "O Allah, I ask You for its good and the good of what it was created upon, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what it was created upon."

When you are congratulated upon marriage, say: "May Allah bless you, and bless upon you, and join between you both in good."

When you repay a debt, say to the one repaid: "May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth"—for the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The recompense of a loan is praise and repayment."

These are supplications that the seeker (murīd) cannot do without memorizing. As for the rest of the supplications—of travel, prayer, and ablution—we have mentioned them in the Book of Pilgrimage, the Book of Prayer, and the Book of Purification.

If you say: "What is the benefit of supplication, when the decree (qaḍāʾ) cannot be repelled?"—know that part of the decree is the repelling of affliction by supplication. For supplication is a cause for repelling affliction and drawing down mercy, just as the shield is a cause for repelling the arrow, and water is a cause for the emergence of vegetation from the earth. As the shield repels the arrow and the two contend, so likewise supplication and affliction wrestle with one another. It is not a condition of acknowledging the decree of Allah, the Exalted, that one refrain from bearing arms—for He has said: {«خُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ»} ("Take your precaution")—nor that one refrain from watering the earth after scattering the seed, such that it be said: "If the decree preceded the growth, the seed grows; and if it did not precede, it does not grow." Rather, the binding of causes to their effects is the first decree, which is like the blink of an eye or nearer. And the gradual arrangement of the details of effects upon the details of causes, with measure and estimation, is destiny (qadar). He who decreed good decreed it by a cause, and He who decreed evil decreed for its repulsion a cause. There is no contradiction among these matters for one whose inner sight has been opened.

Then in supplication there is the benefit we mentioned concerning remembrance (dhikr)—for it summons the presence of the heart with Allah, and that is the ultimate end of acts of worship. For this reason the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Supplication is the marrow of worship." And the prevailing condition of creation is that their hearts do not turn to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, except upon the occurrence of a need or the pressing of a calamity—for when evil touches a man, he is one of abundant supplication. Thus need compels supplication, and supplication returns the heart to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through humility and submissiveness, thereby attaining that remembrance which is the noblest of acts of worship. For this reason, affliction is entrusted to the prophets, peace be upon them, then to the saints (awliyāʾ), then to the most excellent, then the most excellent—because it returns the heart through neediness and humility to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and prevents forgetfulness of Him. As for wealth, it is a cause of insolence in most matters—for man does indeed transgress when he sees himself self-sufficient. This, then, is what we intended to present from the totality of remembrances and supplications. And Allah is the Granter of success to good.

As for the remaining supplications—concerning eating, travel, visiting the sick, and others—they will come in their proper places, Allah willing. And upon Allah is reliance. Completed is the Book of Remembrances and Supplications in its entirety. It is followed, Allah willing, by the Book of Liturgies (al-Awrād). And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our master Muhammad, and upon his family and companions.

| كتاب ترتيب الأوراد وتفصيل إحياء الليل وهو الكتاب العاشر من إحياء علوم الدين وبه اختتام ربع العبادات نفع الله به المسلمين

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
نحمد الله على آلائه حمدا كثيرا ونذكره ذكرا لا يغادر في القلب استكبارا
ولا نفورا ونشكره إذ جعل الليل والنهار خلفة لمن أراد أن يذكر أو أراد
شكورا ونصلي على نبيه الذي بعثه بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وعلى آله الطاهرين
وصحبه الأكرمين الذين اجتهدوا في عبادة الله  غدوة وعشيا وبكرة وأصيلا حتى
أصبح كل واحد منهم نجما في الدين هاديا وسراجا منيرا
أما بعد فإن الله تعالى جعل الأرض ذلولا لعباده إلا ليستقروا في مناكبها
بل ليتخذوها منزلا فيتزودوا منها زادا يحملهم في سفرهم إلى أوطانهم
ويكتنزون منها تحفا لنفوسهم عملا وفضلا محترزين من مصايدها ومعاطبها
ويتحققون أن العمر يسير بهم سير السفينة براكبها فالناس في هذا العالم سفر
وأول منازلهم المهد وآخرها اللحد والوطن هو الجنة أو النار والعمر مسافة
السفر فسنوه مراحله وشهوره فراسخه وأيامه أمياله وأنفاسه خطواته وطاعته
بضاعته وأوقاته رءوس أمواله وشهواته وأغراضه قطاع طريقه وربحه الفوز بلقاء
الله تعالى في دار السلام مع الملك PageV01P329
الكبير والنعيم المقيم وخسرانه البعد من الله تعالى مع الأنكال والأغلال
والعذاب الأليم في دركات الجحيم
فالغافل في نفس من أنفاسه حتى ينقضي في غير طاعة تقربه إلى الله زلفى
متعرض في يوم التغابن لغبينة وحسرة ما لها منتهى ولهذا الخطر العظيم والخطب
الهائل شمر الموفقون عن ساق الجد وودعوا بالكلية ملاذ النفس واغتنموا بقايا
العمر ورتبوا بحسب تكرر الأوقات وظائف الأوراد حرصا على إحياء الليل
والنهار في طلب القرب من الملك الجبار والسعي إلى دار القرار فصار من مهمات
علم طريق الآخرة تفصيل القول في كيفية قسمة الأوراد وتوزيع العبادات التي
سبق شرحها على مقادير الأوقات ويتضح هذا المهم بذكر بابين
الباب الأول في فضيلة الأوراد وترتيبها في الليل والنهار
الباب الثاني في كيفية إحياء الليل وفضيلته وما يتعلق به
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-د (w-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To arrive at water; a watering-place; the point of arrival on a journey; hence, a portion of recitation or devotion assigned to a fixed time.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The appointed portion of worship (ʿibādah) or invocation (dhikr) that the servant "arrives at" as a station of approach (zulfā) to God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: reaching water. Metaphorical (majāz): the soul's scheduled refreshment at the fountain of devotion — a time-bound share of obedience.
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To live; to revive; to keep alive; the opposite of death.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual animation of the heart through worship, contrasted with the death of heedlessness (ghaflah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: biological life. Metaphorical: the enlivening of the night hours with prayer and remembrance, as if the night were a corpse brought back to life.
- Root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To follow in succession; to come after; alternation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The alternation of night and day as a divine sign (āyah) and a rhythm for distributing acts of worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: succession. Metaphorical: the interchange of night and day as two successive "servants" carrying the believer's deeds to God.
- Root: ز-و-د (z-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Provision for a journey; victuals stored for travel.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The provision of taqwā (godliness) that the soul carries from this world to the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: food for a road-journey. Metaphorical: righteous deeds as the only sustenance that survives the crossing to the afterlife.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — The opening sentence "نحمد الله على آلائه حمدا كثيرا" employs an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) to emphasize the verbal action, while the subsequent clauses "نذكره ذكرا لا يغادر..." and "ونشكره إذ جعل..." are coordinated circumstantial qualifiers that specify the manner and occasion of the praise, creating a tripartite rhetorical ascent (praise, remembrance, gratitude) that mirrors the triadic structure of the believer's daily liturgy.
chapters.translation:
I say: This is the Book on the Arrangement of Liturgies (awrād) and the Detailed Practice of Night Vigil (iḥyāʾ al-layl). It is the tenth book of the Revival of the Religious Sciences (Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn), and with it concludes the Quarter of Acts of Worship (rubʿ al-ʿibādāt). May God benefit the Muslims through it.

In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

We praise God for His abundant blessings with abundant praise, and we remember Him with a remembrance that leaves no arrogance in the heart, nor any aversion. And we thank Him, for He made the night and the day to alternate (khilfah) for whoever desires to remember or desires to show gratitude. And we send blessings upon His Prophet, whom He sent with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings and a warner, and upon his pure family and his most noble companions, who strove diligently in the worship of God, morning and evening, at dawn and at dusk, until each one of them became a guiding star in the religion and a luminous lamp.

To proceed: God — exalted be He — did not make the earth subservient to His servants merely that they might settle upon its flanks, but rather that they might take it as a way-station, and from it gather provision (zād) that would carry them on their journey to their true homelands. And from it they amass treasures for their souls — deeds and virtue — while guarding themselves against its snares and perils. And they come to realize with certainty that the lifespan carries them along as a ship carries its rider. Thus, people in this world are travelers: their first way-station is the cradle, their last is the grave (laḥd), and their homeland is either Paradise or the Fire. The lifespan is the distance of the journey: its years are its stages, its months are its leagues (farāsikh), its days are its miles, its breaths are its steps, its obedience is its merchandise, its hours are its capital, and its lusts and desires are the highway robbers along its path. Its profit is the attainment of meeting God — exalted be He — in the Abode of Peace, in the company of the Great King and the everlasting bliss. And its loss is distance from God — exalted be He — together with fetters, chains, and painful chastisement in the lowest depths of the Blazing Fire.

So the heedless one (ghāfil), in every single breath that passes him by without obedience that draws him nearer to God in proximity (zulfā), exposes himself on the Day of Mutual Loss (yawm al-taghābun) to a loss and a regret that has no end. It is on account of this tremendous peril and this colossal calamity that the divinely guided ones (muwaffaqūn) rolled up their sleeves in earnestness, bade farewell entirely to the pleasures of the soul, seized the remnants of their lifespans, and arranged the functions of liturgies (awrād) according to the recurrence of the times — out of eagerness to revive the night and the day in seeking nearness to the Almighty King and in striving toward the Abode of Permanence. Thus, it has become one of the most important matters of the science of the path to the Hereafter to set forth in detail the manner of dividing the liturgies and distributing the acts of worship — whose explanation has already preceded — according to the measures of the times. This important matter is clarified through the mention of two chapters:

Chapter One: On the virtue of liturgies (awrād) and their arrangement in the night and the day.

Chapter Two: On the manner of reviving the night (iḥyāʾ al-layl), its virtue, and what pertains to it.

chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-د (w-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes arrival at water, a place of watering, or a path leading to it; hence a "litany" (wird) is a fixed portion of recitation or supplication that one "arrives at" regularly, like a camel reaching a watering hole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, wird refers to a prescribed, habitual portion of worship (dhikr, Qurʾān, or prayer) that the servant "visits" as a spiritual station, marking the soul's return to its Sustainer—akin to the daily "watering" of the heart.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, wird is the act of arriving at water (ḥaqīqah); metaphorically (majāz), it is the regular devotional practice that quenches the soul's thirst for divine nearness. The plural awrād extends this to a structured sequence of such practices.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "wa-tartībihā wa-aḥkāmihā" (their ordering and their rulings) is governed by the genitive construction (al-ijrāʾ bi-l-jarr) following "faḍīlat al-awrād," where the appended nouns clarify the chapter's scope: virtue (faḍīlah), arrangement (tartīb), and legal rulings (aḥkām) are three coordinate aspects of the same subject, each requiring distinct treatment.
chapters.translation: I say: The first chapter concerns the virtue of the liturgical devotions (awrād), their proper ordering, and the rulings pertaining to them.
