||| بيان أوراد الليل وهي خمسة

الأول إذا غربت الشمس صلى المغرب واشتغل بإحياء ما بين العشاءين فآخر هذا
الورد عند غيبوبة الشفق أعني الحمرة التي بغيبوبتها يدخل وقت العتمة وقد
أقسم الله تعالى به فقال {فلا أقسم بالشفق} والصلاة فيه هي ناشئة الليل
لأنه أول نشوء ساعاته وهو آن من  الآناء المذكورة في قوله تعالى {ومن آناء
الليل فسبح} وهي صلاة الأوابين وهي المراد بقوله تعالى {تتجافى جنوبهم عن
المضاجع} روي ذلك عن الحسن وأسنده ابن أبي زياد إلى رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم أنه سئل عن هذه الآية فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة بين
العشاءين ثم قال صلى الله عليه وسلم عليكم بالصلاة بين العشاءين فإنها تذهب
بملاغات النهار وتهذب آخره (1) والملاغات جمع ملغاة من اللغو وسئل أنس رحمه
الله عمن ينام بين العشاءين فقال لا تفعل فإنها الساعة المعنية بقوله تعالى
{تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع} وسيأتي فضل إحياء ما بين العشاءين في الباب
الثاني وترتيب هذا الورد أن يصلي بعد المغرب ركعتين أولا يقرأ فيهما قل يا
أيها الكافرون وقل هو الله أحد ويصليهما عقيب المغرب من غير تخلل كلام ولا
شغل ثم يصلي أربعا يطيلها ثم يصلي إلى غيبوبة الشفق ما تيسر له وإن كان
المسجد قريبا من المنزل فلا بأس أن يصليها في بيته إن لم يكن عزمه العكوف
في المسجد وإن عزم على العكوف في انتظار العتمة فهو الأفضل إذا كان آمنا من
التصنع والرياء
والورد الثاني يدخل بدخول وقت العشاء الآخرة إلى حد نومة الناس وهو أول
استحكام الظلام وقد أقسم الله تعالى به إذ قال {والليل وما وسق} أي وما جمع
من ظلمته وقال {إلى غسق الليل} فهناك يغسق الليل وتستوسق ظلمته وترتيب هذا
الورد بمراءة ثلاثة أمور الأول أن يصلي سوى فرض العشاء عشر ركعات أربعا قبل
الفرض إحياء لما بين الأذانين وستا بعد الفرض ركعتين ثم أربعا ويقرأ فيها
من القرآن الآيات المخصوصة كآخر البقرة وآية الكرسي وأول الحديد وآخر الحشر
وغيرها والثاني أن يصلي ثلاث عشرة ركعة آخرهن الوتر فإنه أكثر ما روي أن
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى بها من الليل (2) والأكياس يأخذون أوقاتهم من
أول الليل والأقوياء من آخره والحزم التقديم فإنه ربما لا يستيقظ أو يثقل
عليه القيام إلا إذا صار ذلك عادة له  فآخر الليل أفضل ثم ليقرأ في هذه
الصلاة قدر ثلثمائة آية من السور المخصوصة التي كان النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم يكثر قراءتها مثل يس وسجدة لقمان وسورة الدخان وتبارك الملك والزمر
والواقعة (3) فإن لم يصل فلا يدع قراءة هذه السور أو بعضها PageV01P341
قبل النوم فقد روي في ثلاث أحاديث ما كان يقرؤه رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم في كل ليلة أشهرها السجدة وتبارك الملك (1) والزمر والواقعة وفي رواية
الزمر وبني إسرائيل (2) وكان العلماء يجعلونها ستا فيزيدون سبح اسم ربك
الأعلى إذ في الخبر أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يحب سبح اسم ربك الأعلى
وكان يقرأ في ثلاث ركعات الوتر ثلاث سور سبح اسم ربك الأعلى (3) وقل يا
أيها الكافرون والإخلاص (4) فإذا فرغ قال سبحان الملك القدوس ثلاث مرات
الثالث الوتر وليوتر قبل النوم إن لم يكن عادته القيام قال أبو هريرة رضي
الله عنه أوصاني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن لا أنام إلا على وتر (5)
وإن كان معتادا صلاة الليل فالتأخير أفضل قال صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاة
الليل مثنى مثنى فإذا خفت الصبح فأوتر بركعة (6) وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها
أوتر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أول الليل وأوسطه وآخره وانتهى وتره إلى
السحر (7) وقال علي رضي الله عنه الوتر على ثلاثة أنحاء إن شئت أوترت أول
الليل ثم صليت ركعتين ركعتين يعني أنه يصير وترا بما مضى وإن شئت أوترت
بركعة فإذا استيقظت شفعت إليها أخرى ثم أوترت من آخر الليل وإن شئت أخرت
الوتر ليكون آخر صلاتك هذا ما روي عنه والطريق الأول والثالث لا بأس به
وأما نقض الوتر فقد صح فيه نهي فلا ينبغي أن ينقض (8) وروي مطلقا أنه صلى
الله عليه وسلم قال لا وتران في ليلة (9) ولمن يتردد في استيقاظه تلطف
استحسنه بعض العلماء وهو أن يصلي بعد الوتر ركعتين جالسا على فراشه عند
النوم كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يزحف إلى فراشه ويصليهما ويقرأ
فيهما إذا زلزلت وألهاكم (10) لما فيهما من التحذير والوعيد وفي رواية قل
يا أيها الكافرون لما فيها من التبرئة وإفراد العبادة لله تعالى فقيل إن
استيقظ قامتا مقام ركعة واحدة وكان له أن يوتر بواحدة في آخر صلاة الليل
وكأنه صار ما مضى شفعا بهما وحسن استئناف الوتر واستحسن هذا أبو طالب المكي
وقال فيه ثلاثة أعمال قصر الأمل وتحصيل الوتر والوتر آخر الليل وهو كما
PageV01P342
ذكره لكن ربما يخطر أنهما لو شفعتا ما مضى لكان كذلك وإن لم يستيقظ وأبطل
وتره الأول فكونه شافعا إن استيقظ غير مشفع إن نام فبه نظر إلا أن يصح من
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إيتاره قبلهما وإعادته الوتر في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-د (w-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes arrival at water (wurūd), a place of watering, and by extension a set portion or appointed round of recitation or devotion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, wird is the fixed liturgical portion assigned to the servant for a given time, marking the stations of nightly worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "arriving at water"; metaphorically extended to the "arrival" of the servant at his appointed devotional station, as one arrives at a watering-hole.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The five awrād are enumerated with coordinating structure (الأول، الثاني...) each introduced as a distinct syntactic unit, with conditions and subdivisions attached via conditional clauses (إذا، فإن).
chapters.translation:
I say: Now I shall expound the vigils of the night, and they are five.

**The First Vigil:** When the sun has set, one prays the sunset prayer (al-Maghrib) and occupies himself in reviving the interval between the two evening prayers. The end of this vigil is at the disappearance of the twilight (al-shafaq) — I mean the redness by whose disappearance the time of the night prayer (al-ʿAtamah) enters. Allah the Exalted has sworn by it, saying: {«فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ»} ("Nay, I swear by the twilight"). The prayer within it is the "night-rising" (nāshiʾat al-layl), because it is the first arising of its hours, and it is one of the "hours" (ānāʾ) mentioned in His saying: {«وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ»} ("And in the hours of the night, glorify Him"). It is the prayer of the penitent (ṣalāt al-awwābīn), and it is what is meant by His saying: {«تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ»} ("Their sides forsake their beds"). This was related from al-Ḥasan, and Ibn Abī Ziyād attributed it to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) — that he was asked about this verse, and he said: "It is the prayer between the two evening prayers." Then he said: "Upon you is the prayer between the two evening prayers, for it erases the idle talk of the day and refines its end." (1) "Al-malāghāt" is the plural of "malghāh," derived from "laghw" (idle speech). Anas (may Allah have mercy on him) was asked about one who sleeps between the two evening prayers, and he said: "Do not do so, for it is the hour meant by His saying: {«تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ»}." The virtue of reviving the interval between the two evening prayers will come in the second book. The arrangement of this vigil is: after the sunset prayer, one prays two units (rakʿatayn) first, reciting in them "Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn" and "Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad," and he prays them immediately after Maghrib without any intervening speech or occupation. Then he prays four units, prolonging them. Then he prays until the disappearance of the twilight whatever is facilitated for him. If the mosque is near his home, there is no harm in praying them in his house, unless he has resolved upon seclusion (ʿukūf) in the mosque. If he resolves upon seclusion in waiting for the night prayer, that is more virtuous, provided he is safe from ostentation (taṣannuʿ) and hypocrisy (riyāʾ).

**The Second Vigil:** It enters with the entry of the time of the final night prayer (al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah) until the limit of people's sleeping — which is the first firm establishment of darkness. Allah the Exalted has sworn by it, saying: {«وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ»} ("And by the night and what it gathers") — i.e., what it collects of its darkness — and saying: {«إِلَىٰ غَسَقِ اللَّيْلِ»} ("until the darkness of the night"). There the night darkens (yaghsaqu) and its darkness gathers fully (tastawsiq). The arrangement of this vigil is by observing three matters. **The first:** that one prays, besides the obligatory night prayer, ten units: four before the obligatory prayer, reviving the interval between the two calls to prayer (adhān and iqāmah), and six after the obligatory prayer — two units, then four. In them he recites from the Qurʾān the specific verses, such as the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah, Āyat al-Kursī, the beginning of Sūrat al-Ḥadīd, the end of Sūrat al-Ḥashr, and others. **The second:** that he prays thirteen units, the last of which is the witr — for this is the most that has been related that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed of the night. (2) The astute take their time from the beginning of the night, and the strong from its end. But prudence (al-ḥazm) is to advance it, for perhaps one will not wake up, or standing will become burdensome upon him — unless it has become a habit for him, in which case the end of the night is more virtuous. Then let him recite in this prayer the measure of three hundred verses from the specific sūrahs that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite frequently, such as Yā Sīn, Sajdah Luqmān, Sūrat al-Dukhān, Tabāraka al-Mulk, al-Zumar, and al-Wāqiʿah. (3) If he does not pray, let him not abandon reciting these sūrahs or some of them before sleep — for it has been related in three ḥadīths what the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to recite every night, the most famous of which are al-Sajdah and Tabāraka al-Mulk, (1) and al-Zumar and al-Wāqiʿah; and in one narration, al-Zumar and Banī Isrāʾīl. (2) The scholars used to make them six, adding "Sabbiḥ isma rabbika al-aʿlā," for in the report it is stated that he (peace and blessings be upon him) loved "Sabbiḥ isma rabbika al-aʿlā." He used to recite in the three units of the witr three sūrahs: "Sabbiḥ isma rabbika al-aʿlā," (3) "Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn," and "al-Ikhlāṣ." (4) When he finished, he would say: "Subḥāna al-Malik al-Quddūs" three times. **The third:** the witr. Let him perform the witr before sleep if standing at night is not his habit. Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) advised me not to sleep except upon a witr." (5) If he is accustomed to night prayer, then delaying is more virtuous. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The night prayer is two by two; if you fear the dawn, then pray witr with one unit." (6) ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) performed the witr at the beginning of the night, its middle, and its end, and his witr concluded at the dawn (saḥar)." (7) ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The witr is of three kinds: if you wish, you perform the witr at the beginning of the night, then pray two by two — meaning it becomes a witr by what has passed; if you wish, you perform the witr with one unit, and when you wake you add another to it (shaffaʿta), then perform the witr at the end of the night; and if you wish, you delay the witr so that it is the last of your prayer." This is what has been related from him. The first and third ways are permissible. As for breaking the witr (naqḍ al-witr), a prohibition has been authentically established concerning it, so one should not break it. (8) It has been related absolutely that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There are no two witrs in one night." (9) For one who is uncertain about waking up, there is a subtle device that some scholars deemed good: that he prays after the witr two units sitting on his bed at the time of sleep. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to crawl to his bed and pray them, reciting in them "Idhā zulzilat" and "Alhākum" (10) — for what they contain of warning and threat. In another narration, "Qul yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn" — for what it contains of disavowal (tabarruʾ) and the exclusive devotion of worship to Allah the Exalted. It is said: if he wakes up, they stand in the place of one unit, and he may perform the witr with one unit at the end of his night prayer — as if what has passed becomes an even number (shafʿ) by them, and the renewal of the witr is good. Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī deemed this good and said: "In it are three deeds: shortening of hope, securing the witr, and the witr at the end of the night." It is as he mentioned. But perhaps it may occur to one that if they make what has passed an even number, it would be so — yet if he does not wake up and his first witr is nullified, then its being an even-maker if he wakes is not an even-maker if he sleeps. There is some consideration in this — unless it is authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) that he performed the witr before them and then repeated the witr, from which it is understood that the two units are, by their form, an even-maker (shafʿ), and by their meaning, a witr — so they count as a witr if he does not wake, and as an even-maker if he wakes.

Then it is recommended after the salutation of the witr to say: "Subḥāna al-Malik al-Quddūs, Rabbi al-malāʾikati wa al-rūḥ, jallalta al-samāwāti wa al-arḍa bil-ʿaẓamah wa al-jabarūt, wa taʿazzazta bil-qudrah, wa qaharta al-ʿibāda bil-mawt." It has been related that he (peace and blessings be upon him) did not die until most of his prayer was sitting, except the obligatory. (1) And he said to the one sitting: "Half the reward of the standing," and to the one lying: "Half the reward of the sitting." (2) This indicates the validity of supererogatory prayer at all times.

**The Third Vigil:** Sleep. There is no harm in counting this among the vigils, for when its etiquettes are observed, it is reckoned as worship. It has been said: when a servant sleeps in a state of purity and mentions Allah the Exalted, he is recorded as praying until he wakes, and an angel enters into his garment (shiʿār); if he stirs in his sleep and mentions Allah, the angel prays for him and Allah seeks forgiveness for him. (3) In the report: "If one sleeps in purity, his soul is raised to the Throne" (4) — this is weak. (5) The ḥadīth "The sleep of the scholar is worship, and his breath is glorification" — I say: what is well-known concerning it is the fasting person, not the scholar; and it has preceded in the book of fasting. (6) The ḥadīth: Muʿādh said to Abū Mūsā: "How do you do with night prayer?" He said: "I stand the entire night, not sleeping any of it, and I recite the Qurʾān in a measured manner (atafawwaqu al-Qurʾāna tafawwuqan)." Muʿādh said: "But I sleep, then I stand, and I reckon in my sleep what I reckon in my standing." This was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he said: "Muʿādh is more discerning (afqah) than you." Agreed upon, in a similar form from the ḥadīth of Abū Saʿīd — but in it there is no mention that they mentioned that to the Prophet, nor his saying "Muʿādh is more discerning than you"; rather, al-Ṭabarānī added: "And Muʿādh was more virtuous than him." (7) The ḥadīth: "When a servant sleeps in purity, his soul ascends to the Throne, and his vision is true" — this has preceded. (8) The ḥadīth: "He used to use the toothstick (siwāk) every night multiple times, at every sleep and at every waking from it" — this has preceded in the book of purification. (9) The ḥadīth: "Whoever comes to his bed intending to stand for prayer at night, and his eyes overcome him until morning, it is written for him what he intended, and his sleep is a charity (ṣadaqah) from Allah upon him" — related by al-Nasāʾī and Ibn Mājah from the ḥadīth of Abū al-Dardāʾ. (10) **The third:** that one who has a will (waṣiyyah) should not spend the night except with his will written at his head — for he is not safe from being seized (al-qabḍ) in sleep. For whoever dies without a will is not permitted to speak in the Barzakh until the Day of Resurrection; the dead visit one another and converse, while he does not speak, and some of them say to others: "This poor one died without a will." This is recommended out of fear of sudden death (mawt al-fajʾah), and sudden death is a relief — except for one who is not prepared for death, being burdened with grievances (maẓālim) upon his back. **The fourth:** that he sleeps repentant from every sin, with a sound heart toward all Muslims, not whispering to himself any injustice against anyone, nor resolving upon disobedience if he wakes. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever retires to his bed not intending injustice against anyone, nor bearing rancor against anyone, is forgiven for what he has committed." (1) **The fifth:** that he does not indulge in the softness of smooth bedding, but rather abandons it or is moderate in it. Some of the Salaf disliked preparing the bed for sleep and considered it affectation (takalluf). The people of the Suffah placed no barrier between themselves and the earth, saying: "From it we were created, and to it we shall return," and they considered that more softening for their hearts and more fitting for the humility of their souls. For one whose soul does not permit that, let him be moderate. **The sixth:** that he does not sleep unless sleep overcomes him, nor does he labor to bring it on — except when he intends thereby to aid himself in standing at the end of the night. For their sleep was by overcoming (ghalabah), their eating by need (fāqah), and their speech by necessity. Therefore they were described as: {«كَانُوا قَلِيلًا مِّنَ اللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ»} ("They used to sleep but little of the night"). If sleep overcomes one such that he misses prayer and remembrance and becomes unable to know what he says, let him sleep until he comprehends what he says. Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him) disliked sleeping sitting. In the report: "Do not contend with the night (lā tukābidū al-layl)." (2) It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): "So-and-so prays at night, and when sleep overcomes her, she hangs onto a rope." He forbade that and said: "Let each of you pray of the night what is facilitated for him; when sleep overcomes him, let him sleep." (3) He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Take upon yourselves of deeds what you can bear, for Allah will not tire until you tire." (4) He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The best of this religion is the most lenient of it." (5) It was said to him: "So-and-so prays and does not sleep, and fasts and does not break his fast." He said: "But I pray and sleep, and I fast and break my fast. This is my Sunnah; whoever turns away from it is not of me." (6) He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not be harsh upon this religion, for it is firm (matīn); whoever contends with it will be overcome by it. So do not make the worship of Allah hateful to your soul." (7) **The seventh:** that he sleeps facing the qiblah. Facing is of two kinds: one is the facing of the dying person (muḥtaḍar) — lying on his back, his facing being that his face and the soles of his feet are toward the qiblah; the second is the facing of the grave (laḥd) — sleeping on his side, his face toward it along with the front of his body, when he sleeps on his right side. **The eighth:** supplication at sleep, saying: "Bismika rabbī waḍaʿtu jambī, wa bismika arfaʿuhu" — to the end of the transmitted supplications which we have presented in the Book of Supplications. (8) It is recommended to recite the specific verses, such as Āyat al-Kursī, the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and others, and His saying: {«وَإِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ ۖ لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ»} to His saying: {«لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ»} ("And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him... for a people who reason"). It is said that whoever recites it at sleep, Allah preserves the Qurʾān for him and he does not forget it. And let him recite from Sūrat al-Aʿrāf this verse: {«إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ»} to His saying: {«قَرِيبٌ مِّنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ»} ("Indeed, your Lord is Allah who created the heavens and the earth in six days... near to the doers of good"). And the end of Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl: "Qul idʿū Allāha" — the two verses — for an angel enters into his garment entrusted with his protection, seeking forgiveness for him. And let him recite the two muʿawwidhatān (al-Falaq and al-Nās), blowing into his hands and wiping his face and the rest of his body with them — likewise it has been related of the action of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). (1) And let him recite ten from the beginning of Sūrat al-Kahf and ten from its end. These verses are for waking for night prayer. ʿAlī (may Allah honor his face) used to say: "I do not think that a man of complete intellect sleeps before reciting the two verses from the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah." And let him say twenty-five times: "Subḥāna Allāh, wa al-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa Allāhu akbar" — so that the total of these four phrases is one hundred. **The ninth:** that he reflects at sleep that sleep is a kind of death, and waking is a kind of resurrection. Allah the Exalted said: {«اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا»} ("Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died in their sleep"), and He said: {«وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُم بِاللَّيْلِ»} ("And it is He who takes you by night") — so He called it "taking" (tawaffī). Just as the waking person has unveiled to him sights that do not correspond to his states in sleep, so too the resurrected one sees what has never occurred to his mind nor been perceived by his senses. The likeness of sleep between life and death is like the Barzakh between this world and the Hereafter. Luqmān said to his son: "O my son, if you doubt death, then do not sleep — for just as you sleep, so shall you die. And if you doubt the resurrection, then do not wake — for just as you wake after your sleep, so shall you be raised after your death." Kaʿb al-Aḥbār said: "When you sleep, lie on your right side and face the qiblah with your face, for it is a death." ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "The last thing the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say when sleeping, placing his cheek on his right hand, while he thought he would die that very night, was: 'Allāhumma Rabba al-samāwāti al-sabʿi wa Rabba al-ʿarshi al-ʿaẓīm, Rabbanā wa Rabba kulli shayʾin wa malīkahu' (2) — the supplication to its end, as we have mentioned in the Book of Supplications." It is incumbent upon the servant to examine three things at his sleep: upon what he sleeps, and what dominates him — the love of Allah the Exalted and the love of meeting Him, or the love of this world. And let him be certain that he is taken (yutawaffā) upon what dominates him, and that he is resurrected upon what he is taken upon — for a man is with whom he loves and with what he loves.

**The Tenth:** supplication upon waking. Let him say in his wakings and turnings, whenever he wakes, what the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say: "Lā ilāha illā Allāhu al-wāḥidu al-qahhār, Rabbu al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa mā baynahumā, al-ʿazīzu al-ghaffār." (3) And let him strive that the last thing to pass over his heart at sleep is the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, and the first thing to return to his heart upon waking is the remembrance of Allah the Exalted — for that is the sign of love. Nothing accompanies the heart in these two states except what dominates it, so let him test his heart by this — for it is a sign that unveils what is within the heart. These remembrances are recommended only to draw the heart to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted. When he wakes to rise, let him say: "Al-ḥamdu lillāhi alladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhi al-nushūr" — to the end of the supplications of waking we have presented.

**The Fourth Vigil:** It enters with the passing of the first half of the night, until there remains of the night its sixth. At that time the servant rises for the tahajjud — for the name "tahajjud" is specific to what comes after hujūd and hujūʿ, which is sleep. This is the middle of the night, resembling the vigil after the zenith (zawāl), which is the middle of the day. By it Allah the Exalted swore, saying: {«وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ»} ("And by the night when it covers") — i.e., when it becomes still; its stillness is its quieting (hudūʾ) at this time, so no eye remains sleeping except the Living, the Self-Subsistent, whom neither slumber nor sleep overtakes. It was also said: "Idhā sajā" — when it extends and lengthens; and it was said: when it darkens. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: "Which part of the night is most heard?" He said: "The middle of the night (jawf al-layl)." (4) Dāwūd (peace be upon him) said: "My God, I love to worship You — which time is best?" Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "O Dāwūd, do not stand at the beginning of the night nor its end — for whoever stands at its beginning sleeps at its end, and whoever stands at its end does not stand at its beginning. But stand in the middle of the night, so that you are alone with Me and I am alone with you, and raise to Me your needs." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked: "Which part of the night is most virtuous?" He said: "The latter half of the night (niṣf al-layl al-ghābir)" (1) — meaning the remaining. Concerning the end of the night, reports have come of the Throne's vibration, the spreading of winds from the gardens of ʿAdn, the descent of the Almighty (al-Jabbār) to the lowest heaven, (2) and other such reports. The arrangement of this vigil: after finishing the supplications of waking, he performs ablution (wuḍūʾ) as has preceded, with its Sunnahs, etiquettes, and supplications. Then he proceeds to his prayer-place and stands facing the qiblah, saying: "Allāhu akbaru kabīran, wa al-ḥamdu lillāhi kathīran, wa subḥāna Allāhi bukratan wa aṣīlā." Then let him glorify (subbiḥ) ten times, praise (aḥmad) ten times, declare His oneness (hallil) ten times, and say: "Allāhu akbaru dhū al-malakūti wa al-jabarūti wa al-kibriyāʾi wa al-ʿaẓamati wa al-jalāli wa al-qudrah." And let him say these words, for they are transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) in his rising for the tahajjud: "Allāhumma laka al-ḥamdu anta nūru al-samāwāti wa al-arḍ, wa laka al-ḥamdu anta bahāʾu al-samāwāti wa al-arḍ, wa laka al-ḥamdu anta Rabbu al-samāwāti wa al-arḍ, wa laka al-ḥamdu anta qayyūmu al-samāwāti wa al-arḍi wa man fīhinna wa man ʿalayhinna. Anta al-ḥaqqu wa minka al-ḥaqqu wa liqāʾuka ḥaqqun wa al-jannatu ḥaqqun wa al-nāru ḥaqqun wa al-nushūru ḥaqqun wa al-nabiyyūna ḥaqqun wa Muḥammadun ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa sallama ḥaqqun. Allāhumma laka aslamtu wa bika āmantu wa ʿalayka tawakkaltu wa ilayka anabtu wa bika khāṣamtu wa ilayka ḥākamtu, fa-ghfir lī mā qaddamtu wa mā akhkhartu wa mā asrartu wa mā aʿlantu wa asraftu. Anta al-muqaddimu wa anta al-muʾakhkhiru, lā ilāha illā anta." (3) "Allāhumma āti nafsī taqwāhā wa zakkihā anta khayru man zakkāhā, anta waliyyuhā wa mawlāhā." (4) "Allāhumma ihdinī li-aḥsani al-aʿmāli lā yahdī li-aḥsanihā illā anta, wa iṣrif ʿannī sayyiʾahā lā yaṣrifu ʿannī sayyiʾahā illā anta." (5) "Asʾaluka masʾalata al-bāʾisi al-miskīni wa adʿūka duʿāʾa al-muftaqiri al-dhalīli, fa-lā tajʿalnī bi-duʿāʾika Rabbi shaqiyyan, wa kun bī raʾūfan raḥīman, yā khayra al-masʾūlīna wa akrama al-muʿṭīna." (6) ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "When he (peace and blessings be upon him) rose at night, he opened his prayer saying: 'Allāhumma Rabba Jibrīla wa Mīkāʾīla wa Isrāfīl, Fāṭira al-samāwāti wa al-arḍ, ʿĀlima al-ghaybi wa al-shahādah, anta taḥkumu bayna ʿibādika fīmā kānū fīhi yakhtalifūn. Ihdinī limā ikhtulifa fīhi mina al-ḥaqqi bi-idhnika, innaka tahdī man tashāʾu ilā ṣirāṭin mustaqīm.'" (7) Then he opens the prayer and prays two light units, then prays two by two whatever is facilitated for him, and concludes with the witr if he has not already prayed it. It is recommended to separate between the two prayers at his salutation with one hundred glorifications (tasbīḥāt) to rest and increase his vigor for prayer. It has been authentically established concerning the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) that he first prayed two light units, then two long units, then two shorter than the preceding ones, then he continued shortening gradually until thirteen units. (1) ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) was asked: "Did the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) recite aloud in his night prayer or softly?" She said: "Sometimes he recited aloud, and sometimes softly." (2) He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The night prayer is two by two; if you fear the dawn, then pray witr with one unit." (3) He said: "The sunset prayer is the witr of the day's prayers, so make the witr of the night prayers." (4) The most that has been authentically established from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) concerning night prayer is thirteen units. (5) In these units he recites from his portion (wird) of the Qurʾān, or from the specific sūrahs, whatever is light upon him. This vigil is, in its ruling, close to the final sixth of the night.

**The Fifth Vigil:** The final sixth of the night — the time of the dawn (saḥar). For Allah the Exalted said: {«وَبِالْأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ»} ("And in the dawn hours they would seek forgiveness"). It is said: they prayed, because of what is in it of seeking forgiveness. It is near to the dawn (fajr), which is the time of the departure of the angels of the night and the arrival of the angels of the day. Salmān commanded his brother Abū al-Dardāʾ (may Allah be pleased with them both) with this vigil on the night he visited him (6) — in a long ḥadīth, at the end of which he said: "When night came, Abū al-Dardāʾ went to stand (for prayer), and Salmān said to him: 'Sleep.' So he slept. Then he went to stand again, and he said: 'Sleep.' So he slept. When it was near dawn, Salmān said to him: 'Rise now.' So they both rose and prayed. Then he said: 'Indeed, your soul has a right upon you, your guest has a right upon you, and your family has a right upon you — so give every possessor of a right his right.'" This was because the wife of Abū al-Dardāʾ had informed Salmān that he did not sleep at night. He said: "Then they came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and mentioned that to him, and he said: 'Salmān has spoken the truth.'" This is the fifth vigil, and in it the pre-dawn meal (saḥūr) is recommended — at the time of fearing the appearance of dawn. The function (waẓīfah) in these two vigils is prayer. When dawn breaks, the vigils of the night conclude and the vigils of the day enter. So he rises and prays the two units of the dawn (rakʿatay al-fajr) — and this is what is meant by His saying: {«وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ النُّجُومِ»} ("And in the night glorify Him, and at the setting of the stars"). Then he recites: {«شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ»} to its end. Then he says: "And I bear witness to what Allah has borne witness to for Himself, and what His angels and the people of knowledge among His creation have borne witness to. And I entrust Allah with this testimony, and it is with Allah the Exalted a deposit (wadīʿah), and I ask Him to preserve it until He takes me upon it. Allāhumma, remove from me by it a burden (wizr), and make it for me with You a treasure (dhukhran), and preserve it for

chapters.title_en: The Differentiation of Liturgies (Awrād) According to the Diversity of Spiritual States
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان اختلاف الأوراد باختلاف الأحوال

اعلم أن المريد لحرث الآخرة السالك لطريقها لا يخلو عن ستة أحوال فإنه
إما عابد وإما عالم وإما متعلم وإما وال وإما محترف وإما موحد مستغرق
بالواحد الصمد عن غيره الأول العابد وهو المتجرد للعبادة الذي لا شغل له
غيرها أصلا ولو ترك العبادة لجلس بطالا فترتيب أوراده ما ذكرناه نعم لا
يبعد أن تختلف وظائفه بأن يستغرق أكثر أوقاته إما في الصلاة أو القراءة أو
في التسبيحات فقد كان في الصحابة رضي الله عنهم من ورده في اليوم اثنا عشر
ألف تسبيحة وكان فيهم من ورده ثلاثون ألفا وكان فيهم من ورده ثلثمائة ركعة
إلى ستمائة وإلى ألف ركعة وأقل ما نقل في أورادهم من الصلاة مائة ركعة في
اليوم والليلة وكان بعضهم أكثر ورده القرآن وكان يختم الواحد منهم في اليوم
مرة وروى مرتين عن بعضهم وكان بعضهم يقضي اليوم أو الليل  في التفكر في آية
واحدة يرددها وكان كرز بن وبرة مقيما بمكة فكان يطوف في كل يوم سبعين
أسبوعا وفي كل ليلة سبعين أسبوعا وكان مع ذلك يختم القرآن في اليوم والليلة
مرتين فحسب ذلك فكان عشرة فراسخ ويكون مع كل أسبوع ركعتان فهو مائتان
وثمانون ركعة وختمتان وعشرة فراسخ فإن قلت فما الأولى أن يصرف إليه أكثر
الأوقات من هذه الأوراد فاعلم أن قراءة القرآن في الصلاة قائما مع التدبر
يجمع الجميع ولكن ربما تعسر المواظبة عليه فالأفضل يختلف باختلاف حال الشخص
ومقصود الأوراد تزكية القلب وتطهيره وتحليته بذكر الله تعالى وإيناسه به
فلينظر المريد إلى قلبه فما يراه أشد تأثيرا فيه فليواظب عليه فإذا أحس
بملالة منه فلينتقل إلى غيره ولذلك نرى الأصوب لأكثر الخلق توزيع هذه
الخيرات المختلفة على الأوقات كما سبق والانتقال فيها من نوع إلى نوع لأن
الملال هو الغالب على الطبع وأحوال الشخص الواحد في ذلك أيضا تختلف ولكن
إذا فهم فقه الأوراد وسرها فليتبع المعنى فإن سمع تسبيحة مثلا وأحس لها
بوقع قلبه فليواظب على تكرارها ما دام يجد لها وقعا وقد روي عن إبراهيم بن
أدهم عن بعض الأبدال أنه قام ذات ليلة يصلي على شاطىء البحر فسمع صوتا
عاليا بالتسبيح ولم ير أحدا فقال من أنت أسمع صوتك ولا أرى شخصك فقال أنا
ملك من الملائكة موكل بهذا البحر أسبح الله تعالى بهذا التسبيح منذ خلقت
قلت فما اسمك قال مهلهيائيل قلت فما ثواب من قاله قال من قاله مائة مرة لم
يمت حتى يرى مقعده من الجنة أو يرى له والتسبيح هو قوله سبحان الله العلي
الديان سبحان الله الشديد الأركان سبحان من يذهب بالليل ويأتي بالنهار
سبحان من لا يشغله شأن عن شأن سبحان الله الحنان المنان سبحان الله المسبح
في كل مكان فهذا وأمثاله إذا سمعه المريد ووجد له في قلبه وقعا فليلازمه
وأيا ما وجد القلب عنده وفتح له فيه خير فليواظب عليه الثاني العالم الذي
ينفع  الناس بعلمه في فتوى أو تدريس أو تصنيف فترتيبه الأوراد يخالف ترتيب
العابد فإنه يحتاج إلى المطالعة للكتب وإلى التصنيف والإفادة ويحتاج إلى
مدة لها لا محالة فإن أمكنه استغراق الأوقات فيه فهو أفضل ما يشتغل
PageV01P348
به بعد المكتوبات ورواتبها ويدل على ذلك جميع ما ذكرناه في فضيلة التعليم
والتعلم في كتاب العلم وكيف لا يكون كذلك وفي العلم المواظبة على ذكر الله
تعالى وتأمل ما قال الله تعالى وقال رسوله وفيه منفعة الخلق وهدايتهم إلى
طريق الآخرة ورب مسألة واحدة يتعلمها المتعلم فيصلح بها عبادة عمره ولو لم
يتعلمها لكان سعيه ضائعا وإنما نعني بالعلم المقدم على العبادة العلم الذي
يرغب الناس في الآخرة ويزهدهم في الدنيا أو العلم الذي يعينهم على سلوك
طريق الآخرة إذا تعلموه على قصد الاستعانة به على السلوك دون العلوم التي
تزيد بها الرغبة في المال والجاه وقبول الخلق والأولى بالعالم أن يقسم
أوقاته أيضا فإن استغراق الأوقات في ترتيب العلم لا يحتمله الطبع فينبغي أن
يخصص ما بعد الصبح إلى طلوع الشمس بالأذكار والأوراد كما ذكرناه في الورد
الأول وبعد الطلوع إلى ضحوة النهار في الإفادة والتعليم إن كان عنده من
يستفيد علما لأجل الآخرة وإن لم يكن فيصرفه إلى الفكر ويتفكر فيما يشكل
عليه من علوم الدين فإن صفاء القلب بعد الفراغ من الذكر وقبل الاشتغال
بهموم الدنيا يعين على التفطن للمشكلات ومن ضحوة النهار إلى العصر للتصنيف
والمطالعة لا يتركها إلا في وقت أكل وطهارة ومكتوبة وقيلولة خفيفة إن طال
النهار ومن العصر إلى الاصفرار يشتغل بسماع ما يقرأ بين يديه من تفسير أو
حديث أو علم نافع ومن الاصفرار إلى الغروب يشتغل بالذكر والاستغفار
والتسبيح فيكون ورده الأول قبل طلوع الشمس في عمل اللسان وورده الثاني في
عمل القلب بالفكر إلى الضحوة وورده الثالث إلى العصر في عمل العين واليد
بالمطالعة والكتابة وورده الرابع بعد العصر في عمل السمع ليروح فيه العين
واليد فإن المطالعة والكتابة بعد العصر ربما أضرا  بالعين وعند الاصفرار
يعود إلى ذكر ا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ر-د (w-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes arriving at water, a watering-place, or the path leading to it; hence a portion of recitation or devotion regularly undertaken.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, the wird is the appointed portion of remembrance and worship that leads the heart to its source of life—God—just as water sustains the body.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage refers to the place of water; metaphorical usage (majāz) extends to the regular devotional portion that quenches the soul's thirst.
- Root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be empty, vacant, or free from occupation; a state of being unoccupied.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The spiritual state of the seeker who is free from worldly preoccupations, enabling exclusive focus on worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal emptiness of a vessel; metaphorical emptiness of the heart from all save God.
- Root: م-ل-ل (m-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Weariness, boredom, or fatigue that overtakes one in a sustained activity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The spiritual danger of monotony in worship, which the wise devotee must preempt by varying his liturgies.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical fatigue; metaphorical spiritual listlessness that undermines devotion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional sentences (e.g., "if you say... know that") and exceptive clauses to delineate the varying rulings for each category of devotee, requiring careful parsing of the protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the seeker of the harvest of the Hereafter, the traveler upon its path, is not free from six states, for he is either a worshiper, or a scholar, or a student, or a ruler, or a craftsman, or a unifier (muwaḥḥid) wholly absorbed in the One, the Eternal (al-Ṣamad), to the exclusion of all else.

The first is the worshiper—he who has devoted himself exclusively to worship, having no occupation other than it at all; were he to abandon worship, he would sit idle. The arrangement of his liturgies (awrād) is as we have already mentioned. Indeed, it is not improbable that his functions vary, such that he devotes the greater part of his hours either to prayer, or to recitation, or to glorifications (tasbīḥāt). For among the Companions—may God be pleased with them—there was one whose wird was twelve thousand glorifications daily, and among them was one whose wird was thirty thousand, and among them was one whose wird was three hundred rakʿahs, up to six hundred, and up to a thousand rakʿahs. The least that has been transmitted of their liturgies of prayer was one hundred rakʿahs in the day and night. Some of them made the Qurʾān their greater wird, and one of them would complete the entire recitation (khatm) once daily, and twice has been narrated of some of them. And some of them would spend the day or the night in reflection upon a single verse, repeating it. Karz ibn Warbah resided in Mecca, and he would circumambulate (ṭawāf) seventy circuits daily and seventy circuits nightly, and with that he would complete the Qurʾān twice in the day and night. Calculate that: it was ten parasangs (farāsikh), and with each circuit two rakʿahs—thus two hundred and eighty rakʿahs, two khatms, and ten parasangs.

If you say: What then is most fitting to which the greater part of one's hours should be directed among these liturgies? Know that the recitation of the Qurʾān in prayer, standing, with reflection (tadabbur), combines all of these. But perhaps continuous adherence to it is difficult. Thus the superior choice varies according to the varying state of the person. The purpose of the liturgies is the purification of the heart, its cleansing, its adornment with the remembrance of God—exalted is He—and its familiarization with Him. Let the seeker then look to his heart, and whatever he sees as most powerfully affecting it, let him adhere to it. When he senses weariness (malāl) from it, let him move to another. For this reason, we see that the most correct course for most creatures is to distribute these various goods across the hours, as has preceded, and to move among them from one type to another, because weariness dominates the natural disposition. The states of a single person also vary in this matter. But when one understands the jurisprudence (fiqh) of the liturgies and their secret, let him follow the meaning. If he hears a glorification, for example, and senses in his heart an impact (waqaʿ) from it, let him adhere to repeating it as long as he finds in it that impact.

It has been narrated from Ibrāhīm ibn Adham, from one of the substitutes (abdāl), that he stood one night praying upon the shore of the sea, and he heard a loud voice glorifying (tasbīḥ), yet saw no one. He said: "Who are you? I hear your voice but do not see your person." He replied: "I am an angel from among the angels, entrusted with this sea. I have been glorifying God—exalted is He—with this glorification since I was created." He said: "What is your name?" He said: "Mahlahāyīl." He said: "What is the reward of one who utters it?" He said: "Whoever utters it one hundred times will not die until he sees his seat in Paradise, or it is shown to him." And the glorification is his saying: "Glory be to God, the Most High, the Judge (al-Dāyān); Glory be to God, the Mighty in pillars (al-Shadīd al-arkān); Glory be to Him who takes away the night and brings the day; Glory be to Him whom no matter distracts from another matter; Glory be to God, the Tender (al-Ḥannān), the Beneficent (al-Mannān); Glory be to God, the Glorified in every place." So when the seeker hears this and its like, and finds in his heart an impact from it, let him adhere to it. And whatever he finds the heart present with, and in which good is opened to him, let him persist in it.

The second is the scholar who benefits people with his knowledge, whether in legal opinion (fatwā), teaching, or authorship. The arrangement of his liturgies differs from that of the worshiper, for he needs to study books, to author, and to impart benefit, and he needs time for that without fail. If he can devote all his hours to it, it is superior to everything he occupies himself with after the obligatory prayers (maktūbāt) and their regular supererogatory prayers (rawātib). This is indicated by all that we have mentioned concerning the virtue of teaching and learning in the Book of Knowledge. How could it not be so? For in knowledge there is continuous remembrance of God—exalted is He—and contemplation of what God—exalted is He—has said and what His Messenger said, and in it is benefit to creation and their guidance to the path of the Hereafter. Perhaps a single question that the student learns, by which he rectifies the worship of his entire life—had he not learned it, his effort would have been wasted. By knowledge given precedence over worship, we mean only that knowledge which makes people desirous of the Hereafter and ascetic in this world, or that knowledge which aids them in traversing the path of the Hereafter when they learn it with the intention of seeking aid thereby upon the path—not those sciences that increase desire for wealth, status, and the acceptance of creatures.

The more fitting course for the scholar is that he also divide his hours, for devoting all hours to the arrangement of knowledge is not borne by the natural disposition. He should therefore designate the time from dawn (ṣubḥ) until sunrise for remembrances (adhkār) and liturgies, as we mentioned in the first wird; and after sunrise until mid-morning (ḍaḥwah) for imparting benefit and teaching, if he has someone who seeks knowledge for the sake of the Hereafter. If not, let him direct it to reflection, pondering what is problematic to him among the religious sciences, for the purity of the heart after finishing the remembrance and before engaging in the cares of this world aids in grasping difficult matters. From mid-morning until mid-afternoon (ʿaṣr), let him devote himself to authorship and study, not abandoning it except at the time of eating, purification, obligatory prayer, and a light siesta (qaylūlah) if the day is long. From mid-afternoon until the yellowing of the sun (iṣfirār), let him occupy himself with listening to what is read before him of exegesis (tafsīr), ḥadīth, or beneficial knowledge. From the yellowing of the sun until sunset (ghurūb), let him occupy himself with remembrance, seeking forgiveness (istighfār), and glorification. Thus his first wird before sunrise is in the work of the tongue; his second wird until mid-morning is in the work of the heart through reflection; his third wird until mid-afternoon is in the work of the eye and hand through study and writing; and his fourth wird after mid-afternoon is in the work of the ear, so that the eye and hand may rest therein, for study and writing after mid-afternoon may harm the eye. At the yellowing of the sun, he returns to the remembrance of the tongue. Thus no part of the day is devoid of work for him through his limbs, with the presence of the heart in all of it.

As for the night, the best division therein is the division of al-Shāfiʿī—may God be pleased with him—for he divided the night into three parts: a third for study and the arrangement of knowledge, which is the first; a third for prayer, which is the middle; and a third for sleep, which is the last. This is feasible in the nights of winter; in summer, perhaps it is not bearable except if most of the sleep is during the day. This is what we deem commendable of the arrangement of the liturgies of the scholar.

The third is the student. Occupying oneself with learning is superior to occupying oneself with remembrances and supererogatory prayers (nawāfil). His ruling is the ruling of the scholar in the arrangement of liturgies, but he occupies himself with seeking benefit where the scholar occupies himself with imparting benefit, and with annotation (taʿlīq) and copying where the scholar occupies himself with authorship. He arranges his hours as we have mentioned. All that we have mentioned concerning the virtue of learning and knowledge from the Book of Knowledge indicates that this is superior. Indeed, if one is not a student in the sense of one who annotates and acquires so as to become a scholar, but rather is among the common folk, then his attendance at gatherings of remembrance (dhikr), exhortation (waʿẓ), and knowledge is superior to his occupation with the liturgies we have mentioned after dawn, after sunrise, and in the remaining hours. For in the ḥadīth of Abū Dharr—may God be pleased with him—attending a gathering of remembrance is superior to praying a thousand rakʿahs, attending a thousand funerals, and visiting a thousand sick persons. {«وَقَالَ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: إِذَا رَأَيْتُمْ رِيَاضَ الْجَنَّةِ فَارْتَعُوا فِيهَا، فَقِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللهِ، وَمَا رِيَاضُ الْجَنَّةِ؟ قَالَ: حِلَقُ الذِّكْرِ»} And Kaʿb al-Aḥbār—may God be pleased with him—said: "Were the reward of the gatherings of scholars to appear to people, they would fight over them, until every holder of authority would abandon his authority, and every merchant his market." And ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb—may God be pleased with him—said: "A man leaves his house bearing sins like the mountains of Tihāmah; when he hears the scholar, he fears, desists from his sins, and returns to his house without sin. So do not abandon the gatherings of scholars, for God—mighty and majestic is He—has not created upon the face of the earth soil more noble than the gatherings of scholars." And a man said to al-Ḥasan—may God have mercy on him—"I complain to you of the hardness of my heart." He said: "Draw it near to the gatherings of remembrance."

And ʿAmmār al-Zāhidī saw Miskīnah al-Ṭafāwiyyah in a dream—she was among those who persistently attended the circles of remembrance—and he said: "Welcome, O Miskīnah!" She said: "Alas, alas! Poverty (misknah) has gone and wealth has come." He said: "How so?" She said: "Do you ask about one to whom Paradise has been made permissible in its entirety?" He said: "And by what?" She said: "By sitting with the people of remembrance." In sum, what is dissolved from the heart of the knots of love of this world by the speech of a preacher of beautiful words and pure conduct is more noble and more beneficial than many rakʿahs performed while the heart is filled with love of this world.

The fourth is the craftsman who needs to earn for his dependents. It is not for him to neglect his dependents and devote all his hours to acts of worship. Rather, his wird at the time of his craft is attending the market and occupying himself with earning. But he should not forget the remembrance of God—exalted is He—in his craft; rather, let him adhere to glorifications, remembrances, and the recitation of the Qurʾān, for that can be combined with work. What is not feasible with work is prayer, unless he is a watchman (nāẓūr), for he is not incapable of establishing his liturgies of prayer alongside it. Then, whenever he finishes his sufficiency, he should return to the arrangement of liturgies. And if he persists in earning and gives in charity what exceeds his need, that is superior to all the liturgies we have mentioned, because acts of worship whose benefit extends to others (mutʿaddiyah) are more beneficial than those confined to oneself (lāzimah). Charity and earning upon this intention is an act of worship for him in himself, drawing him near to God—exalted is He—then benefit accrues thereby to others, the blessings of the Muslims' supplications are drawn to him, and his reward is multiplied thereby.

The fifth is the ruler, such as the imam, the judge, and one entrusted with the affairs of the Muslims. His standing for the needs of the Muslims and their interests in accordance with the Sacred Law and with the intention of sincerity is superior to the liturgies mentioned. His due is to occupy himself with the rights of the people by day, to confine himself to the obligatory prayers, and to establish the liturgies mentioned by night, as ʿUmar—may God be pleased with him—used to do, for he said: "What have I to do with sleep? If I sleep by day, I ruin the Muslims; if I sleep by night, I ruin myself." You have understood from what we have mentioned that two matters take precedence over bodily acts of worship: one is knowledge, and the other is gentleness toward the Muslims. For each of knowledge and the doing of good is itself an act and a worship that surpasses other acts of worship in that its benefit extends and its usefulness spreads; thus they are given precedence over it.

The sixth is the unifier (muwaḥḥid) wholly absorbed in the One, the Eternal, who awakens with a single concern (hamm wāḥid): he loves none but God—exalted is He—fears none but Him, expects provision from none other than Him, and looks upon nothing except that he sees God—exalted is He—therein. Whoever's rank is elevated to this degree has no need for the diversification of liturgies and their variation. Rather, his wird after the obligatory prayers is one: the presence of the heart with God—exalted is He—in every state. No matter crosses their hearts, no sound strikes their ears, and no sight appears to their eyes except that it becomes for them a lesson (ʿibrah), a reflection, and an increase. There is no mover for them and no stiller except God—exalted is He. These are those whose every state is fit to be a cause of their increase, so no act of worship is distinguished from another for them. They are those who fled to God—mighty and majestic is He—as He—exalted is He—said: {«لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللهِ»} And in them is realized His saying—exalted is He—: {«وَإِذِ اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللهَ فَأْوُوا إِلَى الْكَهْفِ يَنْشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ»} And to this is the allusion in His saying: {«إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ»} This is the utmost of the degrees of the veracious (ṣiddīqīn), and there is no reaching it except after the arrangement of liturgies and persistent adherence to them for a long time. So the seeker should not be deluded by what he has heard of this, claiming it for himself and slackening in the functions of his worship. For its sign is that no whisper (waswās) stirs in his heart, no disobedience crosses his mind, the onslaughts of terrors do not agitate him, and the enormities of occupations do not unsettle him. And how is this rank granted to everyone? Thus the arrangement of liturgies as we have mentioned is incumbent upon all.

All that we have mentioned are paths to God—exalted is He. He—exalted is He—said: {«قُلْ كُلٌّ يَعْمَلُ عَلَى شَاكِلَتِهِ فَرَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ هُوَ أَهْدَى سَبِيلًا»} So all of them are guided, and some of them are more guided than others. And in the report: "Faith is three hundred and thirty-three ways; whoever meets God—exalted is He—with the testimony (shahādah) upon one of these ways enters Paradise." And some scholars said: "Faith is three hundred and thirteen traits, corresponding to the number of the messengers; so every believer is upon one of these traits." Thus, if you ask for the path to God, then people, though their paths differ in worship, are all upon correctness: {«أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَى رَبِّهِمُ الْوَسِيلَةَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ»} They differ only in the degrees of nearness, not in its principle. And the nearest of them to God—exalted is He—is the most knowing of them of Him; and the most knowing of them of Him must necessarily be the most worshipful of them of Him, for whoever knows Him worships none other than Him.

The foundation in liturgies with respect to every class of people is persistence (mudāwamah), for the intent thereof is the transformation of inward traits, and individual acts have little effect—indeed, their effect is not even perceived. Effect is produced only by the aggregate. So when a single act does not produce a perceptible effect and is not followed quickly by a second and third, the first effect is effaced. This is like the jurist who wishes to become a jurist by nature (faqīh al-nafs): he does not become a jurist by nature except through much repetition. Were he to exert himself one night in repetition, then abandon it for a month or a week, then return and exert himself one night, this would not affect him. But were he to distribute that same amount across consecutive nights, it would affect him. For this secret, the Messenger of God—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—said: {«أَحَبُّ الْأَعْمَالِ إِلَى اللهِ أَدْوَمُهَا وَإِنْ قَلَّ»} And ʿĀʾishah—may God be pleased with her—was asked about the work of the Messenger of God—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—and she said: "His work was continuous (dīmah), and when he did an act, he would persist in it (yuthbituhu)." For this reason he—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—said: {«مَنْ عَوَّدَهُ اللهُ عِبَادَةً فَتَرَكَهَا مَلَالَةً مَقَتَهُ اللهُ»} And this was the cause of his praying after mid-afternoon (ʿaṣr), making up for the two rakʿahs from which the delegation had occupied him; thereafter he did not cease praying them after mid-afternoon, but in his house, not in the mosque, lest he be emulated therein. ʿĀʾishah and Umm Salamah—may God be pleased with them both—narrated this.

If you say: Is it permissible for another to emulate him in this, given that the time is a time of disapproval (karāhah)? Know that the three meanings we have mentioned concerning disapproval—namely, guarding against resembling the worshipers of the sun, or prostrating at the time of the appearance of the horn of Satan, or resting from worship out of fear of weariness—are not realized in his case. Thus he is not to be analogized to in this matter. And this is witnessed by his doing it in his house, so that he would not be emulated—may God's peace and blessings be upon him.

chapters.title_en: The Second Chapter on the Facilitating Causes for Night Vigil, the Nights Whose Revival is Recommended, the Virtue of Reviving the Night and the Interval Between the Two Evening Prayers, and the Method of Dividing the Night

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ي س ر (y-s-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ease, facility, readiness; the opposite of difficulty (ʿusr). Connotes a smoothing of paths and removal of impediments.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, refers to divine facilitation (taysīr) — God’s granting of capacity and inclination toward acts of worship, not mere human effort.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical ease; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual preparedness, as in "facilitating causes" (asbāb) that render the night vigil attainable.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, distribution; to allocate shares or portions.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In devotional practice, implies a deliberate, measured partitioning of time into segments for worship, reflection, and rest — a disciplined schedule.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for dividing a whole; metaphorical for organizing one’s spiritual regimen into distinct phases.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — The phrase "وفي الليالي التي يستحب إحياؤها" is coordinated via "wa" (و) with the preceding genitive noun "الأسباب," each governed by the preposition "في," maintaining parallel syntactic structure for enumerative clarity.
chapters.translation: I say: The second chapter concerns the causes that facilitate the night vigil, the nights whose revival is recommended, the virtue of reviving the night and the interval between the two evening prayers (bayn al-ʿishāʾayn), and the method of dividing the night (qismat al-layl).

||| فضيلة إحياء ما بين العشاءين

قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما روت عائشة رضي الله عنها إن أفضل
الصلوات عند الله صلاة المغرب لم يحطها عن مسافر ولا عن مقيم فتح بها فقضى
صلاة الليل وختم بها صلاة النهار فمن صلى المغرب وصلى بعدها ركعتين بنى
الله  له قصر في الجنة
الباب الثاني في الأسباب الميسرة لقيام الليل حديث عائشة إن أفضل
الصلاة عند الله صلاة المغرب لم يحطها عن مسافر ولا عن مقيم الحديث رواه
أبو الوليد يونس بن عبيد الله الصفار في كتاب الصلاة ورواه الطبراني في
الأوسط مختصرا وإسناده ضعيف (5) حديث أم سلمة عن أبي هريرة من صلى ست ركعات
بعد المغرب عدلت له عبادة سنة أو كأنه صلى ليلة القدر أخرجه الترمذي وابن
ماجه بلفظ اثنتي عشرة سنة وضعفه الترمذي وأما قوله كأنه صلى ليلة القدر فهو
من قول كعب الأحبار كما رواه أبو الوليد الصفار ولأبي منصور الديلمي في
مسند الفردوس من حديث ابن عباس من صلى أربع ركعات بعد المغرب قبل أن يكلم
أحدا وضعت له في عليين وكان كمن أدرك ليلة القدر في المسجد الأقصى وسنده
ضعيف // وعن سعيد بن جبير عن ثوبان PageV01P351
قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من عكف نفسه فيما بين المغرب
والعشاء في مسجد جماعة لم يتكلم إلا بصلاة أو قرآن كان حقا على الله أن
يبني له قصرين في الجنة مسيرة كل قصر منهما مائة عام ويغرس له بينهما غراسا
لو طافه أهل الدنيا لوسعهم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم من ركع عشر ركعات
ما بين المغرب والعشاء بنى الله له قصرا في الجنة فقال عمر رضي الله عنه
إذا تكثر قصورنا يا رسول الله فقال الله أكثر وأفضل أو قال أطيب (2) وعن
أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صلى
المغرب في جماعة ثم صلى بعدها ركعتين ولم يتكلم بشيء فيما بين ذلك من أمر
الدنيا ويقرأ في الركعة الأولى فاتحة الكتاب وعشر آيات من أول سورة البقرة
وآيتين من وسطها وإلهكم إله واحد لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم إن في خلق
السموات والأرض إلى آخر الآية وقل هو الله أحد خمس عشرة مرة ثم يركع ويسجد
فإذا قام في الركعة الثانية قرأ  فاتحة الكتاب وآية الكرسي وآيتين بعدها إلى
قوله أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون وثلاث آيات من آخر سورة البقرة من
قوله لله ما في السموات وما في الأرض إلى آخرها وقل هو الله أحد خمس عشرة
مرة (3) وصف من ثوابه في الحديث ما يخرج عن الحصر وقال كرز بن وبرة وهو من
الأبدال قلت للخضر عليه السلام علمني شيئا أعمله في كل ليلة فقال إذا صليت
المغرب فقم إلى وقت صلاة العشاء مصليا من غير أن تكلم أحدا وأقبل على صلاتك
التي أنت فيها وسلم من كل ركعتين واقرأ في كل ركعة فاتحة الكتاب مرة وقل هو
الله أحد ثلاثا فإن فرغت من صلاتك انصرف إلى منزلك ولا تكلم أحدا وصل
ركعتين واقرأ فاتحة الكتاب وقل هو الله أحد سبع مرات في كل ركعة ثم اسجد
بعد تسليمك واستغفر الله تعالى سبع مرات وقل سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله
إلا الله والله أكبر ولا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم سبع مرات ثم
ارفع رأسك من السجود واستو جالسا وارفع يديك وقل يا حي يا قيوم يا ذا
الجلال والإكرام يا إله الأولين والآخرين يا رحمن الدنيا والآخرة ورحيمهما
يا رب يا رب يا رب يا الله يا الله يا الله ثم قم وأنت رافع يديك وادع بهذا
الدعاء ثم نم حيث شئت مستقبل القبلة على يمينك وصل على النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم وأدم الصلاة عليه حتى يذهب بك النوم فقلت له أحب أن تعلمني ممن سمعت
هذا فقال إني حضرت محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث علم هذا الدعاء وأوحي إليه
به فكنت عنده وكان ذلك بمحضر مني فتعلمته ممن علمه إياه (4) ويقال إن هذا
الدعاء وهذه الصلاة من داوم عليهما بحسن يقين وصدق نية رأى رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم في منامه قبل أن يخرج من الدنيا وقد فعل ذلك بعض الناس فرأى
أنه أدخل الجنة ورأى فيها الأنبياء ورأى فيها رسول الله  صلى الله عليه وسلم
وكلمه وعلمه وعلى الجملة ما ورد في فضل إحياء ما بين العشاءين كثير حتى قيل
لعبيد الله مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هل كان رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم يأمر بصلاة غير المكتوبة قال ما بين المغرب والعشاء (5) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم من صلى ما بين المغرب والعشاء تلك PageV01P352
صلاة الأوابين (1) وقال الأسود ما أتيت ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه في هذا
الوقت إلا ورأيته يصلي فسألته فقال نعم هي ساعة الغفلة وكان أنس رضي الله
عنه يواظب عليها ويقول هي ناشئة الليل ويقول فيها نزل قوله تعالى {تتجافى
جنوبهم عن المضاجع} وقال أحمد بن أبي الحواري قلت لأبي سليمان الداراني
أصوم النهار وأتعشى بين المغرب والعشاء أحب إليك أو أفطر بالنهار وأحيي ما
بينهما فقال اجمع بينهما فقلت إن لم يتيسر قال أفطر وصل ما بينهما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Life, vitality, animation; the opposite of death (mawt). To "revive" (iḥyāʾ) a time is to animate it with acts of worship, giving it spiritual life.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, iḥyāʾ denotes the infusion of spiritual vitality into a temporal span through devotional acts, paralleling God's revivification of dead hearts through guidance (hidāyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) refers to biological life; here it is metaphorical (majāz) — the "revival" of a time-period through prayer and remembrance, as if the hours were dead and given life.
- Root: ع-ش-و (ʿ-sh-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The ʿishāʾ is the night prayer; the period of dusk and early night. "Bayna al-ʿishāʾayn" (between the two ʿishāʾs) idiomatically means between sunset (maghrib) and the night prayer (ʿishāʾ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The interval is a liminal zone between day and night — a time of heightened spiritual receptivity, often associated with the "awwābīn" (the penitently returning).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The phrase is a recognized idiom (majāz mursal) where the whole period is named by its two boundary prayers.
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand, to rise, to persist. Qiyām al-layl is the night vigil — standing in prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyām in worship signifies the soul's uprightness before God, a physical posture mirroring spiritual steadfastness (istiqāmah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal standing; metaphorically, the "standing" of the heart in attentive devotion (ḥuḍūr al-qalb).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with "Man" (al-sharṭ bi-man) — The repeated "man" (whoever) constructions introduce protases with apodoses marked by "fa" (e.g., "fa-banā Allāhu lahu"), indicating a causal nexus between the act and its divinely decreed reward. The apodosis is in the perfect tense (māḍī) to express certainty of fulfillment.
chapters.translation:
I say — may God grant us and you success:

**The Virtue of Reviving the Time Between the Two Evening Prayers**

The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said — as narrated by ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her: "The most virtuous of prayers in the sight of God is the sunset prayer (al-maghrib). God has not waived it for the traveler nor for the resident. By it He opens the night prayer and by it He seals the day prayer. Whoever prays the sunset prayer and prays two units (rakʿatayn) after it, God will build for him a palace in Paradise."

**Chapter Two: On the Causes that Facilitate the Night Vigil (Qiyām al-Layl)**

The ḥadīth of ʿĀʾishah — "The most virtuous of prayers in the sight of God is the sunset prayer; God has not waived it for the traveler nor for the resident" — was narrated by Abū al-Walīd Yūnus ibn ʿUbayd Allāh al-Ṣaffār in his Book of Prayer, and by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ in abbreviated form, though its chain (isnād) is weak.

The ḥadīth of Umm Salamah, from Abū Hurayrah: "Whoever prays six units after the sunset prayer, it will be reckoned for him as the worship of a year — or as if he had prayed on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr)." This was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah with the wording "twelve years," and al-Tirmidhī declared it weak. As for his saying "as if he had prayed on the Night of Decree," this is from the saying of Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, as narrated by Abū al-Walīd al-Ṣaffār.

Abū Manṣūr al-Daylamī relates in Musnad al-Firdaws, from the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿAbbās: "Whoever prays four units after the sunset prayer before speaking to anyone, it will be placed for him in ʿIlliyyīn (the Highest Heights), and he will be like one who attained the Night of Decree in the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Aqṣā)." Its chain is weak.

From Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Thawbān, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever confines himself (ʿakafa nafsahu) between the sunset and the night prayer in a congregational mosque, speaking nothing but prayer or Qurʾān, it is incumbent upon God to build for him two palaces in Paradise, each palace spanning a journey of one hundred years, and to plant for him between them such vegetation that if all the people of the earth were to traverse it, it would encompass them."

He also said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever bows ten units (rakʿāt) between the sunset and the night prayer, God will build for him a palace in Paradise." ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "Then our palaces will be many, O Messenger of God!" He replied: "God has more and better" — or he said: "more pleasing (aṭyab)."

From Anas ibn Mālik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever prays the sunset prayer in congregation, then prays two units after it without speaking anything of worldly matters in between, and recites in the first unit the Opening of the Book (Fātiḥat al-Kitāb) and ten verses from the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqarah, and two verses from its middle — {«وَإِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ ۖ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ الرَّحِيمُ ۝ إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ»} to the end of the verse — and {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} fifteen times, then bows and prostrates. When he stands for the second unit, he recites the Opening of the Book, the Throne Verse (Āyat al-Kursī), and the two verses after it up to His saying {«أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ»}, and three verses from the end of Sūrat al-Baqarah from His saying {«لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ»} to its end, and {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} fifteen times." He described its reward in the ḥadīth in a manner beyond enumeration.

Karz ibn Wabarah — who was among the abdāl (substitutes, saintly figures) — said: I said to al-Khiḍr, peace be upon him: "Teach me something I may do every night." He said: "When you have prayed the sunset prayer, stand until the time of the night prayer, praying, without speaking to anyone, and devote yourself to the prayer you are in, concluding every two units with the salutation (taslīm). Recite in every unit the Opening of the Book once and {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} three times. When you finish your prayer, return to your home without speaking to anyone, and pray two units, reciting the Opening of the Book and {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} seven times in each unit. Then prostrate after your salutation and seek forgiveness of God, the Exalted, seven times, and say: 'Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is Greater, and there is no might and no power except through God, the Exalted, the Magnificent' seven times. Then raise your head from prostration, sit upright, raise your hands, and say: 'O Living One, O Self-Subsisting One, O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity, O God of the first and the last, O Merciful of this world and the Hereafter and the Compassionate of them both, O Lord, O Lord, O Lord, O God, O God, O God.' Then stand while raising your hands and supplicate with this invocation. Then sleep wherever you wish, facing the qiblah on your right side, and send blessings upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and persist in blessing him until sleep overcomes you."

I (Karz) said to him: "I would love for you to tell me from whom you heard this." He said: "I was present with Muḥammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when he taught this invocation and it was revealed to him, and I was with him, and it was in my presence. So I learned it from the one who taught it to him."

It is said that whoever persists in this invocation and this prayer with sound certainty (ḥusn yaqīn) and sincere intention (ṣidq niyyah) will see the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, in his dream before departing this world. Indeed, some people did this and saw that they were admitted into Paradise, saw the prophets therein, and saw the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, who spoke to them and taught them.

In sum, what has been reported concerning the virtue of reviving the time between the two evening prayers is abundant, to the point that it was said to ʿUbayd Allāh, the freed slave (mawlā) of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: "Did the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, command any prayer besides the obligatory one?" He said: "What is between the sunset and the night prayer."

He also said, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever prays between the sunset and the night prayer — that is the prayer of the penitently returning (al-awwābīn)."

Al-Aswad said: "I never came to Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, at this time except that I saw him praying. I asked him about it, and he said: 'Yes, it is the hour of heedlessness (ghaflah).'" Anas, may God be pleased with him, would persist in it and say: "It is the night-rising (nāshiʾat al-layl)," and he would say concerning it that the verse was revealed: {«تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ»} ("Their sides forsake their beds").

Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḥawārī said: I said to Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī: "I fast during the day and take my evening meal between the sunset and the night prayer — do you prefer this, or that I break my fast during the day and revive the time between them?" He said: "Combine both." I said: "And if that is not feasible?" He said: "Then break your fast and pray during the time between them."

chapters.title_en: The Virtue of Night Prayer (Qiyām al-Layl)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| فضيلة قيام الليل

أما من الآيات فقوله تعالى {إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل}
الآية وقوله تعالى {إن ناشئة الليل هي أشد وطأ وأقوم قيلا} وقوله سبحانه
وتعالى {تتجافى جنوبهم عن المضاجع} وقوله تعالى أمن هو قانت آناء الليل
الآية وقوله عز وجل {والذين يبيتون لربهم سجدا وقياما} وقوله تعالى
{واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة} قيل هي قيام الليل يستعان بالصبر عليه على
مجاهدة النفس ومن الأخبار قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعقد الشيطان على قافية
رأس أحدكم إذا هو نام ثلاث عقد يضرب مكان كل عقدة عليك ليل طويل فارقد فإن
استيقظ وذكر الله تعالى انحلت عقدة فإن توضأ انحلت عقدة فإن صلى انحلت عقدة
فأصبح نشيطا طيب النفس وإلا أصبح خبيث النفس كسلان (2) وفي الخبر أنه ذكر
عنده رجل ينام كل الليل حتى يصبح فقال ذاك رجل بال الشيطان في ادنه (3) وفي
الخبر إن للشيطان سعوطا ولعوقا وذرورا فإذا أسعط العبد ساء خلقه وإذا ألعقه
ذرب لسانه بالشر وإذا ذره نام الليل حتى يصبح (4) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
ركعتان يركعهما العبد  في جوف الليل خير له من الدنيا وما فيها ولولا أن أشق
على أمتي لفرضتهما عليهم (5) وفي الصحيح عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم قال إن من الليل ساعة لا يوافقها عبد مسلم يسأل الله تعالى خيرا إلا
أعطاه إياه وفي رواية يسأل الله تعالى خيرا من الدنيا والآخرة وذلك في كل
ليلة وقال المغيرة بن شعبة قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى تفطرت
قدماه فقيل له أما قد غفر الله لك ما تقدم من ذنبك وما تأخر فقال أفلا أكون
عبدا شكورا (6) ويظهر من معناه أن ذلك كناية عن زيادة الرتبة فإن الشكر سبب
المزيد قال تعالى {لئن شكرتم لأزيدنكم} وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم يا أبا
هريرة أتريد أن تكون رحمة الله عليك حيا وميتا ومقبورا ومبعوثا قم من الليل
فصل وأنت تريد رضا ربك يا أبا هريرة صل في زوايا بيتك يكن نور بيتك في
السماء كنور الكواكب والنجم عند أهل الدنيا (7) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم
عليكم بقيام الليل فإنه دأب الصالحين قبلكم فإن قيام الليل قربة إلى الله
عز وجل وتكفير للذنوب PageV01P353
ومطردة للداء عن الجسد ومنهاة عن الإثم (1) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم ما
من امرئ تكون له صلاة بالليل فغلبه عليها النوم إلا كتب له أجر صلاته وكان
نومه صدقة عليه (2) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي ذر لو أردت سفرا أعددت له
عدة قال نعم قال فكيف سفر طريق القيامة ألا أنبئك يا أبا ذر بما ينفعك ذلك
اليوم قال بلى بأبي أنت وأمي قال صم يوما شديد الحر ليوم النشور وصل ركعتين
في ظلمة الليل لوحشة القبور وحج حجة لعظائم الأمور وتصدق بصدقة على مسكين
أو كلمة حق تقولها أو كلمة شر تسكت عنها (3) وروي أنه كان على عهد النبي
صلى الله عليه وسلم رجل إذا أخذ الناس مضاجعهم وهدأت العيون قام يصلي ويقرأ
القرآن ويقول يا رب النار أجرني منها فذكر ذلك للنبي صلى الله عليه  وسلم
فقال إذا كان ذلك فآذنوني فأتاه فاستمع فلما أصبح قال يا فلان هلا سألت
الله الجنة قال يا رسول الله إني لست هناك ولا يبلغ عملي ذاك فلم يلبث إلا
يسيرا حتى نزل جبرائيل عليه السلام وقال أخبر فلانا أن الله قد أجاره من
النار وأدخله الجنة (4) ويروى أن جبرائيل عليه السلام قال للنبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم نعم الرجل ابن عمر لو كان يصلي بالليل فأخبره النبي صلى الله
عليه وسلم بذلك فكان يداوم بعده على قيام الليل (5) قال نافع كان يصلي
بالليل ثم يقول يا نافع أسحرنا فأقول لا فيقوم لصلاته ثم يقول يا نافع
أسحرنا فأقول نعم فيقعد فيستغفر الله تعالى حتى يطلع الفجر وقال علي بن أبي
طالب شبع يحيى بن زكريا عليهما السلام من خبز شعير فنام عن ورده حتى أصبح
فأوحى الله تعالى إليه يا يحيى أوجدت دارا خيرا لك من داري أم وجدت جوارا
خيرا لك من جواري فوعزتي وجلالي يا يحيى لو اطلعت إلى الفردوس اطلاعه لذاب
شحمك ولزهقت نفسك اشتياقا ولو اطلعت إلى جهنم اطلاعة لذاب شحمك ولبكيت
الصديد بعد الدموع ولبست الجلد بعد المسوح وقيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم إن فلانا يصلي بالليل فإذا أصبح سرق فقال سينهاه ما يعمل (6) وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم رحم الله رجلا قام من الليل فصلى ثم أيقظ امرأته فصلت فإن
أبت نضح في وجهها الماء (7) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم رحم الله امرأة قامت
من الليل فصلت ثم أيقظت زوجها فصلى فإن أبى نضحت في وجهه الماء وقال صلى
الله عليه وسلم من استيقظ من الليل وأيقظ امرأته فصليا ركعتين كتبا من
الذاكرين الله كثيرا والذاكرات (8) وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل الصلاة
بعد المكتوبة قيام الليل (9) وقال PageV01P354
عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من نام عن حزبه أو عن
شيء منه بالليل فقرأه بين صلاة الفجر والظهر كتب له كأنما قرأه من الليل
(1) الآثار  روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه كان يمر بالآية من ورده بالليل فيسقط
حتى يعاد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand upright, to rise, to undertake; qiyām denotes sustained standing in devotion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyām al-layl is the supererogatory vigil of prayer, a mark of sincere servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) and spiritual exertion (mujāhadah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal standing (ḥaqīqah) vs. metaphorical perseverance in worship (majāz); "nāshiʾat al-layl" is rhetorically the rising after sleep, most potent for devotion.
- Root: ن-ش-أ (n-sh-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To arise, to come into being; nāshiʾah is the soul's awakening from slumber.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The night vigil as a fresh origination of the self in obedience, aligning the creature with the Creator's command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal rising from bed; metaphorically, the spiritual rebirth of attentiveness.
- Root: و-ط-أ (w-ṭ-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tread, to press down; waṭʾ denotes firmness and impact.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "Ashaddu waṭʾan" — the night prayer is more firmly planted in the heart and more potent in effect upon the soul.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal treading of the ground; metaphorically, the weighty consonance of tongue and heart in recitation.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Conditional Emphasis (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — In "fa-in istayqaẓa... inḥallat ʿuqdatun," the protasis-apodosis structure underscores causal efficacy; each awakening act (remembrance, ablution, prayer) sequentially unties the knots of Satan's binding, a syntactic gradation mirroring spiritual ascent.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the merit of night prayer is established by the Book of God, the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace be upon him), and the consensus of the righteous predecessors (salaf).

As for the verses of the Qurʾān, God Most High says: {«إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ»} — "Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night" — and His saying: {«إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْأً وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا»} — "Indeed, the rising of the night is more firmly planted and more upright in speech" — and His saying, Glorified and Exalted: {«تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ»} — "Their sides forsake their beds" — and His saying: {«أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ»} — "Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night..." — and His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا»} — "And those who pass the night prostrating and standing before their Lord" — and His saying: {«وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ»} — "And seek help through patience and prayer." It is said that this refers to night prayer, by which one seeks aid through patience upon it, in striving against the soul (mujāhadat al-nafs).

As for the reports (akhbār), the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Satan ties three knots at the nape of the crown of your head when you sleep, striking at each knot: 'Upon you is a long night, so sleep.' If you awaken and remember God, one knot is untied; if you perform ablution, a knot is untied; if you pray, a knot is untied — and you arise in the morning vigorous and good of spirit. Otherwise, you arise evil of spirit and sluggish."

In another report, a man was mentioned before him who slept the entire night until morning, and he said: "That is a man in whose ear Satan has urinated."

In another report: "Satan has a snuff, a linctus, and a powder. If he snuffs a servant, his character becomes foul; if he licks him, his tongue becomes sharp with evil; if he powders him, he sleeps the night until morning."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "Two rakʿahs that a servant prays in the depths of the night are better for him than the world and all that is in it. Were it not that I would burden my community, I would have made them obligatory upon them."

In the Ṣaḥīḥ, on the authority of Jābir, that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed, in the night there is an hour in which no Muslim servant asks God for good but that He grants it to him." In another narration: "He asks God for good of this world and the Hereafter — and that is every night."

Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) stood in prayer until his feet swelled. It was said to him: "Has not God forgiven you your former and latter sins?" He replied: "Shall I not then be a grateful servant?" The apparent meaning of this is that it is a metaphor (kināyah) for the increase of rank, for gratitude is the cause of increase. God said: {«لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ»} — "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "O Abū Hurayrah, do you wish that God's mercy be upon you living, dead, buried, and resurrected? Rise in the night and pray, seeking the pleasure of your Lord.
