O Abū Hurayrah, pray in the corners of your house, and the light of your house shall be in the heaven like the light of the stars and planets to the people of the earth."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "Upon you is night prayer, for it is the practice (dāʾb) of the righteous before you. Night prayer is a means of nearness to God, Mighty and Majestic, an expiation for sins, a repeller of illness from the body, and a preventer of transgression."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "There is no man who has a night prayer and sleep overcomes him in it, but that the reward of his prayer is written for him, and his sleep is a charity upon him."

And he (peace be upon him) said to Abū Dharr: "If you intended a journey, would you prepare provisions for it?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then what of the journey of the Day of Resurrection? Shall I not inform you, O Abū Dharr, of what will benefit you on that day?" He said: "Yes, may my father and mother be your ransom." He said: "Fast a day of intense heat for the Day of Resurrection, pray two rakʿahs in the darkness of the night for the loneliness of the graves, perform a pilgrimage for the great matters, and give charity to a poor person — or a word of truth you speak, or a word of evil you refrain from."

It is narrated that in the era of the Prophet (peace be upon him) there was a man who, when people took to their beds and eyes grew still, would rise to pray and recite the Qurʾān, saying: "O Lord, the Fire — save me from it." This was mentioned to the Prophet (peace be upon him), and he said: "When that happens, inform me." So he came to him and listened. When morning came, he said: "O so-and-so, why did you not ask God for Paradise?" He said: "O Messenger of God, I am not of that station, nor does my deed reach that." Not long after, Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and said: "Inform so-and-so that God has granted him safety from the Fire and admitted him to Paradise."

It is narrated that Gabriel (peace be upon him) said to the Prophet (peace be upon him): "Excellent is the man Ibn ʿUmar — were he but to pray at night." The Prophet (peace be upon him) informed him of that, and thereafter he persisted in night prayer. Nāfiʿ said: He would pray at night, then say: "O Nāfiʿ, have we reached dawn?" I would say: "No," and he would rise to pray. Then he would say: "O Nāfiʿ, have we reached dawn?" I would say: "Yes," and he would sit and seek God's forgiveness until dawn broke.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: John son of Zachariah (peace be upon them both) was satiated with barley bread, slept past his devotional portion (wird) until morning, and God revealed to him: "O John, have you found a home better for you than My home, or a neighbor better for you than My neighborhood? By My Might and My Majesty, O John, were you to gaze upon Paradise with a single gaze, your flesh would melt and your soul would expire in longing; and were you to gaze upon Hell with a single gaze, your flesh would melt, you would weep blood after tears, and you would don skin after sackcloth."

It was said to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him): "So-and-so prays at night, but when morning comes, he steals." He said: "What he does will prevent him from that."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "May God have mercy on a man who rises at night, prays, then awakens his wife to pray; if she refuses, he sprinkles water on her face."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "May God have mercy on a woman who rises at night, prays, then awakens her husband to pray; if he refuses, she sprinkles water on his face."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever awakens at night and awakens his wife, and they pray two rakʿahs, they are written among the men who remember God much and the women who remember Him much."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "The most excellent prayer after the obligatory one is night prayer."

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may God be pleased with him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever sleeps past his devotional portion (ḥizb) or part of it at night, and recites it between the dawn prayer and the noon prayer, it is written for him as though he had recited it at night."

THE TRADITIONS OF THE PREDECESSORS (ĀTHĀR):
It is narrated that ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) would pass by a verse of his nightly portion and fall down, and would be nursed back for many days as a sick man is nursed.

Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him), when eyes grew still, would rise, and a hum would be heard from him like the hum of bees until morning.

It is said that Sufyān al-Thawrī (may God have mercy on him) was satiated one night and said: "When a donkey is given extra fodder, its work increases." So he stood that night until morning.

Ṭāwūs (may God have mercy on him), when he lay on his bed, would toss upon it as a grain of corn tosses on a frying pan, then would leap up and pray until morning, then say: "The mention of Hell has driven away the sleep of the worshippers."

Al-Ḥasan said: "We know of no deed more severe than enduring the night and spending this wealth." It was said to him: "Why are the night-praying ones (mutahajjidūn) among the most beautiful of people in face?" He said: "Because they have secluded themselves with the Merciful, and He has clothed them with light from His light."

One of the righteous returned from a journey, and a bed was spread for him. He slept upon it until his devotional portion passed him, and he swore that he would never sleep on a bed again.

ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rawwād, when night darkened upon him, would come to his bed, run his hand over it, and say: "You are soft, and by God, in Paradise there is softer than you." And he would continue praying the entire night.

Al-Fuḍayl said: "I face the night from its beginning, and its length terrifies me. So I open the Qurʾān, and morning comes while I have not yet satisfied my desire."

Al-Ḥasan said: "A man commits a sin, and is thereby deprived of night prayer."

Al-Fuḍayl said: "If you are unable to pray at night and fast by day, then know that you are deprived, and your sins have multiplied."

Ṣilah ibn Ashyam (may God have mercy on him) would pray the entire night, and at dawn he would say: "O my God, one like me does not ask for Paradise, but save me by Your mercy from the Fire."

A man said to one of the sages: "I am too weak for night prayer." He replied: "O my brother, do not disobey God, and you will not need to pray at night."

Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ had a slave-girl whom he sold to some people. In the depths of the night, the girl rose and said: "O people of the house, the prayer, the prayer!" They said: "Have we reached morning? Has dawn appeared?" She said: "Do you pray only the obligatory?" They said: "Yes." So she returned to al-Ḥasan and said: "O my master, you sold me to people who pray only the obligatory — take me back." So he took her back.

Al-Rabīʿ said: "I stayed in the house of al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) for many nights, and he would not sleep from the night except a little."

Abū al-Juwayriyyah said: "I accompanied Abū Ḥanīfah (may God be pleased with him) for six months, and in all that time there was not a single night in which he placed his side upon the ground." Abū Ḥanīfah used to revive half the night. He passed by some people who said: "This man revives the entire night." He said: "I am ashamed to be described by what I do not do." Thereafter he revived the entire night. It is narrated that he had no bed at night.

It is said that Mālik ibn Dīnār (may God be pleased with him) spent a night repeating this verse until morning: {«أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ اجْتَرَحُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ أَن نَّجْعَلَهُمْ كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ»} — "Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds..."

Al-Mughīrah ibn Ḥabīb said: "I watched Mālik ibn Dīnār. He performed ablution after the night prayer, then stood at his prayer place, grasped his beard, and sobs choked him. He kept saying: 'The gray hair of Mālik is forbidden to the Fire. O my God, You know the dweller of Paradise from the dweller of Hell — so which of the two men is Mālik, and which of the two abodes is Mālik's abode?' His words continued thus until dawn broke."

Mālik ibn Dīnār said: "One night I desired to skip my devotional portion and slept. Then I saw in a dream a maiden of the most beautiful form, with a scroll in her hand. She said to me: 'Do you know how to read?' I said: 'Yes.' She handed me the scroll, and in it was written:

"Have the pleasures and hopes distracted you / From the white-skinned maidens in the Gardens?
You shall live immortal, no death therein / And delight in the Gardens with the beautiful.
Awaken from your sleep, for better than sleep / Is the night vigil with the Qurʾān."

It is said that Masrūq performed the pilgrimage and did not spend a single night except prostrating.

It is narrated from Azhar ibn Mughīth, who was among those who stood long in prayer, that he said: "I saw in a dream a woman unlike the women of this world. I said to her: 'Who are you?' She said: 'A ḥūrī.' I said: 'Marry me to yourself.' She said: 'Propose to me to my Lord, and give me my dowry.' I said: 'What is your dowry?' She said: 'Length of night vigil (tahajjud).'"

Yūsuf ibn Mahrān said: "It has reached me that beneath the Throne there is an angel in the form of a rooster, its claws of pearl and its comb of green chrysolite. When the first third of the night passes, it beats its wings and crows: 'Let the standers rise.' When half the night passes, it beats its wings and crows: 'Let the night-praying ones (mutahajjidūn) rise.' When two-thirds pass, it beats its wings and crows: 'Let the praying ones rise.' When dawn breaks, it beats its wings and crows: 'Let the heedless rise, and upon them their burdens.'"

It is said that Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamānī did not place his side upon the ground for thirty years. He would say: "To see a devil in my house is dearer to me than to see a pillow in my house, for it invites to sleep." He had a leather cushion; when sleep overcame him, he would place his chest upon it, doze a few moments, then hasten back to prayer.

One of them said: "I saw the Lord of Might in a dream and heard Him say: 'By My Might and My Majesty, I will honor the abode of Sulaymān al-Taymī, for he prayed the dawn prayer to me with the ablution of the night prayer for forty years.'" It is said his view was that when sleep overcomes the heart, the ablution is invalidated.

It is narrated in some ancient books, from God Most High, that He said: "Indeed, My servant who is truly My servant is the one who does not wait for the crowing of the roosters to rise for prayer."

chapters.title_en: The Elucidation of the Causes that Facilitate the Night Vigil (Qiyām al-Layl)
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان الأسباب التي بها يتيسر قيام الليل

اعلم أن قيام الليل عسير على الخلق إلا على من وفق للقيام بشروطه الميسرة
له ظاهرا وباطنا فأما الظاهرة فأربعة أمور الأول أن لا يكثر الأكل فيكثر
الشرب فيغلبه النوم ويثقل عليه القيام كان بعض الشيوخ يقف على المائدة كل
ليلة ويقول معاشر المريدين لا تأكلوا كثيرا فتشربوا كثيرا فترقدوا كثيرا
فتتحسروا عند الموت كثيرا وهذا هو الأصل الكبير وهو تخفيف المعدة عن ثقل
الطعام الثاني أن لا يتعب نفسه بالنهار في الأعمال التي تعيا بها الجوارح
وتضعف بها الأعصاب فإن ذلك أيضا مجلبة للنوم الثالث أن لا يترك القيلولة
بالنهار فإنها سنة للاستعانة على قيام الليل (1) الرابع أن لا يحتقب
الأوزار بالنهار فإن ذلك مما يقسي القلب ويحول بينه وبين أسباب الرحمة قال
رجل للحسن يا أبا سعيد إني أبيت معافى وأحب قيام الليل وأعد طهوري فما بالي
لا أقوم فقال ذنوبك قيدتك وكان الحسن رحمة الله إذا دخل السوق فسمع لغطهم
ولغوهم يقول أظن أن ليل هؤلاء ليل سوء فإنهم لا يقيلون وقال الثوري حرمت
قيام الليل خمسة أشهر بذنب أذنبته قيل وما ذاك الذنب قال رأيت رجلا يبكي
فقلت في نفسي  هذا مراء وقال بعضهم دخلت على كرز بن وبرة وهو يبكي فقلت أتاك
نعي بعض أهلك فقال اشد فقلت وجع يؤلمك قال أشد قلت فما ذاك قال بابي مغلق
وستري مسبل ولم أقرأ حزبي البارحة وما ذاك إلا بذنب أحدثته وهذا لأن الخير
يدعو إلى الخير والشر يدعو إلى الشر والقليل من كل واحد منهما يجر إلى
الكثير ولذلك قال أبو سليمان الداراني لا تفوت أحدا صلاة الجماعة إلا بذنب
وكان يقول الاحتلام بالليل عقوبة والجنابة بعد وقال بعض العلماء إذا صمت يا
مسكين فانظر عند من تفطر وعلى أي شيء تفطر فإن العبد ليأكل أكلة فينقلب
قلبه عما كان عليه ولا يعود إلى حالته الأولى فالذنوب كلها تورث قساوة
القلب وتمنع من قيام الليل وأخصها بالتأثير تناول الحرام وتؤثر اللقمة
الحلال في تصفية القلب وتحريكه إلى الخير ما لا يؤثر غيرها ويعرف ذلك أهل
المراقبة للقلوب بالتجربة بعد شهادة الشرع له ولذلك قال بعضهم كم من أكلة
منعت قيام ليلة وكم من نظرة منعت قراءة سورة وإن العبد ليأكل أكلة أو يفعل
فعلة فيحرم بها قيام سنة وكما إن الصلاة تنهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر فكذلك
الفحشاء تنهى عن الصلاة وسائر الخيرات وقال بعض السجانين PageV01P356
كنت سجانا نيفا وثلاثين سنة أسأل كل مأخوذ بالليل أنه هل صلى العشاء في
جماعة فكانوا يقولون لا وهذا تنبيه على أن بركة الجماعة تنهى عن تعاطي
الفحشاء والمنكر
وأما الميسرات الباطنة فأربعة أمور الأول سلامة القلب عن الحقد على
المسلمين وعن البدع وعن فضول هموم الدنيا فالمستغرق الهم بتدبير الدنيا لا
يتيسر له القيام وإن قام فلا يتفكر في صلاته إلا في مهماته ولا يجول إلا في
وساوسه وفي مثل ذلك يقال
يخبرني البواب أنك نائم ... وأنت إذا استيقظت أيضا فنائم
الثاني خوف غالب يلزم القلب مع قصر الأمل فإنه إذا تفكر في أهوال الآخرة
ودركات جهنم طار نومه وعظم حذره كما قال طاوس إن ذكر جهنم طير نوم العابدين
وكما حكي أن غلاما  بالبصرة اسمه صهيب كان يقوم الليل كله فقالت له سيدته إن
قيامك بالليل يضر بعملك بالنهار فقال إن صهيبا إذا ذكر النار لا يأتيه
النوم وقيل لغلام آخر وهو يقوم كل الليل فقال إذا ذكرت النار اشتد خوفي
وإذا ذكرت الجنة اشتد شوقي فلا أقدر أن أنام وقال ذو النون المصري رحمه
الله
منع القرآن بوعده ووعيده ... مقل العيون بليلها أن تهجعا
فهموا عن الملك الجليل كلامه ... فرقابهم ذلت إليه تخضعا
وأنشدوا أيضا
يا طويل الرقاد والغفلات ... كثرة النوم تورث الحسرات
إن في القبر إن نزلت إليه ... لرقادا يطول بعد الممات
ومهادا ممهدا لك فيه ... بذنوب عملت أو حسنات
أأمنت البيات من ملك المو ... ت وكم نال آمنا ببيات
وقال ابن المبارك
إذا ما الليل أظلم كابدوه ... فيسفر عنهم وهم ركوع
أطار الخوف نومهم فقاموا ... وأهل الأمن في الدنيا هجوع
الثالث أن يعرف فضل قيام الليل بسماع الآيات والأخبار والآثار حتى يستحكم
به رجاؤه وشوقه إلى ثوابه فيهيجه الشوق لطلب المزيد والرغبة في درجات
الجنان كما حكي أن بعض الصالحين رجع من غزوته فمهدت امرأته فراشها وجلست
تنتظره فدخل المسجد ولم يزل يصلي حتى أصبح فقالت له زوجته كنا ننتظرك مدة
فلما قدمت صليت إلى الصبح قال والله إني كنت أتفكر في حوراء من حور الجنة
طول الليل فنسيت الزوجة والمنزل فقمت طول ليلتي شوقا إليها
الرابع وهو أشرف البواعث الحب لله وقوة الإيمان بأنه في قيامه لا يتكلم
بحرف إلا وهو مناج ربه وهو مطلع عليه مع مشاهدة ما يخطر بقلبه وأن تلك
الخطرات من الله تعالى خطاب معه فإذا أحب الله تعالى أحب لا محالة الخلوة
به وتلذذ بالمناجاة فتحمله لذة المناجاة بالحبيب على طول القيام ولا ينبغي
أن يستبعد هذه اللذة إذ يشهد لها العقل والنقل فأما العقل فل
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ease, facility, readiness; the opposite of difficulty (ʿusr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine facilitation (taysīr) as an ontological grant enabling acts of obedience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of physical ease; metaphorical sense of spiritual preparedness granted by God.
- Root: ق-ي-م (q-y-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand, to rise, to uphold; qiyām al-layl as the vigil of standing in prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The devotional act of standing before God in worship, connoting vigilance and presence of heart.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical standing; metaphorical steadfastness in obedience.
- Root: خ-ط-ر (kh-ṭ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cross the mind, to occur; khaṭarāt as passing thoughts or inspirations.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The influx of divine address upon the heart during intimate communion (munājāh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal crossing of a path; metaphorical descent of spiritual realities upon the conscious heart.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — Governing the parsing of "إلا على من وفق" (except upon whom is granted success), where the exception restricts the universal difficulty, and the conditional clauses (e.g., "إذا تفكر... طار نومه") establish causal sequences requiring precise temporal subordination.
chapters.translation:
Know that the night vigil (qiyām al-layl) is arduous upon creation, save upon him whom God has granted success in fulfilling its conditions that render it easy, both outwardly and inwardly.

As for the outward facilators, they are four matters:

**The first:** That one not eat excessively, for then he drinks excessively, and sleep overcomes him, and the vigil becomes heavy upon him. It was the habit of some of the elders (shuyūkh) to stand at the table each night and say: "O company of seekers (murīdīn)! Do not eat much, so that you drink much, so that you sleep much, so that you grieve much at the moment of death." This is the great principle — the lightening of the stomach from the heaviness of food.

**The second:** That one not exhaust himself by day in labors that weary the limbs and weaken the nerves, for that too is a cause that summons sleep.

**The third:** That one not abandon the midday nap (al-qaylūlah) by day, for it is a sunnah that aids in the night vigil.

**The fourth:** That one not accumulate sins (awzār) by day, for that is among the things that harden the heart and interpose between it and the causes of mercy. A man said to al-Ḥasan [al-Baṣrī]: "O Abā Saʿīd, I retire to bed sound and healthy, and I love the night vigil, and I prepare my purification — what ails me that I do not rise?" He replied: "Your sins have bound you in chains." And al-Ḥasan — God's mercy upon him — when he entered the market and heard their clamor and idle talk, would say: "I think that the night of these people is an evil night, for they do not take the midday nap." And al-Thawrī said: "I was deprived of the night vigil for five months due to a sin I committed." It was asked: "And what was that sin?" He said: "I saw a man weeping, and I said to myself: 'This one is showing off (murāʾī).'" And some of them said: "I entered upon Karz ibn Wabrah while he was weeping, and I said: 'Has news of the death of one of your family reached you?' He said: 'More severe.' I said: 'A pain afflicting you?' He said: 'More severe.' I said: 'Then what is it?' He said: 'My door is closed, my curtain is drawn, and I did not recite my portion (ḥizb) last night — and that is only due to a sin I newly committed.'" This is because good calls to good, and evil calls to evil, and the little of each of them drags toward the much. For this reason, Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī said: "No one misses the congregational prayer except due to a sin." And he used to say: "Nocturnal emission (al-iḥtilām) by night is a punishment, and major impurity (al-janābah) after it." And some of the scholars said: "O poor one, if you fast, then consider before whom you break your fast and upon what you break it. For the servant eats a single morsel, and his heart is overturned from what it was upon, and he does not return to his former state." Thus all sins bequeath hardness of heart and prevent the night vigil, and the most specific of them in effect is the consumption of the unlawful (ḥarām). And the lawful morsel (al-luqmah al-ḥalāl) affects the purification of the heart and its stirring toward good in a way that nothing else affects. This is known to the people of watchfulness over hearts (ahl al-murāqabah) by experience, after the testimony of the Sacred Law to it. For this reason, some of them said: "How many a morsel has prevented a night's vigil, and how many a glance has prevented the recitation of a sūrah! Indeed, the servant eats a single morsel or commits a single act, and is thereby deprived of a year's vigil." And just as the prayer prohibits indecency and wrongdoing {«إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنكَرِ»}, so too does indecency prohibit prayer and all other good deeds. And one of the prison wardens said: "I was a warden for over thirty-three years, asking every one seized by night: 'Did you pray the ʿishāʾ in congregation?' And they would say: 'No.'" This is an indication that the blessing of the congregation prohibits the commission of indecency and wrongdoing.

As for the inward facilators, they are four matters:

**The first:** Soundness of the heart from rancor against the Muslims, from innovations (bidʿah), and from superfluous worldly concerns. For he who is engrossed in managing the world finds the vigil not facilitated for him; and if he rises, he does not reflect in his prayer except upon his pressing affairs, and his mind does not wander except among his whisperings (wasāwis). Concerning such a one it is said:

*The doorkeeper tells me that you are asleep —*
*And you, when you awaken, are also asleep.*

**The second:** A prevailing fear that clings to the heart, along with the shortening of hope (qasr al-amal). For when one reflects upon the terrors of the Hereafter and the depths of Hell, his sleep takes flight and his caution becomes immense. As Ṭāwūs said: "The remembrance of Hell puts to flight the sleep of the worshippers." And as it is related that a youth in Baṣrah named Ṣuhayb used to stand the entire night, and his mistress said to him: "Your standing by night harms your work by day." He said: "Ṣuhayb, when he remembers the Fire, sleep does not come to him." And it was said to another youth who stood the whole night: [He replied:] "When I remember the Fire, my fear intensifies; and when I remember Paradise, my longing intensifies — so I cannot sleep." And Dhū al-Nūn al-Miṣrī — God's mercy upon him — said:

*The Qurʾān, by its promise and its threat, has prevented*
*The eyes of the humble from slumbering in their night.*
*They understood from the Majestic King His speech —*
*So their necks bowed low in submission to Him.*

And they also recited:

*O you of prolonged sleep and heedlessness!*
*Much sleep bequeaths regrets.*
*Verily in the grave, when you descend into it,*
*There is a slumber that lengthens after death —*
*And a bed prepared for you therein,*
*Of sins you wrought or of good deeds.*
*Are you secure from the night assault of the Angel of Death,*
*When many a secure one has been seized by night assault?*

And Ibn al-Mubārak said:

*When the night darkens, they endure it —*
*Then dawn breaks upon them while they are bowing.*
*Fear put their sleep to flight, so they arose —*
*While the people of security in this world are slumbering.*

**The third:** That one know the merit of the night vigil through hearing the verses, the reports (akhbār), and the traditions (āthār), until his hope and longing for its reward are firmly established thereby, and longing stirs him to seek increase and desire the ranks of the Gardens. As it is related that one of the righteous returned from his raid, and his wife spread his bed and sat awaiting him. He entered the mosque and did not cease praying until morning. His wife said to him: "We were awaiting you for a time, and when you arrived you prayed until dawn." He said: "By God, I was reflecting upon a ḥūrī from the ḥūr of Paradise the entire night, and I forgot the wife and the home — so I stood my entire night out of longing for her."

**The fourth** — and it is the noblest of the motives — is love for God (al-ḥubb li-Allāh) and the strength of faith that in his standing he utters not a single letter except that he is in intimate communion with his Lord (munājāt), Who is overseeing him, along with the witnessing that what crosses his heart (khaṭarāt) is a discourse from God — exalted be He — addressed to him. So when one loves God, he inevitably loves seclusion with Him and delights in the intimate communion; and the delight of communion with the Beloved carries him to the prolongation of the vigil. It is not fitting to deem this delight remote, for reason and revelation both bear witness to it.

As for reason: Let one consider the state of a lover of a person due to his beauty, or of a king due to his beneficence and wealth — how he delights in seclusion with him and in communing with him, such that sleep does not come to him the whole night. If you say: "The beautiful one is delighted by gazing upon him, whereas God — exalted be He — is not seen," then know that if the beautiful beloved were behind a curtain or in a dark house, the lover would still delight in his mere proximity, without gazing and without coveting anything else besides him; and he would take pleasure in displaying his love to him and mentioning him with his tongue within his hearing, even if that too were known to him. If you say: "He awaits his reply, so let him delight in hearing his answer — and he does not hear the speech of God," then know that even if he knew that he would not answer him and would remain silent toward him, there would still remain for him a delight in presenting his states to him and raising his secret to him. How much more so, when the certain believer hears from God — exalted be He — everything that descends upon his mind during his communion, and delights in it. Likewise, he who secludes himself with a king and presents his needs to him in the depths of the night delights in it through the hope of his beneficence — and hope in God — exalted be He — is more truthful, and what is with God is better, more enduring, and more beneficial than what is with other than Him. So how should one not delight in presenting needs to Him in seclusions?

As for revelation, it bears witness through the states of those who stand the night in their delight with the vigil and their perceiving it as short, just as the lover perceives the night of union with the beloved as short. It was said to one of them: "How are you and the night?" He said: "I have never observed it showing me its face and then departing, nor have I ever contemplated it afterwards." And another said: "I and the night are two racehorses — sometimes it outruns me to dawn, and sometimes it cuts me off from reflection." And it was said to one of them: "How is the night upon you?" He said: "An hour in which I am between two states: I rejoice at its darkness when it comes, and I grieve at its dawn when it rises — my joy in it has never been completed." And ʿAlī ibn Bakkār said: "For forty years, nothing has grieved me except the rising of dawn." And al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ said: "When the sun sets, I rejoice at the darkness for my seclusion with my Lord; and when it rises, I grieve at the entry of people upon me." And Abū Sulaymān said: "The people of the night are in their night more delighted than the people of amusement in their amusement. Were it not for the night, I would not love remaining in this world." And he also said: "If God were to compensate the people of the night for the reward of their deeds with what they find of delight, that would be greater than the reward of their deeds." And some of the scholars said: "There is no time in this world resembling the bliss of the people of Paradise except what the people of supplication (ahl al-tamalluq) find in their hearts by night of the sweetness of communion." And some of them said: "The delight of communion is not of this world; it is of Paradise, which God — exalted be He — has manifested to His friends (awliyāʾ); none find it besides them." And Ibn al-Munkadir said: "Nothing remains of the delights of this world except three: the night vigil, the meeting of brethren, and prayer in congregation." And some of the knowers (ʿārifūn) said: "God — exalted be He — looks at the hearts of the vigilant in the pre-dawn hours (asḥār) and fills them with lights, so the benefits return upon their hearts and they become illumined; then the well-beings (ʿawāfī) spread from their hearts to the hearts of the heedless." And some of the ancient scholars said: "God — exalted be He — revealed to one of the sincerely truthful (ṣiddīqīn): 'I have servants among My servants whom I love and who love Me; they long for Me and I long for them; they remember Me and I remember them; they look upon Me and I look upon them. If you tread their path, I will love you; and if you turn away from them, I will detest you.' He said: 'O Lord, and what is their sign?' He said: 'They tend the shade by day as the shepherd tends his flock, and they yearn toward the setting of the sun as birds yearn toward their nests. When the night envelops them and the darkness mingles and every lover is secluded with his beloved, they plant their feet and spread their faces upon the ground, and they commune with Me through My speech and supplicate Me through My beneficence. Among them is one crying out, one weeping, one sighing, one complaining. With My eye do I behold what they endure for My sake, and with My ear do I hear what they complain of in their love for Me. The first thing I give them is that I cast from My light into their hearts, so they inform of Me as I inform of them. The second: were the seven heavens and the seven earths and all that is in them to be placed in their scales, I would deem it too little for them. The third: I turn My face toward them — do you think that anyone upon whom I turn My face knows what I intend to give him?'"

And Mālik ibn Dīnār — God's mercy upon him — said: "When the servant rises to pray the night prayer (tahajjud), the Omnipotent — mighty and majestic is He — draws near to him." And they used to hold that what they found of tenderness and sweetness in their hearts, and the lights, were from the nearness of the Lord — exalted be He — to the heart. This has a secret and a verification to which allusion will come in the Book of Love (Kitāb al-Maḥabbah). And in the reports from God — mighty and majestic is He: "O My servant, I am God who has drawn near to your heart, and in the unseen you have seen My light." And one of the seekers (murīdīn) complained to his master of the length of wakefulness at night, seeking a stratagem to bring sleep. His master said: "O my son, God has breaths (nafaḥāt) in the night and the day that strike the vigilant hearts and bypass the sleeping hearts — so expose yourself to those breaths." He said: "O my master, you have left me sleeping neither by night nor by day."

Know that these breaths are more to be hoped for by night, due to what the night vigil contains of the heart's purity and the repulsion of distractions. And in the sound report (al-khabar al-ṣaḥīḥ) from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from the Messenger of God — God's blessings and peace be upon him — that he said: {«إِنَّ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ سَاعَةً لَا يُوَافِقُهَا عَبْدٌ مُسْلِمٌ يَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى خَيْرًا إِلَّا أَعْطَاهُ إِيَّاهُ»} ("Verily there is in the night an hour in which no Muslim servant coincides, asking God — exalted be He — for good, except that He grants it to him.") And in another narration: "Asking God for good of the matters of this world and the Hereafter, except that He grants it to him — and that is every night." And that hour is the quest of those who stand the night; it is in the totality of the night like the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) in Ramaḍān, and like the hour of Friday — and it is the hour of the aforementioned breaths. And God knows best.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Methods of Dividing the Parts of the Night
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان طرق القسمة لأجزاء الليل

اعلم أن إحياء الليل من حيث المقدار له سبع مراتب الأولى إحياء كل الليل
وهذا شأن الأقوياء الذين تجردوا لعبادة الليل وتلذذوا بمناجاته وصار ذلك
غذاء لهم وحياة لقلوبهم فلم يتعبوا بطول القيام وردوا المنام إلى النهار
وفي وقت اشتغال الناس وقد كان ذلك طريق جماعة من السلف كانوا يصلون الصبح
بوضوء العشاء حكى أبو طالب المكي أن ذلك حكي على سبيل التواتر والاشتهار عن
أربعين من التابعين وكان فيهم من واظب عليه أربعين سنة قال منهم سعيد بن
المسيب وصفوان بن سليم المدنيان وفضيل بن عياض ووهيب بن الورد المكيان
وطاوس ووهب بن منبه اليمانيان والربيع بن خيثم والحكم الكوفيان وأبو سليمان
الداراني وعلي بن بكار الشاميان وأبو عبد الله الخواص وأبو عاصم العباديان
وحبيب أبو محمد وأبو جابر السلماني الفارسيان ومالك بن دينار سليمان التيمي
ويزيد الرقاشي وحبيب بن أبي ثابت ويحيى البكاء البصريون وكهمس بن المنهال
وكان يختم في الشهر تسعين ختمة وما لم يفهمه رجع وقرأه مرة أخرى وأيضا من
أهل المدينة أبو حازم ومحمد بن المنكدر في جماعة يكثر عددهم المرتبة
الثانية أن يقوم نصف الليل وهذا لا ينحصر عدد المواظبين عليه من السلف
وأحسن فيه أن ينام الثلث الأول من الليل والسدس الأخير منه حتى يقع قيامه
في جوف الليل ووسطه فهو الأفضل المرتبة الثالثة أن يقوم ثلث الليل فينبغي
أن ينام النصف  الأول والسدس الأخير وبالجملة نوم آخر الليل محبوب لأنه يذهب
النعاس بالغداة وكانوا يكرهون ذلك ويقلل صفرة الوجه والشهرة به فلو قام
أكثر الليل ونام سحرا قلت صفرة وجهه وقل نعاسه وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها
كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أوتر من آخر الليل فإن كانت له حاجة
إلى أهله دنا منهن وإلا اضطجع في مصلاه حتى يأتيه بلال فيؤذنه للصلاة (2)
وقالت أيضا رضي الله عنها ما ألفيته بعد السحر إلا نائما (3) حتى قال بعض
السلف هذه الضجعة قبل الصبح سنة منهم أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه وكان نوم هذا
الوقت سببا للمكاشفة والمشاهدة من وراء حجب الغيب وذلك لأرباب القلوب وفيه
استراحة PageV01P359
تعين على الورد الأول من أوراد النهار وقيام ثلث الليل من النصف الأخير
ونوم السدس الأخير قيام داود صلى الله عليه وسلم المرتبة الرابعة أن يقوم
سدس الليل أو خمسه وأفضله أن يكون في النصف الأخير وقبل السدس الأخير منه
المرتبة الخامسة أن لا يراعي التقدير فإن ذلك إنما يتيسر لنبي يوحى إليه أو
لمن يعرف منازل القمر ويوكل به من يراقبه ويواظبه ويوقظه ثم ربما يضطرب في
ليالي الغيم ولكنه يقوم من أول الليل إلى أن يغلبه النوم فإذا انتبه قام
فإذا غلبه النوم عاد إلى النوم فيكون له في الليل نومتان وقومتان وهو من
مكابدة الليل وأشد الأعمال وأفضلها وقد كان هذا من أخلاق رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم (1) وهو طريقة ابن عمر وأولي العزم من الصحابة وجماعة من
التابعين رضي الله عنهم وكان بعض السلف يقول هي أول نومة فإذا انتبهت ثم
عدت إلى النوم فلا أنام الله لي عينا فأما قيام رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم من حيث المقدار فلم يكن على ترتيب واحد بل ربما كان يقوم نصف الليل أو
ثلثه أو سدسه (2) يختلف ذلك في الليالي ودل عليه قوله تعالى في الموضعين من
سورة المزمل إن ربك يعلم أنك تقوم أدنى من ثلثي الليل ونصفه  وثلثه فأدنى من
ثلثي الليل كأنه بصفه ونصف سدسه فإن كسر قوله ونصفه وثلثه كان نصف الثلثين
فيقرب من الثلث والربع وإن نصب كان نصف الليل وقالت عائشة رضي الله عنها
كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقوم إذا سمع الصارخ (3) يعني الديك وهذا يكون
السدس فما دونه وروى غير واحد أنه قال راعيت صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم في السفر ليلا فنام بعد العشاء زمانا ثم استيقظ فنظر في الأفق فقال
ربنا ما خلقت هذا باطلا حتى بلغ إنك لا تخلف الميعاد ثم استل من فراشه
سواكا فاستاك به وتوضأ وصلى حتى قلت صلى مثل الذي نام ثم اضطجع حتى قلت نام
مثل ما صلى ثم استيقظ فقال ما قال أول مرة وفعل ما فعل أول مرة (4) المرتبة
السادسة وهي الأقل أن يقوم مقدار أربع ركعات أو ركعتين أو تتعذر عليه
الطهارة فيجلس مستقبل القبلة ساعة مشتغلا بالذكر والدعاء فيكتب في جملة
قوام الليل برحمة الله وفضله وقد جاء في الأثر صل من الليل ولو قدر حلب شاة
(5) فهذه طرق القسمة فليختر المريد لنفسه ما يراه أيسر عليه وحيث يتعذر
عليه القيام في وسط الليل فلا ينبغي أن يهمل إحياء ما بين العشاءين والورد
الذي بعد العشاء ثم يقوم قبل الصبح وقت السحر فلا يدركه الصبح PageV01P360
نائما ويقوم بطرفي الليل وهذه هي المرتبة السابعة ومهما كان النظر إلى
المقدار فترتيب هذه المراتب بحسب طول الوقت وقصره وأما في الرتبة الخامسة
والسابعة لم ينظر فيهما إلى القدر فليس يجري أمرهما في التقدم والتأخر على
الترتيب المذكور إذ السابعة ليست دون ما ذكرناه في الس
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥayya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Life, vitality, and the opposite of death; reviving that which was lifeless.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Spiritual vivification (iḥyāʾ) of the heart through worship, as opposed to mere bodily wakefulness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for restoring life; metaphorical (majāz) here for dedicating the night to devotional acts, making it "alive" with obedience.
- Root: ق-س-م (qasama)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, and distribution into parts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Systematic categorization of devotional practices by measure (miqdār).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal division of time; metaphorical for methodological classification of worship levels.
- Root: ر-ت-ب (rataba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ordering, arranging, and establishing ranks in sequence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Hierarchical gradation of spiritual stations (marātib).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical arrangement; metaphorical for degrees of excellence in devotion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing the syntactic parsing of "if...then" structures and exceptions (e.g., "unless overcome by sleep"), ensuring precise logical sequencing in the author's prescriptions.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the revival of the night, with respect to its measure (miqdār), has seven ranks. The first is the revival of the entire night. This is the affair of the strong ones who have devoted themselves exclusively to the worship of the night, delighting in its intimate communion (munājāt), and it has become nourishment for them and life for their hearts. Thus, they are not wearied by the length of standing, and they relegate sleep to the daytime, at the time when people are occupied. This was the way of a group of the predecessors (salaf). They used to pray the dawn prayer with the ablution of the evening prayer. Abū Ṭālib al-Makkī narrated that this was reported on the basis of continuous transmission (tawātur) and widespread fame from forty of the Followers (tābiʿūn). Among them were those who persisted in this for forty years. He mentioned among them: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib and Ṣafwān ibn Sulaym, the two Medinese; Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ and Wahīb ibn al-Ward, the two Meccans; Ṭāwūs and Wahb ibn Munabbih, the two Yemenites; al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham and al-Ḥakam, the two Kufans; Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī and ʿAlī ibn Bakkār, the two Syrians; Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Khawwāṣ and Abū ʿĀṣim, the two ʿAbbādians; Ḥabīb Abū Muḥammad and Abū Jābir al-Salmānī, the two Persians; Mālik ibn Dīnār, Sulaymān al-Taymī, Yazīd al-Raqāshī, Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, and Yaḥyā al-Bakkāʾ, the Basrans; and Kahmas ibn al-Minhāl, who would complete the Qurʾān ninety times in a month, and whatever he did not comprehend, he would return and read it again. Also from the people of Medina: Abū Ḥāzim and Muḥammad ibn al-Munkadir, among a group whose number is great.

The second rank is to stand in prayer for half the night. The number of those who persisted in this from the predecessors is not limited. The best manner in this is to sleep the first third of the night and the last sixth of it, so that one's standing occurs in the middle and heart of the night; this is the most virtuous.

The third rank is to stand for a third of the night. One should sleep the first half and the last sixth. In sum, sleep at the end of the night is beloved, because it removes drowsiness in the morning, and they used to dislike that (i.e., morning drowsiness), and it diminishes the pallor of the face and the notoriety (of one's devotion). For if one stood for most of the night and slept at the dawn hour (saḥar), his facial pallor would be less and his drowsiness less. ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, when he performed the witr prayer at the end of the night, if he had need of his family, he would draw near to them; otherwise, he would lie down in his prayer place until Bilāl came to him and called him to prayer." She also said, may God be pleased with her: "I never found him after the dawn hour (saḥar) except sleeping." Until some of the predecessors said: "This lying down before the dawn prayer is a sunnah," among them Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him. Sleep at this time was a cause for unveiling (mukāshafah) and witnessing (mushāhadah) from behind the veils of the unseen, and this is for the masters of hearts. In it is rest that aids one for the first litany (wird) of the day's litanies. Standing for a third of the night, from the latter half, with sleep in the last sixth, is the standing of David, peace be upon him.

The fourth rank is to stand for a sixth of the night or a fifth. The most virtuous is that it be in the latter half, before the last sixth of it.

The fifth rank is not to observe a fixed measure, for that is only facilitated for a prophet to whom revelation comes, or for one who knows the stations of the moon and appoints someone to watch it, persist in it, and wake him. Then perhaps he may be disturbed on cloudy nights. Rather, he stands from the beginning of the night until sleep overcomes him; when he awakens, he stands; when sleep overcomes him, he returns to sleep. Thus, he has two sleeps and two standings in the night. This is among the strenuous struggles of the night (mukābadah al-layl) and the most severe and most virtuous of deeds. This was among the character traits of the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, and it is the way of Ibn ʿUmar, the resolute ones among the Companions, and a group of the Followers, may God be pleased with them. Some of the predecessors used to say: "The first sleep is such; if I awaken and then return to sleep, may God not give my eye sleep." As for the standing of the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, with respect to measure, it was not upon a single arrangement. Rather, sometimes he would stand half the night, or a third, or a sixth, varying across the nights. This is indicated by His saying, the Exalted, in the two places of Sūrat al-Muzzammil: {«إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ»} ("Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it"). For "less than two-thirds of the night" is as if He described half and a sixth. For if one breaks the phrase "and half of it, and a third of it" (with genitive construction), it would be half of the two-thirds, approximating a third and a quarter; and if one reads it in the accusative, it is half of the night. ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "He, peace be upon him, would stand when he heard the crowing one," meaning the rooster, and this is a sixth or less. More than one narrator reported that he said: "I watched the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, on a journey at night. He slept after the evening prayer for a time, then awoke and looked at the horizon, saying: {«رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا»} ("Our Lord, You did not create this in vain") until he reached {«إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ»} ("Indeed, You do not fail the promise"). Then he drew from his bedding a toothstick (siwāk), cleaned his teeth with it, performed ablution, and prayed until I said: 'He prayed as long as he slept.' Then he lay down until I said: 'He slept as long as he prayed.' Then he awoke and said what he said the first time, and did what he did the first time."

The sixth rank, which is the least, is to stand for the measure of four units (rakʿāt) or two units, or if ablution becomes difficult for him, he sits facing the qiblah for an hour, occupied with remembrance (dhikr) and supplication (duʿāʾ), and thus he is recorded among the number of those who stand the night, by God's mercy and bounty. It has come in the tradition (athar): "Pray during the night, even if (it be) the measure of milking a sheep." These are the methods of division. Let the seeker (murīd) choose for himself what he finds easiest, and where standing in the middle of the night becomes difficult for him, he should not neglect reviving the period between the two evening prayers (al-ʿishāʾayn) and the litany (wird) after the evening prayer. Then he stands before the dawn prayer at the time of saḥar, so that dawn does not overtake him sleeping, and he stands at both ends of the night. This is the seventh rank. Whenever the consideration is of measure, the ordering of these ranks is according to the length and shortness of time. As for the fifth and seventh ranks, no measure is considered in them, so their precedence and posteriority do not follow the aforementioned order, for the seventh is not below what we mentioned in the sixth, nor is the fifth below the fourth.

chapters.title_en: Exposition of the Virtuous Nights and Days
chapters.arabic_text:
||| بيان الليالي والأيام الفاضلة

اعلم أن الليالي المخصوصة بمزيد الفضل التي يتأكد فيها استحباب الإحياء
في السنة خمس عشرة ليلة لا ينبغي أن يغفل المريد عنها فإنها مواسم الخيرات
ومظان التجارات ومتى غفل التاجر عن المواسم لم يربح ومتى غفل المريد عن
فضائل الأوقات لم ينجح فستة من هذه الليالي في  شهر رمضان خمس في أوتار
العشر الأخير إذ فيها يطلب ليلة القدر وليلة سبع عشرة من رمضان فهي ليلة
صبيحتها يوم الفرقان يوم التقى الجمعان فيه كانت وقعة بدر وقال ابن الزبير
رحمه الله هي ليلة القدر وأما التسع الأخر فأول ليلة من المحرم وليلة
عاشوراء وأول ليلة من رجب وليلة النصف منه وليلة سبع وعشرين منه وهي ليلة
المعراج وفيها صلاة مأثورة فقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم للعامل في هذه
الليلة حسنات مائة سنة (1) فمن صلى في هذه الليلة اثنتي عشرة ركعة يقرأ في
كل ركعة فاتحة الكتاب وسورة من القرآن ويتشهد في كل ركعتين ويسلم في آخرهن
ثم يقول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر مائة مرة ثم
يستغفر الله مائة مرة ويصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مائة مرة ويدعو
لنفسه بما شاء من أمر دنياه وآخرته ويصبح صائما فإن الله يستجيب دعاءه كله
إلا أن يدعو في معصية وليلة النصف من شعبان ففيها مائة ركعة يقرأ في كل
ركعة بعد الفاتحة سورة الإخلاص عشر مرات كانوا لا يتركونها كما أوردناه في
صلاة التطوع وليلة عرفة وليلتا العيدين قال صلى الله عليه وسلم من أحيا
ليلتي العيدين لم يمت قلبه يوم تموت القلوب (2) وأما الأيام الفاضلة فتسعة
عشر يستحب مواصلة الأوراد فيها يوم عرفة ويوم عاشوراء ويوم سبعة وعشرين من
رجب له شرف عظيم روى أبو هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال من صام
يوم سبع وعشرين من رجب كتب الله له صيام ستين شهرا (3) وهو اليوم الذي أهبط
الله فيه جبرائيل عليه السلام على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالرسالة ويوم
سبعة عشر من رمضان وهو يوم وقعة بدر ويوم النصف من شعبان ويوم الجمعة ويوما
العيدين والأيام المعلومات وهي عشر من ذي الحجة والأيام المعدودات وهي أيام
التشريق وقد روى أنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إذا سلم يوم
الجمعة سلمت الأيام  وإذا سلم شهر رمضان سلمت السنة (4) وقال بعض العلماء من
أخذه مهناة في الأيام الخمسة في الدنيا لم ينل مهناة في الآخرة وأراد به
العيدين والجمعة وعرفة وعاشوراء ومن فواضل الأيام في الأسبوع يوم الخميس
والاثنين ترفع فيهما الأعمال إلى الله تعالى وقد ذكرنا فضائل الأشهر
والأيام للصيام في كتاب الصوم فلا حاجة إلى الإعادة والله أعلم وصلى الله
على كل عبد مصطفى من كل العالمين PageV01P361
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف-ض-ل (faḍl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Excess, surplus, superiority; a virtue that elevates one thing above another in rank or merit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, faḍl denotes divine bounty and the supererogatory merit (thawāb) attached to specific times, distinguishing them from ordinary moments.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for surplus in quantity or quality; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to times, indicating their elevated status as vessels of divine grace.
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥayyā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To live; to revive, to keep awake in vigil; iḥyāʾ implies animation and spiritual wakefulness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Iḥyāʾ al-layl signifies devotional wakefulness—prayer, remembrance, and supplication—as a means of enlivening the heart, paralleling the Quranic notion of reviving hearts through faith.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical life; metaphorical for spiritual vigilance, where the night is "revived" by acts of worship, as if it were dead and brought to life.
- Root: م-ظ-ن (maẓannah)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A place or time where something is expected or sought; a locus of hope and anticipation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Maẓānn al-tijārāt—markets of trade—metaphorically denotes opportunities for spiritual profit, where deeds are exchanged for divine reward.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a place of expectation; metaphorical for times of heightened divine acceptance, where the seeker hopes to "profit" like a merchant.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Temporal Clause Coordination (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-sharṭ)—The sentence "فستة من هذه الليالي... وأما التسع الأخر" employs balanced coordination (tadmin) between enumerated categories, requiring precise parsing of the implicit verb (kāna) and the distributive structure (badal) to maintain syntactic parallelism across the list of nights and days.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the nights specifically distinguished by surplus merit, in which the recommendation of vigil (iḥyāʾ) is emphasized, are fifteen nights in the year—the seeker (murīd) must not be heedless of them, for they are seasons of good deeds and markets of trade (maẓānn al-tijārāt). Whenever the merchant is heedless of the seasons, he does not profit; and whenever the seeker is heedless of the virtues of times, he does not succeed.

Six of these nights are in the month of Ramadan: five in the odd nights of the last ten [nights], for therein the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr) is sought; and the night of the seventeenth of Ramadan—for its morning is the Day of Criterion (yawm al-furqān), the day the two hosts met, wherein occurred the Battle of Badr. Ibn al-Zubayr—may God have mercy on him—said: It is the Night of Power.

As for the remaining nine: the first night of al-Muḥarram; the night of ʿĀshūrāʾ; the first night of Rajab; the night of the middle of it [Rajab]; and the night of the twenty-seventh of it—which is the Night of the Ascension (laylat al-miʿrāj). In it there is an attested prayer (ṣalāh maʾthūrah), for he—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "For the one who acts in this night, [there are] the good deeds of a hundred years." (1) So whoever prays in this night twelve rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah the Opening of the Book (fātiḥat al-kitāb) and a chapter from the Quran, and performs the tashahhud in every two rakʿahs, and gives the salutation at their end, then says: "Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is Greater" one hundred times; then seeks forgiveness from God one hundred times; and sends blessings upon the Prophet—peace and blessings be upon him—one hundred times; and supplicates for himself for whatever he wishes of the matters of his world and his hereafter; and awakens fasting—then God answers all his supplication, unless he supplicates for something in disobedience.

And the night of the middle of Shaʿbān: in it [there are] one hundred rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah after the Opening [sūrat] al-Ikhlāṣ ten times. They would not abandon it, as we have related in the [book of] supererogatory prayer (ṣalāt al-tatawwuʿ).

And the night of ʿArafah, and the two nights of the two Festivals (al-ʿīdayn). He—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Whoever revives the two nights of the two Festivals, his heart will not die on the day when hearts die." (2)

As for the virtuous days, they are nineteen. It is recommended to maintain the regular litanies (awrād) therein: the Day of ʿArafah; the Day of ʿĀshūrāʾ; and the Day of the twenty-seventh of Rajab—it has great honor. Abū Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—said: "Whoever fasts the Day of the twenty-seventh of Rajab, God writes for him the fasting of sixty months." (3) It is the day on which God descended Gabriel—peace be upon him—upon Muḥammad—peace and blessings be upon him—with the message (al-risālah).

And the Day of the seventeenth of Ramadan—it is the Day of the Battle of Badr; and the Day of the middle of Shaʿbān; and the Day of Friday; and the two days of the two Festivals; and the "known days" (al-ayyām al-maʿlūmāt)—which are the ten [days] of Dhū al-Ḥijjah; and the "numbered days" (al-ayyām al-maʿdūdāt)—which are the days of Tashrīq.

And Anas narrated from the Messenger of God—peace and blessings be upon him—that he said: "When Friday is safe, the days are safe; and when the month of Ramadan is safe, the year is safe." (4)

And some scholars said: Whoever takes ease (muhannāʾ) in the five days in this world will not attain ease in the hereafter—meaning thereby the two Festivals, Friday, ʿArafah, and ʿĀshūrāʾ.

And among the virtuous days of the week are Thursday and Monday, wherein deeds are raised up to God—Exalted is He. We have already mentioned the virtues of the months and the days for fasting in the Book of Fasting (kitāb al-ṣawm), so there is no need for repetition. And God knows best, and may God send blessings upon every chosen servant from all the worlds. Page V01P361

chapters.title_en: In the Name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate
chapters.arabic_text: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب س م (b-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes the act of naming, marking, or branding; from it derives "ism" (name), signifying that which elevates and identifies an entity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, "bismillāh" is the invocation of God’s essence (al-dhāt) as the sole source of all acts, blessings, and commencements; it affirms divine sovereignty over every beginning.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, it is a genitive construction (muḍāf ilayh) indicating "with the name of God"; metaphorically (majāz), it signals the consecration of an act by divine authority, not merely a verbal preface.
- Root: ر ح م (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root conveys mercy, tenderness, and compassion; "al-Raḥmān" denotes an all-encompassing, universal mercy, while "al-Raḥīm" indicates a perpetual, specific mercy toward the faithful.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Al-Raḥmān is a divine attribute of essential mercy (raḥmah dhātiyyah) covering all creation, whereas al-Raḥīm is an active, volitional mercy (raḥmah fiʿliyyah) that rewards obedience and forgives transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The pairing distinguishes between the absolute, unqualified mercy (ḥaqīqah) and the conditional, relational mercy (majāz) that manifests in divine acts of forgiveness and grace.
- Sībawayh Rule: Genitive Construction (al-ijārah) — The phrase "bismillāh" is a prepositional phrase (jār wa-majrūr) where the preposition "bi" governs the noun "ism" in the genitive, and "Allāh" is a genitive annex (muḍāf ilayh), establishing a syntactic bond of dependence and consecration.
chapters.translation: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

chapters.title_en: The Book of the Etiquette of Eating — Book One of the Quarter of Customs from The Revival of the Religious Sciences
chapters.arabic_text:
| كتاب آداب الأكل وهو الكتاب الأول من ربع العادات من كتاب إحياء العلوم

الحمد لله الذي أحسن تدبير الكائنات فخلق الأرض والسماوات
وأنزل الماء الفرات من المعصرات فأخرج به الحب والنبات
وقدر الأرزاق والأفوات
وحفظ بالمأكولات قوى الحيوانات وأعان على الطاعات والأعمال الصالحات بأكل
الطيبات والصلاة على محمد ذي المعجزات الباهرات وعلى آله وأصحابه صلاة
تتوالى على ممر الأوقات وتتضاعف بتعاقب الساعات وسلم تسليما كثيرا
أما بعد فإن مقصد ذوي الألباب لقاء الله تعالى في دار الثواب ولا طريق
إلى الوصول للقاء الله إلى بالعلم والعمل ولا تمكن المواظبة عليهما إلا
بسلامة البدن ولا تصفو سلامة البدن إلا بالأطعمة والأقوات والتناول منها
بقدر الحاجة على تكرر الأوقات فمن هذا الوجه قال بعض السلف الصالحين إن
الأكل من الدين وعليه نبه رب العالمين بقوله وهو أصدق القائلين كلوا من
الطيبات واعملوا صالحا فمن يقدم على الأكل ليستعين به على العلم والعمل
ويقوي به على التقوى فلا ينبغي أن يترك نفسه مهملا سدى يسترسل في الأكل
استرسال البهائم في المرعى فإن ما هو ذريعة إلى الدين ووسيلة إليه ينبغي أن
تظهر أنوار الدين عليه
وإنما أنوار الدين آدابه وسننه التي يزم العبد بزمامها ويلجم المتقي
بلجامها حتى يتزن بميزان الشرع شهوة الطعام في إقدامها وإحجامها فيصير
بسببها مدفعة للوزر ومجلبة للأجر وإن كان فيها أوفى حظ للنفس
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الرجل ليؤجر حتى في اللقمة يرفعها إلى فيه
والى في امعليه السلام رأته (1)
وإنما ذلك إذا رفعها بالدين وللدين  مراعيا فيه آدابه ووظائفه
وها نحن نرشد إلى وظائف الدين في الأكل فرائضها وسننها وآدابها ومروءاتها
وهيئاتها في أربعة أبواب وفصل في آخرها
الباب الأول فيما لا بد للآكل من مراعاته وإن انفرد بالأكل
الباب الثاني فيما يزيد من الآداب بسبب الاجتماع على الأكل
الباب الثالث فيما يخص تقديم الطعام إلى الإخوان الزائرين
الباب الرابع فيما يخص الدعوة والضيافة وأشباهها PageV02P002
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of consuming, ingesting; extends to any act of taking in sustenance
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical eating as a means (dhārīʿah) to spiritual ends; not an end in itself
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for mastication; metaphorical (majāz) for deriving benefit or absorbing knowledge
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The clause "fa-man yuqdim ʿalā al-akl..." establishes a conditional protasis whose apodosis carries the normative injunction, requiring careful parsing of the particle "fa" as resumptive.
chapters.translation:
Praise be to God, who perfected the governance of all existent things, creating the earth and the heavens, sending down sweet water from the rain-clouds, bringing forth thereby grain and vegetation, apportioning provisions and their lacks, preserving through foods the vital forces of animals, and aiding in acts of obedience and righteous deeds through the consumption of wholesome things. And blessings upon Muhammad, possessor of dazzling miracles, and upon his family and companions — a blessing that continues across the passage of times and multiplies with the succession of hours — and abundant peace.

To proceed: The aim of those possessed of intellects is the meeting with God Most High in the abode of recompense. There is no path to attaining the meeting with God save through knowledge and action, and perseverance in both is impossible except through soundness of the body, and soundness of the body is not purified except through foods and provisions, partaking of them according to the measure of need, repeated over successive times. From this aspect, some of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-ṣāliḥīn) said that eating is part of religion. Upon this, the Lord of the Worlds — and He is the most truthful of speakers — alerted us in His saying: {«كُلُوا مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَاعْمَلُوا صَالِحًا»} ("Eat of the wholesome things and work righteousness"). So whoever undertakes eating to seek aid thereby for knowledge and action, and to strengthen himself for piety, he ought not to abandon his soul neglected and aimless, letting himself loose in eating as beasts loose themselves in pasture. For that which is a means (dhārīʿah) to religion and a pathway unto it — the lights of religion ought to shine upon it.

And the lights of religion are only its etiquettes (ādāb) and its normative practices (sunān), by whose reins the servant is bridled and with whose bit the God-fearing are reined, until the appetite for food is weighed by the balance of the Sacred Law (al-sharʿ) in its advance and its retreat. Thereby it becomes a repeller of sin and an attractor of reward, even if therein lies the fullest share for the soul. The Prophet — peace be upon him — said: "Indeed, a man is rewarded even for the morsel he raises to his mouth" — and likewise for what his wife raises to his mouth (1). And that is only so when he raises it with religion and for religion, observing therein its etiquettes and its obligatory functions (waẓāʾif).

And here we now guide to the religious functions in eating: their obligatory duties (farāʾiḍ), their normative practices (sunān), their etiquettes (ādāb), their chivalrous proprieties (murūʾāt), and their forms (hayʾāt) — in four chapters, with a concluding section at their end.

Chapter One: What the eater must observe even when eating alone.
Chapter Two: What additional etiquettes arise from gathering together over food.
Chapter Three: What pertains specifically to presenting food to visiting brethren.
Chapter Four: What pertains specifically to invitations, hospitality, and the like.

chapters.title_en: The First Chapter on What the Solitary [Retreatant] Necessarily Requires, Comprising Three Divisions: Before Eating, During Eating, and After Finishing
chapters.arabic_text: || الباب الأول فيما لابد للمنفرد منه وهو ثلاثة أقسام قسم قبل الأكل وقسم مع الأكل وقسم بعد الفراغ منه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ف ر د (f-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Solitude, uniqueness, being alone; al-fard is the single one, and tafarrud denotes isolation from others.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, infirād signifies the soul’s withdrawal from worldly entanglements for devotional focus, aligning with the solitary retreat (khalwah) in spiritual praxis.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical aloneness; metaphorical (majāz) — detachment of the heart from distractions, even amid company.
- Root: ق س م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, categories; qism is a part or share.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for logical partitioning of obligations or conditions into exhaustive types (aqsām), as in jurisprudential taxonomy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — cutting into parts; metaphorical — systematic classification of a subject’s aspects.
- Root: أ ك ل (a-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Eating, consuming; also metaphorically for devouring (e.g., usury).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical nourishment; in religious ethics, regulated by lawful (ḥalāl) and moderation, tied to bodily strength for worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — ingestion; metaphorical — any form of acquisition or consumption (e.g., consuming wealth unjustly).
- Root: ف ر غ (f-r-gh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Emptiness, completion, cessation; faragha means to finish or vacate.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes the end of an act, often followed by another prescribed act (e.g., «فإذا فرغت فانصب» {So when you have finished, then labor}).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — emptying a vessel; metaphorical — concluding a task, transitioning to the next duty.
- Sībawayh Rule: Nominal Sentence with Inceptive Particle (al-ibtidā’ bi-al-ism) — The clause begins with «الباب الأول» as a definite subject (mubtada’) governing the predicate «فيما لابد...», establishing a topical heading. The particle «وهو» introduces an explanatory apposition (badal) or circumstantial clause (ḥāl), clarifying the tripartite division.
chapters.translation: I say: The first chapter concerns what the solitary [retreatant] necessarily requires, and it comprises three divisions: a division before eating, a division during eating, and a division after finishing from it.

chapters.title_en: Section 181 — On the Etiquette Preceding the Meal
chapters.arabic_text:
||| القسم الأول في الآداب التي تتقدم على الأكل وهي

الأول أن يكون الطعام بعد كونه حلالا في نفسه طيبا في جهة مكسبه موافقا
للسنة والورع لم يكتسب بسبب مكروه في الشرع ولا بحكم هوى ومداهنة في دين
على ما سيأتي في معنى الطيب المطلق في كتاب الحلال والحرام وقد أمر الله
تعالى بأكل الطيب وهو الحلال وقدم النهي عن الأكل بالباطل على القتل تفخيما
لأمر الحرام وتعظيما لبركة الحلال فقال تعالى يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا
تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل إلى قوله ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم الآية فالأصل في
الطعام كونه طيبا وهو من الفرائض وأصول الدين
الثاني غسل اليد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم الوضوء قبل الطعام ينفي الفقر
وبعده ينفي اللمم (1)
وفي رواية ينفي الفقر قبل الطعام وبعده ولأن اليد لا تخلو عن لوث في
تعاطي الأعمال فغسلها أقرب إلى النظافة والنزاهة
ولأن الأكل لقصد الاستعانة على الدين عبادة فهو جدير بأن يقدم عليه ما
يجري منه مجرى الطهارة من الصلاة
الثالث أن يوضع الطعام على السفرة الموضوعة على الأرض فهو أقرب إلى فعل
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من رفعه على المائدة كان رسول الله صلى الله
عليه وسلم إذا أتى بطعام وضعه على الأرض (2) حديث أنس ما أكل رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم على خوان ولا في سكرجة الحديث رواه البخاري //
قيل فعلى ماذا كنتم تأكلون قال على السفرة وقيل أربع أحدثت بعد رسول الله
صلى  الله عليه وسلم الموائد والمناخل والأشنان والشبع واعلم أنا وإن قلنا
الأكل على السفرة أولى فلسنا نقول الأكل على المائدة منهي عنه نهي كراهة أو
تحريم إذا لم يثبت فيه نهي
وما يقال إنه أبدع بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فليس كل ما أبدع
منهيا بل المنهي بدعة تضاد سنة ثابتة وترفع أمرا من الشرع مع بقاء علته بل
الإبداع قد يجب في بعض الأحوال إذا تغيرت الأسباب وليس في المائدة إلا رفع
الطعام عن الأرض لتيسير الأكل وأمثال ذلك مما لا كراهة فيه
والأربع التي جمعت في أنها مبدعة ليست متساوية بل الأشنان حسن لما فيه من
النظافة فإن الغسل مستحب للنظافة والأشنان أتم في التنظيف وكانوا لا
يستعملونه لأنه ربما كان لا يعتاد عندهم أو لا يتيسر أو كانوا مشغولين
بأمور أهم من المبالغة في النظافة فقد كانوا لا يغسلون اليد أيضا وكانت
مناديلهم أخمص أقدامهم وذلك لا يمنع كون الغسل PageV02P003
مستحبا
وأما المنخل فالمقصود منه تطييب الطعام وذلك مباح ما لم ينته إلى التنعم
المفرط
وأما المائدة فتيسير للأكل وهو أيضا مباح ما لم ينته إلى الكبر والتعاظم
وأما الشبع فهو أشد هذه الأربعة فإنه يدعو إلى تهييج الشهوات وتحريك
الأدواء في البدن فلتدرك التفرقة بين هذه المبدعات
الرابع أن يحسن الجلسة على السفرة في أول جلوسه ويستديمها كذلك كان رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ربما جثا للأكل على ركبتيه وجلس على ظهر قدميه
وربما نصب رجله اليمنى وجلس على اليسرى (1)
وكان يقول لا آكل متكئا
حديث كان يقول لا آكل متكئا أخرجه البخاري من حديث أبي جحيفة
إنما أنا عبد آكل كما يأكل العبد وأجلس كما يجلس العبد
حديث إنما أنا عبد آكل كما يأكل العبد وأجلس كما يجلس العبد تقدم قبله من
حديث أنس بلفظ وأفعل بدل وأجلس ورواه البزار من حديث ابن عمر دون قوله
وأجلس (2) حديث ما ملأ ابن آدم وعاء شرا من بطنه الحديث أخرجه الترمذي وقال
حسن والنسائي  وابن ماجه من حديث المقداد بن معد يكرب
ومن ضرورة هذه النية أن لا يمد اليد إلى الطعام إلا وهو جائع فيكون الجوع
أحد ما لا بد من تقديمه على الأكل
ثم ينبغي أن يرفع اليد قبل الشبع ومن فعل ذلك استغنى عن الطبيب وسيأتي
فائدة قلة الأكل وكيفية التدريج في التقليل منه في كتاب كسر شهوة الطعام من
ربع المهلكات
السادس أن يرضى بالموجود من الرزق والحاضر من الطعام ولا يجتهد في التنعم
وطلب الزيادة وانتظار الأدم بل من كرامة الخبز أن لا ينتظر به الأدم وقد
ورد الأمر بإكرام الخبز (3)
فكل ما يديم الرمق ويقوي على العبادة فهو خير كثير لا ينبغي أن يستحقر بل
لا ينتظر بالخبز الصلاة إن حضر وقتها إذا كان في الوقت متسع
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا حضر العشاء والعشاء فابدءوا بالعشاء (4)
وكان ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما ربما سمع قراءة الإمام ولا يقوم من عشائه
ومهما كانت النفس لا تتوق إلى الطعام ولم يكن في تأخير الطعام ضرر
فالأولى تقديم الصلاة
فأما إذا حضر الطعام وأقيمت الصلاة وكان في التأخير ما يبرد الطعام أو
يشوش أمره فتقديمه أحب عند اتساع الوقت تاقت النفس أو لم تتق لعموم الخبر
ولأن القلب لا يخلو عن الإلتفات إلى الطعام الموضوع وإن لم يكن الجوع غالبا
PageV02P004
السابع أن يجتهد في تكثير الأيدي على الطعام ولو من أهله وولده
قال صلى الله عليه وسلم اجتمعوا على طعامكم يبارك لكم فيه (1)
وقال أنس رضي الله عنه كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يأكل وحده
(2)
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم خي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, wholesomeness, and freedom from defilement—both sensory and moral.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The licit (ḥalāl) as that which the Law pronounces good; the "good" (ṭayyib) is the operative condition of lawful sustenance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in reference to food's intrinsic permissibility; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to the mode of acquisition.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Precedence (Taqdīm al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (condition of lawfulness) governs the apodosis (obligation to consume), as in the verse's ordering of prohibition before interdiction.
chapters.translation:
I say: The first division concerns the etiquettes that precede eating, and they are as follows.

**First**: That the food, after being lawful in itself, be good (ṭayyib) in the manner of its acquisition—conforming to the Sunnah and to scrupulous piety (waraʿ)—not acquired through something disapproved in the Law, nor through the ruling of caprice and dissimulation in religion, as will come in the discussion of the absolute good in the Book of the Lawful and the Unlawful. God—exalted is He—has commanded the eating of the good, which is the lawful, and He placed the prohibition against consuming wealth wrongfully before the prohibition against killing, as a magnification of the matter of the unlawful and a veneration of the blessing of the lawful. He said—exalted is He: {«O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves wrongfully»} up to His saying {«and do not kill yourselves»} (Q 4:29). Thus the foundational principle regarding food is that it be good, and this is among the obligatory duties and the roots of religion.

**Second**: Washing the hands. The Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "The ablution before food removes poverty, and after it removes minor sins (al-lamam)." In another narration: "It removes poverty before food and after it." This is because the hand is not free from filth in the course of engaging in occupations, so washing it is closer to cleanliness and purity. And because eating, being intended as an aid to religion, is an act of worship, it is fitting that one precede it with what serves as its purification, just as purification precedes prayer.

**Third**: That the food be placed upon a cloth (sufrah) spread on the ground, for this is closer to the practice of the Messenger of God—peace be upon him—than raising it upon a table (māʾidah). The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—when food was brought to him, placed it on the ground. The ḥadīth of Anas: "The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—never ate upon a dining tray (khwān) nor upon a small dish (sukrujjah)"—narrated by al-Bukhārī. It was said: "Then upon what did you eat?" He replied: "Upon the cloth." And it was said: "Four things were innovated after the Messenger of God—peace be upon him: tables, sieves, cleansing earth (ushnān), and satiety."

Know that although we say eating upon the cloth is preferable, we do not say eating upon the table is prohibited—neither by way of disapproval (karāhah) nor by way of unlawfulness (taḥrīm)—since no prohibition has been established regarding it. As for the saying that it was innovated after the Messenger of God—peace be upon him—not everything innovated is prohibited; rather, the prohibited innovation is one that contradicts an established Sunnah and abolishes a matter of the Law while its cause remains. Indeed, innovation may even become obligatory in certain circumstances when the causes have changed. There is nothing in the table except raising the food from the ground to facilitate eating and the like—matters in which there is no disapproval.

The four things gathered as being innovations are not equal in rank. The cleansing earth (ushnān) is good, for it contains cleanliness; washing is recommended for cleanliness, and ushnān is more complete in cleansing. They did not use it because it was perhaps not customary among them, or not readily available, or they were occupied with matters more important than excess in cleanliness. Indeed, they would not wash their hands either, and their napkins were the soles of their feet—yet this does not prevent washing from being recommended.

As for the sieve, its purpose is to refine the food, and that is permissible so long as it does not reach excessive indulgence.

As for the table, it facilitates eating, and it too is permissible so long as it does not reach arrogance and self-aggrandizement.

As for satiety, it is the most severe of these four, for it incites the appetites and stirs diseases in the body. So perceive the distinction among these innovations.

**Fourth**: That one perfect his sitting posture at the cloth from the beginning of his sitting and maintain it. The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—would sometimes kneel for eating upon his knees and sit upon the tops of his feet, and sometimes he would erect his right leg and sit upon his left. He would say: "I do not eat reclining." And he said: "I am but a servant; I eat as the servant eats, and I sit as the servant sits." From the necessity of this intention is that one not extend his hand to food except while hungry, so that hunger becomes one of the things that must precede eating.

Then one should raise his hand before satiety. Whoever does this dispenses with the physician. The benefit of eating little and the manner of gradual reduction in it will come in the Book of Breaking the Appetite for Food, from the Quarter of the Destroyers.

**Sixth**: That one be content with what is present of provision and available of food, and not strive for indulgence, nor seek increase, nor wait for a relish (udm). For it is part of honoring bread that one not wait for a relish with it. The command to honor bread has been reported. For whatever sustains life and strengthens one for worship is abundant good that should not be belittled. Rather, one should not delay the prayer for bread if its time has arrived, when there is ample time. He—peace be upon him—said: "When the evening meal is served and the night prayer is called, begin with the evening meal." And Ibn ʿUmar—may God be pleased with them both—would sometimes hear the recitation of the imam and not rise from his supper.

When the soul does not crave food and there is no harm in delaying it, then giving precedence to prayer is preferable. But when food is served and the prayer is established, and delaying it would cool the food or disturb its condition, then giving it precedence is more beloved when the time is ample—whether the soul craves it or not—due to the generality of the report, and because the heart is not free from attention to the food placed before it, even if hunger is not dominant.

**Seventh**: That one strive to multiply the hands upon the food, even if from his family and children. He—peace be upon him—said: "Gather together upon your food, and it will be blessed for you." Anas—may God be pleased with him—said: "The Messenger of God—peace be upon him—never ate alone." And he—peace be upon him—said: "The best food is that upon which many hands are placed."
